The F2b release-clears-exhaustion path is a concurrent-only scenario not deterministically reproducible in a single-request test (once a slot transitions exhausted intra-request, subsequent reservations fail the `exhausted_at IS NULL` guard and set `budget_hit`, so no release-after-transition occurs within one request) — covered by the shape test + code reasoning, matching the no-Docker precedent. **Post-review hardening, round 2 (PR #979, two more Codex P2 findings):** (F3) **re-arm `next_run_at` when the release clears a tick-nulled exhaustion.** The scheduler tick's `max_runs` exhaustion path nulls `next_run_at` (`tick_one_workflow_schedule` in `scheduler.rs`), and the due-list query requires `next_run_at IS NOT NULL` — so when a concurrent tick exhausts the schedule DURING a backfill and the backfill then releases below cap, F2b's `exhausted_at`/`exhausted_reason` clear left the schedule un-exhausted yet off the due-list (previously documented as a known limitation). Fixed by giving `release_backfill_budget_slot` a new `rearm_next: Option<DateTime<Utc>>` parameter — **corrected by round 3 F5 below** to the pre-tick due `next_run_at` snapshot (`schedule.next_run_at`, loaded at backfill request start) rather than a recompute from `now`. The clear UPDATE now captures its rows-affected, and **only when it actually un-exhausted a `max_runs_exhausted` row** does a follow-up guarded UPDATE re-arm `next_run_at` — guarded on `next_run_at IS NULL` (so the common intra-backfill case, where our own transition never nulled it, is a no-op) and `exhausted_at IS NULL` (so only a just-un-exhausted row is touched), via a new `rearm_backfill_next_run_stmt!` macro + `rearm_backfill_next_run_generates_the_guarded_rearm_update` no-DB shape test. Every `release_backfill_budget_slot` call site in both dispatch loops passes the per-slot `rearm_next`. **Post-review hardening, round 3 (PR #979, Codex F5):** the round-2 F3 re-arm computed `rearm_next` as `next_run_after_pub(parsed_schedule.as_ref(), now)` — the first slot AFTER `now` — which, when a concurrent tick exhausted an already-DUE catchup schedule (`next_run_at <= now`) mid-backfill and the backfill then released below cap, advanced PAST the due slot the tick skipped, silently dropping that scheduled run. Fixed by re-arming to the pre-tick due `next_run_at` **snapshot** (`schedule.next_run_at`, the `HarvestSchedule` loaded once at the top of `schedule_backfill`, immutable within the handler and captured before any concurrent tick nulled it) instead of a recompute from `now`, so a catchup schedule retries the exact slot the tick skipped; `next_run_after_pub` is now unused in `api.rs` and its import was removed. The `rearm_backfill_next_run_stmt!` macro, its shape test, and the guards are unchanged — only the source of the bound value changed. Manual-schedule correctness is preserved (a manual schedule has `next_run_at = NULL` → `rearm_next = None` → no re-arm). (F4) **connection self-deadlock at pool size 1 (regression from #679's own fix).** #679 acquired a loop-level `sched_conn` on the schedule shard held across the ENTIRE dispatch loop while each slot also checked out a per-slot exec `conn`; on a **single-shard** deployment with a web pool of size 1 (`pool.rs` only rejects size 0), the schedule and exec shards are the SAME pool, so holding `sched_conn` while acquiring `conn` self-deadlocks (the route waits on a connection it already holds). The original pre-#688 backfill held only one connection at a time and was pool-size-1 safe. Fixed by choosing the budget connection per loop arm: each arm computes `let same_pool = schedule_shard == exec_shard;` (workflow: `exec_shard = runtime.router.default_shard()`; DAG: `exec_shard = shard_id` from `pick_for_dag`) and acquires a separate `sched_conn_opt = if same_pool { None } else { Some(acquire_conn(pool.pool_for(schedule_shard)).await?) }` held across the loop ONLY for a genuinely different (multi-shard) pool; at each reserve/release/transition call site `let budget_conn = sched_conn_opt.as_mut().unwrap_or(&mut conn);` reuses the per-slot exec `conn` in the `same_pool` case. When `same_pool`, all budget ops run sequentially on the single `conn` (never two concurrent connections → pool-size-1 safe); when different-pool, the two connections are from distinct pools so concurrent holds don't contend. Borrow-ordering: the two throttle-refund start arms now call `refund_rate_limit_token(&mut conn, ...)` FIRST (that borrow ends) before taking `budget_conn` for the release, and each `budget_conn` borrow is scoped to a single statement so `conn` is free for the following throttle/start work. Assumption: distinct `ShardId`s map to distinct pools in standard single/multi-shard topologies (single-shard always has `schedule_shard == exec_shard`). Regression guard: `backfill_single_shard_pool_size_one_does_not_deadlock` (a non-dry-run backfill against a size-1 pool wrapped in a `tokio::time::timeout` so a deadlock is a clear failure, not a hung binary). Both fixes: no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration; DB/HTTP tests compile-checked here (no Docker), CI runs them Docker-backed. **Post-review hardening, round 4 (PR #979, Codex F6): exhaust the backfill from the LIVE row, not a request-start snapshot.** `transition_backfill_exhausted_if_reached` decided exhaustion from `backfill_budget_reached(reserved_runs_started, schedule.max_runs)` — a `max_runs` value snapshotted at request start — while the reservation UPDATE already evaluated `max_runs`/`runs_started` from the live row. A concurrent `PATCH /admin/schedules/{id}` (issue #771) changing `max_runs` between the reservation and the transition could therefore wrongly exhaust on a raised/removed cap (disabling the schedule from a stale higher `max_runs`) or wrongly skip exhausting an at-cap row on a lowered cap. Fixed by rewriting the transition to a single conditional UPDATE whose WHERE clause reads `max_runs`/`runs_started` from the row itself (`WHERE exhausted_at IS NULL AND max_runs IS NOT NULL AND max_runs > 0 AND runs_started >= max_runs`), so it always matches the same live row the reservation touched — both budget decisions (reserve and exhaust) are now snapshot-free. `next_run_at` is still deliberately untouched (backfill doesn't own the forward-cadence pointer). The transition helper drops its `new_runs_started`/`max_runs` params (all three call sites in both dispatch loops updated), the reservation match no longer captures the returned `runs_started` (`Ok(Some(_)) => {}`, value unused), and the now-dead pure `backfill_budget_reached` helper + its `backfill_budget_reached_truth_table` unit test were removed (the SQL `max_runs > 0 AND runs_started >= max_runs` predicate encodes the same rule; non-positive/NULL = unlimited). The UPDATE is extracted into a `transition_backfill_exhausted_stmt!` macro (mirroring the sibling `reserve_backfill_budget_slot_stmt!` / `clear_stale_max_runs_exhaustion_stmt!` / `rearm_backfill_next_run_stmt!`) so the live path and the new no-DB `transition_backfill_exhausted_generates_the_live_row_guarded_update` shape test share one source of truth. No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration; the existing integration tests (`backfill_over_window_*`, `backfill_max_runs_zero_*`, the money test) still assert exhaustion when `runs_started` reaches `max_runs`, compile-checked here (no Docker), CI runs them Docker-backed.
- **Phase 3.50** (implemented): Serve query handlers on terminal (closed) workflows for post-mortem state inspection — see issue #612. Before: `GET/POST /workflows/{id}/query/{name}` and `GET /workflows/{id}/queries` returned `409 WorkflowNotRunning` for any terminal execution, via a single unconditional `is_terminal_state(...)` guard in `autumn-harvest-plugin/src/api.rs::hydrate_ctx_for_query`. After: an operator can run a workflow's own registered query handlers against a `COMPLETED`/`FAILED`/`CANCELLED`/`TIMED_OUT`/`TERMINATED`/`CONTINUED_AS_NEW` run and read its **final reconstructed internal state** — the answer a query handler exists to give (e.g. "how many items had you processed when you failed?"), which the recorded output (usually just an error string) hides. **The capability is a read-only replay drive, not a new event surface: no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no shard-routing change, no replay-determinism impact** (queries never emit `WorkflowCommand`s and append nothing to `harvest_events`, so serving on terminal runs stays inside the append-only contract by construction). New reusable, single-sourced, **read-only** replay driver `executor::drive_query_replay(ctx, handler, input, timeout) -> QueryReplayOutcome` (`ReachedTerminal`/`Suspended`/`TimedOut`) — a bounded manual poll loop (its own `ArcWake` waker detects `yield_now`-style immediate re-wakes vs a genuine workflow-command suspension) that drives the handler purely in replay against recorded history, resolving recorded events via pre-sent oneshots; it never persists anything and ignores the workflow's `Ok`/`Err` return so a `FAILED` run still reconstructs final state. `hydrate_ctx_for_query`'s unconditional terminal guard is **removed**; for a terminal execution it now classifies the drive outcome — `ReachedTerminal` → serve (200), `TimedOut` → `HarvestError::QueryTimedOut` (**408**, closing a real pre-existing gap: the old plugin loop merely `break`d on the deadline and served a partial answer rather than erroring; `handle.rs::execute_query_in_process`'s sibling loop already returned `QueryTimedOut` and was the template), `Suspended` (recorded history insufficient to reach the workflow's final state — pruned by retention or released on reset) → the **new** `HarvestError::HistoryUnavailable { exec_id, reason }` (**410 Gone**, distinct from `NotFound`/404). **Running/suspended executions are byte-for-byte unchanged**: the drive still stops at the first genuine suspension (or the deadline) and the query reads current partial state, regardless of outcome, exactly as before. **Erased-history guard (issue #495 interaction):** a PII-erased terminal history replays *structurally* but over `{"_harvest_erased": true}` payload tombstones — which would compute a misleading answer — so before driving, a terminal query scans the loaded history via the new pure `erase::history_events_contain_tombstone(events)` and short-circuits to **410** with reason "payloads erased" rather than serving tombstoned state. Contract: **404** = "row gone" (a fully retention-**deleted** execution — `load_execution` still `NotFound`); **410** = "row present but history unqueryable" (pruned/released/erased); **408** = spinning replay bounded by `WorkerConfig::query_timeout`; **404** = unregistered query name on a terminal run (identical to the running contract — never a silent empty success, since `execute_query` still resolves against the reconstructed registry). New `map_error` arm maps `HistoryUnavailable` → `410 Gone` (body "history unavailable: {reason}"), placed before the catch-all so it isn't swallowed to 503. **Zero-writes (AC4) holds by construction** — the DB connection is dropped before the drive, and the drive is pure in-memory replay. `handle.rs::execute_query_in_process` (the in-process typed-client path) keeps its own terminal guard **unchanged** — the issue scopes to the HTTP/plugin path, and that sibling already both returns `QueryTimedOut` and converts a `FAILED` run's `Err` to `WorkflowFailed` (a deliberately different, out-of-scope contract); noted for parity, not touched. Docs: the "Query Handlers" usage section in CLAUDE.md rewritten with the 200/404/410/408 terminal matrix and the pruned/released/erased caveats. Tests, TDD red→green (red = compile error against the not-yet-existing driver/helper, per the #593 precedent): 7 **runnable** pure tests in `autumn-harvest/tests/integration/query_terminal_tests.rs` (wired into `tests/integration/mod.rs`; no DB, `--features testing` not required — they use `WorkflowContext::for_replay_with_state_and_history_policy` + `drive_query_replay` directly) covering `ReachedTerminal`+final-count, `FAILED`-serves-internal-state-not-error, `Suspended`-on-insufficient-history, deterministic `TimedOut` on a zero-length budget, unregistered-name→`QueryHandlerNotFound`, running-partial-history-still-serves (regression guard that a `Suspended` drive is still queryable and never becomes a 410), and erasure detection; **all 7 pass** in the sandbox. DB/HTTP integration tests in `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/query_integration.rs` (testcontainers, mirrors `fail_now_integration.rs`) cover AC1 (COMPLETED GET+POST 200 + queries-list), AC2 (FAILED/CANCELLED/TIMED_OUT → 200 internal state), AC3 (unregistered → 404), AC4 (event-count + execution-row unchanged → zero writes), AC5 (released → 410, erased → 410 distinct body, unknown → 404), AC6 (spinning workflow + 50ms `query_timeout` → 408) — **compile-checked only** in this sandbox (no Docker), added to both the plugin `--no-run` compile list and the Docker-backed `--test-threads=1` list in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (append-only), so CI runs them Docker-backed on Linux (per the #543/#544/#601 precedent). **Post-review hardening (three-angle review, PR #986):** (1) **BLOCKER — sealed-while-parked terminals must serve 200, not 410.** The initial cut classified *every* `Suspended` drive outcome on a terminal execution as `410`, but a run the engine seals while its function is parked mid-command replays to `Suspended`, not `Poll::Ready`: `CONTINUED_AS_NEW` (`continue_as_new` calls `park_until_dropped().await` = `std::future::pending()`, so it **always** suspends), `TIMED_OUT` (history ends with an incomplete command + `WorkflowExecutionTimedOut`), and a mid-await external/hard `CANCELLED`/`FAILED` (same shape). Those are legitimately queryable (200, reconstructed partial state at the terminal point) — the 410 (with a false "pruned by retention" reason) violated AC2 and the PR's own docs. Fix: the distinguishing signal is whether the recorded history **reached its terminal seal**. New `impl WorkflowEvent { pub const fn is_terminal_lifecycle(&self) }` was already present (authored for replay's unconsumed-event skip) and covers exactly the terminal-seal set (`WorkflowCompleted`/`WorkflowFailed`/`WorkflowCancelled` — the latter also seals `TERMINATED` since terminate reuses it — `WorkflowContinuedAsNew`/`WorkflowResetTerminated`/`WorkflowExecutionTimedOut`, plus the trailing bookkeeping `ChildWorkflowCascadeApplied`/`WorkflowRetryScheduled`); new pure `executor::history_reached_terminal_seal(events)` scans it `rev().any(..)` (O(1) on the common sealed case, robust to trailing bookkeeping) and new pure `executor::classify_terminal_query(outcome, sealed) -> TerminalQueryDecision::{Serve, TimedOut, HistoryUnavailable}` encodes the rule: `ReachedTerminal` → Serve; `TimedOut` → 408; `Suspended` → **Serve when the history reached a terminal seal** (the sealed-while-parked case) / `HistoryUnavailable` (410) only when it genuinely did not (truncated/released/empty). The erased check still takes precedence (410 "payloads erased") regardless of the seal. The running/suspended (non-terminal) branch is untouched. (2) **checked_add deadline (Gemini):** `drive_query_replay` now uses `Instant::now().checked_add(timeout)` — `None` (overflow) means "no deadline, never time out" — keeping the deadline-checked-**before**-poll ordering (the `Duration::ZERO` → `TimedOut` pure test depends on it). (3) **O(1) erasure detection (perf):** the erased signal is now the O(1) `erase::execution_input_is_erased(&execution.input)` (production `erase_workflow_payloads` always tombstones the row's own `input` column) instead of the removed `history_events_contain_tombstone` full-history tree-walk that ran on every terminal query; the erased test fixture now tombstones the row too, matching production. (4) **Running-path HTTP regression test** (`running_partial_history_serves_query_with_partial_state`) added to `query_integration.rs`. (5) Docs: the 404-vs-410 "pruned" ambiguity in `docs/autumn-workflow-architecture.md` fixed (404 = "the row itself no longer exists", "pruned by retention" reserved for 410), the sealed-while-parked 200 semantics added to both docs, and an honesty caveat that the 408 bound applies only to async-yielding replays. New/changed tests: pure `every_terminal_seal_variant_is_terminal_lifecycle`/`non_terminal_events_are_not_terminal_lifecycle` (event.rs), `detects_erased_execution_row_input`/`does_not_flag_a_clean_execution_row_input` (erase.rs), `continued_as_new_sealed_history_serves_partial_state_not_gone`/`cancelled_sealed_mid_activity_serves_partial_state`/`timed_out_sealed_mid_activity_serves_partial_state`/`truncated_history_with_no_seal_classifies_as_history_unavailable`/`erased_execution_row_is_detected` (query_terminal_tests.rs — the AC2 HTTP test now seeds realistic mid-flight-sealed histories with a trailing incomplete command + terminal event, plus a new `ac2_continued_as_new_answers_200_with_internal_state` HTTP case). **Post-merge follow-up hardening (Codex P2, PR #986 discussion):** the initial cut's `classify_terminal_query` classified *every* `ReachedTerminal` drive as `Serve`, so a post-code-drift query — where the workflow code changed since the run executed such that the driven handler reaches `Poll::Ready` (or a sealed run parks) after consuming only *part* of the recorded history — served the diverged/partial reconstructed state as an authoritative `200`. Fixed by threading a **drift guard**: `classify_terminal_query` gained a third `has_unconsumed_history: bool` argument (supplied by `ctx.history_has_unconsumed_events()`, computed in `hydrate_ctx_for_query` *after* the read-only drive), and **both** `Serve` outcomes (`ReachedTerminal`, and `Suspended` + terminal-seal) are now downgraded to `HistoryUnavailable` (→ `410`) when genuine recorded non-lifecycle history remains unconsumed. **AC2 non-regression holds by construction**: the check is `HistoryMatcher::has_non_lifecycle_unconsumed`, which *excludes* trailing terminal-lifecycle events (`WorkflowEvent::is_terminal_lifecycle`) — and `match_activity` advances the cursor *past* an in-flight `ActivityScheduled` on suspend — so a truthfully-replayed completed run and every sealed-while-parked run (`CONTINUED_AS_NEW`/`TIMED_OUT`/mid-await `CANCELLED`/`FAILED`) leave only the terminal seal unconsumed → `false` → still `200`. Tests, TDD red→green (red = `classify_terminal_query` arity compile error): 2 new pure tests in `query_terminal_tests.rs` — `code_drift_reaching_terminal_early_with_unconsumed_history_is_gone` (a 3-activity history driven by a 1-item handler reaches `ReachedTerminal` with 2 pairs unconsumed → `HistoryUnavailable`) and `completed_history_fully_consumed_still_serves` (a faithful full replay with a trailing `WorkflowCompleted` seal → still `Serve`) — plus the 4 existing `classify_terminal_query` call sites updated to pass the drift flag; the plugin's `query_integration.rs` `410` mapping is unchanged (compile-checked only in this sandbox — no Docker). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route change.**
- **Phase 3.50** (implemented): `ctx.sleep_until(id, deadline)` — absolute-time durable timer (issue #749). The blessed, replay-safe companion to the relative, whole-second `ctx.timer(id, secs)`: a workflow waits until an *absolute instant* (24h before an expiry, midnight UTC, a coupon lapse) with one call instead of the hand-rolled `ctx.timer(id, (deadline - ctx.system_now()).num_seconds() as u64)` pattern, which carries two foot-guns — reaching for `chrono::Utc::now()` breaks replay (guardrail HVG001), and a deadline already in the past underflows `as u64` into a multi-year sleep. **Design A (system_now + delegate to timer):** `sleep_until` captures the current wall clock **once** via the deterministic `WorkflowContext::system_now` (frozen into history as an existing `SideEffectRecorded { kind: Now }` event, issue #384 — so every replay recomputes the identical remaining duration from that frozen instant and resolves at the same instant on every worker regardless of the replaying worker's clock), then delegates to `self.timer(timer_id, remaining_secs)` — reusing the whole-second suspension, `match_timer_strict` divergence detection (a non-deterministic author-supplied `deadline` surfaces as ordinary timer non-determinism, not a panic), and the #526 virtual-clock advance uniformly. The remaining duration is computed by the pure, unit-tested `pub(crate) context::remaining_secs_until(deadline, now)`: a past-or-equal deadline clamps to `0` (fires on the next poll — AC3, never a wrapped multi-year sleep); any positive sub-second remainder rounds **up** to the next whole second (nanosecond-precise via `chrono::Duration::subsec_nanos`, matching `wait_for_signal_timeout` — harvest timers have whole-second granularity, so the wait never resolves *before* the deadline); a defensive `u64::MAX` fallback covers a delta whose whole seconds overflow `i64`→`u64` (unreachable for any chrono-valid `DateTime<Utc>` pair, since chrono's own range caps the delta far below that; were it hit, the worker's `chrono_duration_from_secs` would surface it as a `Config` error at persist, exactly like an overflowing `ctx.timer` duration). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no worker/event/schema change** — a `sleep_until` timer is byte-identical to a `ctx.timer` timer of the same computed duration; like `ctx.timer`, exactly one timer suspends per call and it cannot share a suspension batch with activity/child-workflow/signal commands. Tests, TDD red→green: pure `remaining_secs_until` truth table (incl. sub-millisecond micro/nanosecond round-up cases) + three context-level unit tests (live emits `RecordSideEffect(Now)` + `StartTimer`; past deadline → zero-duration timer; recorded history replays with no new commands) in `context.rs`; the falsifiable #749 bar `sleep_until_replays_deterministically` (**1000 distinct** fixtures — the frozen `system_now()` instant and the deadline offset both vary with the iteration, walking sub-second jitter through the round-up boundary — each replaying `ReplaySucceeded` with zero divergences) plus a past-deadline-clamp replay, a mutated-duration `TimerMismatch` test (`sleep_until_duration_mismatch_surfaces_as_timer_nondeterminism`), and a genuine structural-divergence test (`sleep_until_missing_side_effect_surfaces_as_nondeterminism` — dropping the frozen `SideEffectRecorded(Now)` event surfaces as `NonDeterminismKind::SideEffectDrift`, not a panic) in `tests/integration/replayer_tests.rs`; `WorkflowTestEnv` fixtures (future deadline resolves without real sleep, with the recorded `TimerStarted.duration_secs` reconstructed against the frozen `SideEffectRecorded(Now)` capture to prove it equals `remaining_secs_until(deadline, frozen_now)`; past deadline records a zero-duration timer — the concrete AC3 test) in `tests/integration/workflow_test_env_tests.rs`. Example `autumn-harvest/examples/sleep_until_renewal_reminder.rs` (a "send a renewal reminder 24h before expiry" workflow with embedded `WorkflowTestEnv` tests). All executed locally (no DB required — the entire slice is `context.rs` + `testing`-gated tests). **Post-review hardening (PR #985):** (1) `remaining_secs_until` switched from millisecond truncation to nanosecond-precise round-up (`chrono::Duration::subsec_nanos`) so any positive sub-second remainder rounds up, with sub-millisecond unit-test coverage; (2) the `WorkflowTestEnv` resolves-without-real-sleep test now reconstructs the expected timer duration from the frozen `system_now()` capture (a genuine `sleep_until` assertion, not the test-env clock-advance invariant); (3) the mutated-timer test renamed to `..._duration_mismatch_...` (it mutates duration, not order) and a genuine structural-divergence test added; (4) the 1000-pass money test builds 1000 *distinct* fixtures instead of cloning one; (5) rustdoc/CLAUDE.md wording clarified — the `u64::MAX` case is a defensive fallback, plus usage notes on deriving `deadline` deterministically, preferring `ctx.timer` for relative waits, the `WorkflowTestEnv` real-vs-virtual-clock caveat, and the reserved `__`-prefixed `timer_id` namespace. **Known limitation (Codex review of PR #985, documented not fixed — deliberately out of scope for this additive, no-worker-change slice):** the "never resolves before `deadline`" guarantee is scoped to sub-second *rounding* (no truncation-induced early fire), not to absolute wall-clock precision. `remaining` is computed against the captured *worker* clock, but the durable timer's absolute fire instant is anchored to the *Postgres* clock (`fires_at = db_now + remaining`, identical to `ctx.timer` — load-bearing, since timer due-ness (`fires_at <= NOW()`) and signal `received_at` are both compared against Postgres `NOW()` so the signal-or-deadline race #476 reasons about one clock regardless of worker skew), so sub-second *absolute* honoring assumes NTP-synced worker/DB clocks (skew normally well below the whole-second granularity). A deadline-anchored persist path (`fires_at = deadline`) would make it fully skew-proof but is a `persist_started_timer` worker-path change beyond this slice; noted as a possible follow-up. The rustdoc now scopes the guarantee and documents the DB-clock frame explicitly.
- **Phase 3.49** (implemented): Per-workflow-type history retention overrides — see issue #737. `RetentionConfig` (in `retention.rs`) gains `overrides: BTreeMap<String, u64>` (workflow_name → max-age seconds) alongside the existing global `max_age_secs` fallback, with fluent `with_workflow_override(name, Duration)` / `with_workflow_overrides(iter)` builders and accessors `effective_max_age(name)` (override → global → `None`), `loosest_cutoff_age()` (min of global + all overrides), `history_retention_active()`, and `workflow_overrides()`. Deliberate scope: overrides live on the operator-facing `RetentionConfig`, **not** on `WorkflowInfo` and **not** a macro attribute — a small, config-only change matching the issue's framing. **Per-candidate effective-age resolution (the seam):** `run_shard_tick` now takes `(now, loose_cutoff)` instead of a single global `cutoff`; the SQL candidate SELECT pre-filters on `loose_cutoff` (the *smallest* effective age → cutoff closest to now → a correct **superset** of every deletable row across all types: any row deletable under `age(T)` satisfies `completed_at < now - age(T) <= now - min_age`), then a per-candidate Rust check resolves `effective_max_age(workflow_name)` and either routine-skips (a type with neither an override nor a global age is **never** deleted; a type not yet old enough for its own age is skipped) or proceeds to archive/delete. The `resolved_cutoff` (`now - age`, per-type), **not** the loose cutoff, is passed to `should_skip_candidate` so its continue-as-new chain-link check (`completed_at >= $cutoff`) is correct. A single `routine_skip_candidate` helper dedupes the lease-release + cursor-advance + active-id bookkeeping across all three skip paths and is the clearly-named per-candidate decision point for #747 (legal hold: a "frozen?" check) and #752 (tiered summary: a "summarize-instead-of-delete" branch) to hook into. **Validation (AC5/AC6):** `RetentionConfig::validate()` bounds-checks each override against the same `MIN_MAX_AGE..=MAX_MAX_AGE` range as the global `max_age` (out-of-range fails the build, never silently clamps); new builder-time `validate_retention_overrides` (mirrors `validate_completion_triggers`, wired into `try_build` right after `retention.validate()`) rejects any override naming a workflow type that is neither a registered `#[workflow]` nor an auto-registered DAG workflow, via `HarvestBuilderError::InvalidRetention` — catching typos rather than silently ignoring them. `enabled()` now also returns `true` for an overrides-only config (no global `max_age`, no audit/schedule window) so the janitor still spawns. **Metric (AC8):** new `MetricsRecorder::record_retention_deleted(workflow, count)` default-no-op trait method, bridged in `metrics_rs_adapter` to emit `harvest.retention.deleted` labeled by the low-cardinality `workflow` registry key — **the counter's label changed from `shard` to `workflow`**; the old aggregate-`deleted_count`-by-`shard` emission was removed from the adapter's `record_retention_tick` (now a documented no-op for the counter) so there is **no double-count** (`sum(harvest.retention.deleted)` equals the aggregate **workflow-history** deletion count for the tick, *excluding* orphaned `harvest_completion_deliveries` reclaims from issue #921, which have no owning execution / workflow name to attribute — so it may read below the tick's total `deleted_count`). Emitted for **real deletes only** (never dry-run), so a long-retained type reads `0` on the counter until its own age. Dashboard (`docs/dashboards/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json`), alert-pack expr (`docs/alerts/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json` — retention-lag now `sum(increase(...[6h])) == 0`), telemetry.md/ADR-0001 §7 label tables, and the `dashboard_pack_docs.rs` `SERIES_LABELS` ground truth all updated to the `workflow` label. **Reporting (AC7):** `deleted_by_workflow: BTreeMap<String, u64>` added to `ShardTickOutcome` and surfaced on `RetentionTickResult` (→ `RetentionStatus` / `GET /admin/retention`); accumulated in **both** dry-run (would-delete counts) and real-delete paths, so `dry_run` reports per-type counts using resolved per-type ages while the #345 archival hook still fires for every deleted row regardless of which policy selected it. **Backward compat (AC9):** with `overrides` empty (default), `effective_max_age(any) == max_age()`, `loosest_cutoff_age() == max_age()`, and the SQL/scan path is byte-identical to a single-`max_age` deployment. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no replay impact — read-side / janitor only.** Tests, TDD red→green→refactor: config unit tests (`retention.rs`: resolution, loosest-cutoff, `history_retention_active`/`enabled` truth tables, override bounds, empty-overrides backward compat); builder unit tests (`validate_retention_overrides` unknown/registered/DAG/empty, plus a `try_build` rejection test); telemetry no-op + `metrics_rs_adapter` bridge tests for `record_retention_deleted`; DB behavioral tests in a new `tests/integration/retention_overrides_tests.rs` driving `RetentionRuntime` end-to-end (longer-override survives the global age / shorter-override deleted at its own earlier age / dry-run per-type would-delete reporting with zero deletes and no metric / no-overrides == global-only / overrides-only never touches an unlisted type — each asserting surviving rows + `deleted_by_workflow` + a capturing recorder's `record_retention_deleted` samples). The DB suite uses `HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL` when set (else testcontainers) and was **executed green against a real local Postgres 16** in the implementing sandbox (all four tests pass — genuine delete/metric/dry-run verification, not compile-check); CI gains a dedicated Docker-backed `retention_overrides_tests` step on Linux. Extensibility seam for #747 (legal hold) / #752 (tiered summary) kept as the single `effective_max_age` + delete/skip branch in `run_shard_tick`.
- **Phase 3.50** (implemented): Per-execution timeline read API — reconstruct a single run's wall-clock breakdown from recorded history (issue #739). New read-only management route `GET /api/harvest/workflows/{id}/timeline` (handler `get_workflow_timeline` in plugin `api.rs`) answers "where did this run's time go?" from the events already in `harvest_events` — no external OTel backend, no manual timestamp-diffing of `/history/export`, and (unlike the pre-existing `DagProfiler`, a pre-run *simulation* over a DAG definition) a real executed run. Pure, `db`-free core module `autumn-harvest/src/timeline.rs`: `derive_timeline(rows: &[TimelineEventRow], started_at, now, completed_at, exec_id, workflow_id, workflow_name, state) -> Timeline` maps an ordered `(timestamp, WorkflowEvent)` slice → the timeline document; types `Timeline`/`TimelineStep`/`TimelineRollup`/`SlowestStep`/`StepKind`/`StepOutcome`/`TimelineEventRow` are re-exported from `lib.rs`. Because `WorkflowEvent` carries no in-enum timestamp, the derivation consumes the per-row `harvest_events.timestamp` surfaced by the new read-only loader `store::load_timestamped_history` (undecoded, ordered by `id`). **Bounded `step_kind`**: `activity` | `local_activity` | `timer` | `child_workflow` | `signal_wait` | `side_effect`; external activities (`ActivityAwaitingExternal`/`ActivityCompletedExternally`/`ActivityFailedExternally`) render as `activity` steps with the split always null. **Bounded `outcome`**: `completed` | `failed` | `timed_out` | `cancelled` | `fired` | `pending`. **Wait/exec split (`wait_ms`/`exec_ms`) is present ONLY for a regular activity with a recorded `ActivityStarted` claim timestamp** and is `null` everywhere else (child_workflow, local_activity, external activity, timer, signal_wait, side_effect) — never fabricated; `total_ms` is always present. For a retried activity, `wait_ms` spans prior attempts' execution + backoff (an upper bound on queue wait) and `attempt` is the max attempt on Failed/Exhausted (a lower bound) — both documented on the fields. A local activity mid-retry (a bare `LocalActivityFailed` with no `LocalActivityExhausted`) is `pending`, not `failed`. A reused `timer_id` (the poll-loop idiom) is paired by occurrence via a per-id FIFO so it yields N distinct timer steps rather than collapsing. **Rollup** (`TimelineRollup`): `total_wall_clock_ms` (started_at→terminal, or→`now` if running), `busy_ms`/`wait_ms`, `slowest_step`, `step_count_by_kind` — `busy + wait` need not equal total (unattributed orchestration gaps are expected and documented). **In-flight**: open steps report `pending`, `ended_at` null, `total_ms` measured to `now`. O(1) shard routing via `exec_id.shard()` (`db_conn_for_execution`, no fan-out); an unknown exec id → `404` (a classic DAG run, not on the execution path, → `404` with a clear message; a unified DAG run → `200`). The endpoint surfaces no payloads, so there is **no #608 read-path decode, no audit row, and no write** of any kind. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no write-path change.** Registered in the axum router, `management_api_routes()`/`management_api_response_fields()`, `docs/api-contract.json`, and `autumn_harvest::audit` (`CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` ReadOnly / `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES` `None` / `EXCLUDED_ROUTES`). CLI: `harvest workflow timeline <id>`. Runbook: "Where did the time go?" section in `docs/runbooks/triage-pending-tasks-idle-workers.md`. **Composition contract for the stacked follow-up #701** (continue-as-new run-chain timeline): a `TimelineStep` carries no `exec_id`, so #701 must *wrap* per-execution `Timeline` envelopes (a list with an exec boundary), not *flatten* steps into one `Vec` — flattening would lose per-execution attribution. Out of scope (per issue): a graph-aware DAG critical path, cross-execution aggregation, and a rendered Gantt UI. Tests, TDD red→green: 25 pure no-DB unit tests in `timeline.rs` (per-kind derivation, wait/exec split presence/absence, retry upper/lower bounds, local-activity-mid-retry pending, reused-timer-id FIFO pairing, in-flight-measured-to-now, rollup slowest/busy/wait); plugin `timeline_integration.rs` (unknown→404, malformed→400, completed-run split+slowest+ordering, running→pending, classic-DAG→404, unified-DAG→200) compile-checked in this sandbox (no Docker), added to the CI `--no-run` compile line + a Docker-backed Linux run step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, per the #543/#544/#601 precedent. `timeline_route_is_classified` pin in `contract_regression.rs`; CLI mapping/coverage tests in `request_mapping.rs`/`contract_coverage.rs`.
- **Phase 3.50** (implemented): Serve query handlers on terminal (closed) workflows for post-mortem state inspection — see issue #612. Before: `GET/POST /workflows/{id}/query/{name}` and `GET /workflows/{id}/queries` returned `409 WorkflowNotRunning` for any terminal execution, via a single unconditional `is_terminal_state(...)` guard in `autumn-harvest-plugin/src/api.rs::hydrate_ctx_for_query`. After: an operator can run a workflow's own registered query handlers against a `COMPLETED`/`FAILED`/`CANCELLED`/`TIMED_OUT`/`TERMINATED`/`CONTINUED_AS_NEW` run and read its **final reconstructed internal state** — the answer a query handler exists to give (e.g. "how many items had you processed when you failed?"), which the recorded output (usually just an error string) hides. **The capability is a read-only replay drive, not a new event surface: no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no shard-routing change, no replay-determinism impact** (queries never emit `WorkflowCommand`s and append nothing to `harvest_events`, so serving on terminal runs stays inside the append-only contract by construction). New reusable, single-sourced, **read-only** replay driver `executor::drive_query_replay(ctx, handler, input, timeout) -> QueryReplayOutcome` (`ReachedTerminal`/`Suspended`/`TimedOut`) — a bounded manual poll loop (its own `ArcWake` waker detects `yield_now`-style immediate re-wakes vs a genuine workflow-command suspension) that drives the handler purely in replay against recorded history, resolving recorded events via pre-sent oneshots; it never persists anything and ignores the workflow's `Ok`/`Err` return so a `FAILED` run still reconstructs final state. `hydrate_ctx_for_query`'s unconditional terminal guard is **removed**; for a terminal execution it now classifies the drive outcome — `ReachedTerminal` → serve (200), `TimedOut` → `HarvestError::QueryTimedOut` (**408**, closing a real pre-existing gap: the old plugin loop merely `break`d on the deadline and served a partial answer rather than erroring; `handle.rs::execute_query_in_process`'s sibling loop already returned `QueryTimedOut` and was the template), `Suspended` (recorded history insufficient to reach the workflow's final state — pruned by retention or released on reset) → the **new** `HarvestError::HistoryUnavailable { exec_id, reason }` (**410 Gone**, distinct from `NotFound`/404). **Running/suspended executions are byte-for-byte unchanged**: the drive still stops at the first genuine suspension (or the deadline) and the query reads current partial state, regardless of outcome, exactly as before. **Erased-history guard (issue #495 interaction):** a PII-erased terminal history replays *structurally* but over `{"_harvest_erased": true}` payload tombstones — which would compute a misleading answer — so before driving, a terminal query scans the loaded history via the new pure `erase::history_events_contain_tombstone(events)` and short-circuits to **410** with reason "payloads erased" rather than serving tombstoned state. Contract: **404** = "row gone" (a fully retention-**deleted** execution — `load_execution` still `NotFound`); **410** = "row present but history unqueryable" (pruned/released/erased); **408** = spinning replay bounded by `WorkerConfig::query_timeout`; **404** = unregistered query name on a terminal run (identical to the running contract — never a silent empty success, since `execute_query` still resolves against the reconstructed registry). New `map_error` arm maps `HistoryUnavailable` → `410 Gone` (body "history unavailable: {reason}"), placed before the catch-all so it isn't swallowed to 503. **Zero-writes (AC4) holds by construction** — the DB connection is dropped before the drive, and the drive is pure in-memory replay. `handle.rs::execute_query_in_process` (the in-process typed-client path) keeps its own terminal guard **unchanged** — the issue scopes to the HTTP/plugin path, and that sibling already both returns `QueryTimedOut` and converts a `FAILED` run's `Err` to `WorkflowFailed` (a deliberately different, out-of-scope contract); noted for parity, not touched. Docs: the "Query Handlers" usage section in CLAUDE.md rewritten with the 200/404/410/408 terminal matrix and the pruned/released/erased caveats. Tests, TDD red→green (red = compile error against the not-yet-existing driver/helper, per the #593 precedent): 7 **runnable** pure tests in `autumn-harvest/tests/integration/query_terminal_tests.rs` (wired into `tests/integration/mod.rs`; no DB, `--features testing` not required — they use `WorkflowContext::for_replay_with_state_and_history_policy` + `drive_query_replay` directly) covering `ReachedTerminal`+final-count, `FAILED`-serves-internal-state-not-error, `Suspended`-on-insufficient-history, deterministic `TimedOut` on a zero-length budget, unregistered-name→`QueryHandlerNotFound`, running-partial-history-still-serves (regression guard that a `Suspended` drive is still queryable and never becomes a 410), and erasure detection; **all 7 pass** in the sandbox. DB/HTTP integration tests in `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/query_integration.rs` (testcontainers, mirrors `fail_now_integration.rs`) cover AC1 (COMPLETED GET+POST 200 + queries-list), AC2 (FAILED/CANCELLED/TIMED_OUT → 200 internal state), AC3 (unregistered → 404), AC4 (event-count + execution-row unchanged → zero writes), AC5 (released → 410, erased → 410 distinct body, unknown → 404), AC6 (spinning workflow + 50ms `query_timeout` → 408) — **compile-checked only** in this sandbox (no Docker), added to both the plugin `--no-run` compile list and the Docker-backed `--test-threads=1` list in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (append-only), so CI runs them Docker-backed on Linux (per the #543/#544/#601 precedent). **Post-review hardening (three-angle review, PR #986):** (1) **BLOCKER — sealed-while-parked terminals must serve 200, not 410.** The initial cut classified *every* `Suspended` drive outcome on a terminal execution as `410`, but a run the engine seals while its function is parked mid-command replays to `Suspended`, not `Poll::Ready`: `CONTINUED_AS_NEW` (`continue_as_new` calls `park_until_dropped().await` = `std::future::pending()`, so it **always** suspends), `TIMED_OUT` (history ends with an incomplete command + `WorkflowExecutionTimedOut`), and a mid-await external/hard `CANCELLED`/`FAILED` (same shape). Those are legitimately queryable (200, reconstructed partial state at the terminal point) — the 410 (with a false "pruned by retention" reason) violated AC2 and the PR's own docs. Fix: the distinguishing signal is whether the recorded history **reached its terminal seal**. New `impl WorkflowEvent { pub const fn is_terminal_lifecycle(&self) }` was already present (authored for replay's unconsumed-event skip) and covers exactly the terminal-seal set (`WorkflowCompleted`/`WorkflowFailed`/`WorkflowCancelled` — the latter also seals `TERMINATED` since terminate reuses it — `WorkflowContinuedAsNew`/`WorkflowResetTerminated`/`WorkflowExecutionTimedOut`, plus the trailing bookkeeping `ChildWorkflowCascadeApplied`/`WorkflowRetryScheduled`); new pure `executor::history_reached_terminal_seal(events)` scans it `rev().any(..)` (O(1) on the common sealed case, robust to trailing bookkeeping) and new pure `executor::classify_terminal_query(outcome, sealed) -> TerminalQueryDecision::{Serve, TimedOut, HistoryUnavailable}` encodes the rule: `ReachedTerminal` → Serve; `TimedOut` → 408; `Suspended` → **Serve when the history reached a terminal seal** (the sealed-while-parked case) / `HistoryUnavailable` (410) only when it genuinely did not (truncated/released/empty). The erased check still takes precedence (410 "payloads erased") regardless of the seal. The running/suspended (non-terminal) branch is untouched. (2) **checked_add deadline (Gemini):** `drive_query_replay` now uses `Instant::now().checked_add(timeout)` — `None` (overflow) means "no deadline, never time out" — keeping the deadline-checked-**before**-poll ordering (the `Duration::ZERO` → `TimedOut` pure test depends on it). (3) **O(1) erasure detection (perf):** the erased signal is now the O(1) `erase::execution_input_is_erased(&execution.input)` (production `erase_workflow_payloads` always tombstones the row's own `input` column) instead of the removed `history_events_contain_tombstone` full-history tree-walk that ran on every terminal query; the erased test fixture now tombstones the row too, matching production. (4) **Running-path HTTP regression test** (`running_partial_history_serves_query_with_partial_state`) added to `query_integration.rs`. (5) Docs: the 404-vs-410 "pruned" ambiguity in `docs/autumn-workflow-architecture.md` fixed (404 = "the row itself no longer exists", "pruned by retention" reserved for 410), the sealed-while-parked 200 semantics added to both docs, and an honesty caveat that the 408 bound applies only to async-yielding replays. New/changed tests: pure `every_terminal_seal_variant_is_terminal_lifecycle`/`non_terminal_events_are_not_terminal_lifecycle` (event.rs), `detects_erased_execution_row_input`/`does_not_flag_a_clean_execution_row_input` (erase.rs), `continued_as_new_sealed_history_serves_partial_state_not_gone`/`cancelled_sealed_mid_activity_serves_partial_state`/`timed_out_sealed_mid_activity_serves_partial_state`/`truncated_history_with_no_seal_classifies_as_history_unavailable`/`erased_execution_row_is_detected` (query_terminal_tests.rs — the AC2 HTTP test now seeds realistic mid-flight-sealed histories with a trailing incomplete command + terminal event, plus a new `ac2_continued_as_new_answers_200_with_internal_state` HTTP case).
- **Phase 3.48** (implemented): Surface last-failure detail on pending activities in the stack API — see issue #773. `GET /workflows/{id}/stack`'s `PendingActivity` and `PendingLocalActivity` gain an optional `last_failure` object (`LastFailure { error_type, error, attempt, non_retryable, failed_at?, details? }`) so an operator triaging a backing-off/flapping activity reads the root-cause error in one request instead of a second `/history` pull. **Sourced by path, not uniformly from events**: a retryable (backing-off) regular activity does NOT append an `ActivityFailed` event (those fire only on a *terminal* failure → `queue::fail_task` → FAILED, which is excluded from the pending list); its last error lives in the `harvest_task_queue.error` column (written by `queue::requeue_for_retry`), so `PendingActivity.last_failure` is built inline from the already-loaded task row (`error_type` defaults `"Error"`, `non_retryable=false`, `failed_at`/`details` omitted — the task row carries no typed metadata and AC5 forbids a migration). Local activities ARE event-sourced per attempt (`LocalActivityFailed`), so `PendingLocalActivity.last_failure` is folded from the latest such event via `latest_failures_by_activity` (keyed on `activity_id`, max event-id wins) with a real `failed_at` from the event timestamp. **Correlation-key gotcha**: the join keys on `harvest_task_queue.activity_id` (== `ActivityFailed.activity_id`), NOT the response's `activity_exec_id` (= task PK `t.id`). `failed_at` is `Option` + `skip_serializing_if`, and `details`/`last_failure` are `skip_serializing_if`, so a never-failed pending activity is byte-identical to pre-#773 (AC3). #608 read-path decode composes: when the `decoder` is admin-active, `error`/`details` are lossy-decoded inline per surfaced row and folded into the `payload.decode_read` audit outcome; the failure-events query is `LocalActivityFailed`-only and decode is restricted to surfaced ids (no over-scope). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no new route** — a read-only presentation change derived from existing `harvest_events`/task rows at request time. AC7: nested `/stack` fields aren't enumerated in the top-level `management_api_response_fields()`/`docs/api-contract.json` `fields` list (precedent: `next_retry_at`/`input`), so `last_failure` is documented in the stack route's `success_response.notes` (the build-routing `notes` precedent) — the code-registry↔contract cross-check stays green. Runbook `docs/runbooks/triage-pending-tasks-idle-workers.md` "why is this activity retrying?" step updated. Tests: api.rs serde omission/presence unit tests + `latest_failures_by_activity_*` fold unit tests (LocalActivityFailed-only, latest-wins, out-of-order); integration tests in `read_path_decode_integration.rs` (backing-off regular activity seeded via the task-row `error` column → `last_failure` present with no `failed_at`; local activity seeded via `LocalActivityFailed` → `last_failure` present with `failed_at`; never-failed → omitted) — DB/testcontainers tests compile-checked in this sandbox (no Docker), executed by CI, per the #543/#544/#601 precedent.
- **Phase 3.49** (implemented): DAG run graph view read API — see issue #690. An operator triaging a failed multi-node unified-DAG run previously had to pull raw `harvest_events` and rebuild the node graph by hand (and then guess a node name for the #366 retry endpoint). New read-only, admin-guarded management route `GET /api/harvest/dags/{dag_name}/runs/{run_exec_id}` (handler `get_dag_run_graph` in plugin `api.rs`) reconstructs a run's node topology annotated with per-node status/timing/attempts/error purely from the registered `DagDefinition` plus the run's recorded history. Response (`DagRunGraphResponse`, snake_case): run summary (`run_exec_id`, `dag_name`, `state`, `started_at`, `finished_at`) + `nodes[]`, each a `DagRunNode` with `node_name` (== activity name), bounded `status` enum (`DagNodeStatus`: `succeeded`/`failed`/`timed_out`/`cancelled`/`running`/`pending`/`skipped`), `depends_on` (upstream activity names — AC3 static topology edges, so a UI renders the graph without a second registry lookup), `started_at`/`finished_at` (per-node latest-attempt timing), `attempts` (execution-attempt count), and for a failed node the low-cardinality `error_type` + a truncated first-line `error`. **Pure builder** `dag_graph::build_run_graph(def, timestamped_events, exec_state)` in the new plugin module `autumn-harvest-plugin/src/dag_graph.rs`; **base node classification delegates to `dag_retry::node_outcome` (#366)** so statuses are consistent with the retry resolver (AC5, pinned by `status_projects_node_outcome_for_every_node`). Running-vs-cancelled split by execution terminality (`is_live_state` = `!erase::is_terminal_state`, so **PAUSED counts as live/`running`**, not cancelled); skipped-vs-pending split by the `dag_skip:{task_index}` marker (#482 data-dependent branches → `skipped`; a `SkipByTriggerRule` skip records no marker and reports `pending` — documented v1 limitation). **One core-crate touch**: new additive read helper `store::load_history_with_timestamps` (zips each `harvest_events.timestamp` with the deserialized event, since `WorkflowEvent` variants carry no timestamp and `load_history` discards the column; payloads deserialized directly like `load_history_undecoded`, **never for replay**). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no writes to `harvest_dag_runs`.** Error handling: classic (non-unified) DAG → `400` JSON (AC6, `DagDefinition` topology absent); unknown `dag_name` or an exec whose `workflow_name` ≠ `dag_name` → `404`; malformed `run_exec_id` → `400` JSON. Cross-shard correct (AC8) via `db_conn_for_execution` (`ExecutionId::shard()` routing, no fan-out). v1 limitation: a DAG that reuses an activity name yields ambiguous duplicated nodes (the same assumption #366 enforces by rejecting duplicate names). Route registered in the four parallel plugin registries (`harvest_api_router` with a `require_admin` route-layer per AC1, `management_api_routes()`, `management_api_response_fields()`), `docs/api-contract.json`, and `autumn_harvest::audit` (`CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` ReadOnly / `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES` None / `EXCLUDED_ROUTES`) with dedicated pinned classification tests in `audit.rs` (`dag_run_graph_route_is_classified_read_only`) and plugin `contract_regression.rs` (`dag_run_graph_route_is_classified` — closing the gap where audit's own exhaustiveness cross-check stays green if a route is dropped from both lists). Tests, TDD red→green: 13 pure unit tests in `dag_graph.rs` (AC5 consistency-vs-`node_outcome`, running/cancelled/skipped/pending, PAUSED→running, multi-attempt, concurrent fanout, duplicate-name, error first-line truncation); 11 DB/HTTP integration tests in `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/dag_run_graph_integration.rs` executed against real Postgres. Out of scope (per issue): the rendered Vantage UI page, classic DAGs (400), live streaming, per-node output payloads. **Post-review hardening (PR #989, two Codex P2 findings, both confirmed against engine source):** (CLAIM A) `attempts`/`started_at` are now derived from `ActivityStarted`, not `ActivityScheduled`. An activity-level retry (a `RetryPolicy` firing) **reuses the same task row and `activity_id`** — `queue::requeue_for_retry` re-pends the row and appends no event, and a *retryable* failure appends **no** `ActivityFailed` (only the retry-exhausting terminal failure does); the engine appends a fresh `ActivityStarted` on every worker claim (`append_activity_started_if_pending`). So a node the engine attempted N times has exactly **one** `ActivityScheduled` and **N** `ActivityStarted`. The pre-fix `count_attempts` (counting `ActivityScheduled`) reported `attempts: 1` forever and anchored `started_at` to the original schedule. Fixed via `started_attempts(events, activity_id)` — counts `ActivityStarted` for the node's authoritative (latest-scheduled) `activity_id`, floored to 1 for a scheduled-but-not-yet-claimed node; `started_at` is the latest `ActivityStarted` timestamp (falling back to the schedule timestamp when not yet claimed). The unrealistic hand-crafted retry fixtures (two `ActivityScheduled`, no `ActivityStarted`) were rewritten to realistic engine output. (CLAIM B) `has_skip_marker` now validates the `dag_skip:{idx}` marker's recorded `details.task` (and `details.upstreams` when present) against the current node at that index before reporting `skipped` — mirroring the Vantage UI's condition-skip validation (`ui.rs`) — so a DAG reordered/renamed after a run recorded its markers no longer mislabels the wrong current node as `skipped` (it falls through to `pending`). Tests, TDD red→green: unit tests in `dag_graph.rs` (realistic-retry `attempts`/timing, retry-exhaust, authoritative-latest-id scoping, scheduled-but-unclaimed floor-to-1, skip-marker task/upstreams mismatch ignored) and integration tests in `dag_run_graph_integration.rs` (rewritten realistic-retry case, stale-task-fingerprint marker ignored). (CLAIM C, documentation-only) A mapped (fan-out) task — one `DagTask` the handler dispatches per input-array element, all sharing the activity name with distinct `activity_id`s and no `fan_out:` marker — **collapses to its latest-scheduled instance's outcome** because both `dag_graph::latest_scheduled` and `dag_retry::node_outcome` select the latest-scheduled `ActivityScheduled` for the name; on a `FAILED` run an earlier failed element can therefore be reported `succeeded`/`cancelled`. This is a documented v1 limitation **intentionally shared with #366** (aggregating here would break AC5 consistency with the retry endpoint — a map-aware aggregate is deferred to a #366 change that updates `node_outcome` and this view together), pinned by `mapped_task_collapses_to_latest_scheduled_instance` and matching the duplicate-name limitation's stance. A further sub-case of the same mapped-task v1 limitation (issue #690 review, Codex): a mapped task over an **empty** upstream array dispatches zero instances — the unified DAG handler returns `TaskStatus::Succeeded` without any `execute_activity_raw_with_opts` call (`autumn-harvest-macros/src/dag.rs` `__n_instances == 0` guard), so the node appends **no** events; with zero events `node_outcome` returns `NotAttempted` and this view reports the node `pending` (not `succeeded`) on a completed run, since a zero-event no-marker node is indistinguishable from a not-yet-reached node (and from a `SkipByTriggerRule` skip, which also records no marker). This is AC5-consistent with `node_outcome` (same `NotAttempted` for the same history); a precise `succeeded` classification is deferred to the same coordinated #366 change, pinned by `empty_mapped_fan_out_reports_pending_on_completed_run`. **Post-review hardening, round 2 (PR #989, Codex P2 CLAIM D — codec/offload-deployment skip-detection regression):** CLAIM B's `details.task`/`details.upstreams` validation reads a payload field — `details` is in `PAYLOAD_FIELD_KEYS`, so `transform_event_data` codec-encodes it on write (payload_store.rs / payload_codec.rs). On a deployment with a non-identity `PayloadCodec` (or, in principle, large-payload offload) the stored `dag_skip:{idx}` marker's `details` is an opaque envelope (`_harvest_codec_envelope` / `_harvest_offload_envelope`), and the graph read path (`store::load_history_with_timestamps`) deliberately does **not** codec-decode — so `details.task` was unreadable and `has_skip_marker` returned `false`, wrongly reporting a condition-skipped node as `pending` instead of `skipped`. (The default identity codec produces no envelope, so this was invisible to the existing tests.) The Vantage UI's own `dag_skip` detection (`ui.rs`) reads `details` raw too and had the identical latent bug. **Fix (graceful index-only fallback, no codec plumbing, no 500 risk):** when the marker's `details` yields a readable `task` string, validate the fingerprint (CLAIM B reorder-safety preserved for the identity/readable case — the default and vast majority of deployments); when it doesn't (opaque codec/offload envelope or erasure tombstone), fall back to matching by the always-in-the-clear marker **name/index** alone and report `skipped`. Reorder-safety is not available in that opaque case (accepted — this equals the pre-CLAIM-B behavior, and skip detection itself stays correct in every deployment). Applied identically to `dag_graph::has_skip_marker` and the UI's `dag_skip` filter so the two surfaces stay consistent; `store::load_history_with_timestamps` correctly stays raw (non-decoding), and its doc comment now records that the classifier tolerates opaque `details`. Tests, TDD red→green: `skip_marker_with_opaque_codec_envelope_details_is_still_skipped` (`dag_graph.rs` unit) and `dag_run_graph_skip_marker_with_opaque_codec_details_is_still_skipped` (`dag_run_graph_integration.rs`, seeding an envelope-shaped `details` — stored verbatim by the identity codec, reproducing a codec deployment's on-disk state — and asserting the node is reported `skipped`); all existing CLAIM B reorder-safety tests still pass.
- **Phase 3.49** (implemented): Typed workflow failures — carry a structured, replay-safe failure cause from a workflow (and its children) to callers and to workflow code — see issue #767. Completes the typed-failure story the per-activity circuit breaker (#369) and operator force-fail (#765) started for activities, now for whole workflows. New public `WorkflowFailure { error_type, message, details: Option<serde_json::Value>, non_retryable: bool }` (`failure.rs`) with a fluent builder — `WorkflowFailure::new(error_type, message)` / `.with_details(value)` / `.non_retryable()` (the last a `const fn`). **Opt-in and non-breaking**: a `#[workflow]` whose signature returns `Result<_, WorkflowFailure>` is detected at macro-expansion time (`autumn-harvest-macros/src/workflow.rs::workflow_returns_workflow_failure`, mirroring the activity `IntoActivityErrorString` path) and its `Err` is routed through an `encode_err` shim into the typed `harvest_workflow_failure_v1` String-channel envelope; a workflow returning `Result<_, String>` (or any other `E: ToString`) is byte-for-byte unchanged, encoding to a bare message the decoder maps back to `error_type = None`. The envelope's explicit `harvest_workflow_failure_v1` discriminator prevents collision with a caller-authored message that happens to be JSON; `decode_workflow_failure(payload) -> DecodedWorkflowFailure` is the single tolerant decoder (a non-envelope string → all-`None` typed fields, the human message preserved). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration**: the typed cause rides three **additive** `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` fields — `error_type: Option<String>`, `details: Option<serde_json::Value>`, `non_retryable: Option<bool>` — on the *existing* `WorkflowFailed` and `ChildWorkflowFailed` event variants, and the same three on `HarvestError::WorkflowFailed`; pre-#767 stored JSON deserializes to all-`None`, preserving the append-only + adjacently-tagged-JSON invariants (`ChildWorkflowFailed.error_type` keeps its `#[serde(default = "default_error_type")]` `"Error"` legacy fallback for backward-compatible decode, while `WorkflowFailed.error_type` is a plain `Option` so a genuinely untyped failure reads as `None`). **Decode threading**: the worker (`worker.rs`) decodes the envelope when finalizing a workflow failure and when a child terminal is recorded, freezing the typed fields into the event once on the live frontier and replaying them verbatim on every subsequent cycle (replay-deterministic — captured, never re-derived); the `execution.error` TEXT column stores the *human message*, never the wire envelope. Accessors on `HarvestError`: `workflow_error_type() -> Option<&str>`, `workflow_details() -> Option<&serde_json::Value>` (`const fn`), `is_workflow_non_retryable() -> bool`; construction via `HarvestError::workflow_failed(name, payload)` (decoding) / `workflow_failed_untyped(name, reason)`. **A failed child now surfaces to its parent as a typed `HarvestError::WorkflowFailed`** (was `ActivityFailed`; the `child-workflow:{name}` name prefix is kept for log disambiguation) so a parent branches on `err.workflow_error_type()` with zero substring matching on the message — the headline success metric. **Behavior change (downstream migration)**: parent code that previously matched a failed child as `HarvestError::ActivityFailed` — or called `.activity_error_type()`/`.activity_details()` on a child result — must switch to the `WorkflowFailed` variant and the `workflow_error_type()`/`workflow_details()`/`is_workflow_non_retryable()` accessors (documented in `docs/typed-workflow-failures.md`). `replay::HistoryMatch::Failed` gained a `non_retryable: bool` field and `HistoryMatcher::match_child_workflow` now surfaces the typed failure. Handle surface (AC5): `WorkflowHandle::terminal_typed_failure` loads the terminal `WorkflowFailed` event and reconstructs the typed `HarvestError`; `TypedWorkflowHandle::result()`/`result_snapshot()` expose it, and `TypedWorkflowResult` gained `error_type`/`error_details`/`non_retryable` fields. `WorkflowFailure` + `IntoWorkflowErrorString` re-exported from `prelude.rs`. Tests, TDD red→green: unit tests in `failure.rs`/`event.rs`/`error.rs` (builder, envelope round-trip, pre-#767 backward-compat decode, accessors), macro-expansion tests in `tests/integration/macros_workflow.rs`, the non-DB **headline success-metric** test `routing_is_stable_across_reworded_messages_for_the_same_error_type` + the legacy-fallback test in `tests/integration/typed_workflow_failure_tests.rs` (F1, runs in the no-DB `--test integration` CI step across ≥3 error categories, asserting a parent's routing decision is identical for two histories differing only in the child's *message* but sharing `error_type`, with zero substring matching), the DB-gated F2a handle-surface test `failed_handle_surfaces_typed_fields_across_categories` (testcontainers, Docker-backed CI step), a replay-determinism proof, docs, and the worked example `autumn-harvest/examples/typed_workflow_failure.rs`. CI: non-DB integration step (line 57) covers F1; example test step (issue #767); Docker-backed `typed_workflow_failure_tests` step. **Verified against real Postgres in this sandbox** (the F2a DB handle-surface suite `failed_handle_surfaces_typed_fields_across_categories` executed green via testcontainers/Docker — sealing typed `WorkflowFailed` events across ≥3 error categories and reading them back through the typed handle), alongside the non-DB fmt/build/clippy/unit/integration/example suites. Regression closed during finalization: the #601 child-fan-out collect-all per-slot classification (`spawn_child_workflow_fan_out_collect_raw`) was extended to match the new `HarvestError::WorkflowFailed` (a failed child previously matched `ActivityFailed`), so a failed child is captured per-slot rather than aborting the batch.
- **Phase 3.50** (implemented): Rolled-up management health summary — one-call incident triage (issue #679). New read-only admin route `GET /api/harvest/admin/status` composes five existing read models into one JSON document with a single worst-of verdict (`healthy`|`degraded`|`critical`) so an operator (or a dashboard/CI gate) answers *"is Harvest healthy right now?"* in **one** request instead of polling `/workers/health`, `/admin/shards/health`, `/dead-letters/aggregate`, and `/workflows?no_progress_minutes=N` separately and reconciling by hand. Module `autumn-harvest-plugin/src/status_summary.rs`; **never duplicates or changes any per-domain check's semantics** — the `shards` subsystem is `crate::shard_health::build_shard_health_report` verbatim, and the workers/DLQ/queues/stalled numbers come from the same core helpers those endpoints use (`workers::list_workers` deduped via `dedup_workers_by_freshest`; `dlq::dead_letter_count` + a newest-entry-age read; `queue::claimable_pending_demand_by_queue` for busiest-queue backlog; a bounded stalled-candidate count mirroring `load_stalled_workflows`'s predicate, capped at `stalled_critical_count+1`), fanned out across shards with the shared `crate::shard_fanout` scaffold (`pools_by_shard`/`expected_shards`/`ShardObservation`/`summarize_shard_errors`). Response shape: top-level `{ status, as_of, subsystems[], unavailable_shards[] }`; each `SubsystemHealth` block is `{ name, status, reason_codes[], drill_down, <flattened headline metrics> }` where `name` ∈ `workers`/`shards`/`dead_letters`/`queues`/`stalled_workflows`, `drill_down` is `Some(path)` **only when the subsystem is not `healthy`** (`null` otherwise) and points at the investigating endpoint (`workers`→`/workers/health`, `shards`→`/admin/shards/health`, `dead_letters`→`/dead-letters/aggregate`, `queues`→`/admin/shards/health`, `stalled_workflows`→`/workflows?no_progress_minutes={stalled_no_progress_minutes}`). Verdict is **worst-of subsystems** (`SubsystemStatus::rank` fold, `Critical` dominates `Degraded` dominates `Healthy`; empty = `Healthy`). Per-subsystem `reason_codes` are bounded/deduped/sorted (`worker_no_active`/`worker_unhealthy_fraction`/`dlq_backlog`/`dlq_recent_entry`/`queue_backlog`/`stalled_workflows`, plus the shard-health `shard_unreachable` vocab reused verbatim for both the shard subsystem and the partial-degradation escalation). **Partial-shard degradation, never a 500**: an unreachable shard drops each non-shard subsystem to at least `degraded` with the `shard_unreachable` code (they cannot assert `healthy` on incomplete data), the `shards` subsystem reflects it through its own readiness, and the unreachable shard is named in `unavailable_shards` (the two unavailable-shard lists — from the shard-health pass and the bundle fan-out — merged and deduped by `shard_id`). All classification is pure, unit-testable functions (`worst_status`, `classify_workers`/`classify_dead_letters`/`classify_queues`/`classify_stalled`/`classify_shards`, `build_status_response`); the async `build_status_report` runs the shard-health pass and the per-shard bundle fan-out concurrently (`tokio::join!`) then merges with the pure builder. **Configurable `StatusThresholds`** on the plugin builder via `HarvestPlugin::with_status_thresholds(..)` (mirrored onto `HarvestApiState` as `set_status_thresholds`/`status_thresholds`), framed as **starter defaults, not universal SLOs** — defaults: `dlq_degraded_total=1`, `dlq_critical_total=100`, `dlq_critical_recent_secs=300`, `queue_degraded_backlog=1000`, `queue_critical_backlog=10000`, `stalled_no_progress_minutes=60`, `stalled_degraded_count=1`, `stalled_critical_count=50`, `worker_degraded_unhealthy_fraction=0.25`, `worker_critical_unhealthy_fraction=0.5` (zero active workers while any are registered is always `critical`). Route registered in `management_api_routes()`/`management_api_response_fields()`, `autumn_harvest::audit::CLASSIFIED_ROUTES`/`AUDITED_OPERATIONS` allowlists (`GET /admin/status`, `RouteClass::ReadOnly`), and `docs/api-contract.json`; admin-guarded (`401` without admin). AC7 runbook: a "First 60 seconds — one-call incident triage" section added at the top of `docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md` (curl + example JSON, subsystem→drill_down table, worst-of/partial-degradation explanation, threshold table with defaults + builder method, and the PULL-triage vs PUSH-alert-pack vs `/health`-liveness vs `/admin/preflight`-startup cross-reference). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no core change** — purely a read-only plugin route composing existing read models. Tests: ~29 pure unit tests in `status_summary.rs` (`worst_status`, every classifier, `build_status_response` incl. drill-down-only-when-non-healthy, partial degradation, unavailable-shard merge/dedup, lowercase serde, configured-`no_progress_minutes` drill-down) plus audit/contract/security pins (`audit.rs`, `tests/contract_regression.rs`, `tests/security.rs`) and 4 compile-checked testcontainers scenarios in `tests/status_summary_integration.rs` (healthy fleet → 5 subsystems + null drill-downs, seeded dead-letter → non-healthy + critical rollup, admin-guard 401, one-shard-down → degraded + named in `unavailable_shards`, never 500).
- **Phase 3.50** (implemented): Effective-config introspection endpoint — answer "what config is this fleet actually running with, right now?" without reading source/env/builder — see issue #695. New read-only, admin-gated route `GET /api/harvest/admin/config` (handler `effective_config` in plugin `api.rs`) serves the resolved effective runtime configuration with **secrets redacted by construction**. Home: new core module `autumn-harvest/src/effective_config.rs` owning `EffectiveConfigView` (+ `WorkerConfigView`/`PayloadCapsView`/`ShardTopologyView`/`FeatureFlagsView`/`PoolConfigView` sub-structs, all `Serialize`), the `compiled_feature_flags()` core accessor (evaluates `cfg!` INSIDE the core crate so flags reflect the engine binary, not the plugin's own feature set), and the `EffectiveConfigView::capture(...)` assembly fn. **Redaction by construction:** the view struct never holds a secret-bearing value — `WorkerConfig::notification_database_url`, `shard_notification_database_urls`, and the `sharded_pool` handle are surfaced ONLY as `notification_channel_configured: bool` / `shard_notification_channels_configured: usize` / `sharded_pool_configured: bool` + `sharded_pool_shard_count: usize`, so a connection string (which can embed a password) can never appear in a response; a core unit test + a plugin HTTP test both assert the serialized body carries no `password`/`@host`/`postgres://` fragment. **Coverage guard (the falsifiable #695 AC):** `WorkerConfigView::from_worker_config` destructures `WorkerConfig` with an **EXHAUSTIVE pattern and NO `..`** (the `#[cfg(feature = "db")] sharded_pool` field is bound under a cfg attribute) — adding a new operator-tunable `WorkerConfig` field is a **compile error** here until the author surfaces it (a value, a derived boolean, or an explicit presence-only-for-secrets mapping); an inline `// exhaustive destructure is the #695 coverage guard — do NOT add ..` comment documents it. **Duration representation:** every duration serializes as whole milliseconds (`u64`) with a `_ms`-suffixed field name (one tunable, `poll_interval`, is 500 ms so seconds would lose precision); unset `Option<Duration>`/ceilings serialize as an explicit JSON `null` with the key preserved (unbounded is unambiguous, distinguishable from "field omitted"). **Derived triage booleans** (green-hat additions answering the issue's example incidents): `sticky_routing_enabled` (sticky_timeout > 0), `poison_pill_quarantine_enabled` (threshold > 0), `slot_tuner_enabled`; plus `build_id`/`deployment_name`/`labels`/`queue_weights` all surfaced (triage-useful, no secrets). Plumbing: `HarvestApiState` gains an `effective_config: Arc<Mutex<Option<EffectiveConfigView>>>` snapshot + `set_effective_config`/`effective_config()` (mirroring the existing `set_*` scalar-mirror pattern); the plugin captures the view once at `start_harvest_runtime` (before `harvest_pool`/`router` are moved into `HarvestRunnerResources`, using `harvest_pool.status().max_size` for pool sizing, `router` for shard topology, and `WorkerRuntimeConfig::from(...).poll_interval` for the poll interval); the handler fails closed with the standard `HarvestError::Config("harvest runtime is not started")` (→ 400) when the snapshot is unset (boot window). Route registered in all four parallel registries — `harvest_api_router` (with `.route_layer(require_admin.clone())`), `management_api_routes()`, `management_api_response_fields()` (NOT request_fields — GET has no body), and `docs/api-contract.json` (read_only:true, category "admin", 200 with the five top-level section fields) — plus `autumn_harvest::audit` `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` (`ReadOnly`), `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES` (route manifest, `None` op), and `EXCLUDED_ROUTES`, matching every sibling read-only admin GET. Runbook: a first-triage `curl .../admin/config | jq` step added to `docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md`. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no replay-determinism impact — read-only introspection over already-resolved config.** Tests, TDD red→green: 8 core no-DB unit tests in `effective_config.rs` (redaction-never-leaks, sentinel-coverage, unbounded-explicit-null, derived-bools, shard-topology single+multi, feature-flags-reflect-cfg, capture-assembles-all-sections, payload-caps-ms-conversion) + the 22-test `audit.rs` exhaustiveness guards (which validate the route is in both `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` and `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES` with matching counts); 3 plugin no-DB HTTP tests in `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/effective_config_http_tests.rs` (unauthenticated → 401 admin-guard, admin-authorized-but-no-snapshot → 400 fail-closed, admin happy-path → 200 + secret-free body with the five top-level keys) driving the real `harvest_api_router` via `tower::oneshot` (mirrors `security.rs`); the `contract_regression.rs` router↔contract parity test stays green. All executed (no Docker needed — this feature is entirely no-DB).
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Circuit-breaker phase in the read-only stuck-task eligibility explainer — see issue #611. The eligibility explainer (`GET /api/harvest/admin/queues/{queue_name}/eligibility`, `GET /api/harvest/admin/tasks/{id}/eligibility`) now emits `circuit_open`/`circuit_half_open` reason codes for a pending task whose next activity's circuit breaker is OPEN/HALF-OPEN — closing a real gap where an open-breaker-blocked task previously had an EMPTY reason set and its otherwise-eligible worker was wrongly reported eligible (an operator triaging idle workers with a full queue would see no impediment at all). The existing `rate_limit_saturated` reason code was renamed to `rate_limit_exhausted` — a response-contract label change flagged for operator tooling; it is a live label, not persisted data, so nothing is orphaned by the rename. **#369 interaction (dispatch-vs-claim suppression):** for an activity that carries a circuit breaker, rate limiting is enforced at dispatch rather than at claim, so `queue::claim_task` skips the rate-limit gate (and token debit) for CB activities; the explainer therefore suppresses `rate_limit_exhausted` for a CB activity and surfaces the breaker phase (`circuit_open`/`circuit_half_open`) instead — never a stale rate-limit reason. **Lazy Open→HalfOpen read caveat:** `CircuitBreakerRegistry::list()` reads (and prunes each breaker's rolling failure window on) phase without transitioning it — the Open→HalfOpen transition is driven exclusively inside `on_dispatch` — so a cooled-down breaker reads `circuit_open` here through the cooldown until a probe dispatch is admitted, and `circuit_half_open` is only observable after that probe; the endpoint is strictly read-only (`list()`/`snapshot` only, never `on_dispatch`/`on_result`/`force_*`). **Documented boundary (from adversarial review):** a CB activity whose breaker is CLOSED but whose rate-limit bucket is exhausted surfaces NO claim-time impediment through this explainer — its stall is dispatch-side (visible via `GET /admin/circuits/{activity_name}` + the token bucket), a pre-existing #369 consequence deliberately out of scope for #611's open/half-open focus. AC2 (concurrency-only labeling) and AC5 (multi-reason accumulation) were already shipped; the genuinely new work is the circuit codes (AC3/AC4), the rename (AC1), docs (AC6), and tests (AC7). **Implementation:** a pure, no-DB, unit-tested `task_intrinsic_impediment_reasons` helper in `api.rs` computes the task-intrinsic impediments (per-key concurrency saturation, rate-limit exhaustion, and circuit-breaker phase) that block every worker equally; a `cb_phase` map is built once per shard-eval via `circuit_breakers().list(Instant::now())` and passed in. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no new route, no replay/determinism impact, no shard-semantics change, no core-crate behavior change** — plugin-only, read-only labeling. Files: `autumn-harvest-plugin/src/api.rs`, `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/eligibility_tests.rs`, `docs/runbooks/triage-pending-tasks-idle-workers.md`, `docs/api-contract.json`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Tests: 9 pure unit tests in `api.rs` (`eligibility_reason_tests`, covering AC1–AC5, the #369 suppression, and the documented closed-breaker-CB-activity boundary that reports nothing); integration tests in `eligibility_tests.rs` (open-circuit → `circuit_open` with worker-absent / `no_eligible_workers` assertions and end-to-end #369 suppression via a shared-key non-CB sibling task; concurrency-only exact; rate-limit-exhausted exact). The eligibility integration tests are testcontainers-based and were NOT previously wired into CI at all — this slice adds both a `--no-run` compile step and a Docker-backed Linux execution step; the DB-backed tests are compile-checked in this sandbox (no Docker) and executed by CI, matching the repo's #543/#544/#601 precedent.
- **Per-execution stall diagnosis** (implemented) — see issue #809. **Before:** `StallReason` (#486) gave a coarse fleet-discovery bucket and `/stack` listed raw pending items, but neither answered *"is this a healthy wait or a pathological stall, and what is the actionable root cause?"*.
