The `pending_activity` bucket hid "running normally", "in retry backoff", "**no live worker polls this queue**", "**circuit breaker open**" and "**rate-limited / concurrency-deferred**" behind one label, so an operator correlated ≥4 endpoints by hand. **After:** one admin-gated, read-only call — `GET /api/harvest/workflows/{id}/diagnose` — returns a one-word triage `health` (`healthy` | `stalled` | `blocked_external` | `terminal`), a discriminated `blocked_on` object, and `last_event_age_seconds`. **Pure core classifier:** new `autumn-harvest/src/stall_diagnosis.rs` owns `BlockedOn` (internally tagged on `type`, snake_case, closed over 18 variants: `healthy_in_progress`, `awaiting_signal`, `sleeping_timer`, `timer_overdue`, `pending_child`, `activity_retrying`, `activity_deferred`, `activity_no_worker`, `activity_circuit_open`, `activity_rate_limited`, `activity_concurrency_deferred`, `activity_queue_paused`, `awaiting_external_handoff`, `paused`, `awaiting_replay_wait`, `workflow_no_worker`, `workflow_queue_paused`, `no_pending_work`), `ExecutionHealth`, the `*Facts` input structs, `classify_pending_activity`, `activity_precedence`, `classify_execution`, `classify_workflow_task` and `summarize` — all pure, no I/O, no DB, 81 inline unit tests. The three output-only enums are `#[non_exhaustive]` (nothing outside the crate constructs them), so adding a variant is a non-breaking wire addition for Rust consumers too; the `*Facts` input structs deliberately are NOT, because the plugin builds `PendingActivityFacts { .. }` as a cross-crate struct literal. `activity_queue_paused` is beyond the AC's literal list (permitted by its "at least" wording) and **correctness-required**: a paused queue with live workers and no other impediment would otherwise report `healthy_in_progress`, which is flat wrong. **Precedence ladder** (fixed, strictly ordered, unit-pinned): `queue_paused > no_worker > circuit_open > concurrency_deferred > rate_limited > retrying > deferred > healthy`. Every pending activity is classified and the **worst** wins, so one wedged slot in a wide fan-out is never masked by healthy siblings; `no_worker` deliberately outranks `retrying` because a task backing off on a pollerless queue will never run, so reporting "retrying" would promise an impossible retry. Category ladder above that: terminal → paused → activities → external handoffs → children → awaited signals → timers → `no_pending_work`. **Health is derived from the verdict class alone and never from event age**, so a long durable sleep reports `healthy` no matter how old its last event is (AC4). **Correlation, shard-local:** the plugin handler gathers the pending stack, per-queue worker liveness (reusing the canonical #774 `worker_covers_queue` + `fetch_potentially_live_workers`, promoted to `pub(crate)`, so it cannot drift from `/admin/queue-coverage` — the exact drift class that bit `shard_health` in #1150), the in-process circuit registry (#369, via `list()` **only** — never `on_dispatch`/`on_result`/`force_*` — so diagnosing can never advance a breaker's phase), rate-limit bucket and per-key concurrency saturation (SQL shaped exactly like `claim_task`'s own gates; a CB-tracked activity's bucket is deliberately skipped, matching #369's dispatch-time enforcement), the operator queue-pause table (#619, propagated on error rather than defaulting to "nothing is held"), and the task row's own `attempt`/`error`/`scheduled_at`. Shard resolution uses the execution row's **own** `shard_id` column, not `exec_id.shard()` — a pre-sharding (or `ExecutionId::new()`) id carries the `ShardId::UNENCODED` sentinel (`0xFFFF`), which would match no worker's `shard_assignments` and report a **false** `activity_no_worker` for a perfectly covered queue (a genuine bug caught by the integration suite). **Replay consulted only when it can change the answer:** an awaited-but-unsent signal exists solely as a parked command inside the coroutine, so observing one requires the #615 replay drive — which is comparatively expensive and ranks *below* activities/handoffs/children. The drive therefore runs **only** when the database-observable categories would otherwise resolve to `sleeping_timer` or `no_pending_work` (the two verdicts an awaited signal outranks); `wait_set` reports `replayed` / `history_only` (with `wait_set_reason`) / `not_consulted`. The verdict is identical either way, and the common triage path — a wedged pending activity — never pays for a replay, protecting the p95 < 500 ms metric. A replay failure **degrades** (`wait_set_unavailable`), never fails the request. **Multi-reason completeness alongside the single verdict:** `contributing_reason_codes` is the UNION of every claim-time impediment across ALL of the execution's activity rows — not just the row `blocked_on` names — so a lower-ranked cause is never hidden behind a higher-ranked sibling in a fan-out (that union is what makes the success metric's "surfaced 100% of the time it holds" literally true). Sourced verbatim from the eligibility explainer's own pure `task_intrinsic_impediment_reasons` (#611) so the two surfaces can never drift in how a cause is named. **Payload-free apart from the task row's own error text** (names, ids, timestamps and queue/bucket keys otherwise); that one error string IS routed through read-path payload decoding (#608) exactly as `/stack` routes the same column for its own `last_failure`, with the usual best-effort `payload.decode_read` audit row — otherwise an admin would read plaintext there and a ciphertext envelope here for the same column of the same row. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no task-queue mutation, no cross-shard fan-out — safe to call repeatedly.** Terminal executions return `health = terminal` with `terminal_outcome` and **no** `blocked_on`; unknown id → `404`, malformed id → `400`, missing admin → `401`. Registered `RouteClass::ReadOnly` in all three `audit.rs` lists (with a pinned `diagnose_route_is_classified_read_only` test), in `management_api_routes()`/`management_api_response_fields()`, and in `docs/api-contract.json`. CLI: `harvest workflow diagnose <exec-id>` renders a human-readable verdict (leading with `health` + `summary`, then every `blocked_on` member), `--json` prints the raw body. Runbook: a "Start here for a single wedged run" stanza with a `blocked_on.type` → action table at the top of `docs/runbooks/triage-pending-tasks-idle-workers.md`. **Tests:** 89 pure classifier unit tests (`stall_diagnosis.rs`), 38 DB/HTTP integration tests (`autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/stall_diagnosis_integration.rs`, dual-mode `HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL`/testcontainers, registered in `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`) covering AC3 (no-worker + its live-worker control), AC4 (future timer healthy with a two-year-old last event), AC5 (open circuit with cooldown; backing-off task with attempt/last_error/next_attempt_at), AC6 (`no_pending_work` stalled), AC7 (terminal outcome, 404/400, and a zero-writes + breaker-phase-unchanged assertion across three repeated calls), AC2 (replay-derived awaited signal, pending child, paused, and the fan-out worst-of rule), plus admin gating; and CLI mapping/coverage/renderer tests. Out of scope (per the issue): auto-remediation, fleet-wide stall *discovery* (#486), new stall-detection thresholds or scanners, historical/trend analysis, cross-shard aggregation. **Post-review hardening (four parallel adversarial reviews — correctness/classifier semantics, performance/read-only-safety/drift, test-quality/AC-evidence, and API-design/repo-conventions — every genuine finding fixed):** (1) **P1 — an unfired durable timer past its deadline reported `healthy`.** Timers fire ONLY when a worker claims the owning workflow task (`worker::ingest_due_timers_and_signals`); there is no independent timer scanner, so a long-missed deadline proves that task was never claimed. The mere presence of a timer therefore DOWNGRADED the genuine lost-task stall the same wedge reports without one (`no_pending_work`). New `timer_overdue { fires_at, overdue_by_seconds }` variant (`stalled`), gated by `TIMER_OVERDUE_GRACE_SECONDS` (60 s) so ordinary poll latency is never reported as a wedge, and checked ABOVE the signal/child/handoff categories so a signal-or-deadline race (#476) whose deadline the engine missed cannot hide behind the healthy-looking `awaiting_signal`. (2) **P1 — the task-queue read loaded five jsonb payload columns it never used.** `TaskQueueItem::as_select()` on a stalled wide fan-out of large activity inputs — the exact shape this endpoint exists to diagnose — moved hundreds of megabytes to answer a triage question, twice on the replay path. Replaced with a ten-scalar projection; deliberately still unbounded, because the worst-of fold must see every row and the narrow projection already removed the cost. (3) **P2 — a claimed (`RUNNING`) row whose queue has no live poller reported `healthy`.** That is a poison-pill orphan (#367); the reclaimer heals it within a poll interval EXCEPT when the whole fleet for that queue is down, which is the flagship `activity_no_worker` case, so the endpoint answered "fine" forever for a run that could never move. Claimed rows now require a live poller to read healthy, and `queues_in_play` is built from ALL loaded rows (not just PENDING ones) so liveness is genuinely evaluated rather than defaulting to `false` because it was never checked. (4) **P2 — `saturated_rate_limit_keys` was fail-OPEN while `claim_task`'s gate is fail-CLOSED.** The gate is `EXISTS(bucket >= 1.0)`, so a key with no bucket row at all (registration failed, the row was deleted, or startup skipped an invalid config) is permanently unclaimable — but the positive "which keys are saturated?" query returned nothing for it and the classifier reported `healthy`. Inverted to ask the admissible set and subtract. (5) **P2 — a not-yet-due task was misreported as rate-limited/concurrency-deferred.** A backing-off task has not reached the claim gates at all, so a momentarily-empty bucket says nothing about it — and reporting one dropped `attempt`, `last_error` and `next_attempt_at`, the three fields an operator wants. Retry backoff now sits above the two SELF-HEALING gates in the per-row ladder while the three non-self-healing ones (`queue_paused`, `no_worker`, `circuit_open`) still outrank it. (6) **P2 — `contributing_reason_codes` could drop or misattribute reasons.** `diagnosed_activity` re-sampled `Utc::now()` instead of the handler's snapshot, so a task whose backoff expired mid-request could flip the winner's kind and silently empty the list — or attribute one row's reasons to a different row's verdict. The second scan is deleted outright: reasons are now unioned across all rows, which also fixes the masking hole and stops fabricating `no_live_worker` for a claimed row whose coverage was never evaluated. (7) **P2 — `last_error` bypassed #608 read-path decode** that `/stack` applies to the same column, so an admin saw plaintext there and ciphertext here; now decoded with the audit row. (8) **P2 — the AC5 `cooldown_until` clause had no proof at any level**: the one test claiming it used `force_open`, which sets `forced_open` and therefore structurally CANNOT produce a cooldown. Renamed to pin the forced-open shape (asserting the field is ABSENT — the signal that recovery needs an explicit `force-close`) and added an organically-tripped test that exercises the real `time_until_probe_secs` → `DateTime` derivation, plus unit tests for `circuit_cooldown_until` over NaN/±inf/negative/overflow. (9) **P2 — the replay was un-deadlined**: `build_awaitables_report` inflates offloaded payloads per event (#524) outside the query timeout, so a long history with a remote `PayloadStore` could run for minutes on a latency-budgeted triage endpoint; now bounded by the server's query timeout, degrading to `wait_set_timed_out`. A `terminal` wait-set answer from the TOCTOU race where the run goes terminal mid-request is mapped to `execution_went_terminal` rather than leaking a fourth undocumented vocabulary value. (10) **P3s:** rate-limit/concurrency key vectors deduped (a wide fan-out sharing one key bound one array element per row); the phantom `CLAIMED`/`BACKOFF` task states corrected in the docs (the engine's CHECK constraint admits only `PENDING`/`RUNNING`/`COMPLETED`/`FAILED`/`CANCELLED`, and retry backoff is `PENDING` with a future `scheduled_at`); an unnamed activity in backoff no longer falls through to healthy (`ActivityRetrying.activity_name` is now `Option<String>`, uniform with every sibling variant); `summarize` re-exported from `lib.rs` alongside its three siblings; a Module Guide row added; the two `diagnose` / `replay-diagnosis` CLI subcommands cross-reference each other; and the runbook now notes that `cooldown_until` is absent for an operator-forced-open breaker. **Ten new integration tests** close the wire-coverage gaps the review found: `activity_rate_limited` (plus a missing-bucket case pinning the fail-closed fix), `activity_concurrency_deferred`, `activity_queue_paused`, `awaiting_external_handoff`, the orphaned-`RUNNING` case, `timer_overdue`, the cross-row reason union, the organically-tripped cooldown, and the replay degrade path (which revealed the endpoint passes the precise upstream `handler_not_registered` reason through verbatim — strictly better than its own generic fallback). **Known limitation, documented not fixed:** `has_live_worker` answers "does any live worker poll this queue?", not the full per-task claim predicate — a task whose `required_build_id` (#171/#604), `required_capabilities` (#804) or session pin (#606) matches no live worker sits on a covered queue and still reports healthy. Modelling those needs the eligibility explainer's per-worker predicate and is a follow-up. **Post-review hardening, round 2 (Codex bot review of PR #1188 — two P2s fixed, one P1 refuted with evidence):** (a) **P2 (fixed) — a future `scheduled_at` alone was read as "failed and retrying".** The dispatcher also pushes a task forward with NO failure at all: `queue::defer_rate_limited_task` (dispatch-time rate limiting, #699/#369) even decrements the claim-time attempt back down because "a rate-limit deferral is not an attempt", and the session-capacity (#606) and capability-miss (#804) paths reuse the same `CleanContinuationChangeset`. Reporting those as `activity_retrying` sent an operator hunting a failure that never happened. The not-yet-due branch now turns on **failure evidence** — a recorded `error`, which `CleanContinuationChangeset` never clears, so its presence is durable proof an attempt really did fail and its absence proof that none ever did — and reports the new `activity_deferred { activity_name?, next_attempt_at }` variant otherwise (`healthy`; it self-heals). It ranks directly below `activity_retrying` in the cross-task ladder (failure evidence is the more actionable of the two) and the three non-self-healing gates still outrank both. (b) **P2 (fixed) — the terminal fast path returned `execution.error` verbatim**, skipping the #608 read-path decode the pending-activity path applies to the same TEXT column, so on a codec-encrypting deployment an admin received a ciphertext envelope while the decode audit recorded nothing. Now routed through `decode_error_field` + `decode_outcome`, mirroring the activity site exactly. (c) **P1 (refuted, pinned by regression test) — "check overdue timers before returning an activity verdict".** Hoisting the overdue-timer check above the activity bucket would introduce a **false positive**, the one verdict this endpoint must never emit. Whether an overdue unfired timer is a wedge depends entirely on whether the owning workflow task was scheduled to wake at that deadline: a timer-only suspension (and the `receive_signal_timeout` deadline race, which routes to the same persist path) calls `queue::reschedule_task(task_id, fires_at)`, so an unfired timer past it proves the wake never happened — and those shapes leave no pending activity row, so they already reach the check. But `persist_scheduled_activities` parks the task on the ACTIVITY and explicitly discards the armed deadline (`_min_fires_at`, commented in the engine "armed timers observed on next wake; deadline unused here"), so a cancellable timer (#768) armed alongside an activity — `join!(handle.await_fire(), ctx.execute_activity(..))` — goes overdue as a matter of course while the activity runs and fires on the activity's completion wake. Hoisting would report that healthy run `stalled`. The ordering is now documented in-code with that engine evidence and pinned by three tests: `healthy_activity_alongside_an_overdue_timer_is_not_a_stall`, `overdue_timer_still_wins_when_no_activity_is_pending`, and `wedged_activity_alongside_an_overdue_timer_reports_the_activity`. **Post-review hardening, round 3 (Codex bot review of PR #1188 — two more findings, both genuine and both fixed):** both are the same root defect — `no_pending_work`, the most alarming verdict this endpoint can return, was reached before two whole classes of evidence had been consulted. (a) **P1 — the run's OWN workflow task row was discarded.** The task query filtered `task_type = 'activity'`, so the `task_type = 'workflow'` row — which every non-terminal run has exactly one of — was invisible. That row is the only place three states are distinguishable: the handler EXECUTING right now (`worker_id` held, canonically a run mid-way through a long local activity (#98), which schedules no queue row of any kind), the decision cycle AWAITING DISPATCH (`PENDING`), and the genuinely PARKED row (`RUNNING` with a NULL worker, per `park_workflow_task`'s own SQL). Without it, a perfectly healthy in-flight or about-to-be-claimed run fell through every category and reported `no_pending_work`/`stalled`. Fixed with a single-row indexed lookup feeding the new `WorkflowTaskFacts` + pure `classify_workflow_task`, consulted **as a fallback below every side-table cause** (a workflow task always exists, so consulting it higher would flatten every specific verdict): a held claim → `healthy_in_progress`; a `PENDING` row → `healthy_in_progress` when a live worker polls its queue or it is deliberately deferred, the new `workflow_queue_paused { queue }` (`blocked_external`) when an operator holds that queue (#619), and the new `workflow_no_worker { queue }` (`stalled`) — the workflow-task analogue of AC3's flagship no-live-worker condition — when nothing polls it; a **parked** row yields `None` so the lost-task verdict is unchanged (a parked row advances on a *wake*, not a claim, so a live worker proves nothing). The workflow queue joins `queues_in_play` so its liveness is answered by the same canonical #774 predicate as every activity queue. (b) **P2 — every non-`Signal` replay awaitable was dropped.** The replay filter kept only `AwaitableKind::Signal`, discarding `Condition`, `Mutex`, `Update`, `ExternalWorkflow` (and `Activity`/`ChildWorkflow`/`Timer`) — and a command-less `ctx.await_condition` park, a durable mutex acquire (#691), an admitted update awaiting its handler, and a parked external-workflow operation (#492/#757/#751) leave **no row in any side table this endpoint reads**, so replay is the only source that can see them. A run legitimately parked on any of them reported `no_pending_work`/`stalled`. Fixed with the new `awaiting_replay_wait { wait_kind, name?, since? }` variant (`blocked_external`), fed from every non-`Signal` awaitable in recorded/command order (deterministic) and consulted **below every side-table cause** — so it can only ever replace a false lost-task verdict and can never mask a more precise one such as `sleeping_timer` (pinned by `replay_wait_never_masks_a_sleeping_timer`); signals keep their own dedicated, higher-ranked verdict. Both fixes are additive to `DiagnosisInputs` (`workflow_task: Option<_>`, `replay_waits: Vec<_>`, both defaulting empty), so every pre-existing caller and the classifier's prior behaviour are byte-identical. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration.** RED→GREEN verified by neutering the two ladder branches (6 unit tests fail, the ordering/regression guards stay green). 15 new pure unit tests and 5 new DB/HTTP integration tests (claimed → healthy, `PENDING` on a dead queue → `workflow_no_worker` naming it, its live-worker control, parked → still `no_pending_work`, and the fallback-never-masks-a-wedged-activity guard). **Post-review hardening, round 4 (Codex bot review of PR #1188 — two more findings, both genuine and both fixed):** both are the round-3 workflow-task classifier reintroducing, for the workflow row, two defects already fixed for ACTIVITY rows in round 1 — a stored claim treated as progress without checking liveness, and a self-healing deferral returned ahead of a non-self-healing gate. (a) **P1 — a stale claim reported `healthy_in_progress`.** `classify_workflow_task`'s `has_worker` fast path returned healthy unconditionally, but a crashed worker leaves its workflow task `RUNNING` with a non-null `worker_id` until the poison-pill reclaimer processes it (issue #367) — exactly the orphan shape `orphaned_running_tasks_query` selects. With nothing polling the queue that claim never advances, so the endpoint answered “fine” forever for a run that could not move (indefinitely, if the reclaimer is itself impaired). (b) **P2 — a not-yet-due deferral was accepted before the coverage check.** For a `PENDING` row with `scheduled_at` in the future, `healthy_in_progress` was returned *above* the `has_live_worker` gate, so an uncovered queue read healthy until the timestamp arrived even though nobody would claim it then; unlike a timed sleep, a dispatcher deferral only self-heals if something claims the row. Both fixed by reordering `classify_workflow_task` onto `classify_pending_activity`'s **hard-impediment-first ladder**: a held claim is healthy only when a live worker still polls its queue (else `workflow_no_worker`), and a `PENDING` row resolves `queue_paused` → `no_worker` → not-yet-due → healthy. Liveness uses the same fleet-coverage proxy (`worker_covers_queue`, #774) the activity classifier uses, carrying the same documented limitation. The **parked** case (`RUNNING` with a NULL worker) is deliberately unchanged — it advances on a *wake*, not a claim, so a live poller proves nothing and it still yields `None` to the lost-task verdict. A pause remains a claim-time gate and so never downgrades an already-executing handler. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration.** RED→GREEN verified (2 new unit tests fail against the old ordering, both controls stay green). 3 new pure unit tests + 2 controls and 3 new DB/HTTP integration tests (stale claim on a dead queue → `workflow_no_worker`, not-yet-due on a dead queue → `workflow_no_worker`, and its live-worker control); the round-3 `claimed_workflow_task_reports_healthy_not_a_lost_task` DB test named its worker `w-live` but never registered it as live, so it now seeds one to exercise the healthy path its name describes. **Post-review hardening, round 5 (Codex bot review of PR #1188, one P1 — genuine, and broader than reported):** the `timer_overdue` verdict was returned for **any** unfired timer past the grace window, without checking whether that timer actually owns the run's wake. Codex named the external-handoff case (`persist_scheduled_external_activity` parks the task and discards `_min_fires_at`, so a partner callback slower than the window leaves a legitimately-overdue row); auditing `worker.rs` showed the defect is a **class**, not a case — `_min_fires_at` is discarded at eight sites across seven persist functions (`persist_signal_wait_park`, `persist_mutex_acquire_park`, `persist_activity_wait_park`, `persist_scheduled_activities`, `persist_started_timer`, `persist_all_started_child_workflows`, and `persist_scheduled_external_activity` twice), and **only** `persist_started_timer` then calls `queue::reschedule_task(task_id, fires_at)` to hand the timer ownership of the wake. Because the overdue check ranked ABOVE external handoffs, children and awaited signals, a timer armed alongside **any** of those reported a false `timer_overdue`/`stalled` — activities were spared only by the round-2 ordering guard. Fixed with the precise gate Codex suggested rather than a reorder (which would be whack-a-mole across four ranked-below categories): the new pure `workflow_wake_was_missed(task, now)` keys on the workflow task row's **own** wake — a *claimed* row means the handler is executing, a *parked* row (`RUNNING`, NULL worker) means some other wake owns the run, and only a `PENDING` row past its own `scheduled_at` by the grace window is a genuinely missed timer wake. Absent facts resolve to `true`, so every pre-gate caller is byte-identical. This also handles the multi-timer case in both directions (an overdue passenger timer alongside a later-armed owning timer no longer wins) and **preserves** the round-2 refutation: the issue #476 `receive_signal_timeout` deadline race still routes to `persist_started_timer` (verified — `should_requeue_signal_wait`'s allowlist excludes `StartTimer`, so a mixed `StartTimer + WaitForSignal` batch falls through to `extract_started_timer_for_suspension`), so a genuinely missed deadline race still outranks `awaiting_signal`. The ordering guard is kept as well, because it remains load-bearing for the activity case specifically: `persist_scheduled_activities` leaves the row `PENDING` at a *retry* `scheduled_at`, which the gate alone cannot distinguish from a missed timer wake. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration.** RED→GREEN verified at both levels (5 pure tests and the new DB test fail against the ungated classifier, each reporting `timer_overdue` where a precise verdict is expected). 7 new pure unit tests (parked-task → handoff/child/signal, the preserved genuine-miss case, claim-suppressed, next-wake-still-ahead, and a `workflow_wake_was_missed` truth table) and 2 new DB/HTTP integration tests (an overdue timer alongside a parked external handoff reports the handoff; a `PENDING` row long past its own `scheduled_at` still reports `timer_overdue`). `classify_workflow_task`, `workflow_wake_was_missed`, `WorkflowTaskFacts`, `ReplayWaitFacts` and `TIMER_OVERDUE_GRACE_SECONDS` are now re-exported from `lib.rs` alongside their siblings, making the module-guide claim accurate. **Post-review hardening, round 5 (Codex bot review of `7e7478c`, one P1): a timer cannot fire if its own workflow task can never be claimed.** Round 4 stopped `timer_overdue` from false-firing when some *other* wake owned the run; Codex found the mirror-image gap on the healthy side. A durable timer fires only when a worker claims the owning workflow task and `worker::ingest_due_timers_and_signals` runs — there is no independent timer scanner — so a run "sleeping" on a timer whose **workflow** queue is operator-held (#619) or has no live poller is not sleeping: it can never wake. `classify_execution` returned `sleeping_timer`/`healthy` (before the deadline) or `timer_overdue` (after it) before `classify_workflow_task` could ever report `workflow_queue_paused`/`workflow_no_worker`, so the endpoint answered "fine" for a permanently wedged run and, past the deadline, named the elapsed timer rather than the queue an operator must actually fix. Fixed with a new pure `workflow_task_hard_impediment(&WorkflowTaskFacts) -> Option<BlockedOn>` that returns **only** the two hard impediments (`WorkflowQueuePaused`, `WorkflowNoWorker`) — never the ordinary healthy-dispatch verdict, which stays in the fallback so it cannot mask the more specific `sleeping_timer` — consulted in `classify_execution` immediately **above** the `timer_overdue` gate. Placement is deliberate in both directions: **below** the activity bucket, because a wedged activity names the specific thing to fix (pinned by `wedged_activity_still_outranks_a_workflow_queue_impediment`); **above** the handoff/child/signal categories is harmless *by construction*, because every one of those parks the workflow task and a parked row (`RUNNING` with a NULL worker) advances on a wake rather than a claim, so no claim-time gate applies and the helper returns `None` (pinned by `parked_workflow_task_never_masks_a_sleeping_timer`). `classify_workflow_task` was refactored to delegate to the same helper, so the fallback verdict and the timer gate can never drift about whether a row is claimable; its `now` parameter became dead and was removed (the deferral branch and the due branch both resolved to `HealthyInProgress`, so the ladder is behaviour-identical — verified case-by-case and pinned by the pre-existing `classify_workflow_task` tests). **Known residual, deliberately scoped:** a *healthy* activity on a different, live queue alongside a dead/paused **workflow** queue still reports `healthy_in_progress` — hoisting above the activity bucket to catch it would mask wedged-activity verdicts, a strictly worse trade. (When the two queues are the same, the activity row reports `activity_no_worker` itself, so the common case is covered.) **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/response-shape change.** Tests, TDD red→green (RED verified as 4 behavioural failures against the unwired classifier): 8 pure tests — `sleeping_timer_on_a_paused_workflow_queue_reports_queue_paused`, `sleeping_timer_on_a_dead_workflow_queue_reports_no_worker`, `sleeping_timer_with_a_healthy_workflow_queue_is_still_a_sleeping_timer`, `overdue_timer_on_a_dead_workflow_queue_reports_no_worker`, `claimed_workflow_task_on_a_dead_queue_outranks_a_sleeping_timer`, `parked_workflow_task_never_masks_a_sleeping_timer`, `wedged_activity_still_outranks_a_workflow_queue_impediment`, and the `workflow_task_hard_impediment_truth_table` — plus 3 DB/HTTP tests (`sleeping_timer_on_a_dead_workflow_queue_reports_no_worker`, its live-poller control `sleeping_timer_with_a_live_workflow_queue_is_still_a_sleeping_timer`, and `sleeping_timer_on_a_paused_workflow_queue_reports_queue_paused`). `workflow_task_hard_impediment` is re-exported from `lib.rs` alongside its siblings.
- **Per-execution legal hold** (implemented) — see issue #747. **Before:** an operator could not exempt a single workflow execution's history from the retention janitor (issue #737) or from targeted PII erasure (issue #495). A subpoena/litigation hold on one run required disabling retention globally or racing the janitor. **After:** `POST /api/harvest/workflows/{id}/legal-hold` places a durable, per-execution hold that exempts that execution's `harvest_events` history from retention deletion **and** from PII erasure until it is released (`POST /workflows/{id}/legal-hold/release`) or auto-expires (optional `hold_until`). A held execution is skipped as the *first* per-candidate gate in the retention tick, so `harvest.retention.deleted` never counts a held id; an erase attempt on a held execution returns `409` naming the active hold. Additive nullable columns only (`legal_hold_set_at` / `legal_hold_until` / `legal_hold_reason` / `legal_hold_actor`) on `harvest_workflow_executions` (migration `20260709000001_harvest_legal_hold`), plus a partial discovery index. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no replay impact, shard-local.** Active-hold predicate is single-sourced in `legal_hold_active(set_at, until, now)` (re-exported from the crate root), shared by the retention gate, the erase gate, the describe/list surfaces, and the set/release core functions. Idempotent: re-holding an actively-held execution preserves provenance (`newly_held: false`); releasing an unheld execution is a `200` no-op (`released: false`). `GET /workflows/{id}` surfaces a derived `legal_hold` boolean (plus the four raw columns); `GET /workflows?legal_hold=true` filters to actively-held runs. Admin-only, audited under `legal_hold.set` / `legal_hold.release`. CLI: `harvest legal-hold set <id> --reason <r> [--until <rfc3339>]` and `harvest legal-hold release <id>`.
- **Tooling — property-based testing + cargo-fuzz harness bootstrap** (implemented, PR #1004): Bootstrapped a randomized-testing workstream with two complementary layers plus CI wiring — no product-code behavior change. **Property tests** (`proptest`, foundation commit `be8aaa7`): a single external `autumn-harvest/tests/property/` target (mirrors the `tests/integration/` one-`mod.rs`-entry-point convention), bounded to 128 cases by default and overridable upward via proptest's native `PROPTEST_CASES` env knob, with on-disk `failure_persistence` disabled so CI runners stay artifact-free. Pure, non-`db`-gated suites (`policy_props`, `queue_fairness_props`, `task_duration_props`, `completion_trigger_props`, `completion_callback_props`, `event_serde_props`) run under `--no-default-features`; `db`-gated suites (`build_routing_props`, `dlq_props`) are `#[cfg(feature = "db")]` submodules that target **pure functions** in `#[cfg(feature = "db")]` modules and need no live Postgres. Coverage: `policy::compute_retry_delay` (cap/monotonicity/jitter-band), `queue_fairness::weighted_queue_order`/`effective_queue_weights` (permutation, zero-weight-last), `task_duration` (round-trip/sum/totality), `completion_trigger::TriggerCondition::evaluate`/`gate_stored_condition` (totality + gate/evaluate agreement over corrupt stored values), `completion_callback::validate_target_url` (internal IPv4/IPv6 literals never validate even under the permissive policy), `WorkflowEvent` serde round-trip + #521/#488 additive-field back-compat, `build_routing::ramp_bucket`/`validate_ramp_percent` (with the inclusive `0`/`100`/`101` bounds explicitly seeded), `dlq::failure_signature` (**deterministic** — the documented contract, not idempotence, which is false at the cap boundary — plus a guaranteed-oversized-input arm that exercises the `<= SIGNATURE_MAX_LEN` truncation branch); in-crate proptests for non-public targets `worker::nd_block_backoff` (private, db-gated) and `context::remaining_secs_until` (`pub(crate)`). **Fuzz harness** (`cargo-fuzz` / libFuzzer, PR #1004): a new `fuzz/` crate **excluded** from the root workspace (root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace] exclude = ["fuzz"]` + its own empty `[workspace]` table), so the root resolver never builds these nightly/libFuzzer-only binaries — verified via `cargo metadata --no-deps` (`autumn-harvest-fuzz` is not a member) and a clean `cargo build -p autumn-harvest --no-default-features` with `fuzz/` present. Four targets over the functions where raw-bytes coverage-guided fuzzing genuinely beats structured proptest: `fuzz_workflow_event_deser` (`serde_json::from_slice::<WorkflowEvent>` totality — every history read path deserializes this append-only enum), `fuzz_det_check_source` (`det_check::check_source` totality — the highest-value target given the historical parity churn against the proc-macro determinism lint; a hand-rolled line/brace scanner run over user code in CI/editors), `fuzz_validate_target_url` (`completion_callback::validate_target_url` totality under the most-permissive SSRF policy — issue #605 security boundary), `fuzz_failure_signature` (`dlq::failure_signature` totality + `<= SIGNATURE_MAX_LEN`; `db`-gated, so the fuzz crate enables the `db` feature). `fuzz/smoke.sh` runs each target ~15s for local/manual use. In-sandbox `cargo +nightly fuzz build` built all four; each ran ~9s clean (hundreds of thousands of executions, zero crashes). **CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): (1) a new **"Run db-gated property suites"** step in the existing `test` job (`cargo test -p autumn-harvest --features db --test property`) — `build_routing_props`/`dlq_props` were previously only *compiled* (never executed) by the `--no-run`/`--lib` db steps; they need no Docker. (2) A new opt-in **`fuzz-smoke`** job gated `workflow_dispatch`-only (never push/PR — Actions minutes are tight and fuzzing needs nightly), 30s per target, plus a `workflow_dispatch:` trigger added to `on:`. (Rebased onto current trunk: the line-186 `if:` YAML indentation fix already landed independently in #988, so this branch adds only the two CI items above and requires no ci.yml re-indent.) **Docs**: `docs/testing/property-and-fuzz.md` — how to run both layers (incl. the db-featured line and `PROPTEST_CASES` deep runs), the target-selection rationale (pure functions / parsers / totality), and a per-subsystem follow-up backlog including the two deferred items **C12** (det_check ↔ macro-guardrail differential — needs a proc-macro test harness since `determinism_lint.rs` isn't an invocable `pub fn`) and **C13** (`WorkflowReplayer`-based replay-determinism property under `--features testing`, reusing the #476 1000-ordering precedent), plus scheduler cron parsing, `resolve_concurrency_key`/`project_json_path`, `throttle::parse_rate`, rendezvous shard-routing stability, and `validate_against_schema`-vs-serde candidates. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route change, no replay/determinism impact, no product-code change** — test/tooling/docs/CI only. Local verification: property suites `21 passed` (no-db) / `26 passed` (db), both sub-second; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.
- **Phase 3.47** (implemented): SSRF guard — block `0.0.0.0/8` and `198.18.0.0/15` callback targets (issue #605 hardening / PR #1004 review notes). Closed two IP-literal SSRF bypasses in the completion-callback URL validator (`completion_callback::validate_target_url` → `is_ipv4_non_routable`), surfaced by the `validate_target_url` internal-IP property/fuzz coverage added in PR #1004. **Before:** the classifier blocked the bare `0.0.0.0` (via `is_unspecified()`) but not the rest of `0.0.0.0/8` ("this host on this network", RFC 1122) — on Linux the whole range routes to localhost, so `http(s)://0.0.0.1/`, `http(s)://0.1.2.3/`, `http(s)://0.255.255.255/` all passed the callback host allowlist. It also missed the entire `198.18.0.0/15` benchmarking range (RFC 2544), so `198.18.0.1` … `198.19.255.255` validated. **After:** both ranges are rejected as `SsrfRejection::IpNotRoutable` (the existing machine-readable code — no new variant), alongside the previously covered loopback (`127.0.0.0/8`), private (`10/8`, `172.16/12`, `192.168/16`), link-local (`169.254/16`), CGNAT/shared (`100.64.0.0/10`), unspecified, multicast, documentation, and broadcast ranges. IPv6 v4-mapped forms (`::ffff:0.0.0.1`, `::ffff:198.18.0.1`) inherit the fix through the existing `to_ipv4_mapped()` canonicalization. **Blast radius / call sites that inherit the fix for free** (all four reuse the one pure `validate_target_url`): builder-default callback registration (`try_build`), the per-start HTTP registration route (rejects with `422`), enqueue-time re-validation (defense in depth), and the scanner's fire-time re-validation before each POST. The inbound webhook receiver (`autumn-harvest-plugin`) does **not** reuse this guard — it verifies inbound deliveries via autumn-web's `[security.webhooks]` — so it is unaffected. **Scope:** validator + tests only. No new `SsrfRejection` code, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no API/wire change. TDD red→green: the two new range tests and the v4-mapped test failed against the old classifier (addresses returned `Ok`); the fix makes them pass while the added already-covered-range audit tests and the just-outside-`198.18.0.0/15` neighbor tests (`198.17.255.255`, `198.20.0.0` still pass validation) stay green. Verified with `cargo test -p autumn-harvest {--no-default-features,--features db} ssrf_tests` (33 passed), `cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest --all-features --tests -- -D warnings` and `-p autumn-harvest-plugin` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- **Phase 4** (implemented, testing infra): Loom concurrency model checking for the in-process state machines. Bootstraps a [loom](https://github.com/tokio-rs/loom) model-checking workstream that exhaustively explores the thread interleavings of harvest's two genuinely-concurrent, in-process, `Mutex`-guarded data structures — the per-activity circuit breaker (`circuit_breaker.rs`) and the worker session-slot registry (`sessions.rs`). Loom `= "0.7.2"` was already an (unused) dev-dependency; this wires it up. **No production behavior change, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration** — the entire change is test infrastructure plus a `cfg`-gated sync-primitive alias. **Contained `cfg(loom)` shim.** New `src/loom_sync.rs` re-exports `Arc`/`Mutex`/`MutexGuard` — `std::sync` under a normal build (byte-for-byte identical to before), `loom::sync` under `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg loom"`. Only `circuit_breaker.rs` and `sessions.rs` import from it; the swap is deliberately **not** swept across the crate. Loom's `Mutex::lock()` returns the same `std::sync::LockResult` and never poisons, so the existing `.unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner)` call sites compile and behave identically under both configs with no `cfg`-gating of the lock call. `std::time::Instant` is deliberately left as std (loom does not model time; real `Instant`s are passed through). **Models (`tests/loom_models.rs`, `#![cfg(loom)]`-gated so `cargo test` never runs them).** Four models, each two `loom::thread` threads / ≤2 ops, driving the real types: (1) `circuit_breaker_stale_failure_cannot_retrip_a_reset_breaker` (headline) — a generation-stamped `DispatchToken` captured before an operator reset races the `force_close`; the stale retryable failure is fenced under every interleaving (breaker ends CLOSED, empty window), proving the generation fence + `forced_open` guard compose under concurrency; (2) `circuit_breaker_admits_at_most_one_half_open_probe` — two dispatches race for the single half-open probe slot; exactly one is admitted; (3) `session_slot_bound_admits_at_most_one_at_capacity_one` — the capacity bound holds under a concurrent acquire race; (4) `session_slot_acquire_release_balances_and_never_underflows` — concurrent acquire/release drains the registry to empty. **Build wiring.** loom is moved to `[target.'cfg(loom)'.dependencies]` (not `[dev-dependencies]`) because the shim references `loom::sync::*` from the *library* sources (the `SessionSlotRegistry` type alias is production code), and dev-deps are not available to the normal library build the integration test links against. Under a global `--cfg loom`, tokio's `net` module is compiled out (`#![cfg(not(loom))]`), so every `tokio::net` consumer must be kept out of the loom graph: the run uses `--no-default-features` (drops `db`→`tokio-postgres`) and `testcontainers` is gated to `[target.'cfg(not(loom))'.dev-dependencies]` (it pulls `hyper-util`). `cfg(loom)` is registered in `[workspace.lints.rust]` `check-cfg` so `unexpected_cfgs` does not fire under normal `-D warnings` builds. **No interleaving bug found** — all four models pass. Run manually: `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg loom" cargo test -p autumn-harvest --no-default-features --test loom_models --release`. **CI.** New `.github/workflows/loom.yml` runs the suite on `workflow_dispatch` **only** — never in the required-status matrix, so zero added cost on normal PR/push runs (respecting #999). **Docs.** `docs/testing/loom.md` (what loom can/can't do, the module include/exclude rationale, an honest coverage caveat that the majority of harvest's concurrency lives in Postgres and is out of loom's reach, run instructions, how to add a model, and model-size/preemption-bound guidance) and `docs/testing/concurrency-model-checking.md` (an honest loom/Shuttle/Turmoil evaluation: loom adopted now; Shuttle recommended fast-follow for the async `slot_tuner.rs` semaphore-accounting invariant loom structurally cannot reach — backlogged rather than shipping a non-running PoC; Turmoil recommended against, since harvest coordinates through Postgres and has no custom peer networking for Turmoil to simulate — verified by repo search — with a recommendation matrix).
- **Continue-as-new run-chain timeline API** (implemented): expose the complete, ordered continue-as-new succession for a workflow, resolvable from **any** member run (head, middle, or latest) in one call — see issue #701. Before this change, an operator holding a workflow's *latest* continue-as-new run had no way to see its predecessors: continue-as-new successors are inserted with `parent_id: None` and carried no backward link, so the sole forward link (the `WorkflowContinuedAsNew` event) could not be walked backward, and there was no single API for the whole chain — reconstructing a succession meant manual database spelunking. New read-only management route `GET /api/harvest/workflows/{id}/run-chain` (handler in plugin `api.rs`) and CLI subcommand `harvest workflow run-chain <exec_id> [--json]` return `{ head_unknown, workflow_id, runs: [{ exec_id, run_id, sequence, state, started_at, completed_at, outcome, continued_to_exec_id }] }` — `sequence` is zero-based over the ordered chain and `continued_to_exec_id` is `null` for the tail (AC2). **Additive back-link, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, zero replay-determinism impact**: two nullable columns on `harvest_workflow_executions` — `continued_from_exec_id` (immediate predecessor) and `first_exec_id` (chain origin) — are stamped at the existing `persist_workflow_continue_as_new` successor-insert site; migration `20260710000002_harvest_workflow_continue_chain` is additive/nullable only, with partial indexes on both columns. **Design decisions**: (1) the dual-column back-link records both the immediate predecessor and the chain origin, so `first_exec_id` gives O(1) head resolution and a single indexed query (`WHERE id = head OR first_exec_id = head`) fetches the whole chain from any member — no per-hop history loads on a post-feature chain, hitting the p99 < 100 ms / N ≤ 100 success metric. (2) Pure core module `run_chain.rs` (`RunChainRecord`/`RunChainResponse`, `assemble_run_chain`, ordering + `head_unknown` derivation) is unit-tested without a database; ordering is bounded and cycle-safe (a `continued_from` linked-list walk with a deterministic `(started_at, exec_id)` fallback). (3) The `head_unknown` flag has a crisp rule — set when the resolved head lacks a back-link **and** participates in a continue-as-new chain **and** is not a confirmed origin (`head_lacks_backlink && head_participates_in_can && !confirmed_origin`), and additionally set when the resolved head declares a predecessor that is missing from the gathered set (e.g. a retention-pruned origin, from the correctness review). (4) **Graceful legacy degradation (AC5)**: pre-feature runs (which have no back-link columns populated) are forward-walked via the existing `WorkflowContinuedAsNew` events and the head is flagged `head_unknown: true` rather than ever returning a 500. **Shard-local by construction**: routing uses `db_conn_for_execution` (never `iter_shards`), and the legacy forward-walk reuses the held connection so the route is pool-size-1-safe (the #601 F4 precedent). The route is registered read-only across all four parallel plugin registries (`management_api_routes()`, request-fields, response-fields) plus `docs/api-contract.json` and the three `audit.rs` route lists (`CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` ReadOnly / `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES` `None` / `EXCLUDED_ROUTES`), with a `contract_regression` pin test guarding the classification. **No mutation, no task claims, no `WorkflowEvent` appended, no macro impact.** Out of scope (per issue): parent→child spawn lineage (#621), reset-fork tree branching (#148/#538), cross-shard fan-out, merging chain event histories, and Vantage UI chain navigation. Tests: 14 pure `run_chain` unit tests (four canonical cases plus ordering/sequence/serialization/pruned-origin), 6 plugin integration scenarios in `run_chain_integration.rs` (404 + JSON body, 400 malformed id, 4-run chain resolved from head/middle/tail, standalone single run, legacy `head_unknown`, partial-shard) — compile-checked in this sandbox (no Docker) and executed by CI under Postgres, per the repo's #543/#544/#601 precedent — plus CLI mapping, contract-coverage, and contract-regression pin tests. Local CI mirror green (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, 1264 no-default-features + 1659 all-features lib + 442 plugin lib + 271 CLI + 18 contract_regression); testcontainers/HTTP tests compile-checked only where Docker is unavailable. **Review hardening (post-review):** (1) `head_unknown`/`continued_to_exec_id` no longer synthesize a false continuation across a retention gap — per-execution legal hold (#747) can delete a *middle* run while a held head and tail survive, so a direct head→tail `continued_to` link is no longer fabricated across the hole and `head_unknown=true` is flagged on **any** gathered row whose `continued_from_exec_id` names a predecessor missing from the gathered set. (2) Legacy (pre-feature) chains queried from the tail or a middle run — which carry no back-link columns — reconstruct from the tail via shared `(workflow_name, workflow_id)` plus `WorkflowContinuedAsNew`-event linkage (id-reuse-safe by construction: a run sharing the `workflow_id` but pointing at a different successor is excluded; bounded by `MAX_LEGACY_CANDIDATES`, else served best-effort with `head_unknown=true`), and the candidate scan is scoped to the queried row's `shard_id` so a shared-physical-database topology never pulls another logical shard's same-id rows into the walk (shard-local by construction). Post-feature origins keep the cheap single-query fast path. (3) A non-partial `(workflow_name, workflow_id, shard_id)` index `idx_harvest_wfx_workflow_identity` backs that candidate scan — the pre-existing pair index is partial and excludes terminal `CONTINUED_AS_NEW` predecessors, exactly the rows the reconstruction needs. (4) The two additive nullable columns are `continued_from_exec_id` (immediate predecessor) and `first_exec_id` (chain origin). (5) The testcontainers `run_chain_integration` suite was wired into `ci.yml` — added to the plugin `--no-run` compile allowlist and given a dedicated Docker-backed Linux run step, mirroring the `timeline_integration` (#739) sibling.
- **Phase 3.50** (implemented): Cancellable / renewable durable timers — see issue #768. Author-controlled durable timers that can be **cancelled** and **reset** (re-armed) without leaving orphaned firings — the missing complement to the fire-once `ctx.timer`/`ctx.sleep_until` primitives, for idle-session timeouts and sliding-window debounces. New `WorkflowContext::start_timer(id, secs) -> TimerHandle<'_>` arms a durable timer via a **non-suspending bookkeeping command** (returns immediately, does not park the coroutine); `TimerHandle` exposes `cancel()`, `reset(secs)`, and `await_fire() -> HarvestResult<TimerOutcome>` (`TimerOutcome::{Fired, Cancelled}`). `ctx.cancel_timer(id)` / `ctx.reset_timer(id, secs)` are the untyped equivalents. `TimerHandle`/`TimerOutcome` re-exported from `lib.rs` and the prelude. **Design (Option C — bookkeeping arm, non-suspending):** the worker has no mixed-batch suspension (`handle_suspended_workflow` only recognizes single-shape batches), so a suspending arm could never be cancelled in-flight. Arm/cancel/reset are modelled as **bookkeeping commands** (`WorkflowCommand::ArmTimer`/`CancelTimer`, no `result_tx`), exactly like `CancelRaceLosers`/`RecordMarker`. The durable side runs in **two phases** inside the persist transaction at every persist site (sibling of `apply_race_loser_cancellations`): `worker::plan_timer_lifecycle` performs the `harvest_timers` row mutations (`ArmTimer` upserts the row and resolves a `TimerStarted` only when newly created — dedup, incl. within one batch, mirrors `persist_started_timer`; `CancelTimer` deletes the pending `fired = false` row via `queue::delete_pending_timer` and resolves `TimerCancelled`) and returns the resolved events **aligned to command indices** plus the minimum armed `fires_at`; `worker::build_suspension_events` then **interleaves** those `TimerStarted`/`TimerCancelled` events into the single suspension event batch at their `ArmTimer`/`CancelTimer` command-emission positions — exactly like `ChildWorkflowSpawnedDetached` — so `replay`'s strictly positional `match_timer_arm` sees the same order the live cycle emitted. (An earlier revision appended timer-lifecycle events at the *end* of the batch, which nd-blocked a `start_timer` + `side_effect`/`new_uuid`/`system_now` same-cycle run on first resume, since `drain_early_signals` does not skip `SideEffectRecorded`/`MarkerRecorded` and the cursor landed on them ahead of the positional timer-arm match.) A bookkeeping-only batch that armed a timer reschedules the workflow task to the armed `fires_at` (via `persist_bookkeeping_and_requeue_workflow`) so the armed timer actually wakes the workflow — unless a wake raced the park (`had_wake_requested`), in which case the task is woken now rather than deferred to the deadline. `await_fire` observes the outcome by re-arming idempotently (the durable row is deduped by `timer_id`) and parking (`park_until_dropped`); the next cycle resolves `Fired`/`Cancelled` by recorded-history order. On a **terminal cycle** an `ArmTimer` **skips only the `harvest_timers` row insert** but **still emits the `TimerStarted` event** at the `ArmTimer` command's position (via the pure `worker::terminal_arm_timer_events`), so a `start_timer`/`reset` that arms a timer and then completes in the **same** task replays deterministically. **One new `WorkflowEvent` variant** — `TimerCancelled { timer_id }`, appended at the END of the enum; adjacently-tagged serde is automatic, and pre-#768 histories deserialize unchanged. **No migration** — the `harvest_timers` row deletion is the fire-suppression mechanism, and `delete_pending_timer` (filtering `fired = false`) already existed and is race-safe; recorded-history order (`TimerFired` vs `TimerCancelled`) decides the observed outcome (AC3). **Replay (`replay.rs`):** new `match_timer_arm(id, dur)` (positional, consumes `TimerStarted` like a marker), `match_timer_cancel(id)` (forward-scan claim of `TimerCancelled`), and `match_timer_or_cancel(id) -> TimerFireMatch { Fired, Cancelled, NoMatch }`; `TimerCancelled` is a command-bearing event that can interleave into unrelated scans, so a **transparent, non-consuming** skip-arm was added to every forward scan that could step over it (`scan_activity_terminal`, `match_timer_strict`, `match_signal_or_timer`, `is_timer_started_next`, `match_signal`, `match_external_cancel`, `peek_u64_marker`, `match_saga_marker`) — leaving the event claimable by its own matcher. `TimerFireMatch` re-exported from `lib.rs`. **Non-determinism classification:** new `NonDeterminismKind::TimerCancelMismatch` (`testing.rs`) — an unconsumed `TimerCancelled` is classified precisely; a renamed timer id surfaces as the ordinary `TimerMismatch`. **Test harness (`WorkflowTestEnv`):** `ArmTimer` records `TimerStarted` + defers a `TimerFired` (idempotent re-arm no-ops); `CancelTimer` records `TimerCancelled` and retain-filters the deferred fire — so both branches are driven deterministically with no real sleep. **No worker-suspension-shape change** (arm/cancel are bookkeeping added to every `extract_*`/predicate ignore-list; `await_fire` parks with an idempotent re-arm, routed through the existing `only_bookkeeping_commands` → `persist_bookkeeping_and_requeue_workflow` path). Example `autumn-harvest/examples/cancellable_timer_sla.rs`. **Composition note:** composing an armed handle with a signal wait in one `select!`-style call is a documented follow-up — use `ctx.receive_signal_timeout` (#476) for the two-branch signal-or-deadline shape today. **Post-review hardening (Codex, PR #1010) — one P1 + three P2s (reset-interleaving / terminal-cycle family):** **P1 (worker.rs terminal persist)** the initial FINDING-6 cut passed `skip_arm_inserts = true` to `plan_timer_lifecycle`, dropping the `ArmTimer` **entirely** — a workflow that armed a timer and completed in the same task committed a terminal history with **no** `TimerStarted`, diverging strict replay; fixed by splitting the two effects (skip only the row insert, still emit the event via the pure, unit-tested `worker::terminal_arm_timer_events`). **P2 (match_timer_strict)** the `ctx.timer` fire scan skipped an interleaved `TimerCancelled` but stopped on the reset's paired `TimerStarted` → `TimerStarted` added to the transparent skip branch. **P2 (match_signal)** a `wait_for_signal` polled before a same-cycle `reset()` stopped on the re-arm → `TimerStarted` added to the transparent branch. **P2 (reset.rs `apply_event_to_pending`)** the pending-side-effect scan inserted on `TimerStarted` and closed only on `TimerFired` → a `TimerCancelled` now closes the pending arm. **Symmetry audit:** every forward-scan loop transparent to an interleaved `TimerCancelled` must also be transparent to the reset's paired `TimerStarted`; `scan_activity_terminal`/`peek_u64_marker`/`match_external_cancel`/`ctx.race()` scan already handled both; `match_timer_strict`/`match_signal` fixed; `match_saga_marker` got `TimerStarted` added; `scan_local_activity_terminal` got both added (closing the same class for a reset interleaved with a *retrying local activity*); `match_timer_or_cancel`/`match_child_workflow` already transparent; `is_timer_started_next` legitimately stops at `TimerStarted`. **Round 2 (Codex 3× P2):** **(context.rs `await_timer_fire`)** same-cycle cancel-then-await re-armed a cancelled timer — fixed with a per-context logical timer-lifecycle map (`cancellable_timer_state: HashMap<timer_id, Armed|Cancelled>`): `await_fire` consults recorded history first (`match_timer_or_cancel`) and only on `NoMatch` falls back to the logical state, resolving `Cancelled` without re-arming. **(testing.rs)** an armed timer fired during a mixed non-timer suspension — fixed by gating the deferred `TimerFired` on a new `is_competing_suspension` check. **(worker.rs history hard-cap preflight)** timer-lifecycle events uncounted near `event_hard_cap` — fixed with the new pure `worker::timer_lifecycle_event_count` folded into `pre_suspension_event_count`. **Round 3 (Codex 2× P2):** **(context.rs `start_timer`)** a duplicate ACTIVE `start_timer` diverged on replay — fixed by making a duplicate arm of an already-`Armed` id a true idempotent no-op (no second `match_timer_arm`, no second `ArmTimer`); new helper `timer_logically_armed`. **(testing.rs)** an already-armed timer never fired on a later bookkeeping-only `await_fire` — fixed by splitting the `already_armed` guard so an `ArmTimer` for a timer already active in *history* fires on a bookkeeping-only batch. **Round 4 (Codex 2× P2) + semantic clarification** — a cancellable timer's deadline is now measured from when it is **awaited** (`await_fire`), not from `start_timer`; arming records only `TimerStarted` and inserts no row, the row is created at `await_fire`. **(worker.rs `plan_timer_lifecycle`)** an armed-but-unawaited timer fired spuriously and broke a later `reset()`/replay — fixed by inserting the row only on the `await_fire` path via a new `for_await: bool` field on `WorkflowCommand::ArmTimer` (renamed the emission helper to `arm_timer_events`, used on all paths; the previous `skip_arm_inserts` flag subsumed and removed). **(worker.rs `persist_started_timer`)** a classic `ctx.timer` re-using a just-cancelled cancellable id could reschedule to a deleted row — fixed defensively by moving the classic timer's `existing`/`is_new`/`fires_at` resolution into the transaction after `plan_timer_lifecycle`. **Round 5 (Codex 2× P2):** **(context.rs `start_timer`)** a duplicate ACTIVE `start_timer` with a DIFFERENT duration silently changed the live deadline — fixed by carrying the recorded duration in `TimerLogicalState::Armed(u64)` (a duplicate active `start_timer(id, new_dur)` returns a handle preserving the RECORDED duration and ignores `new_dur`; a genuine change goes through `reset`). **(replay.rs `match_timer_or_cancel`)** the `await_fire` timer-outcome scan crossed intervening command events (replay-soundness false-negative) — fixed by making the crossable set EXPLICIT (only `is_consumed` events plus a bounded allowlist of genuinely transparent/interleaved events), STOPPING at any UNCONSUMED command-bearing event not on the allowlist. **Round 6 (Codex 2× P2):** **(replay.rs `match_timer_cancel`)** the cancel scan crossed intervening command events — fixed by sharing `match_timer_or_cancel`'s exact crossable set via the new `HistoryMatcher::timer_scan_cross_or_stop` helper; `cancel_timer`/`reset_timer` now surface the resulting `NoMatch` in strict replay via `check_strict_replay_no_match`. **(context.rs `await_timer_fire`)** the `Armed` logical state was not cleared when a fire was consumed, so a loop reusing the timer id lost its fresh arm — fixed by clearing the logical state (`clear_timer_logical_state`) on a consumed fire (the `Cancelled` path is deliberately NOT cleared). **Timer-matcher lifecycle audit** closes the scan-past-a-command class across all four timer replay matchers. **Round 7 (Codex 2× P2) + a completeness pass:** **(worker.rs `plan_timer_lifecycle`)** an `await_fire` raced by a same-task `cancel` rescheduled the parked task to a deleted row instead of waking now — fixed by excluding any id cancelled in the same batch from `min_fires_at` via the pure, unit-testable `plan_timer_lifecycle_pure(commands) -> (events_by_index, armed_indices)`. **(timeline.rs `derive_timeline`)** cancelled/reset timers were left open forever, distorting the rollup — fixed by adding a `TimerCancelled` arm that closes the OLDEST still-open step for that id as `StepOutcome::Cancelled` (FIFO-by-id pairing). **Timer-event-consumer audit (closing the class):** every consumer outside the already-fixed `replay.rs` matchers and worker persist path was checked for `TimerCancelled`-handling completeness — `replay.rs` matchers already fixed (rounds 5/6); `worker.rs` `plan_timer_lifecycle` FIX A this round; `timeline.rs` `derive_timeline` FIX B this round; `history_export.rs` already handles it (payload-field filter + human-label match); `reset.rs` `rebuild_pending` already handles it (`TimerFired | TimerCancelled` resolve identically, with a test); `autumn-harvest-plugin/src/ui.rs` `human_label` had a cosmetic gap → FIX C this round (added "Timer cancelled"); `analyzer.rs` `SuspiciousTimerRule` inspects individual `TimerStarted { duration_secs }` only (no change); `context.rs` already handles it; `testing.rs` `WorkflowTestEnv` `final_now()` sums `TimerStarted` incl. cancelled (test-harness virtual clock, deliberate — revised in round 8); `simulator.rs` never emits cancels (revised in round 14); `store.rs`/`erase.rs`/`executor.rs` are test fixtures / event-type-name only. **Round 8 (Codex 2× P2) — duration/clock accounting:** **FIX A (`context.rs await_timer_fire`)** used the awaiting handle's stale cached duration — now reads the CURRENT armed duration from the logical state map (`timer_logically_armed`) for both the live deadline and `advance_timer_clock`. **FIX B (`testing.rs` `final_now`/`elapsed`)** the virtual clock counted non-fired arms — new pure `fired_timer_duration_secs(events)` sums only `TimerStarted`s paired with a matching `TimerFired` (per id, FIFO; a `TimerCancelled` discards the earliest pending arm uncounted). **Round 9 (Codex 1× P2)** reset-then-await in one task must arm the durable row in the transaction that recorded the reset — `plan_timer_lifecycle_pure`'s contribution rule is now order-sensitive (a `for_await: true` arm for id X contributes iff the last establish/cancel op for X is not a trailing cancel), satisfying both reset-then-await and cancel-then-await shapes with one rule. **Round 10 (Codex 2× P2):** **Fix B (replay.rs)** the timer outcome/cancel scans now stop at an UNCONSUMED SAME-id `TimerStarted` — `timer_scan_cross_or_stop` is now **id-aware** (only a FOREIGN-id `TimerStarted`/`TimerCancelled` stays crossable). **Fix A (reset boundary scanner) DEFERRED pending maintainer decision** — a lazy cancellable arm records a `TimerStarted` without a durable row, yet `reset.rs::apply_event_to_pending` treats every open `TimerStarted` as unresolved; the correct history-based fix is an additive `cancellable: bool` field on `TimerStarted`, deferred (breaks ~109 exhaustive-binding sites); SAFE (refuses valid resets, never a wrong fork), left as a documented known limitation. **Round 11 (Codex 1× P2)** `plan_timer_lifecycle` contributes a firing row for a `for_await: true` arm only when no same-id `CancelTimer` follows it in the batch (forward) AND the timer is not sitting cancelled-without-reset before it (backward, round 9) — replacing round 10's end-of-batch-liveness rule, which was wrong for an `await_fire()` polled BEFORE a sibling `reset()` in the same task (armed a firing row off the stale await duration). **Round 12 (Codex 1× P2)** a blocked cancellable-timer scan (stopped at an unconsumed command with the recorded `TimerCancelled`/`TimerFired` still ahead) is now treated as a non-determinism divergence in NORMAL worker replay too (via `HistoryMatcher::timer_scan_stopped_at_command()`), not only under strict `WorkflowReplayer` mode — closing a silent-corruption path where issue #603 should have nd-blocked. **Round 13 (regression fix)** round 7 made `match_signal` skip interleaved timer events unconditionally, so a `wait_for_signal` over a history with a STRAY unconsumed `TimerStarted` and NO matching signal ran off the end and parked forever instead of nd-blocking — fixed by making `match_signal` diverge (not swallow to `NoMatch`) when the scan reaches end-of-history after crossing one or more UNCONSUMED interleaved timer/detached-spawn commands; an already-consumed reset's timers still suspend correctly. **Round 14 (Codex 2× P2):** **Fix 1 (`simulator.rs`)** `WorkflowSimulator` now handles `ArmTimer`/`CancelTimer` (previously fell through the wildcard arm → deadlock/omitted events), mirroring `WorkflowTestEnv`. **Fix 2 (`replay.rs`)** foreign (sibling) `TimerFired` is crossable in the timer outcome scan (`tokio::join!(slow.await_fire(), fast.await_fire())` no longer diverges) while a SAME-id `TimerFired` stays the target/anchor and a genuine command still stops the scan. **Command-consumer audit** re-confirmed `ArmTimer`/`CancelTimer` handling across `worker.rs`/`testing.rs`/`context.rs`/`executor.rs`; `simulator.rs` was the sole gap. **Round 15 (Codex 2× P2):** same-id collision across the two timer APIs now fails fast (was: silent event drop → replay corruption) — `WorkflowContext::timer` returns a clear `HarvestError::Config` when `timer_id` is held by a LIVE, un-cancelled cancellable timer (state `Armed`), before pushing any `StartTimer`; a defensive persist-time guard `same_batch_uncancelled_arm_start_collision` backs it. And `WorkflowTestEnv` now fires concurrent awaited timers in DEADLINE order (was: poll/command order). **Round 16 (Codex 3× P2):** **Findings 1 & 2 — comprehensive bidirectional, order-independent namespace disjointness** (enforced at the source in `WorkflowContext`): a given `timer_id` belongs to at most ONE timer API per run — `classic_timer_ids` set populated by `ctx.timer`/`sleep_until`; `start_timer(id)` records a deterministic deferred nd error (→ #603) when `id` is already a classic timer id (reverse of round 15's cancellable-first rejection), the worker backstop scans the WHOLE batch, and `cancel_timer(id)`/`reset_timer(id)` are pure NO-OPs when `id` is a classic timer id (so `delete_pending_timer` can never delete a classic `ctx.timer` row out from under its parked waiter). **Finding 3 — concurrently-armed timers advance the test clock to the MAX deadline, not the SUM** (test-harness fidelity only) — each cancellable arm records a deadline anchor (`TimerLogicalState::Armed { anchor_secs }`) and the clock advances to `anchor + duration` via a monotonic `fetch_max`; concurrently-armed timers share an anchor → MAX, sequential timers still SUM. All fixes: no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration. Falsifiable success bar `reset_1000_times_replays_with_bounded_history` (1000 GENUINELY DISTINCT fixtures, every third interleaving a same-cycle `new_uuid()` side effect; plain fixtures pin 2 events/reset, interleaved 3 events/reset; all `ReplaySucceeded`, all ≤1 `TimerFired`), plus the full Armed/Cancelled logical-state matrix fixture-covered.
- **Phase 3.52** (implemented): Handler-panic containment at the dispatch boundary — see issue #782. Before, a `panic!()` in a `#[workflow]` or `#[activity]` handler body (a stray `unwrap()` on `None`, an out-of-bounds index, an arithmetic overflow) was **not** contained: the handler runs inside a fire-and-forget spawned tokio task, so the panic unwound past the DB state-transition boundary without ever reaching the completion/failure code and left the `harvest_task_queue` row stuck `RUNNING`. Because the worker *process* survives (the panic is isolated to one async task), the poison-pill reclaimer (#367) — which only reclaims rows whose worker has **no live heartbeat** — never touched it, so an un-timed workflow task could sit `RUNNING` indefinitely and the eventual operator signal (a DLQ `PoisonPill` entry / consumed `crash_strikes`) told the wrong story for an ordinary code bug. Now the panic is caught at the dispatch boundary via `catch_unwind` and routed into the engine's existing clean failure paths, the same way returning `Err` does; the worker process stays up and the task leaves `RUNNING` within one poll interval. **Activity / local-activity panic** → converted to a retryable typed `ActivityFailed` (`error_type = "HandlerPanic"`, panic message captured as the failure detail) that follows the activity's **existing retry policy**, then fails terminally — no DLQ row, `crash_strikes` never consumed. **Workflow-body panic** → caught in the executor and surfaced through a new internal `WorkflowOutcome::Failed { handler_panic }` flag into a bounded, configurable panic-retry gate in `process_workflow_task` (an in-process per-execution strike map + capped-exponential backoff); after the budget is exhausted the execution fails terminally via the existing `WorkflowFailed` event (`error_type = "HandlerPanic"`); budget `WorkerConfig::workflow_panic_max_attempts` (default **3**; `0` = terminal on first panic); #523 workflow-level retry is explicitly skipped for a panic terminal so a panicking workflow is not double-retried. **Two panic-distinct counters** for alerting on handler-panic rate separately from process-crash quarantine: `harvest.activity.panic` (labels `activity`, `queue`) and `harvest.workflow.panic` (labels `workflow`, `queue`), each getting a panel under the "Handler panics" row of `docs/dashboards/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json`, catalogued in `docs/telemetry.md` and ADR-0001 §7, and enforced by the anti-drift `dashboard_pack_docs.rs` coverage gate (`execution.id` stays span-only). **Determinism preserved**: a workflow-body panic is treated like any other workflow-task failure on replay. **Documented caveats surfaced by review:** the inline-append-before-terminal limitation is inherited from the ND-block work (#603), not introduced here (a workflow-body panic re-dispatches under the panic-retry budget, so a hotfix that changes replay-relevant history *structure* before an already-committed inline event may re-diverge that in-flight run into a non-determinism *block* rather than data corruption; the common case — fixing the panicking line without reordering — replays cleanly and resumes); **containment requires `panic = "unwind"`** (a binary compiled with `panic = "abort"` aborts the process instead, so the stuck-`RUNNING` row is recovered by the poison-pill reclaimer's missing-heartbeat path); a **repeatedly-panicking activity trips its circuit breaker (#369) exactly like a repeated `Err(String)`, by design**. **Post-review hardening (Codex bot, PR #1012): contain panics during future *construction*, not just poll.** The initial `catch_unwind` boundaries wrapped only the *future* returned by a handler, but a handler `fn` is *called* (constructed) first — so synchronous work a hand-written `WorkflowInfo`/`ActivityInfo` handler does before returning its `Box::pin(...)` future still unwound the spawned worker task uncaught, bypassing the `HandlerPanic` conversion, the panic metric, and leaving the task on the old `RUNNING`/poison-pill path. (Macro-generated `#[workflow]`/`#[activity]` handlers can't hit this; the public `handler` fields and `WorkflowReplayer::register_fn` are a supported hand-written surface.) Closed uniformly by wrapping the synchronous handler *call* itself in `catch_unwind` (new `pub(crate) crate::error::catch_construct`) at every invocation site — activity (`worker.rs`), local activity (`worker.rs`), the shared workflow drive/strict/canary cycle (`executor::run_workflow_handler_cycle`), and both query-replay drives (`executor::drive_query_replay`, `handle::execute_query_in_process`); a construction panic maps to the same contained path as a poll panic. `AssertUnwindSafe` is sound — on a construction panic the future is never produced and the borrowed context is dropped without reuse. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant and no migration** — contained panics reuse the existing `ActivityFailed` / `WorkflowFailed` events, preserving the append-only invariant. Files: `builder.rs`, `executor.rs`, `failure.rs`, `metrics_rs_adapter.rs`, `queue.rs`, `telemetry.rs`, `testing.rs`, `worker.rs`, plus the new `tests/integration/panic_containment_tests.rs` (and a one-line `workflow_panic_max_attempts` field added to the `WorkerRuntimeConfig` literals across ~14 existing integration-test files). Tests: `catch_construct` unit tests (`error.rs`), a construction-panic workflow unit test (`executor.rs`), a construction-panic query-replay test (`query_terminal_tests.rs`), an activity construction-panic envelope test (`worker.rs`), and 4 integration tests in `panic_containment_tests.rs` (`activity_handler_panic_is_contained_and_retried_then_terminal`, `local_activity_handler_panic_is_contained_and_retried_then_terminal`, `workflow_handler_panic_is_re_dispatched_then_terminal_within_budget`, `workflow_panic_max_attempts_zero_is_terminal_on_first_panic`) asserting the worker process stays up, the task leaves `RUNNING` within a poll interval, activities retry per policy, the workflow fails terminally after the bounded budget, and no spurious crash-strike / poison-pill entry — run against a real local Postgres 16; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest --all-features --tests -- -D warnings`, and the 1704 library unit tests green locally. Out of scope (per issue): unbounded retry-the-workflow-task-forever mode, any change to poison-pill process-crash semantics (#367), hung/infinite-loop detection (#494/#703), operator force-fail (#765).
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Tiered / summary retention — see issue #752. When the history-retention janitor (issue #737) hard-deletes a terminal execution, it can now optionally **demote** it into a compact, queryable `harvest_execution_summaries` row instead of losing all trace of the run — a "tiered" retention policy where full histories expire on one horizon and lightweight summaries live (far longer, or forever) on a second, decoupled horizon; the summary answers "did this run exist, when, and what did it produce?" in one management-API call at ~<1 KB/execution, long after the event log is gone. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no replay impact** — a summary is a retention-time projection of terminal state, never part of the append-only event contract (AC8). **Configuration (AC1):** new `RetentionConfig.summary: Option<SummaryPolicy>` (`policy.rs`/`retention.rs`); `None` (default) is byte-for-byte identical to pre-#752 behavior (hard delete, no summary). `SummaryPolicy { retention: SummaryRetention, capture_payload: bool, max_payload_bytes: usize }` with `SummaryRetention::{For(Duration), Unbounded}`; builders `SummaryPolicy::for_days(u64)`/`::for_duration(Duration)`/`::unbounded()`, chained `.with_payload_capture()`/`.with_max_payload_bytes(usize)`, and on `RetentionConfig` `with_summary_retention(...)`/`with_summary_retention_days(u64)`/`with_summary_retention_unbounded()`; default payload cap `DEFAULT_SUMMARY_PAYLOAD_CAP` = 4 KiB; `validate()` bounds the summary horizon by the same `[MIN_MAX_AGE, MAX_MAX_AGE]` range as `max_age`; `enabled()` returns `true` for an overrides-only or summary-only config. **Atomic demotion in the delete transaction (AC2/AC7):** summarization happens inside `delete_candidate_execution`'s existing `FOR UPDATE` transaction, *after* the #747 legal-hold re-check and *before* the execution-row delete (the select is widened to fetch `output`/`error`/`search_attrs`/timing/shard/identity/state); the `INSERT` (with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`) is atomic with the delete — no window where both the execution and its summary are absent, and a rolled-back delete leaves no orphan summary; a legally-held execution is never summarized until released; summary disabled ⇒ no `INSERT`. **Opt-in capped payload with typed markers (AC3):** captured `result`/`error` payloads are opt-in (default off ⇒ identity + timing + search-attrs only) and byte-bounded; pure helpers `cap_result_payload`/`cap_error_text` store the value **verbatim** (codec-encoded form preserved, matching history-export *Full*) except an offload reference envelope (#524) becomes `{"_harvest_omitted": true, "reason": "offloaded"}` (never store a blob ref whose backing blob may be GC'd out from under the summary), an oversized value becomes `{"_harvest_omitted": true, "reason": "too_large", "bytes": N}`, and oversized error text becomes `[omitted: too_large, N bytes]`. Migration `20260710000001_harvest_execution_summaries` adds the table (`execution_id` PK, `workflow_name`/`workflow_id`/`state`, `started_at`/`completed_at`/`duration_ms`, `shard_id`, `search_attrs` JSONB, `result` JSONB, `error` TEXT, `parent_id` UUID, `summarized_at`) with a `(completed_at, execution_id)` GC/keyset index, a `(workflow_name, completed_at DESC)` filter index, a GIN index on `search_attrs`, and a partial `(parent_id) WHERE parent_id IS NOT NULL` index for the erase cascade. **Codec caveat:** the summary stores the `output`/`search_attrs` *columns* verbatim (the same codec-encoded columns #608 decodes on read), so encryption-at-rest is preserved. **Horizon caveat:** the summary horizon should exceed the history horizon to be useful (a bounded summary window at or below the history window means the summary is GC'd almost immediately); `RetentionRuntime::spawn` logs a one-time non-fatal warn when a bounded `summary_age() <= max_age()`. **Read-only list route (AC4):** new admin-guarded `GET /api/harvest/workflows/summaries` (handler `list_workflow_summaries`), registered **before** `/workflows/{id}` (per the #544 precedent) so axum does not capture `summaries` as a path param; filters mirror `GET /workflows` (`workflow_name`, `workflow_id`, `state` repeatable/CSV, `completed_after`/`completed_before` RFC 3339, `search_attr` repeatable `key:value` JSONB containment, and `order=asc|desc` default `desc` — any other value → `400`), same keyset-cursor pagination keyed on `(completed_at, execution_id)` (`limit` default 50 / max 500); cross-shard fan-out + k-way merge via `retention::list_execution_summaries` + `load_summaries_from_shards`; each item carries the summary columns plus `summarized: true` and `history_available: false`;
