Fixed by adding `execution_timeout`/`deadline_at` to the `db`-gated `CandidateExecution` `QueryableByName` struct (`Nullable<Interval>` → `Option<chrono::Duration>`, `Nullable<Timestamptz>` → `Option<DateTime<Utc>>`), SELECTing both columns in both candidate-query string variants (the WHERE-clause bind numbering is untouched — the SELECT column list is independent of it), and populating `req.execution_timeout = candidate.execution_timeout` / `req.deadline_at = candidate.deadline_at`. **(B) Batch history export (`autumn-harvest-plugin/src/api.rs`, Codex Finding B).** `GET /admin/history/exports` builds each candidate's document via `export_history_for_candidate`, which hardcoded `execution_timeout: None, deadline_at: None` because `HistoryExportCandidate`/`HISTORY_EXPORT_CANDIDATES_SQL` did not select those columns — so every batch export dropped the deadline budget even though the single-execution export already carried it. Fixed by adding `execution_timeout`/`deadline_at` to the `HistoryExportCandidate` `QueryableByName` struct, SELECTing `w.execution_timeout`/`w.deadline_at` (and adding them to the `GROUP BY`, harmless since they are functionally dependent on the grouped PK `w.id`) in `HISTORY_EXPORT_CANDIDATES_SQL`, and populating `execution_timeout: candidate.execution_timeout` / `deadline_at: candidate.deadline_at` in `export_history_for_candidate`. **Comprehensive closure of the deadline-threading theme.** With rounds 6–8 the entire producer/consumer surface is threaded; the theme is closed. - **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Admission gate authoritative across all workflow-start producers — see issue #618. **Make the admission gate authoritative across all workflow-start producers** (implemented) — see issue #618. The admission gate (#377) lets an incident operator halt new workflow starts fleet-wide or by name/queue/shard/owner while in-flight work drains, but it was **not** authoritative: three in-process producers started workflows without consulting it. It is now either gated or **explicitly, observably exempt** on every in-process producer. New bounded `admission_gate::StartProducer` enum (`Api`/`BatchStart`/`CompletionTrigger`/`WebhookDelegate`/`Scheduler`/`Debounce`/`Throttle`/`Outbox`, `as_str()` + `ALL`) plus the discoverable `producer_contract()` (`ProducerContractEntry { producer, status: ProducerGateStatus::{Gated, ExemptByDesign}, rationale }`). **Completion triggers (AC1) — the main gap, now closed:** `completion_trigger::evaluate_triggers_for_execution` reaches the shared `AdmissionGateCache` through a new process-global `GLOBAL_ADMISSION_GATE_CACHE` static (mirroring `GLOBAL_WORKFLOW_METADATA`/`GLOBAL_CALLBACK_CONFIG`), published by the plugin at boot with the **same `Arc`** the management API and background refresh loop use — so no cache is threaded through the ~17 call sites and gate creates/lifts propagate automatically. The gate is checked **inside the source workflow's terminal-commit transaction**, before the fires-row insert, evaluating every scope (routing + owner resolved up-front). A block is a **clean skip that never rolls back the source terminal** (mirroring the #810 `condition_unmet` resolved-skip shape): it records `record_admission_blocked` (the *same* `AdmissionBlocked` outcome a direct API start records) and writes an exactly-once resolved-skip row in `harvest_completion_trigger_fires` with the new `outcome = 'admission_blocked'` through the existing `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` PK path, so cascade re-entry dedupes it and this terminal never retries the start. A blocked completion-trigger start is therefore **dropped, not deferred** — identically to a direct API start being refused during an incident. When no gate cache is installed (standalone integrations, or the plugin's brief boot window) the check is skipped and behaviour is **byte-identical to pre-#618** (no extra DB read on the no-gate path). **Webhook delegate (AC2):** the inbound webhook receiver (#344) delegates `Starts`/`SignalsWithStart` straight to `api::start_workflow`/`signal_with_start_workflow`, which already check the gate — so a scoped gate blocks a matching webhook-triggered start and lets a non-matching one through, by construction. **Outbox relay (AC3) — exempt-by-design + observable:** `outbox::dispatch_workflow_start_request` relays workflow-start requests durably committed *before* any gate was raised; gating them would drop already-accepted in-flight work (the opposite of the gate contract, "halt **new** starts while in-flight work drains"). It is left un-gated but now increments the new `harvest.admission.bypassed{producer="outbox"}` counter on every relayed start so the exemption is never silent. **New metric (AC4)** via the standard 3-touchpoint recipe: `METRIC_ADMISSION_BYPASSED = "harvest.admission.bypassed"` + `METRIC_LABEL_PRODUCER = "producer"` (telemetry.rs), a no-op-default `MetricsRecorder::record_admission_bypassed(producer)` trait method, and the `metrics_rs_adapter` bridge (`execution.id` is never a label, ADR-0001 §7). **Discoverable contract (AC5):** `GET /admin/gates` now returns a `producers` block alongside `gates` listing each producer's `gated`/`exempt_by_design` status and rationale, so the contract is discoverable without reading source; documented in `docs/operations/admission-gate-producers.md` and `docs/api-contract.json`. **Known-gaps note removed (AC6):** the stale "Known gaps — ungated workflow producers" comment in `src/admission_gate.rs` is replaced by a "Start-producer contract" section since all three gaps are resolved. Scheduler already gated (`scheduler.rs` `check_admission`); debounce/throttle are gated at admission time on the HTTP start route (their scanners only relay already-admitted work), so they are classified `gated` in the contract. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no change to event JSON tagging, NO migration, no `::autumn_harvest::` macro-path change (AC7)** — the `admission_blocked` outcome reuses the existing nullable `harvest_completion_trigger_fires.outcome TEXT` column from #810; the gate cache is an in-process static; the whole change is start-path policy resolution + telemetry + a read-only API field. **Success metric:** with a `Fleet` gate raised, 100% of workflow-start attempts across the in-process producers this PR touches (API start, completion trigger, outbox) are either blocked-and-counted or bypassed-and-counted — measured by the `fleet_gate_leaves_zero_uncounted_admissions` integration test, which drives all three with a gate active, asserts exactly one target execution (the exempt outbox one) is created, and asserts every start attempt landed in either the blocked or the bypassed counter (zero un-counted admissions), verified against a shared `CapturingMetrics` recorder. **Tests, TDD red→green:** core unit tests in `admission_gate.rs` (`StartProducer::as_str` bounded/unique, `producer_contract` covers every producer + outbox exempt, `GLOBAL_ADMISSION_GATE_CACHE` set/get shared-Arc round-trip), `telemetry.rs` (constant name + no-op default), `metrics_rs_adapter.rs` (bridge does-not-panic); core DB integration `autumn-harvest/tests/integration/admission_gate_authoritative_tests.rs` (Fleet gate blocks a completion-trigger start with the block counted + `admission_blocked` fires row + source terminal not rolled back; no-gate-cache backward compat starts the target with a NULL-outcome fire; scoped `WorkflowName` gate match blocks / miss proceeds); plugin HTTP+outbox integration `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/admission_gate_authoritative_localpg.rs` (`GET /admin/gates` producer contract; outbox relay exempt + bypass counted under a live Fleet gate; scoped gate blocks/passes the start route the webhook delegate forwards to; the zero-un-counted-admissions success-metric test). **All DB/HTTP tests were actually executed against a real local Postgres 16** (the core `admission_gate_authoritative` suite via `HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL` and the plugin `admission_gate_authoritative_localpg` suite over the real axum router + real outbox relay), not merely compile-checked. Out of scope (per issue): new gate scopes/matching semantics, gating starts from outside the plugin process, auto-lifting/scheduling gates, rate-limited recovery replay. **Post-review hardening (four-reviewer pass, all fixed TDD-style):** (F1) the four deferred-fire producers that could relay a start past a gate raised *after* admission are now exempt-with-bypass-counter, mirroring the outbox: `debounce`/`throttle`/`event_batch` scanner fires and the completion-trigger **cross-shard** relay (`enforce_completion_triggers_outbox`, now threaded a `metrics` recorder from `enforce_timeouts_once`) each increment `harvest.admission.bypassed{producer=…}` with a distinct label. (F2) `StartProducer` gains `EventBatch` + `CompletionTriggerOutbox` variants (now 10), and `ProducerGateStatus` gains a `GatedAtAdmission` variant so the contract distinguishes the deferred-fire producers' split behaviour (gated at HTTP admission; scanner fire exempt-with-counter) from a flat `gated`. (F3) `AdmissionGateCache::check()`'s fail-closed sentinel (`Uuid::nil()`, now single-sourced via `admission_gate::sentinel_gate_id()`) no longer permanently drops a completion-trigger start on a transient gate-DB blip: the completion-trigger path distinguishes the sentinel from a real operator gate and **proceeds** (no block, no fires row, no count) rather than dropping already-committed in-flight continuation; a real gate still blocks + drops + counts. (F4) the `admission_blocked` block is counted exactly once — the fires-row `inserted` count now gates the `record_admission_blocked` call, and cascade re-entry records a `deduped` outcome instead of a second block. (F5) `set_global_admission_gate_cache` warns on a divergent re-publish, and `stop_harvest_runtime` clears the global (ptr-eq guarded so a stopping plugin never clobbers a live sibling's cache). (F9) the target queue is resolved at most once on the gate-present completion-trigger path. (F10) the global-cache accessor/setter recover a poisoned lock (`into_inner`) rather than failing to `None`. (F11) the global cache is published *before* `HarvestRunner::start` spawns the workers/scanners (safe now that F3 makes a boot-window fail-closed sentinel proceed). (F12) the event-batch HTTP gate pre-check's bounded TOCTOU window is documented (it shares the debounce path's non-atomic check-then-admit shape); a start that slips it is durably deferred and its scanner fire is counted as a bypass, so no un-counted admission results. (F13) the module docs and `docs/operations/admission-gate-producers.md` gain an explicit **out-of-scope — in-flight continuation** section (workflow-level retry #523, continue-as-new, child/detached-child spawn, reset forks, in-process client handle), and the ops doc is linked from `docs/runbooks/contain-runaway-execution.md` and `docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md`. **Deferred (noted, not fixed):** a completion-trigger evaluation on the cancel/terminate path passes `metrics: None`, so a block there is gated-but-uncounted (pre-existing `None`-passing pattern; correctness unaffected). **F6:** the `fleet_gate_leaves_zero_uncounted_admissions` success-metric test now drives all seven in-process producers (API + completion-trigger blocked-and-counted; outbox + CT cross-shard relay + debounce + throttle + event-batch bypassed-and-counted) under a live Fleet gate and asserts zero un-counted admissions; the plugin local-PG suite is dual-mode (`HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL` preferred, testcontainers fallback) and runs Docker-backed in CI. New core DB tests cover the F3 sentinel-proceeds and F4 no-double-count paths. All DB/HTTP suites executed against a real local Postgres 16. **Post-review hardening, round 3 (two Codex findings on commit `956178c`):** (F1, P1 — `plugin.rs` boot ordering) the F11 change published the gate-cache `Arc` to the process-global static *before* `HarvestRunner::start` spawned the workers/scanners, but the boot-time `load_active_gates` that populates the snapshot ran **after** the runner started — so a scanner tick or completion trigger firing in the startup window ran `check_cached()` against an EMPTY snapshot and PROCEEDED, bypassing persisted Fleet/queue/name gates uncounted at boot. Fixed by reordering `start_harvest_runtime`: the boot-time `load_active_gates` → `refresh` now runs on `harvest_pool` **before** it is moved into `runner_resources` — i.e. before the cache is published to the global and before the runner spawns — so the published `Arc` (and the one workers see) already carries the persisted gates. A genuine gate-DB outage at boot is unchanged: the snapshot stays empty and completion triggers proceed (the same bounded caveat as a mid-run fail-closed with no cached match), never converted into a permanent block-drop; the direct HTTP start path still fails closed via `check()`. (F2, P2 — `completion_trigger.rs` cross-shard queue resolution) for a cross-shard trigger (target hashing to a shard other than the source's, no explicit trigger queue), the inline gate check called `resolve_target_queue(conn, …)` on the SOURCE transaction connection — which for a `target_shard == 0` target queries the source shard's `harvest_schedules`, missing the target's schedule and falling back to the default queue, so a `Queue(q)` gate scoped to the real target queue was MISSED (and the outbox relay, which resolves the real queue on the target connection at fire time, is exempt-with-counter, so nothing downstream caught it). Fixed with the new `pub` `completion_trigger::resolve_cross_shard_target_queue`, which — for a cross-shard target — resolves the queue on the **target shard's** connection (mirroring how `enforce_completion_triggers_outbox` resolves it at fire time), falling back to the source connection only when the target-shard pool is unavailable (Fleet/name gates still match; only a Queue gate could be missed in that unreachable-pool edge). Same-shard targets keep the single-connection (no extra DB read) path. Tests, TDD red→green: `boot_load_of_persisted_gate_blocks_completion_trigger` (persist a Fleet gate, run the exact `load_active_gates` → `refresh` boot-load path, evaluate a matching trigger → blocked + counted + `admission_blocked` fires row — the behavioural guarantee the reordering provides; the private-`start_harvest_runtime` ordering itself is verified by code reading); `cross_shard_gate_check_resolves_target_queue_on_target_shard` (a genuine two-database multi-shard setup — shard 0/target owns the `ag_target_wf -> ag_priority_q` schedule, shard 1/source does not — proving `resolve_cross_shard_target_queue` resolves on the target shard where the pre-fix `resolve_target_queue(source_conn, …)` missed it; needs only `harvest_schedules`, so it runs against a fresh `INIT_SQL` DB). Both new tests plus the full core suite (9/9) and the plugin `admission_gate_authoritative_localpg` suite (4/4) executed green against a real local Postgres 16. **CI-correctness gap fixed in round 4 (below):** the suite's curated `INIT_SQL` was incomplete for `start_or_load`, so its Docker-backed CI step would have failed; round 4 replaces it with the full migration set. **Post-review hardening, round 4 (three items in one pass — CI-correctness gap + two more Codex findings on `90f4f76`):** **(INIT_SQL — CI-correctness, the actual merge-blocker for this new suite.)** The suite is new in this PR, so its `INIT_SQL` const IS this PR's code, and the "Docker-backed admission-gate authoritative" CI step boots a fresh Postgres seeded from ONLY that const (no `HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, no Postgres service, no `diesel migration run` anywhere in `ci.yml` — verified). The curated const omitted `harvest_build_policies`/`harvest_build_compat` (`build_routing`) **and** — schema had drifted further — `harvest_workflow_executions.legal_hold_set_at` (a much later migration), both read by `start_or_load_workflow_execution`, so all six `start_or_load`-calling tests would panic in CI (`relation "harvest_build_policies" does not exist`, then `column ... legal_hold_set_at does not exist`). **Reproduced exactly** against a fresh DB seeded with only the const's bytes. Fixed by replacing the hand-picked subset with the **COMPLETE 72-migration set in timestamp order** (identical to `diesel migration run`) — drift-proof by construction: a hand-picked subset silently rots every time the start path gains a column read, whereas the applied superset never over-constrains a test. **Proof (the exact CI Docker reproduction):** a fresh DB seeded from ONLY the const → the ENTIRE suite runs **9/9 green**, including `deferred_scanner_fires_are_counted_as_bypass` (the test that failed distinctly on the pre-F2 code) and the new cross-shard fallback assertions. (Executed against local Postgres 16 via a TCP `HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL` matching the testcontainer URL shape — Docker/testcontainers is unavailable in this sandbox; the const's exact byte-content was independently confirmed to apply cleanly to a fresh DB with every required table/column present.) **(Finding A, P1 — the outbound webhook delegate was ungated; the "authoritative" contract was FALSE.)** There are two webhook producers: the INBOUND receiver (`webhook_receiver.rs`, already gated — it delegates to `api::start_workflow`/`signal_with_start_workflow`), and the OUTBOUND `WebhookDelegateExt` (`plugin.rs`), which started the `webhook_delivery` workflow directly via `client.start_or_load` **without consulting the gate cache** — so a Fleet/queue/workflow gate did not stop these fresh in-process starts, and they weren't counted. This is one of the three original ungated producers issue #618 names ("the Autumn webhook delegate"). Fixed by gating the outbound start: before `start_or_load`, the delegate consults `global_admission_gate_cache()` via the new tested helper `webhook_delivery_admission_block(cache, shard, owner)` (fixed match inputs `workflow_name = "webhook_delivery"`, `queue = "webhooks"`, resolved `shard`/`owner`; `check_cached` honours the last-known snapshot even under a transient fail-closed blip and never returns the sentinel). A matching gate **blocks** the start (record `record_admission_blocked` with the same `(scope_kind, reason)` the API path records, then return an error — a `webhook_delivery` start is a fresh start and the operator's gate halts new starts, so block, not exempt); a non-matching gate proceeds unchanged. The `producer_contract()` entry + module-doc table now accurately describe BOTH webhook paths as gated. The generic embedder `WorkflowHandle::start_or_load` stays out-of-scope (an embedder's own start) — only the internal webhook-delivery producer is gated. Tests (RAN under `--features webhooks`): 5 unit tests in `plugin::webhook_admission_tests` (Fleet / `WorkflowName("webhook_delivery")` / `Queue("webhooks")` gates block; a different-workflow and different-queue gate and an empty cache proceed) exercising the exact helper the delegate calls. **CI coverage closed:** the `webhooks` feature had ZERO CI steps (its receiver tests never ran; `--all-targets` clippy without the feature never even compiled the gated code), so this PR adds a `webhooks`-feature plugin clippy step and a `cargo test -p autumn-harvest-plugin --features webhooks --lib` step to `ci.yml` — otherwise the new tests would be CI-dead. The full delegate-driven start-blocking (return `Err` + record on a match) is verified by code reading, since wiring the whole `webhook_outbound` + `AppState` + DB path in a unit test is impractical. **(Finding B, P2 — F2's connection-failure fallback resolved on the wrong shard.)** F2's `resolve_cross_shard_target_queue` fell back to `resolve_target_queue(source_conn, …)` when the target-shard connection was unavailable; for `target_shard == 0` that path queries `harvest_schedules` on the connection it holds — the SOURCE connection — reintroducing the exact wrong-shard bug F2 fixed, in the connection-failure edge. Fixed by removing the `source_conn` parameter from `resolve_cross_shard_target_queue` entirely (so a wrong-shard read is now **structurally impossible** from it): on a target-shard connection failure it falls back to the shard-INDEPENDENT `default_workflow_queue()` (the process-global registered default, else `"default"`) — never the source connection. `WorkflowMetadata` carries no per-workflow queue, so the only queue answer that genuinely needs the target shard is the schedule-level override; the documented bounded double-fault edge is that a `Queue(schedule-override)` gate can be missed only while the target shard is unreachable (strictly better than returning a wrong-shard queue). Fleet/name/owner/shard gates don't depend on the queue and still evaluate correctly. `default_workflow_queue()` also single-sources the two prior inline default-queue copies in `resolve_target_queue`. Test: the `cross_shard_gate_check_resolves_target_queue_on_target_shard` test gains a fallback leg — it seeds the SOURCE shard with a WRONG `ag_target_wf -> ag_source_wrong_q` schedule, installs a sharded pool mapping ONLY shard 1 (so `exact_pool_for(0)` is None → fallback), and asserts the resolver returns `"default"`, NOT `ag_source_wrong_q` (proving it never queried the source connection's schedules) and not the unreachable target's `ag_priority_q`. All five CI-mirror checks green (fmt; core `--all-features --tests` clippy `-D warnings`; plugin `--all-targets` default/`webhooks`/`mcp`/`metrics` clippy `-D warnings`; core `admission_gate::`/`completion_trigger::` unit 43/43; plugin lib default 513/513 and `--features webhooks` 533/533) and the full core `admission_gate_authoritative` suite **9/9 against a fresh INIT_SQL-only DB**, all executed against local Postgres 16. **Post-review hardening, round 2 (Codex P1 on PR #1014):** the round-1 F3 fix over-corrected. `AdmissionGateCache::set_fail_closed()` retains the cached gates snapshot (it only flips the `initialized` flag), but the completion-trigger path collapsed *every* fail-closed result onto the nil sentinel and PROCEEDED — so a real Fleet/name/queue gate already loaded into the cache, followed by a failed refresh (fail-closed), would let completion-trigger starts BYPASS the active gate uncounted while direct API starts still blocked: a gate leak during exactly the incident the gate exists for. Fixed by adding `AdmissionGateCache::check_cached()` (runs the pure `check_admission` matcher against the current snapshot regardless of the initialized flag, returning only a REAL matching gate, never the sentinel) and rewriting the completion-trigger branch to use it: a real cached gate matching the start → block + drop + count (keeping the F4 `inserted > 0` no-double-count guard); no cached gate matches → proceed (transient-blip / boot-window case, still avoiding a permanent drop). The `sentinel_gate_id()` special-casing was removed from `completion_trigger.rs` (the helper stays — `check()` still returns it for the API block-everything path). Deliberate, documented divergence: when initialized-and-healthy the API and triggers see identical gates; under fail-closed the API blocks everything (caller retries) while triggers honour only known-cached gates (they cannot retry). Bounded caveat (documented in `docs/operations/admission-gate-producers.md`): a gate ADDED during a gate-DB outage — never loaded into the snapshot — won't block completion triggers until the next successful refresh; strictly better than either permanent-drop or unconditional-bypass. Tests, TDD red→green: new core DB `completion_trigger_fail_closed_with_cached_gate_blocks` (a real Fleet gate loaded then `set_fail_closed()` → target NOT started, `admission_blocked` counted, fires row present — confirmed FAILING against the round-1 code, then green); the former `completion_trigger_fail_closed_sentinel_proceeds` renamed to `completion_trigger_fail_closed_no_cached_gate_proceeds` (empty snapshot → proceeds); unit tests `check_cached_honours_snapshot_under_fail_closed` / `check_cached_returns_none_on_empty_snapshot`. Executed against local Postgres 16. **Post-review hardening, round 5 (two Codex P2s on `34a6ac5`):** **(Finding A, P2 — the outbound webhook delegate must fail CLOSED.)** Round-4's `webhook_delivery_admission_block` used `check_cached()`, which deliberately ignores the fail-closed/uninitialized sentinel — a semantic chosen for COMPLETION TRIGGERS (in-flight continuation of already-committed work, where a permanent drop is worse than a brief bypass). That rationale does NOT apply to an outbound `webhook_delivery` start, which is a FRESH, retryable workflow start equivalent to an HTTP API start: after a boot-time gate-load failure or a refresh outage (`check_cached` returns `None`), the webhook delivery would start while the HTTP start path fails closed and blocks — an inconsistency and an uncounted bypass. Fixed by switching the helper to the sentinel-aware `check()` (mirroring the HTTP start path): under fail-closed, `check()` returns the synthetic block → the delegate blocks the `webhook_delivery` start and records `record_admission_blocked` (as it already does for a real match). Failing closed here can never permanently drop anything (the delivery is retryable). Tests (RAN under `--features webhooks`): 2 new webhook unit tests — `uninitialized_cache_fails_closed_and_blocks` (`AdmissionGateCache::new_fail_closed()` → blocks with the `"fleet"` sentinel scope) and `set_fail_closed_reverts_to_blocking` (a populated cache reverted via `set_fail_closed()` blocks regardless of its cached gates) — plus the existing match/no-match tests and `initialized_empty_cache_lets_the_outbound_start_proceed` (an *initialized* empty cache is fail-open, so it still proceeds). **(Finding B, P2 — count completion-trigger blocks on the cancel/terminate/parent-close-cascade paths.)** A gate-blocked completion-trigger start inserts the durable `admission_blocked` fires row but emitted `harvest.admission.blocked` only inside `if let Some(m) = metrics`. The cancel/terminate/parent-close-cascade paths in `execution.rs` call `evaluate_triggers_for_execution(..., None)`, so a cancelled/terminated source with a completion trigger under an active gate was blocked-and-dropped but NEVER counted — a hole in the issue's "zero un-counted blocks" bar. **Least-invasive fix (a global recorder fallback, mirroring `GLOBAL_ADMISSION_GATE_CACHE` established earlier in this PR):** `apply_parent_close_cascade` alone has 16 callers, so threading a recorder through the cancel/terminate/cascade signatures would cascade widely; instead a new `admission_gate::GLOBAL_ADMISSION_METRICS` static (`set_global_admission_metrics`/`global_admission_metrics`, poison-recovering `into_inner` like the gate-cache global) is published by the plugin at boot with the SAME `Arc<dyn MetricsRecorder>` the workers/scanners use, and cleared on stop (ptr-eq guarded against this runtime's recorder so a stopping plugin never clobbers a live sibling's). The block-count path in `evaluate_triggers_for_execution` resolves an effective recorder = the explicit `metrics` param when supplied, else the global fallback (a tuple `match` so the `&dyn MetricsRecorder` → annotated `+ Send + Sync` coercion applies at the expression site, matching how the worker passes `registry.telemetry().metrics.as_ref()`; a plain `if let/else` tripped `clippy::nursery`'s `option_if_let_else`). Still guarded on the fires-row `blocked_inserted > 0` so cascade re-entry records `deduped` instead of double-counting — the invariant holds: a completion-trigger start blocked by an active gate is counted on `harvest.admission.blocked` **exactly once** regardless of whether the source reached terminal via completion, cancel, or terminate. This also fixes every other `None`-passing caller uniformly. Test (TDD red→green, red confirmed): `completion_trigger_block_counted_via_global_recorder_on_cancel_path` — a completion trigger on a CANCELLED source under a Fleet gate, evaluated with `metrics: None` and the recorder supplied ONLY via the global, asserts target NOT started + `admission_blocked` fires row + the capturing recorder counted exactly one block; confirmed RED (`left: 0, right: 1`) against the fallback-disabled code before the fix. Round-5 verification (all RAN, executed against local Postgres 16; Docker/testcontainers unavailable in-sandbox): fmt clean; core `--all-features --tests` clippy `-D warnings` clean; plugin `--all-targets` default + `webhooks` clippy `-D warnings` clean; core `admission_gate::`/`completion_trigger::` unit 43/43; plugin lib default 513/513 and `--features webhooks` 535/535 (incl. the 7 webhook admission tests); the full core `admission_gate_authoritative` suite **10/10 against a fresh INIT_SQL-only DB** (the 9 prior + the new Finding B test); and the plugin `admission_gate_authoritative_localpg` suite **4/4** against a fully-migrated DB (core + plugin migrations), confirming the boot-time global-recorder publish/clear does not regress plugin startup. **Post-review hardening, round 6 (one Codex P2 on `ad37cac`): count the IMMEDIATE completion-trigger outbox relay, not just the scanner.** For a cross-shard completion trigger, `evaluate_triggers_for_execution` writes an outbox row and returns a `DeferredTriggerStart`; the normal callers immediately call `DeferredTriggerStart::spawn()`, which starts the target and deletes the row on success. Round-1's `record_admission_bypassed("completion_trigger_outbox")` counter was added ONLY in the later scanner `enforce_completion_triggers_outbox` — so the COMMON successful path (the immediate `spawn()` relay) never hit the counter: a gate raised after the source commit but before the immediate relay left that intentionally-exempt start UNCOUNTED, breaking the "zero un-counted bypass" contract. Fixed by counting the bypass in `spawn()`'s `Ok(start)` arm too, via the process-global recorder (`global_admission_metrics()` — `spawn` has no explicit `metrics` param), mirroring the scanner's `record_admission_bypassed(CompletionTriggerOutbox)`. **Exactly-once (verified):** an outbox row is started by EITHER the immediate `spawn()` OR the scanner (only if the immediate spawn didn't run / failed before deleting). The immediate count is gated on the delete actually removing the row (`matches!(deleted, Ok(n) if n >= 1)`) — tightened beyond the scanner's count-on-`Ok(start)` to close the start-ok/delete-fail edge for the immediate path: if the start failed (Err arm) or the delete removed nothing, `spawn()` does NOT count and the row persists for the scanner to count once. So exactly one count per started relay across both paths, each gated on its own successful start + row removal; matches the scanner's "any successful start (incl. `AllowDuplicate` attach), not just a fresh `created`" condition. Test (TDD red→green, red confirmed): `immediate_outbox_relay_counts_the_bypass_exactly_once` — a genuine two-database multi-shard test (source shard 0 owns the outbox row, target shard 1 receives the start) inserts an outbox row, publishes a capturing recorder via the global, fires `DeferredTriggerStart::spawn()` (fire-and-forget, so it polls for completion), then asserts the target started on shard 1, the outbox row was deleted, `bypassed == ["completion_trigger_outbox"]` exactly once, AND running the scanner afterward relays 0 (row already gone) so the count stays exactly 1 (no double-count). **Red confirmed** by removing the `spawn()` count: the test fails ("the immediate spawn relay did not complete within the poll window", bypassed stays empty), then green after restoring. Round-6 verification (all RAN, local Postgres 16, Docker/testcontainers unavailable in-sandbox): fmt clean; core `--all-features --tests` clippy `-D warnings` clean; plugin `--all-targets` default + `webhooks` clippy `-D warnings` clean; core `admission_gate::`/`completion_trigger::` unit 43/43; plugin lib default 513/513 and `--features webhooks` 535/535; the full core `admission_gate_authoritative` suite **11/11 against a fresh INIT_SQL-only DB** (the 10 prior + the new immediate-relay test). **Post-review hardening, round 7 (two Codex P2s on `2411fc4`):** (Finding A, P2 — `plugin.rs`: clear the admission globals on a startup failure.) `start_harvest_runtime` published `GLOBAL_ADMISSION_GATE_CACHE` and `GLOBAL_ADMISSION_METRICS` *before* `HarvestRunner::start`; if start (or any later step) returned `Err`, the process-global statics were left pointing at a half-started runtime's `Arc`s, so a later boot attempt or an in-flight scanner saw stale gate/metrics state. Fixed with an RAII `AdmissionGlobalsGuard` that owns the published `Arc`s: on `Drop` it clears whichever globals it published, each **ptr-eq-guarded** against *this* runtime's `Arc` (so a concurrent healthy sibling's cache is never clobbered — the same guard `stop_harvest_runtime` uses); the guard is defused with `.commit()` on the success path immediately before `Ok(())`. Publishing the gate cache and the metrics recorder are two separate guard calls (`publish_gate_cache`/`publish_metrics`), so a failure *between* them clears only the gate cache and leaves the never-published metrics slot untouched. Unit tests (`admission_globals_guard_tests`, serialized on a dedicated lock): drop clears both; drop before the metrics publish clears only the gate cache; `.commit()` keeps both; drop does not clobber a sibling cache published under a different `Arc`. (Finding B, P2 — `completion_trigger.rs`: gate the cross-shard relay AUTHORITATIVELY at relay time.) The inline gate check in `evaluate_triggers_for_execution` runs on the SOURCE terminal-commit connection and can only *approximate* a cross-shard target's real queue (round-3's `resolve_cross_shard_target_queue` reads the target shard, but a transiently-unavailable target pool falls back to the source connection and can MISS a `Queue(real-q)` gate). Rather than chase a perfect inline approximation, the relay is now gated **authoritatively at relay time on the target shard**, where the real resolved queue is known — in BOTH `DeferredTriggerStart::spawn()` (the immediate path) and the scanner `enforce_completion_triggers_outbox`. New `relay_gate_block(workflow_name, resolved_queue, target_shard, owner)` helper consults the process-global cache via `check_cached` (NOT `check()` — the relay materializes a *pre-committed* in-flight-continuation start, so a fail-closed sentinel must not permanently drop it; only a real known-cached gate blocks). Gate matches → **BLOCK**: drop the outbox row and record `record_admission_blocked` (via the explicit scanner `metrics` recorder, or the global recorder in `spawn()`); no gate → start + count the bypass. The inline check is kept as a best-effort fast path (it can still short-circuit a same-shard block before writing the row). `StartProducer::CompletionTriggerOutbox`'s `producer_contract()` status changes from `ExemptByDesign` to the new `ProducerGateStatus::GatedAtRelay` variant; module docs, `docs/operations/admission-gate-producers.md`, and `docs/api-contract.json` updated accordingly. **Exactly-once / block-vs-bypass never double-counts:** an outbox row is processed by exactly one path (immediate `spawn()` OR scanner — the scanner only claims rows the immediate spawn didn't delete). BOTH the block count and the bypass count are gated on the delete actually removing the row (`matches!(deleted, Ok(n) if n >= 1)`), so a given row is counted EITHER `record_admission_blocked` (gate matched → drop) OR `record_admission_bypassed` (no gate → start → drop) — never both, exactly once, and a start-ok/delete-fail edge leaves the row for the other path rather than double-counting. The lock closes the window: a live run cannot seal under the held lock (so it is attached, `created=false`, gate skipped) and a sealed/absent run cannot gain a live row under the lock (so a fresh create is correctly gated — a matching gate blocks, else it proceeds). The plugin webhook delegate (`plugin.rs`) now calls `gate_checked_start_or_load` with `move |locked_live| webhook_delivery_gate_decision(locked_live, global_admission_gate_cache().as_deref(), shard, owner)` instead of the round-9 unlocked `try_load_by_key` + separate `client.start_or_load`, and records the block (round-9's `record_admission_blocked` + 500) when the outcome is `Blocked`. So a successfully-started target was reported and counted as dropped by the gate (a false block + a corrupted durable audit). **Fix — route the relay's start/block decision through the round-12 existence-aware `execution::gate_checked_start_or_load` primitive, in BOTH relay paths.** New shared `completion_trigger::relay_gate_checked_start(target_conn, source_conn, params, gate_workflow_name, gate_resolved_queue, gate_owner, target_shard, outbox_id, source_exec_id, trigger_id, metrics)` builds the gate closure `move |locked_live| if locked_live { None /* a LOCKED live target already exists → this is a delivery/idempotent-load, NOT a fresh admission → skip the gate */ } else { check_cached(real_resolved_queue, target_shard, owner) }` and calls `gate_checked_start_or_load`, which locks the target's existence on the TARGET shard through the gate/start decision (the same `try_load_active_execution_for_update` `FOR UPDATE` seam round 12 added). Routing by outcome: **target already exists** (`Started { created: false }`, the stale-row case) → DELIVERED: delete the source outbox row + count the `completion_trigger_outbox` bypass, leaving the fires row `NULL`/fired — NOT blocked, NOT marked `admission_blocked`; **fresh + matching gate** (`Blocked`) → `relay_block_drop_outbox` on the source shard (delete outbox + mark fires `admission_blocked`) + count the block; **fresh + no gate** (`Started { created: true }`) → delete outbox + count bypass. The two-shard split is preserved (target-shard existence-lock + gate + start atomic; source-shard outbox delete + fires mark), and exactly-once is still gated on the source-shard delete actually removing the row (block XOR bypass, never both, across the immediate-xor-scanner relay paths). Both `DeferredTriggerStart::spawn()` (uses the process-global recorder + a fresh source-shard connection from `GLOBAL_SHARDED_POOL`) and the scanner (passes its own `conn` as the source connection + the `shards`-scoped `target_shard` assignments) now funnel through this one helper; the now-dead round-7 `relay_gate_block` free function was removed. Rationale: applying a *known* delta means the snapshot is no longer blind — it is the last-known-good full list ± our change — so arming fail-closed is unnecessary for correctness and actively harmful on the lift path (it would make `check()` return the block-everything sentinel, RE-BLOCKING the very work the operator just unblocked, until the next successful refresh). The same divergence is possible scanner-vs-scanner for two replicas assigned the same shard. **Fix — Preferred (mutual exclusion) at the single shared choke point.** `relay_gate_checked_start` (called by BOTH the immediate `spawn()` and the scanner) now opens a source-shard transaction, claims the source outbox row `SELECT id ... WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, and holds the claim across the ENTIRE relay (existence check → gate → cross-shard target start → source delete/block), returning a new `RelayOutcome` (`Skipped`/`Delivered`/`Blocked{scope_kind,reason}`); metrics are recorded by the caller AFTER the claim transaction commits so a rollback never leaves a phantom count. Exactly one path owns a given source row; a concurrent path's `SKIP LOCKED` returns nothing → `Skipped` (no metric, no double-process). If the owner crashes mid-flight the claim transaction rolls back → the row stays present + unlocked and the round-15 delivered-if-target-exists retry makes the next attempt correct. The two now-inlined helpers (`relay_block_drop_outbox`, `relay_mark_delivered`) were removed; the round-15 any-state existence check, the round-18 `will_create` gate decision, and the round-13 delivered-vs-blocked bookkeeping are preserved verbatim, now executed *under the claim* (so the round-15 check is genuinely stable, no longer relying on the false invariant). Since both callers funnel through this one function, both the immediate relay's latency fast-path AND the scanner are made race-free at once — the immediate relay is NOT removed (the fire-and-forget latency benefit is kept; the coordinator's Option-2 collapse-to-scanner-only was unnecessary). The claim is a bounded per-row source-shard row lock on a tiny transient row held across the cross-shard start; a peer never *waits* on it (`SKIP LOCKED`) — it retries the row on the next tick. Lock ordering is source-outbox-row → target-execution-row within every relay (never the reverse), so no ABBA deadlock. **The same-shard inline path (`evaluate_triggers_for_execution`) is unaffected** (it starts the target directly and never touches the outbox), and rounds 13/15/18 semantics are preserved. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no new metric, no schema change** (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` is a query modifier on the existing table). - **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Child-or-deadline waits for bounded sub-orchestrations — see issue #779. `WorkflowContext::execute_child_workflow_timeout::<O>(info, input, timeout) -> HarvestResult<Option<O>>` (typed) and the untyped sibling `spawn_child_workflow_timeout(name, input, timeout) -> HarvestResult<Option<Value>>` bound a **child-workflow** await with a durable deadline — the primitive for a sub-orchestration that must not run past an SLA. It mirrors `receive_signal_timeout` (#476) one level up: instead of racing a signal against a timer, it races a child workflow's terminal outcome against a timer. `Ok(Some(output))` = child terminal **success** before the deadline; `Ok(None)` = deadline fired first (the still-running child is **request-cancelled**); `Err(_)` = child **failure** before the deadline, with the typed failure preserved end-to-end (issue #767 — `err.workflow_error_type()`/`workflow_details()`/`is_workflow_non_retryable()` all readable on the parent side). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, core-only.** The race composes the existing `ChildWorkflowStarted`/`ChildWorkflowCompleted`/`ChildWorkflowFailed` events with the existing `TimerStarted`/`TimerFired` events; the winner is decided by **recorded history order** (order-stable across workers and replays), via the new `HistoryMatcher::match_child_or_timer` returning the new `ChildOrTimerMatch` enum (exported from `lib.rs`). The matcher positionally matches **both** `ChildWorkflowStarted` (capturing the `child_id`) and `TimerStarted`, then forward-scans for the earliest-recorded resolution: a child-win consumes the stray `TimerFired` transparently; a timer-win genuinely consumes the loser child's terminal (so `has_non_lifecycle_unconsumed` stays clean) and returns a `child_already_terminal` flag used to gate the on-deadline cancel to exactly one live cycle. Reserved-signal-events machinery is untouched — child-timeout timers use a `__child_timeout:{seq}:{name}` id namespace disjoint from `__signal_timeout:`. **Worker path (additive):** the two-phase "spawn child then arm the timer in a later batch" shape was rejected — it deadlocks if the child hangs (the parent is never woken until the child terminates, so the deadline would never arm). Instead the primitive spawns the child and arms the deadline in **one** mixed `StartChildWorkflow + StartTimer` suspension batch via a dedicated `extract_child_timeout_race` (accepts exactly one child + one timer + bookkeeping; any extra command falls through to the generic "unsupported commands" failure) and a new `persist_child_timeout_race` transaction (child new-vs-existing resolution + `ChildWorkflowStarted`, then the durable timer arm + `reschedule_task(fires_at)`, factoring shared helpers out of `persist_all_started_child_workflows`/`persist_started_timer`), plus a child-terminal **self-wake re-check** after commit so a child that reaches terminal in the park window is not missed. A new dispatch branch is inserted before the timer branch and a matching branch added to the history-cap event-count predictor. On-deadline request-cancel reuses `ctx.race()`'s existing `WorkflowCommand::CancelRaceLosers { children }` → `apply_race_loser_cancellations` (synchronously seals the awaited child and appends its terminal in the same transaction; benign no-op on replay). Per-context `child_timeout_seq` counter added to `WorkflowContext` and initialised in all three constructors. **Composition caveats** (mirroring #476): cannot share a single suspension batch with a *new* `ScheduleActivity`/`StartChildWorkflow` — the child is spawned+raced in this call's own single mixed batch, so `tokio::join!`-ing two child-timeouts or racing a child-timeout against other new work is rejected fail-loud; the deadline default is request-cancel (no "abandon" variant — a follow-up); detached children are out of scope; and on a child-win the deadline timer is **proactively torn down** (see the post-review note below). **Post-review hardening (Codex P2):** on a child-win (both the `ChildCompleted` and `ChildFailed` branches) the still-armed `__child_timeout:{seq}` durable timer is now proactively torn down via a `WorkflowCommand::CancelRaceLosers { timers: [...] }` bookkeeping command (`queue::delete_pending_timer`), mirroring `ctx.race()`'s `race_timer_signal_impl` signal-won branch. Left armed, the unfired `harvest_timers` row (`fired = false`) is treated as an in-flight dependency by `retention::has_inflight_dependencies`, which would **pin the terminal parent forever** (retention never collects it). The delete appends **no event**, so pushing it on every replay cycle (not just the first) is strict-replay-safe — the executor's completion-time drain-command check already excludes `CancelRaceLosers` from the "new commands beyond recorded history" divergence check, so the child-win replayer fixture still reports `ReplaySucceeded`. Verified end-to-end by the new DB e2e `child_win_tears_down_deadline_timer_no_retention_pin` (child completes → parent COMPLETED → no unfired `__child_timeout:` row remains) and the updated context unit tests (child-completed / child-failed both assert exactly one `CancelRaceLosers` targeting the race timer). **Follow-up:** `wait_for_signal_timeout` has the same latent retention leak on signal-win (its timer is still left armed) — tracked separately, out of scope for this PR. **Post-review hardening (Codex P1) — order a due deadline ahead of an out-of-band child terminal:** a child that completes/fails **after** its deadline appends its terminal to the parent history out-of-band (via `wake_parent_for_child_completion`/`wake_parent_for_child_failure`), while the deadline `TimerFired` was otherwise only ingested at parent claim (`ingest_due_timers_and_signals`). If the parent was claimed late, the child terminal landed in history *before* the overdue `TimerFired`, so the pure recorded-order `match_child_or_timer` declared the child the winner and the primitive returned `Some`/`Err` instead of `None` — even though the deadline genuinely elapsed first (confirmed reproduced against real Postgres 16). Fixed in the wake path: a new `worker::materialize_due_child_timeout_deadlines(conn, parent_exec_id)` materializes every currently-due `__child_timeout:` deadline as a `TimerFired` event **before** the child terminal is appended, in **both** wake functions, so the recorded order becomes `[.., TimerFired, ChildWorkflowCompleted|ChildWorkflowFailed]` and the race resolves to the timeout branch (`None`) — restoring the #476 "deadline reached ⇒ deadline won regardless of when the parent is claimed" guarantee for the child case. Correlation to the completing child is deliberately not required (this child's own due deadline lands before its terminal; an unrelated sibling race's due deadline landing early is resolved by that race's own scan). Scope is strictly the escaped-LIKE `\_\_child\_timeout:%` prefix, so unrelated `ctx.timer()` rows are never fired or reordered, and a child with no due deadline (plain child-await, or a child that beat its deadline) materializes nothing — **byte-identical** to the pre-fix wake path. Double-fire vs the parent-claim ingest is prevented by selecting the due rows `FOR UPDATE` (EvalPlanQual re-evaluates `fired = false` against the latest committed version, so a deadline already fired-and-committed by ingest is excluded, and a deadline this path fires blocks ingest's `SET fired = true` until the wake transaction commits). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no change to `match_child_or_timer` or `ingest_due_timers_and_signals` — the fix is contained to the child-wake path.** `match_child_or_timer`'s existing timer-win branch already consumes a loser child terminal recorded after the fire (via `consume_loser_child_terminal`, which handles both `ChildWorkflowCompleted` and `ChildWorkflowFailed`) and reports `child_already_terminal`, so no cancel command is pushed for the already-sealed loser. Tests, red→green (red confirmed by temporarily disabling the fix — the ordering assertion fails and the primitive returns `Some`): DB e2e `over_deadline_child_completion_orders_deadline_first_and_resolves_none` + `over_deadline_child_failure_orders_deadline_first_and_resolves_none` (drive the REAL doc-hidden-`pub` wake functions over a hand-built overdue-timer prefix, assert the `[TimerFired, terminal]` history order + `None`), the focused helper test `materialize_due_child_timeout_deadlines_fires_only_due_child_timeout_timers` (fires exactly the due `__child_timeout` timer, leaves a not-yet-due one alone, ignores a due non-`__child_timeout` timer), and two context replay-determinism unit tests (`..._over_deadline_completion_loser_is_none`/`..._over_deadline_failure_loser_is_none` — the post-fix `[TimerFired, loser-terminal]` order resolves to `None` across 3 independent replay cycles). Verified green against a real local Postgres 16 (Docker/testcontainers unavailable in the implementing sandbox); Docker-run in CI. **Post-review hardening (Codex P2) — preserve the canary-at-frontier exception for in-flight replay:** the deploy replay canary (`run_workflow_canary`) samples still-running executions and expects a workflow parked at the recorded-history frontier to *suspend* → `ReplaySucceeded`. A workflow parked on `spawn_child_workflow_timeout` replays to `ChildOrTimerMatch::InProgress` at the frontier (the `ChildWorkflowStarted`/`TimerStarted` pair is recorded, but neither resolution is), and the primitive's `InProgress` arm unconditionally reported non-determinism whenever `strict_replay` was set — so healthy in-flight child-timeout workflows surfaced as *false* canary failures and could block deploy verification. Fixed by mirroring `check_strict_replay_no_match`'s existing canary-at-end exception exactly in the `InProgress` arm: the hard error is now suppressed only when `self.canary_mode && position >= len` (the recorded-history frontier), letting the arm fall through to re-park (which suspends). Genuine-divergence detection is untouched — a real code-vs-history divergence resolves as `ChildOrTimerMatch::Diverged` (a different arm that always nd-errors, never canary-excepted), and strict `WorkflowReplayer` runs (non-canary) still treat an unresolved race as a fixture problem. Contained to the context suspend branch: `match_child_or_timer`, `ingest_due_timers_and_signals`, `merge_wake_events`, and the Codex-P1 wake-path fix are all untouched; no new event variant, no migration. Tests, red→green (red confirmed as the exact `NonDeterminismDetected(expected="ChildOrTimerResolved", actual="ChildOrTimerInProgress")` at the frontier): the money test `child_timeout_in_flight_canary_replays_succeeded` (in-flight history in canary → `ReplaySucceeded`) plus two mandatory guards — `child_timeout_in_flight_strict_still_reports_nondeterminism` (same history in strict/non-canary → still non-determinism, the exception must not weaken strict) and `child_timeout_genuine_divergence_still_detected_in_canary` (a child-input mismatch replayed in canary → still non-determinism, the exception must not mask real divergence) — all in `tests/integration/replayer_tests.rs`. **Note:** `wait_for_signal_timeout` (#476) has the same latent behavior in its own `InProgress`/strict arm; left untouched here (a separate, shipped feature) and tracked as a follow-up. Verified via the no-DB `--features testing` replayer suites (Docker/testcontainers for the DB child_timeout suite unavailable in the implementing sandbox; the fix is pure replay and touches no worker/DB path). **Post-review hardening (Codex P2) — shard-encode the fresh child id:** the timeout child id was minted via `ExecutionId::new()` (the `ShardId::UNENCODED` sentinel), even though the child row is inserted into the **parent's** shard database (`persist_child_timeout_race` uses the parent's `conn` and stamps the parent `shard_id`). Shard-aware APIs route from `ExecutionId::shard()`, so a later lookup of that child id by shard (an unencoded sentinel → default shard) would target the wrong database on a non-default-shard parent. Fixed by minting the fresh id with the parent shard — `ExecutionId::new_for_shard(self.exec_id.shard())` — exactly as `spawn_child_workflow_detached_raw` already does. Replay-safe: the id is only minted on the first-live `NoMatch` path; on replay `match_child_or_timer` recovers the recorded `child_id` verbatim, so pre-fix in-flight children keep their unencoded ids and replay unchanged (both `new()` and `new_for_shard()` produce fresh v4 UUIDs, so determinism is identical). **Note:** the regular awaited `spawn_child_workflow_raw` shares the same latent unencoded-id minting (line ~4936) via the same `persist_all_started_child_workflows` insert; left untouched here (pre-existing, out of scope for #779) and flagged as a follow-up. **Post-review finding (Codex P2) — atomic child-timeout timer fire: REFUTED, no change.** The finding hypothesised that the P1 wake-path materializer (`materialize_due_child_timeout_deadlines`), as a *second* deadline-fire path alongside the parent-claim ingest (`ingest_due_timers_and_signals`), could append a **duplicate** `TimerFired` when an overdue child completion races the parent being claimed. Confirmed against the real code and **refuted**: both fire paths append `TimerFired` **and** set `fired = true` **atomically in one transaction**, and `harvest_events` carries `UNIQUE(workflow_exec_id, event_id)`. When the ingest's unlocked `WHERE fired = false` SELECT sees the timer unfired, the materializer has not yet committed (its append + `fired = true` are atomic), so the ingest's stale `start_id` (= old `MAX + 1`) *equals* the materializer's own `MAX + 1` append id → the second append aborts on the unique constraint; when the materializer commits first, the ingest's `fired = false` SELECT (and a second materializer's `FOR UPDATE` re-select) excludes the row and appends nothing. A durable duplicate `TimerFired` is therefore impossible without any compare-and-set on the shared ingest path. Empirically verified against real Postgres 16: the finding's exact two-connection interleaving (materializer holds an uncommitted `TimerFired` at `event_id = K+1`; ingest, seeing `fired = false`, tries to append at its stale `start_id = K+1`) fails with `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "harvest_events_workflow_exec_id_event_id_key"` and the ingest transaction aborts, leaving **exactly one** durable `TimerFired`; the exclusion ordering (`fired = true` first) leaves both writers' `WHERE fired = false` reads empty. The shared ingest/signal path is therefore **not** modified (a CAS there would risk the #476 signal / normal-timer fire path for zero observable benefit, since the event-id collision already coordinates). Regression guard added: `materialize_due_child_timeout_deadlines_is_idempotent_no_duplicate_timerfired` (`tests/integration/child_timeout_tests.rs`) — a second materialize over an already-fired timer returns `0` and appends no second `TimerFired`. *(Observation, out of scope: the racing-collision ordering makes the ingest transaction roll back, which propagates through `fail_execution_on_error`; this is the pre-existing coordination shared with any concurrent `append_single_event` child-terminal writer, predates #779, and is not a duplicate.)* **Post-review hardening (Codex P2-C) — the extractor must require the reserved `__child_timeout:` prefix:** `extract_child_timeout_race` previously matched **any** batch of one `StartChildWorkflow` + one `StartTimer` + bookkeeping regardless of the timer id, so a hand-rolled `tokio::join!(ctx.spawn_child_workflow(..), ctx.timer("mytimer", n))` (one plain child + one ordinary timer) was silently treated as the child-timeout primitive — bypassing the previous fail-loud "unsupported commands" behavior, and on a child-win no `spawn_child_workflow_timeout` teardown would run to delete that ordinary timer row, so the parent could complete with an unfired `harvest_timers` dependency. Fixed: the extractor now additionally requires the `StartTimer`'s `timer_id` to begin with the new shared `context::CHILD_TIMEOUT_TIMER_PREFIX` (`"__child_timeout:"`, the exact prefix `spawn_child_workflow_timeout` stamps, now referenced by both the context's timer-id `format!` and the extractor so the two can't drift). A batch whose timer lacks the prefix returns `None` → falls through to the generic fail-loud path, exactly as before #779. The real primitive still matches (its timer always carries the prefix). Tests (extractor unit tests, `worker.rs`): a new `extract_child_timeout_race_requires_reserved_timer_prefix` asserts (a) a `__child_timeout:`-prefixed batch still matches and (b) a `child + ordinary-timer` batch is rejected, alongside the existing 2nd-child / 2nd-timer / extra-activity / WaitForSignal reject cases. **Post-review hardening (Codex P2-D) — materialize a due deadline before ALL out-of-band child-terminal appends, not just the worker wake path:** the P1 fix only ordered the overdue `__child_timeout:` deadline ahead of the child terminal in `worker::wake_parent_for_child_completion`/`_failure`, but three OTHER out-of-band paths append a child terminal to a parent without going through those, so the over-deadline bug (returns `Some`/`Err` instead of `None`) persisted for them. **Full enumeration** of real DB append-to-parent child-terminal paths (child terminal recorded on the *parent's* history): (1) `worker::wake_parent_for_child_completion` and (2) `worker::wake_parent_for_child_failure` — already fixed by P1; (3) `execution::notify_awaited_parent_of_child_terminal` — the awaited-child operator **cancel** *and* **terminate** paths (its two callers, `cancel_workflow_execution` and `terminate_workflow_execution`); and (4) `timeout::wake_parent_for_child_timeout` — the child hitting its **own** execution timeout (its three callers: `commit_workflow_execution_timeout` + the two activity/external-timeout scanners). *(Read/simulation/replay sites in `simulator.rs`/`testing.rs`/`analyzer.rs`/`history_export.rs`/`timeline.rs`/`reset.rs` and the `context.rs` test fixtures do not append to a live parent's DB history and are out of scope.)* Fixed by calling the **same** helper `crate::worker::materialize_due_child_timeout_deadlines(conn, parent_exec_id)` immediately before the child-terminal `append_single_event` in (3) and (4), under the same parent-row `FOR UPDATE` + `MAX(event_id)` discipline the P1 wake paths use — so an over-deadline child that is operator-cancelled, operator-terminated, or hits its own execution timeout also records `[.., TimerFired(deadline), ChildWorkflowFailed]` and the parent's `spawn_child_workflow_timeout` resolves to `None`. The helper was already `#[doc(hidden)] pub` in `crate::worker`; no move needed (minimal-churn visibility choice). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration; the shared `ingest_due_timers_and_signals`/`merge_wake_events` fire path and `fail_execution_on_error` boundary are untouched.** Tests, red→green (red confirmed by temporarily neutralizing both new `materialize` calls — the ordering assertion fails, tail is `[.., ChildWorkflowFailed]` with no `TimerFired`): three DB e2e tests in `tests/integration/child_timeout_tests.rs` drive the REAL out-of-band entry points over a hand-built overdue-timer prefix with a real parent-linked child row — `over_deadline_child_operator_cancel_orders_deadline_first_and_resolves_none` (via `execution::cancel_workflow_execution`), `over_deadline_child_operator_terminate_orders_deadline_first_and_resolves_none` (via `execution::terminate_workflow_execution`), and `over_deadline_child_execution_timeout_orders_deadline_first_and_resolves_none` (via `timeout::enforce_workflow_execution_timeouts`) — each asserting the `[TimerFired(deadline), ChildWorkflowFailed]` tail order and that the primitive replays to `None`. Verified green (red→green) against a real local Postgres 16 (Docker/testcontainers unavailable in the implementing sandbox — the committed DB tests are compile-checked here via `cargo clippy --all-features --tests` and Docker-run in CI). **Post-review hardening (coordinator-approved, shared-path) — requeue the parent on a transient wake-event-ingest event-id conflict instead of terminally failing it:** the worker's wake-event ingest (`worker::ingest_due_timers_and_signals`) appends `TimerFired`/`SignalReceived` at a `next_event_id` **precomputed from an earlier `load_history`**, with no execution-row lock and no `MAX(event_id)` recompute. When a concurrent `store::append_single_event` writer commits an event at that same `event_id` first, the ingest's batch insert hits `UNIQUE(workflow_exec_id, event_id)` (`harvest_events_workflow_exec_id_event_id_key`). That `Err` previously flowed through `fail_execution_on_error` and **terminally FAILED a healthy execution** on a transient, self-inflicted conflict — with no retry. This is a **pre-existing shared-path hazard** (the ingest's own comment already acknowledged it): it already affected the concurrent-`append_single_event` racers in `timeout.rs` / `external_task.rs`, and #779's `materialize_due_child_timeout_deadlines` (the P1 fix) newly exercises it — a child completing late while the parent is claimed for its due `__child_timeout` deadline. **Fixed** by a precise classification at the ingest boundary: a UNIQUE violation on the events `(workflow_exec_id, event_id)` constraint is now treated as a **transient conflict → re-drive the parent workflow task** (park + wake, the existing pause/resume re-pend mechanism), not a terminal failure. No event is appended, no state is changed, no retry attempt is consumed. **Convergent in one retry, no hot loop:** the winner's event is already committed, so the re-driven task's fresh `load_history` advances `next_event_id` past it and an already-`fired` timer is excluded from the next ingest — the same conflict provably cannot recur. **Precise, non-over-broad classification:** new `HarvestError::is_event_id_unique_violation()` matches **only** that exact constraint name (verified on real Postgres 16 to be carried in the `HarvestError::Database` message) — a genuine/unrelated database error, or a UNIQUE violation on any *other* constraint, is unmatched and still fails as before (`error.rs` unit tests cover other-constraint / genuine-error / non-`Database`-variant rejection). The interception is scoped to the two ingest call sites (`load_workflow_replay_state` cache-miss + `prepare_workflow_task_with_cache` cache-hit), threaded up as an `Option` (`None` = requeued) so `process_workflow_task` returns `Ok(())` (task handled, re-claimed on the next poll) — mirroring the #383 pause and #603 nd-block re-park precedents. It uniformly protects the #476 signal fire, the normal `ctx.timer()` fire, and the #779 child-timeout fire — a transient event-id conflict should never terminally fail any run. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration; the shared `ingest_due_timers_and_signals`/`merge_wake_events` fire logic and `fail_execution_on_error` boundary are otherwise untouched.** Tests, red→green (RED = with the classification reverted, the raw conflict propagates as a genuine `Err` and the parent is terminally FAILED; GREEN = requeued + clean re-drive): DB e2e `transient_event_id_conflict_requeues_parent_instead_of_failing` (`tests/integration/child_timeout_tests.rs`) drives the REAL ingest at a stale `next_event_id` after a concurrent `append_single_event` committed that id, asserting (a) the raw error is classified as the transient conflict — the exact input the pre-fix path failed on, (b) `ingest_wake_events_or_requeue` returns `None` (re-driven, not failed), (c) the execution stays `RUNNING` with no `WorkflowFailed` event and the timer un-fired (ingest rolled back), (d) the parent task is re-pended `PENDING` and immediately claimable, and (e) a fresh re-claim + re-drive completes the ingest cleanly (`Some`, the due timer fires). Verified red→green against a **real local Postgres 16** (Docker/testcontainers unavailable in the implementing sandbox — the committed DB test is compile-checked here via `cargo clippy --all-features --tests` and Docker-run in CI); `error.rs` classifier unit tests RAN. `WorkflowTestEnv` exercises both branches deterministically without real sleeping (a resolving child mock → child branch; omitting it auto-fires the deadline timer). Example `examples/child_with_timeout.rs` (both branches via `WorkflowTestEnv`). Tests: `match_child_or_timer` matcher unit tests in `replay.rs` (child-win / timer-win / `child_already_terminal` / typed-child-failure / diverged / in-progress / interleaved-sibling transparency), context unit tests in `context.rs`, `extract_child_timeout_race`/predictor unit tests in `worker.rs`, `WorkflowReplayer` fixtures in `tests/integration/replayer_tests.rs` (incl. 1,000 randomized child-vs-timer orderings, parallel to #476), `WorkflowTestEnv` harness tests, and Docker-backed DB e2e (`tests/integration/child_timeout_tests.rs`: child completes before deadline → `Some`; child hangs → `None` + child sealed `CANCELLED`; child fails → typed `Err`). **Post-review hardening (Codex P2) — advance `next_event_id` by the materialized-deadline count in the race-loser child-cancel path:** the P2-D deadline-materialization fix made `notify_awaited_parent_of_child_terminal` append a **variable** number of events onto the parent's own history — the `ChildWorkflowFailed` terminal PLUS zero or more preceding `__child_timeout` `TimerFired` deadlines — but `apply_race_loser_cancellations` (the `ctx.race()` loser-teardown path, issue #600) still advanced its in-memory `next_event_id` cursor by a hardcoded `+1` after each genuinely-cancelled loser child. When a race loser child is cancelled **while another child-timeout deadline is due in the same workflow task**, the materializer appends the overdue `TimerFired` before the child terminal (N+1 events), so the caller's cursor was left short by N; the winner-marker / terminal-outcome / synthetic-loser `store::append_events` that the winner-persist path (`persist_terminal_outcome_commands` and the four other `apply_race_loser_cancellations` call sites) performs next then reused a consumed `event_id` and aborted on `UNIQUE(workflow_exec_id, event_id)` (`harvest_events_workflow_exec_id_event_id_key`) — rolling back and **wrongly failing the otherwise-healthy race-winning parent**. **Per-call-site audit** of every `materialize_due_child_timeout_deadlines` caller: `worker::wake_parent_for_child_completion`, `worker::wake_parent_for_child_failure`, and `timeout::wake_parent_for_child_timeout` all append the child terminal via `store::append_single_event` (which re-reads `MAX(event_id)+1` under the parent-row lock) and maintain **no** subsequent in-memory cursor → **safe**; `execution::notify_awaited_parent_of_child_terminal` is itself internally safe (same `append_single_event`), but its only caller that both maintains a cursor *and* can append-to-self is `apply_race_loser_cancellations` (a race loser is always an awaited child of the racing execution) → **the single affected site**. The other four `cancel_workflow_execution_collect` callers (`persist_external_signal_inline`, the external-cancel outbox, and the two `TerminateIfRunning` pre-cancels) either cancel an arbitrary external target whose parent is not the cursor-maintaining execution, or are structurally unreachable for append-to-self (a parent parked on an awaited child cannot simultaneously be running its own decision cycle) → **safe**, no path outside the audited sites is affected. **Fixed** by replacing the hardcoded `+1` with a re-read of the true next id — new `store::next_event_id_for(conn, exec_id)` (`MAX(event_id)+1` under the same `FOR UPDATE` row lock `append_single_event` uses, which `notify_awaited_parent_of_child_terminal`'s append already holds), so the cursor re-synchronises to however many events were appended (1 + N), self-correcting for any future change to the child-terminal append count. **Byte-identical when N = 0** (a child race with no due deadline appends exactly the `ChildWorkflowFailed`, so the re-read returns the same value the `+1` did) — only the bug case (child-race loser + a concurrently-due `__child_timeout` deadline) changes. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration; `match_child_or_timer`, the extractor, the payload-cap reorder, and the transient-conflict requeue are all untouched** — the fix is event-id accounting in the one race-loser call site plus a read-only store helper. Tests, red→green: DB e2e `race_loser_child_cancel_materializing_deadline_advances_event_id_past_all_appends` (`tests/integration/child_timeout_tests.rs`) drives the REAL `apply_race_loser_cancellations` (now `#[doc(hidden)] pub`) over a parent with an overdue `__child_timeout` deadline + a real awaited RUNNING loser child, then performs the real subsequent winner-terminal `append_events` at the returned cursor — RED (revert to `+1`): the cursor is `4` (still pointing at the `ChildWorkflowFailed` id) and the terminal append fails on `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "harvest_events_workflow_exec_id_event_id_key"`; GREEN: the cursor is `5` and the parent history is gap-free `[WorkflowStarted, ChildWorkflowStarted, TimerStarted, TimerFired, ChildWorkflowFailed, WorkflowCompleted]`. Verified red→green against a **real local Postgres 16** (Docker/testcontainers unavailable in the implementing sandbox; Docker-run in CI). **Test-infra fix shipped alongside:** the P2-D real-child helper `setup_parent_racing_overdue_real_child` inserted the parent and child with the *same* hardcoded `workflow_id` (via two `insert_workflow_execution` calls), colliding on the partial `UNIQUE(workflow_name, workflow_id)` active index — so the three P2-D real-child DB tests (operator-cancel/terminate/execution-timeout) could never actually execute. Added `insert_workflow_execution_with_id(conn, workflow_id)` and gave the child a distinct id, unblocking those three tests (now confirmed green on real PG 16) plus the new one; the whole `child_timeout_tests.rs` DB suite (15 tests) was pointed at the new env-honoring `setup_test_database_url_or_env` helper (identical container path when `HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset, per the `retention_overrides_tests.rs` precedent) so it runs locally and Docker-backed in CI. **Post-review hardening (Codex P2) — check the child-input payload cap BEFORE the replay matcher so cap-failure histories replay deterministically:** `spawn_child_workflow_timeout` previously called `match_child_or_timer` first and only enforced the child-input cap inside the `NoMatch | InProgress` arm. On a live **over-cap** call the child is never dispatched, so no child/timer events are recorded and the run terminates as `WorkflowFailed` (propagate) or continues after catching the error. On **replay** of that history the cursor sits on the next real event (`WorkflowFailed`, or a caught-and-continued activity/completion), not a recorded `ChildWorkflowStarted`, so `match_child_or_timer` returned `Diverged` and the call reported a spurious `NonDeterminismDetected(expected="ChildWorkflowStarted", actual="WorkflowFailed")` instead of reproducing the same `PayloadTooLarge`. Fixed by moving the cap check to the **top** of the method, before the matcher — the cap decision is a pure function of the deterministic input size + the (normally stable) `payload_max_workflow_input`, so it must run first. The check is gated to a fresh dispatch via a new **read-only** `HistoryMatcher::peek_child_start_at_cursor` (mirroring the fan-out's `peek_fan_out_count` marker peek, and its skip set — consumed indices + leading early-drainable signal/external-signal/external-cancel/update events — so it agrees with where `prepare_match` will land): an already-recorded child (under-cap at record time) is never re-judged against a possibly-changed cap, and the redundant inner cap check was removed. **For every under-cap input this is byte-identical to the prior behavior** — the top cap check is a no-op and the matcher proceeds exactly as before; only over-cap inputs change, now failing fast before the matcher on both live and replay. Scope (config-stable, honest): the cap decision reads the live `payload_max_workflow_input`, so replay-consistency holds when the cap is stable (the normal case) — this does **not** claim replay-safety across a cap change, matching the documented fan-out `validate_child_payload_caps` limitation. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration; `match_child_or_timer` resolution logic, the extractor, the deadline-materializer, and the transient-conflict fix are all untouched** — the change is a pure reorder within `spawn_child_workflow_timeout` plus one read-only matcher helper. Tests, red→green (red confirmed by reverting the reorder — both new tests fail with the exact `NonDeterminismDetected(expected="ChildWorkflowStarted(process_order)", actual="WorkflowFailed")`): `child_timeout_oversized_input_caught_replays_succeeded` (fresh over-cap input caught + continued → `ReplaySucceeded`, reproducing `PayloadTooLarge` instead of diverging on the `WorkflowCompleted` at the cursor) and `child_timeout_oversized_input_propagated_replays_deterministically` (fresh over-cap input propagated → deterministic `WorkflowFailed` carrying the `PayloadTooLarge` message across 2 cycles, asserting the error is NOT a history-matcher divergence) in `tests/integration/replayer_tests.rs`; the existing `child_timeout_oversized_input_rejected` (cap fires before any command on a fresh live call) and all child-win / timer-win / canary fixtures stay green. Verified via the no-DB `--features testing` replayer/lib suites (the fix is pure replay and touches no worker/DB path).
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Address existing workflows by business `workflow_id` over HTTP — see issue #805. Embedders assign their own business `workflow_id` at start (e.g. `order-12345`, `subscription:user-42`), but every act-on-existing management route (`GET /workflows/{id}`, `/result`, `POST .../signal/{name}`, `/query/{name}`, `/cancel`, `/pause`, `/resume`, `/stack`, `/children`) previously accepted only the internal `exec_id` UUID (`parse_execution_id` rejects anything else). Acting on a workflow you already named required a list-then-act round-trip, and a cached `exec_id` is a **stale handle** — continue-as-new and reset fork a **new** `exec_id` under the **same** `workflow_id`, so code that pinned an `exec_id` can silently signal or read a terminal predecessor instead of the live run. This shipped a **business-id form** addressed by `(workflow_name, workflow_id)` alongside the existing `exec_id` routes, which stay **byte-for-byte backward compatible**. **New routes** (prefix `P = /workflows/by-id/{workflow_name}/{workflow_id}`): `GET P` (describe), `GET P/result`, `GET P/stack`, `GET P/children`, `POST P/signal/{signal_name}`, `GET P/query/{query_name}`, `POST P/query/{query_name}`, `POST P/cancel`, `POST P/pause`, `POST P/resume`. Each **resolves** `(workflow_name, workflow_id) → ExecutionId` then **delegates** to the existing `exec_id` handler (no existing handler body changed), so admin posture and audit classification mirror the `exec_id` counterparts exactly: `cancel`/`pause`/`resume` carry the same `require_admin` route layer and `OP_WORKFLOW_CANCEL`/`OP_WORKFLOW_PAUSE`/`OP_WORKFLOW_RESUME` audit ops; `signal` is `OP_WORKFLOW_SIGNAL`; describe/result/stack/children/query are `ReadOnly` + `EXCLUDED_ROUTES`. **Resolution rule (AC2):** the single **active** (non-terminal — `RUNNING`/`PAUSED`) run if one exists; otherwise the **most recent terminal** run by `started_at`; otherwise `404` (never `500`). Well-defined because at most one active run exists per `(workflow_name, workflow_id)` (the per-shard partial unique index). `workflow_name` is **required** (AC3): both path segments are mandatory, so a bare `workflow_id` never matches a by-id route. **AC4 — the resolved `execution_id` is always returned:** every by-id response carries it in the `X-Harvest-Execution-Id` header (uniform, covers empty-body cases like `/result`'s `204`), and in the JSON body wherever one exists — `signal`/`query` responses are re-wrapped to add a top-level `execution_id`; `cancel`/`pause`/`resume` already carry it; `describe`/`stack` carry it nested; `result`/`children` surface it via the header. **Shard strategy — always fan out.** `resolve_workflow_by_business_id` (plugin) fans out across `iter_shards()` rather than trusting a single rendezvous-hash fast path: `ShardRouter::pick_for_new_workflow` can drift from where a run actually lives once the writable shard subset changes, so a fast-path-then-miss design could resolve a live run to `404`. Resolution is not a hot path and the single-shard default is exactly one query. Per-shard candidates are merged by the pure `select_resolved_run`. **Core (`autumn-harvest/src/execution.rs`, db-gated), no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration** — resolution is read-only over the existing `UNIQUE (workflow_name, workflow_id)` index. New `ResolvedRun { exec_id, state, started_at }`; pure, no-DB, unit-tested `select_resolved_run(Vec<ResolvedRun>) -> Option<ResolvedRun>` (active-first, else most-recent-terminal, using `erase::is_terminal_state` so classification cannot drift — guarded by `resolve_terminal_states_matches_is_terminal_state`); shard-local `resolve_execution_id_by_workflow_id(conn, name, id)` (active-first query, else most-recent overall). Both re-exported from `lib.rs`. **Registration surfaces:** all 10 routes registered in `management_api_routes()`, `management_api_request_fields()` (signal free-form, query POST `args`, cancel/pause `reason`, resume empty), `management_api_response_fields()` (describe/result/stack/children free-form; signal/query/cancel/pause/resume structured incl. `execution_id`), `docs/api-contract.json`, and `autumn_harvest::audit` (`CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` + `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES` + `EXCLUDED_ROUTES` for the read-only ones).
