Docs: new "Addressing workflows by business id" section in `docs/management-api.md` (resolution semantics, required-name rule, always-present `execution_id`, shard-aware note, continue-as-new note). **Tests:** pure `select_resolved_run` unit tests in `execution.rs` (empty/single/active-wins-over-terminals/most-recent-terminal/paused-active/sealed-terminal/two-actives-defensive/drift-guard); plugin HTTP integration `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/by_id_integration.rs` (describe 200 + header/body execution_id match, unknown `(name,id)` → 404 not 500, malformed exec-id on the old route still 400, signal lands + execution_id in body/header, cancel + `401` unauthenticated, **continue-as-new correctness** — resolves to the RUNNING successor not the sealed predecessor, all-terminal resolves to the COMPLETED run, exec-id route unchanged); `contract_regression.rs` `*_route_is_classified` pins for every by-id route; one sorted line in `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`. DB/HTTP integration tests are compile-checked in-sandbox and executed against a local Postgres 16 where available; the pure unit tests run under `cargo test -p autumn-harvest --lib`.
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Admission gate authoritative on the single-start throttle route — see issue #607. **Post-review hardening (Codex P1):** the committed-prior idempotent-retry bypass added below was **policy-blind** — it treated *any* non-sealed prior as an attach, matching `AllowDuplicate` unconditionally. But `reuse_policy = allow_duplicate_failed_only` over a `FAILED`/`CANCELLED` prior, and `terminate_if_running` over any prior, actually **create** a fresh (replacement) execution, so bypassing the gate on the token-empty `Deferred` path let a fresh replacement start slip an armed gate (the deferred row fires gate-less at the next scanner tick). Fixed by making the committed-prior bypass **reuse-policy-aware**: it now loads the prior's *state* (same non-sealed filter the authoritative locked gate uses) and bypasses only when `execution::start_will_create_new_execution(prior_state, reuse_policy)` is `false` (attach or `AlreadyExists`) — the exact predicate the core locked gate (`GateMode::Check`) keys on. A create-on-retry policy now correctly faces the gate → `503`. The `has_pending_throttle_for_workflow_id` bypass (an already-durably-deferred retry) is unchanged (it is orthogonal to the reuse policy). Regression test `armed_gate_blocks_fresh_creating_start_under_reuse_policy_on_empty_bucket` (armed gate + empty bucket + `allow_duplicate_failed_only`/FAILED and `terminate_if_running`/RUNNING → `503` + zero pending throttle rows; plus an `allow_duplicate`/attach no-over-block guard). The **batch route** (`POST /workflows/batch`) inherits the same policy-blind heuristic and is tracked separately in **#1053** (out of scope for this PR). Production bug fix. The single-start workflow-start route (`POST /workflows/{name}/start`) has a throttle branch (issue #607) that, when a throttled workflow's token bucket is empty, durably **defers** the start and returns `202 Accepted` — and it did so **before** any admission-gate check. The admission gate (#377 / #618, PR #1014) is a "halt starts during an incident" control that must win over throttle's "pace starts" control (`"halt beats pace"`): PR #1014 wired `gate_cache().check()` into the debounce branch and the batch route, and made the plain/keyed start gate-check authoritatively inside the core start primitive (`GateMode::Check`), but a throttle DEFER returns `202` from this branch and never reaches that core create path — so a genuinely-new throttled start submitted while a gate was armed silently slipped it (`202` instead of `503`). The fix adds the gate check in the single-start throttle branch, **before `reserve_or_defer`**, mirroring the batch route exactly — including its two idempotent-retry bypasses (an explicit caller-supplied `workflow_id` whose start already committed as an active execution, matching `AllowDuplicate`; or one already durably deferred in `harvest_start_throttle`, via `throttle::has_pending_throttle_for_workflow_id`) — so #808 keyed-replay and idempotent retries are **not** regressed (a retry of a committed or already-deferred start still gets its idempotent `202`, only a genuinely-new fresh start under an armed gate becomes `503`), reusing the same `record_admission_blocked` + `503 {"error":"admission blocked","gate_id","reason"}` response the debounce/batch branches emit. **Behavior change:** a fresh throttled start under an armed admission gate now returns `503` instead of `202`. Throttle semantics are otherwise unchanged (gate open → defer `202` exactly as before). `start_throttle_integration` was moved off the `ci_run_coverage` allowlist onto a `linux` CI run row in `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`, so the throttle-vs-gate contract now runs against live Docker Postgres. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no test changes** (the existing `retry_with_a_pending_throttle_row_bypasses_the_admission_gate` test was already correct). Surfaced by the #1045 diagnosis of the 202-vs-503 discrepancy on this route.
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Fix race-primitive canary replay false-positive on interleaved bookkeeping siblings — see issue #1048. A canary replay of an in-flight `wait_for_signal_timeout` (#476) or `spawn_child_workflow_timeout` (#779) race started concurrently with a bookkeeping side effect — e.g. `tokio::join!(race, async { ctx.side_effect(...) })` — incorrectly reported the run as `NonDeterminismDetected`, spuriously failing deploy-safety canary checks even though the workflow is fine and merely still parked on the race. Root cause: both race primitives carried a byte-identical inline "canary-frontier guard" that decided non-determinism from inside the race matcher by reading whether the cursor was at the frontier (`!has_non_lifecycle_unconsumed()`). But on an `InProgress` result the matcher **rewinds** the cursor to the interleaved sibling command so the sibling's own matcher can consume its event — so the guard read "not at frontier" (the sibling's `SideEffectRecorded` was momentarily unconsumed) and false-fired, poll-order-dependently, before the sibling future ran. Fixed by deleting both inline guards in `context.rs` **symmetrically** (avoiding the twin↔sibling asymmetry the issue calls out) and deferring the `InProgress` decision to the executor's already-wired end-of-cycle authority: `history_has_unconsumed_events()` in `run_workflow_canary`, and `outcome_to_report`'s `Suspended` mapping for strict replay. That authority runs *after* all joined siblings have consumed their rewound events, so a clean parked race reads no unconsumed events (→ `ReplaySucceeded`) while a genuine leftover is still caught (→ `NonDeterminismDetected`). The `Diverged` arms are untouched — a real divergence always errors. **Live-worker no-op:** the guards' load-bearing `return Err` was `strict_replay`-gated, so the live worker / crash-recovery replay (`strict_replay = false`) never executed it; the guard's `match_history` read that did run live was a redundant duplicate of the race matcher's own post-hook `pump_signal_handlers`, so its removal drops no signal-handler dispatch. **Diagnostic granularity:** a genuinely-parked race under strict `WorkflowReplayer` now surfaces the generic executor `NonDeterminismDetected` ("workflow suspended before all history events were replayed") rather than the old specific `SignalOrTimerResolved`/`ChildOrTimerResolved` message (status unchanged; no test asserted the old strings). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no production/live-worker behavior change.** Tests (all no-DB, `--features testing`, in `tests/integration/replayer_tests.rs`): AC1 canary-plus-interleaved-bookkeeping-sibling → `ReplaySucceeded` for both primitives (`signal_timeout_in_flight_with_bookkeeping_sibling_canary_replays_succeeded`, `child_timeout_in_flight_with_bookkeeping_sibling_canary_replays_succeeded`, both new red-first repros); AC2 strict-parked-race still errors (`signal_timeout_in_flight_strict_still_reports_nondeterminism`, `child_timeout_in_flight_strict_still_reports_nondeterminism`), genuine `Diverged` under canary still errors (`signal_timeout_genuine_divergence_still_detected_in_canary`, `child_timeout_genuine_divergence_still_detected_in_canary`), and the deferral does not blind canary to a genuine `InProgress` leftover (`signal_timeout_in_flight_genuine_leftover_event_still_detected_in_canary`, `child_timeout_in_flight_genuine_leftover_event_still_detected_in_canary`, both new); AC3 fixed symmetrically (both inline guards deleted identically, every test row present for both twins). Full local CI mirror green: fmt, clippy `--all-features --tests -D warnings` and `--no-default-features --features testing`, `--test integration` (949 passed), `--lib` (1563 passed).
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Admission-gate hardening: throttle fire-time gate + reuse-policy-aware batch bypass — see issue #1053. Consolidated admission-gate (#377 / #618 / #1014) hardening follow-up split out of PR #1051's review. Two pieces, each carrying its own contract decision. **(1) Throttle scanner now honors the admission gate at fire time — deliberate contract change.** A deferred throttle start (issue #607) creates no execution at defer time — it persists a `harvest_start_throttle` row and returns `202`. The actual create-vs-attach commits later in the scanner (`throttle::fire_claimed_throttle_row`), which previously called `start_or_load_workflow_execution_collect(..., gate: None)` — gate-exempt by construction (the deliberate #618-F1 `GatedAtAdmission` exemption). **Before:** a throttled start deferred while no gate was armed would fire the instant its tokens refilled, *even if an operator had since armed an admission gate on its scope* — the last deferred-fire leak past an active gate. **After:** the scanner passes `Some(GateMode::CheckCached)` and re-checks the gate on the workflow's real queue immediately before firing. When a gate matches it **blocks and RE-DEFERS** the row: it leaves the `harvest_start_throttle` row in place, **refunds** the token it reserved for the attempt, starts nothing, counts `harvest.admission.blocked`, and bumps the row's `deferred_at` forward by a modest backoff (`GATE_REDEFER_BACKOFF`, 5s) — so the held start fires the instant the gate opens. This reverses the #618-F1 exemption: the throttle deferred-start `202` now means *"will run when tokens allow **AND** the admission gate is open at fire time"*, not merely *"will run when tokens allow"* — the correct halt-beats-pace semantics for an operator slamming a gate mid-incident. **A gate block never drops a start** — the row is re-deferred, not deleted. **One pre-existing, orthogonal caveat holds unchanged:** a start given a `schedule_to_start` deadline (issue #607 AC-c) that is held under a gate *past that deadline* is still dropped as stale (the row is deleted, a `warn!` is logged) exactly as it would be for any other reason it missed its deadline — the gate does not exempt a start from its own staleness bound, and (because the gate can hold a start until its deadline elapses) a long-armed gate makes such staleness drops materially more likely. The staleness drop is emitted on a `warn!` log only (no dedicated metric today). **Re-defer backoff — cross-key fairness (review finding B-G1).** A gate is **queue-scoped**, so the SQL candidate pre-filter that selects the tick's fire batch cannot see it (it only knows token levels and `schedule_to_start` expiry). Without bumping `deferred_at`, a gate-blocked-but-tokened row keeps its original (older) `deferred_at`, stays the oldest candidate in the `ORDER BY deferred_at ASC` fire ordering, and is re-selected every tick; ≥100 such rows gated together (a queue-wide incident gate over many tenant keys on one shard) would monopolize the fixed-size fire batch and **starve newer un-gated throttle keys on other queues** until the gate lifts — reopening the exact cross-key fairness pathology the per-key cap + token pre-filter (#607) closed. Bumping `deferred_at` forward on re-defer rotates a gated row *behind* every un-gated row, so un-gated keys fire first and a gated row is re-attempted less often. Because the re-defer is per-tick, `harvest.admission.blocked` for throttle reflects re-defer **attempt volume** (at-least-once per gated row per tick), not distinct blocked rows — unlike the completion-trigger cross-shard outbox relay, which drops on block and so counts once per row (the block log was also demoted to `debug!` to avoid a per-tick flood). **Producer contract flip.** `throttle` moves from `gated_at_admission` to `gated_at_relay` at `GET /admin/gates` (`admission_gate::producer_contract`). It shares the `check_cached` relay-time mechanism with the completion-trigger cross-shard outbox (also `GatedAtRelay`) but **differs in disposition**: the completion-trigger outbox **drops** its row on block (its source terminal decision has already fired, so a permanently gated relay must not accumulate forever); the throttle scanner **re-defers** its row (its `202` "nothing lost" promise). A blocked fire counts `harvest.admission.blocked` and a genuinely-fired start counts `harvest.admission.bypassed{producer="throttle"}` — never both (block-vs-bypass never double-counts). `debounce` and `event_batch` **remain** `gated_at_admission` — #1053 scopes only throttle. **Coverage.** Closes BOTH (a) the pre-existing looseness where ANY deferred throttle start fires gate-exempt if the gate arms after deferral, and (b) the narrow PR-#1051 residual — an attach-policy bypass whose prior is force-terminated between the unlocked read and the scanner fire, so the deferred fire becomes a fresh CREATE. (b) is a subset of (a): every deferred fire now faces the fire-time gate; force-terminate is merely what turns a would-be attach into a would-be CREATE. **(2) Batch route reuse-policy-aware bypass (structural / defensive).** The batch-start Phase-1 idempotent-retry pre-check (`autumn-harvest-plugin/src/api.rs`) previously bypassed the admission gate on a bare "any non-sealed prior exists" existence boolean. **After:** it loads the prior's *state* and decides the bypass with `execution::start_will_create_new_execution(prior_state, AllowDuplicate)`, mirroring the single-start route fixed in #1051. **No behavior change today** — the batch route starts every item under `AllowDuplicate` (`BatchStartItem` has no reuse-policy field), so the predicate agrees with the old existence boolean for every prior state — but it stays correct if a per-item reuse policy is ever added, and the throttled batch item's real residual is closed by (1) since a deferred batch item fires through the same `fire_claimed_throttle_row` scanner. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration.** A blocked fire rolls the start transaction back (no row, no events), so there is no replay surface. The metrics recorder is now threaded through `fire_claimed_throttle_row` / `fire_due_on_conn` (mirroring `debounce` / `event_batch`) so the fire-time block is counted on the passed recorder rather than only the process-global fallback. Tests: `throttle_scanner_re_defers_under_a_closed_gate_and_fires_when_open` (money — block+re-defer under a closed gate, fire once open), `throttle_row_deferred_before_gate_is_held_when_gate_arms_before_fire` (coverage (a)), `throttle_deferred_fire_over_a_force_terminated_prior_faces_the_gate` (coverage (b)), `batch_gate_bypasses_an_attaching_item_but_blocks_a_would_be_fresh_create` (batch gate-bypass decision regression-lock; renamed + strengthened by the #1085 heal — was `batch_bypass_uses_start_will_create_predicate_not_bare_existence`, whose runtime assertion never ran under Docker-only CI); four existing tests flipped from the old "fires despite the gate" contract to the new fire-time-gate contract.
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Read-only operator role for least-privilege triage access — see issue #776. Promotes `autumn_harvest::audit`'s route classification from "used for audit" to also "used for authz": a **read-only operator role** an embedder enables in **one builder call**. A principal the embedder marks read-only reaches **100%** of `RouteClass::ReadOnly` routes but receives **403 Forbidden** on **every** `Mutating` management route **and every mutating MCP tool** (see *Post-review hardening* below) — for exposing triage/status dashboards to support/on-call users without granting the mutate-everything credential, replacing "write a custom reverse proxy" with a single call. **Enforcement = one opt-in, class-aware tower layer** (`enforce_read_only_class`, `autumn-harvest-plugin/src/api.rs`) installed on `harvest_api_router` **only** under the new `HarvestPlugin::api_with_role_auth(path, middleware)`. Driven **purely** by `autumn_harvest::audit::CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` — the single source of truth, so there is no second hand-maintained mutating-route list to drift (AC3). Keys on `request.method()` + the nest-stripped `request.uri().path()`, matched via **`matchit`** (the radix-tree matcher axum itself uses) built once into a per-method `HashMap<Method, matchit::Router<RouteClass>>` with **positional param normalization** (`{id}`→`{p0}`) so a single router accepts the full template set without a name conflict, preserving **static-beats-param precedence** (`POST /workflows/batch_start` is never mistaken for the `ReadOnly` `/workflows/{id}` — a privilege-escalation bug if wrong). Deliberately **not** `axum::extract::MatchedPath`, which is unreliable when read from a layer on a nested router (axum #1441) — the exact position this layer occupies. Classification keys on the route class, **never the HTTP verb**: the two `ReadOnly` POST routes (`POST /workflows/{id}/query/{query_name}`, `POST /admin/build-routing/retire`) are correctly reachable. **Pure decision fn (core `audit.rs`):** `deny_readonly_mutation(is_readonly, class) -> bool` = `is_readonly && !matches!(class, ReadOnly | PublicSafe)`. **Fail closed by construction:** the matcher resolves an unmatched path / unknown method to `RouteClass::Mutating`, so a route a contributor forgot to classify is denied to read-only principals — never silently exposed (AC4). Pinned by a truth-table unit test. **Read-only principal predicate (`has_harvest_readonly_access`):** true iff the autumn-web `Session` carries an explicit read-only marker (`role` ∈ {`harvest_readonly`,`harvest_operator`,`operator`,`readonly`,`read_only`} or a truthy `is_harvest_readonly`/`is_harvest_operator`) **and** no explicit admin marker (`role` ∈ {`admin`,`harvest_admin`} or truthy `is_harvest_admin`/`is_admin`). Admin marker present, no session, or no marker → `false` (full access — the read-only restriction is opt-in per principal, preserving existing boundary semantics; documented contract that the embedder must explicitly mark a principal read-only). **Opt-in (`HarvestPlugin::api_with_role_auth`):** mirrors `api_with_auth` (sets `api_path` + the embedder auth middleware, which makes `admin_auth_boundary = true`) **and** sets a new `role_auth_enabled` flag on `HarvestApiState` (mirrored from the plugin builder in `build()`, same `Arc<Mutex<bool>>` setter/getter pattern as `set_decode_payloads_on_read`). In `build()`, when role-auth is enabled the class layer is installed on the combined router **before** the embedder middleware wraps it, so the request order is: embedder auth mw (sets `Session`) → class layer (enforce) → per-route `require_admin` (a no-op under the boundary) → handler. **Because `admin_auth_boundary = true`, per-route `require_admin` and the SSE in-handler admin check pass for the read-only principal → AC1 is satisfied with NO router/SSE surgery.** This is safe: the class layer 403s a read-only principal at the route boundary *before* any handler's in-handler admin write-gate runs, and every state-writing handler sits on a `Mutating` (or unclassified→fail-closed→`Mutating`) route. The only extra capability the boundary grants a read-only principal is **READS** (payload decode #608, the SSE event stream) — explicitly scoped out by the issue (verb restriction, not field/row restriction). **`api_with_auth` and the default `api(path)` mount are byte-for-byte unchanged (AC6):** the class layer is installed *only* under `api_with_role_auth`; `role_auth_enabled` defaults off. **403, not 401 (AC2):** a read-only principal on a `Mutating` route gets `403 Forbidden` (`{"error":"read-only principal: mutation not permitted"}`), distinct from the anonymous `401` the admin gate returns, built directly (no dependency on an autumn-web `forbidden` helper). **Observability (AC7):** every denial emits `tracing::warn!(method, path, "harvest: read-only principal denied mutation (403)")`; a best-effort DB audit row is deliberately *not* written (the layer runs before a pooled connection is acquired; forcing a write on every probe would be a DoS vector). The stable 403 body marker is also a distinguishable signal. **Classification scope (the largest work item):** 31 routes were mounted in `harvest_api_router` but had drifted without a `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` entry — **8 Mutating** (`update-with-start`, `dag runs/{}/retry`, circuit `force-open`/`force-close`, `POST /admin/completion-triggers`, `POST /calendars`, `PUT /calendars/{name}`, `DELETE /calendars/{name}`) and **23 ReadOnly** (`batches/pending`, `workflows/registered`(+/`{name}`/schema), the two `workflows/by-id/{workflow_name}` 400-stubs, `workflows/types/{name}/handlers`, `dead-letters/aggregate`, `admin/circuits`(+/`{name}`), `admin/queues/scaling`, `admin/metrics`, `admin/completion-triggers` GET, `admin/schedules/{id}`(+/runs+/decisions+/preview), `admin/schedules/decisions`, `POST /admin/schedules/preview`, `calendars` GET(+/`{name}`), `workers/{id}/pinned`, `admin/queues/{queue}/eligibility`, `admin/tasks/{id}/eligibility`). Each Mutating handler was verified to write state; each ReadOnly handler verified not to (privilege-escalation guard). The 4 circuit/dag/update ops reuse pre-existing constants (`OP_WORKFLOW_UPDATE_WITH_START`, `OP_DAG_RETRY`, `OP_CIRCUIT_FORCE_OPEN`, `OP_CIRCUIT_FORCE_CLOSE`) that had never been registered in `AUDITED_OPERATIONS` — now wired, with `Some(op)` manifest entries; the calendar + completion-trigger CRUD (no op constant, audit wiring out of scope) use `None` + `EXCLUDED_ROUTES`. `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` and `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES` stay size-synced (137 each); the 3 router-only routes (`/handlers` + the two by-id missing-id stubs) were added to `management_api_routes()` and `docs/api-contract.json` so the coverage sweep and contract parity cover them. **Deviation from the issue's literal wording:** AC8 says the change is "confined to the `autumn-harvest-plugin` auth/router layer", but `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES`/`ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES`/`AUDITED_OPERATIONS`/`EXCLUDED_ROUTES` live in the **core crate** `autumn-harvest/src/audit.rs`, so classifying the drifted routes necessarily edits core (const arrays + `#[cfg(test)]` tests). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no replay-determinism impact, no `::autumn_harvest::` macro-path change** — so it is allowed, but the "plugin-only" claim is inaccurate (flagged for spec-owner review). **Known limitation (documented follow-up):** the nested `/ui` sub-router's paths are not in `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES`, so under fail-closed enforcement a read-only principal receives 403 on `/ui`. Admins reach `/ui` unchanged. Classifying the UI routes so read-only principals can view (but not act through) the dashboard is a follow-up. **Read-capability breadth** is also out of scope by design: a read-only principal, mounted behind the auth boundary, gets admin-level *reads* (payload decode #608, the SSE stream) — this slice restricts verbs, not fields or rows. **Post-review hardening (three-reviewer pass):** **BLOCKER (F1) — MCP mutating tools were an unguarded write surface.** The generated MCP tool routes (issue #597) are registered app-level (via `AppBuilder::routes`), **outside** the nested management router the `enforce_read_only_class` layer wraps, so under `mcp_tools() + api_with_role_auth()` a read-only principal could start / signal / update / dag-start a workflow through a tool — via the tool's direct HTTP path OR the `/mcp` JSON-RPC `tools/call` envelope (autumn-web re-dispatches it through the same route). Closed by threading `role_auth_enabled` into `build_mcp_tool_routes` → `build_tool_route` and gating every mutating tool (`ToolKind::is_mutation()` — `Start`/`DagStart`/`Signal`/`Update`) with the new `enforce_read_only_mcp_mutation` layer (403 for read-only principals), applied *inner* of the embedder auth layer so the Session is populated before the gate reads it. Read tools (`Status`/`Watch`) stay reachable. One gate closes both invocation paths. Off when `api_with_role_auth` is not used. **F2 — read-only detection failed OPEN on case mismatch.** `has_harvest_readonly_access` matched markers case-sensitively, so `role="ReadOnly"`/`"READONLY"` fell through to full access. Now normalizes claim VALUES (trim + lowercase) and accepts `true`/`1`/`yes`/`on` case-insensitively; admin-marker detection normalized too so "admin wins" is case-robust. **F3 — HEAD/OPTIONS over-restriction.** `classify_route` now maps `HEAD → GET`'s class (axum serves HEAD via GET), and the layer lets `OPTIONS` pass, so a read-only principal can HEAD-probe reads and a cookie-bearing CORS preflight is not 403'd. **F4 — matcher build no longer panics.** A future post-normalization route collision logs an error and degrades fail-closed (the route stays unclassified → `Mutating` → denied) instead of panicking the first read-only request; a `debug_assert` keeps the build-time CI guard. **F8 / vestigial flag.** The Session `role` claim is fetched once (was twice). The write-only `HarvestApiState::role_auth_enabled` mirror (set but never read — enforcement gates on the plugin `build()` var) was removed so no misleading flag remains. **M2 — contract read_only cross-check.** `docs/api-contract.json`'s `read_only` bool was a second read/mutate source never compared to `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES`. Reconciled the one pre-existing drift (`POST /admin/build-routing/retire` is `ReadOnly` but was `read_only:false`) and added `contract_read_only_flag_matches_classified_routes` to guard the two sources. Docs: `docs/operator-role.md` (opt-in, Session claim contract, 403/fail-closed semantics, MCP-tool coverage, verb-not-field/row scope, `/ui` limitation), cross-linked from `docs/security-posture.md`. **Tests (all no-DB, RAN locally):** `audit.rs` — `deny_readonly_mutation_truth_table`, `newly_classified_mutations_are_mutating_and_covered`, `newly_classified_reads_are_read_only` (+ all existing exhaustiveness guards green). `api.rs` — `readonly_access_recognizes_readonly_markers_and_rejects_admin`, `readonly_access_normalizes_marker_case_and_truthy_spellings` (F2), `classify_route_matches_class_and_precedence`, `classify_route_head_inherits_get_class` (F3), `classify_route_fails_closed_on_unknown`, `route_class_matchers_build_without_conflict`, `normalize_route_template_rewrites_params_positionally`. `mcp_tools.rs` — `tool_kind_is_mutation_classifies_the_read_only_boundary` (F1). `mcp_tools_http_tests.rs` (feature `mcp,unified-dag-execution`) — `readonly_principal_is_denied_mutating_mcp_tools_but_reaches_reads` (403 on start/signal/update/dag-start, reachable on status/watch, admin/unmarked reach all), `role_auth_off_leaves_mcp_tools_ungated`. `contract_regression.rs` — `every_management_route_is_classified` (AC4 sweep), `readonly_role_new_mutations_are_classified_mutating`, `readonly_role_new_reads_are_classified_read_only`, `contract_read_only_flag_matches_classified_routes` (M2). `security.rs` — the headline `eris_readonly_principal_reaches_all_reads_and_no_mutations` (synthetic router over every `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` (method,path); asserts **0 of N mutation routes reachable, N of N read routes reachable** by a read-only principal, and admin reaches everything), `eris_readonly_role_auth_reaches_admin_reads_and_403s_mutations_through_the_nest` (H2 — real `harvest_api_router` + `admin_auth_boundary` + enforce layer, nested under `/api/harvest`, proving the layer is live and reconciled through the nest), `eris_role_auth_off_leaves_the_router_unchanged_through_the_nest`, `eris_readonly_denied_on_unclassified_ui_path_through_the_layer` (L4), `eris_readonly_options_preflight_is_not_denied` (F3), `eris_readonly_post_for_body_read_routes_are_reachable`, `eris_unmarked_and_admin_principals_are_not_verb_restricted`, `eris_readonly_denial_body_is_distinguishable` (AC7 — the mandatory `tracing::warn!` is verified in code; asserting it in the parallel test binary is unreliable due to `tracing` global callsite-interest caching, so the stable 403 body marker is the pinned distinguishability signal). CI-mirror at the pinned toolchain: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo +1.97.0 clippy -p autumn-harvest --all-features --tests -- -D warnings`, `cargo +1.97.0 clippy -p autumn-harvest-plugin --all-targets -- -D warnings` (+ `mcp,unified-dag-execution` / `metrics` / `webhooks` combos), `cargo +1.88.0 check --workspace` — all green. New plugin dependency: `matchit = "0.8"` (same major version axum 0.8 uses; in `Cargo.lock` at 0.8.4).
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Workflow start provenance (`StartSource`) across every start path — see issue #740. **Implemented.** Every workflow execution now durably records *what created it, and from where* — the answer that previously required reverse-engineering `workflow_id` prefixes (`sched:…`) and hand-walking `parent_id`. A new bounded `StartSource` enum (`types.rs`, non-`db`-gated; snake_case serialization; `from_str` falls back to `unknown` and **never errors**) is threaded through `StartWorkflowParams` and `NewWorkflowExecution` and stamped at construction on every start path: schedule tick / backfill / manual trigger-now / Vantage UI trigger → `schedule` / `backfill` (both non-throttled workflow **and** DAG branches, plus the throttled/deferred branch) / manual-trigger with `start_source_ref = schedule_id` and `started_by = operator`; `signal_with_start` / `update_with_start`; completion-trigger (inline + deferred + cross-shard outbox), `start_source_ref = triggering source exec id`; child (fan-out / single / detached), `start_source_ref = parent exec id`; `continue_as_new` — records its **own** `continue_as_new` source (with `start_source_ref = predecessor`), never misattributed as a fresh `api` start (falsified in test by stamping the predecessor a *distinct* `schedule` source and asserting the successor does not inherit it); `reset` — own `reset` source + `start_source_ref = source exec id`; batch (immediate + throttle-carrier branches); generic outbox; inbound webhook (override via `StartWorkflowParams::from_webhook`); the deferred throttle / debounce / batch paths — source is captured at **admission** and restored at **fire** time from the JSONB start-options carrier; workflow-level retry — **inherits** the predecessor's source, so a retried scheduled run stays `schedule`. Pre-upgrade rows report `unknown`. **Storage.** Three additive nullable columns (`start_source`, `start_source_ref`, `started_by`) plus a partial index on `harvest_workflow_executions` (migration `20260712000000_harvest_execution_start_source`), with **no backfill**. The read struct serializes NULL `start_source` as `"unknown"` and omits `start_source_ref` / `started_by` when absent. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant** and no change to the adjacently-tagged event JSON: provenance lives on a row column that is never read on replay, so the value is **replay-safe by construction** and immutable once frozen at start. **Read / query surface.** `GET /workflows?start_source=` filter applied at **both** the standard (`load_workflows`) and stalled (`load_stalled_workflows`) loaders (mirroring the `sla_breached` / `nd_blocked` / `legal_hold` predicates), fanned across shards: an invalid value returns a `400` JSON error (never `500`, never a silent empty match); `?start_source=unknown` matches NULL/pre-upgrade rows via `IS NULL OR = 'unknown'`; a blank `?start_source=` is treated as absent (no filter), matching the `state` / `workflow_name` / `owner` siblings; omitting the param preserves today's behavior. AC4 read-path surfacing on the describe/details API and list rows is automatic (the `WorkflowExecution` read struct is serialized directly). CLI: `harvest workflow list --start-source <value>` + describe passthrough. `docs/api-contract.json` gains the `start_source` param entry. Operator triage stanza added to `docs/runbooks/triage-pending-tasks-idle-workers.md` (find the culprit mechanism during a spawn-storm with one call). **Tests.** AC3 enumeration directly asserts the recorded `start_source` (and predecessor ref for `continue_as_new` / `reset`) for every listed start path, driven via public entrypoints where reachable and the module-local worker harness for the engine-internal insert paths (`continue_as_new`, `child`) — RED→GREEN against Postgres; backfill is asserted through `POST /admin/schedules/{id}/backfill` in the plugin suite (this direct assertion uncovered and fixed a real gap where the two non-throttled backfill branches still carried the neutral `api` placeholder). Filter/describe HTTP integration tests: filter narrows results (proves exclusion), `?start_source=unknown` matches NULL rows, invalid → `400`, absent ref/`started_by` omitted; deferred-carrier restore, webhook override, and workflow-retry inheritance each asserted end-to-end. Full local CI mirror green (`fmt`, per-crate clippy `-D warnings`, MSRV `check --workspace`, DB suites).
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): with-start keyed committed-replay validation ordering — see issue #1092. `signal_with_start_workflow` and `update_with_start_workflow` (the HTTP handlers for the atomic start-or-attach + signal (#244) / + update (#479) primitives) ran their fresh-start-only validation — the #610 payload/schema gate, and for update-with-start the #373 `start_input` schema gate and the #684 semantic validator — **before** their idempotency dedup. So a retry of an *already-committed keyed with-start* — which must replay to its documented no-op — was instead rejected `400`/`422` whenever validation had **tightened** between the original delivery and the retry (a schema published/made stricter, a lowered payload cap, or a validator that would now reject the same args). At-least-once webhook/event retries broke precisely when a schema change landed. Fixed with an early, **read-only** committed-replay probe at each handler's edge (keyed requests only) that short-circuits to the documented replay response BEFORE any fresh-start-only *rejection* — validation AND the #377 admission gate; a probe MISS falls through to the untouched authoritative in-lock path, which reserves the exactly-once signal/update and remains the source of truth for the concurrent-first-delivery race. Mirrors #808 (plain start route) and #1092 (plain signal route). **Core (`execution.rs`)**: promoted the two committed-replay lookups the in-lock dedup already uses to `pub` so the probe and the authoritative dedup share one source of truth (they can never drift): `lookup_idempotent_signal_dedupe`, `lookup_idempotent_update_dedupe`, and the `UpdateDedupeRow` it returns (now a `pub` struct with `pub` fields, deriving `Debug, Clone`). **`signal-with-start` handler**: new `probe_committed_sws_replay` (plugin `api.rs`) fans out across shards via `lookup_idempotent_signal_dedupe`; on a hit it returns `200 { signal_delivered: false }` with a best-effort SUCCEEDED audit (intentional asymmetry with the fresh-start arm's 503-on-audit-failure: the original start was already audited). It runs right after signal-payload extraction, keyed-only, before the #610 signal-payload schema gate. **`update-with-start` handler**: the `update_id` derivation (UUIDv5 over the DNS namespace of the idempotency key) and `probe_committed_uws_replay` are hoisted **above the found-shard scan and the #377 admission gate** (mirroring signal-with-start, whose probe already precedes both), not merely above the #373 gate. The probe fans out via `lookup_idempotent_update_dedupe` and returns the resolved `UpdateWithStartOutcome` (`update_admitted: false`) — which flows through the handler's existing `Ok` arm (polling for the cached update result, writing the SUCCEEDED audit), giving a committed replay the SAME behavior as a fresh admission. The #377 admission gate, the #373 gate, and the #610+#684 blocks are all guarded `if probe_outcome.is_none()` (on a hit the handler short-circuits before the gate; on a miss the gate runs unconditionally for genuinely-fresh work); the authoritative call becomes `match probe_outcome { Some(o) => Ok(o), None => authoritative }`. This closes a P1 review finding: pre-hoist, update-with-start ran the admission gate BEFORE the probe, so a committed keyed replay retried while an operator had RAISED a gate returned a spurious `503` instead of the cached `200`/`update_admitted:false` — divergent from its own signal-with-start sibling and from the #808 invariant. **Fail-closed probes (P2 review finding)**: both probes previously swallowed any per-shard conn-acquire or lookup error into a dedup MISS, then fell through to fresh-start validation — reintroducing the bug under a transient owning-shard error. Both now track a `had_error` flag across the fan-out (three-state: hit / clean-miss / inconclusive): on a hit they short-circuit; a conn/lookup `Err` sets the flag and keeps scanning other shards (a later shard may hold the hit); after a no-hit loop they fail **closed** with a `503` when `had_error`, else return the clean-miss sentinel so the caller runs the authoritative in-lock path. `probe_committed_sws_replay` still returns `Option<Response>` (`Some` now also carries the `503`); `probe_committed_uws_replay` returns `Result<Option<UpdateWithStartOutcome>, Response>` (`Err` = `503`). Deliberately more conservative than #808's plain-start probe — the sibling found-shard scan in both handlers already fails closed on the same error class, and fail-closed preserves the never-reject invariant; a keyed client retries `503` idempotently. **Committed uws replay skips fresh-start shard routing (P2 review finding)**: after the admission-gate hoist above, the `update-with-start` handler still ran the storage-pool lookup, the multi-shard `found_shard` scan, AND `pick_for_new_workflow` on a committed-replay HIT before the later `match probe_outcome` — so a dedupe hit could STILL return `503` (a shard-scan `Err`, or `pick_for_new_workflow` selecting an unavailable shard, in a multi-shard partial outage or terminal-prior case), partially undoing the admission-gate hoist via fresh-start infrastructure. The `(shard, conn, exec_id)` resolution now branches on `probe_outcome.as_ref()`: on a HIT it acquires ONLY the hit execution's OWN shard connection (O(1) from `outcome.exec_id` via `db_conn_for_execution`) for the `Ok` arm's audit + result poll, skipping the scan / admission gate / `pick_for_new_workflow` entirely; on a MISS the full fresh-start routing runs byte-identically. A fresh-shard partial outage can now never `503` a dedupe hit (the #808 invariant: a committed replay is never rejected by fresh-start-only infrastructure). `signal-with-start` was already clean here — its probe returns a finished `Response` and `return`s before the routing scan, so this fix is uws-only. New RED→GREEN proof `uws_committed_keyed_replay_hit_never_503s_on_dead_fresh_start_shard` (`interface_schema_integration.rs`) builds a TWO-shard app (shard 0 live, shard 1 an unreachable URL — mirroring the `workflow_reachability_integration.rs` partial-outage harness) and seeds a TERMINATED prior + committed `UpdateAdmitted` on shard 0: the read-only probe (no state filter) resolves the hit on shard 0, but the fresh-start `found_shard` scan EXCLUDES `TERMINATED`, so pre-fix it reaches the dead shard 1 and returns `503`; post-fix the hit path resolves audit polling on shard 0 via `db_conn_for_execution` and returns `200` (`started_fresh: false`, no second `UpdateAdmitted`). The rest of the `interface_schema_integration` suite (every existing uws committed-replay hit test — attach / running / validator-not-rerun / gate-bypass) stays green, proving the hit-shard audit + polling path is unchanged. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/contract change.** The in-lock exactly-once machinery is untouched — the probe is an additive read-only fast path for committed replays only, never a replacement (two simultaneous first deliveries both miss the probe and are serialized by the in-lock `ON CONFLICT` reserve). The non-keyed and fresh-keyed paths are byte-for-byte unchanged (the probe is keyed-only; a fresh key misses and the existing validation + authoritative path runs). Tests (`autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/interface_schema_integration.rs`, Docker-backed on Linux in CI, manifest line 85; ran green against local Postgres 16): the 4 committed-replay RED→GREEN proofs — `sws_committed_keyed_replay_after_attach_short_circuits_before_schema_gate`, `sws_committed_keyed_replay_after_terminal_fresh_start_short_circuits`, `uws_committed_keyed_replay_after_running_short_circuits_before_validation`, `uws_committed_keyed_replay_validator_not_rerun` — plus the two admission-gate RED→GREEN proofs `uws_committed_keyed_replay_bypasses_a_raised_admission_gate` (new; fails with `503` pre-hoist) and its symmetric guard `sws_committed_keyed_replay_bypasses_a_raised_admission_gate` (both raise a `WorkflowName` gate on the router's own `gate_cache` and assert `200`, not `503`), plus the guard tests `sws_fresh_keyed_malformed_still_400`, `uws_fresh_keyed_malformed_still_400`, `sws_uws_unkeyed_behavior_unchanged`, `uws_paused_fresh_keyed_still_409` proving the fresh/unkeyed/paused paths are preserved. Full 28-test suite green, no regression.
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): workflow-type reachability follow-up: samples, orphan summary, boot gate — see issue #700. Thin follow-up on the already-shipped workflow-type reachability check (issue #520 / Phase 3.35), closing the four re-scoped ACs of #700. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no new route** — this is a read-path (samples + top-level summary) plus a startup-read gate, entirely additive. **AC2 — bounded execution-id samples.** `execution::non_terminal_counts_by_workflow_name` now returns up to `REACHABILITY_SAMPLE_CAP` (=5, documented) representative *non-terminal* execution ids per workflow type via `(ARRAY_AGG(id ORDER BY started_at ASC, id ASC))[1:5]` folded into the existing `GROUP BY` — so an operator can drill straight into a stuck run of an `orphaned` type instead of paginating `GET /workflows`. Terminal executions are excluded by the existing state filter (`RUNNING`/`SUSPENDED`/`PAUSED` only), so a sample never points at a completed run. New `sample_execution_ids: Vec<Uuid>` on `WorkflowTypeNonTerminalCount` (core) and `WorkflowTypeReachability` (plugin); the plugin caps the cross-shard union to the same cap in shard-iteration order — documented as *representative and bounded*, not a guaranteed global-oldest-across-shards set. Empty for `safe_to_remove` types. (The `ARRAY_AGG` slice materialises the full ordered id array per group before slicing — transient memory proportional to group size, acceptable under the < 2 s / 100k-execution budget; the drop-in fallback for very large groups is a `LATERAL (SELECT … ORDER BY started_at LIMIT n)` per group.) **AC3 — top-level orphan summary.** `WorkflowReachabilityReport` gains `orphaned: bool` (true when any type has an `orphaned` verdict) and `total_orphaned_executions: i64` (sum of `non_terminal_count` over `orphaned`-verdict types — a count of stranded *executions*, not types), so a CI/CD gate asserts "zero orphans" against a single field instead of walking `items[]`. Both reflect only the inspected shards; when `status` is `partial`/`unavailable` an unreachable shard could still host an orphaned type. Registered in `management_api_response_fields()` and `docs/api-contract.json` (kept in sync, guarded by `contract_regression`); nested `sample_execution_ids` is documented in the route description (precedent: `next_retry_at`/`input` on `/stack` live in the description, not the top-level `fields` list). **AC4 — boot-time fail-fast (default warn).** New `[harvest.startup] orphaned_workflows = off|warn|fail` config (env override `AUTUMN_HARVEST_STARTUP__ORPHANED_WORKFLOWS`, case-insensitive), mirroring the `require_shard_readiness` precedent. `start_harvest_runtime` runs the gate **before** `HarvestRunner::start` — before any worker poll loop, scheduler, or scanner is spawned, so no task can be claimed or terminally failed when it fires — computing `registered` directly from the owned `built` (workflow-info names UNION unified-DAG names) and querying the single-shard `workflow_reachability::build_reachability_report_single_shard(registered, pool, filter)` core against the runner-resolved shard-0 pool (selected via the shared `pick_runtime_pool_source` + the read-only `select_runtime_shard0_pool`, which installs no process global). It feeds `(report.orphaned, report.status)` into the pure `startup_orphan_decision(action, orphaned, status) -> StartupOrphanDecision` — the single source of the fail/warn/partial policy (AC4 reads AC3's two fields). `off` skips the check; `warn` (default, non-breaking — a mixed fleet mid-rollout must not crash-loop) logs the orphaned types and continues; `fail` refuses startup with a bare `return Err` — the gate runs before the runner, gate-refresh, and outbox are spawned and before any admission globals are published, so a refused boot has nothing to tear down and leaks no background tasks. A failure of the check *itself* only warns (never blocks boot on its own error). **Crash-loop safety:** `fail` aborts **only** when orphaned types are present **and** the report is `Complete`; an incomplete (`partial`/`unavailable`) report always degrades to `Warn` — a boot loop has no human in the loop, so a transient unreachable shard/DB must never hard-fail startup. This is deliberately **asymmetric** with the CLI gate (`harvest workflow-types reachability`), which fails *closed* (exit 2) on a partial report because a human reads its exit code. Truth-table clarification: only a `Complete` report with `orphaned == false` resolves to `Continue` (a *confirmed* clean boot never warns); an incomplete report always warns (see hardening item (7) below). **Architecture deviation (deliberate):** the gate lives in the plugin (`[harvest.startup]` + `startup_orphan_decision`), not on `HarvestBuilder` — the boot gate is a single-shard *pre-runner preflight* over the owned `built` and the runner's shard-0 pool (the plugin is single-shard-only; multi-shard configs are rejected upstream, so it reads the identical rows the started-runtime cross-shard fan-out would), while the cross-shard `GET /admin/workflow-types/reachability` route (`build_workflow_reachability_report`) stays plugin territory and *is* the programmatic embedder access the AC's "e.g. a `HarvestBuilder` method" refers to (both share the `observe_shard` + `build_report_from_observations` helpers, so they cannot drift). **AC9 — runbook.** `docs/runbooks/safe-deploy.md` gains a "Pre-cutover handler-coverage gate" section ahead of the #512 replay canary: its deploy-ladder position (worker drain #386 → this gate → #512 canary → #480 → #614 → #538/#510), the CLI (exit 2 on orphan/partial) and API single-field `orphaned`/`total_orphaned_executions` gate, the per-group `sample_execution_ids` drill-in, and the boot-time `[harvest.startup] orphaned_workflows` option with its crash-loop-safe partial-shard behavior. Cross-linked to `safe-handler-removal.md` (type-level vs build-id vs `ctx.version()` distinction), with a back-pointer added there. **CI:** wired the plugin `workflow_reachability_integration` suite (previously ALLOWLIST debt, only compile-checked) and the new core `workflow_reachability_samples_tests` module into `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`; removed the now-covered ALLOWLIST entry and lowered `ALLOWLIST_MAX_LEN` 74 → 73. **Tests, TDD red→green:** pure unit tests in `workflow_reachability.rs` (samples cap/merge/empty, orphan summary, `startup_orphan_decision` truth table) and `config.rs` (default/TOML/env/unknown-value on both the env AND TOML paths); core DB `workflow_reachability_samples_tests` (executed against Postgres — includes a `samples_are_oldest_first` test seeding staggered `started_at` values in reverse insertion order to pin the `started_at ASC, id ASC` ordering); plugin HTTP `orphaned_group_surfaces_bounded_execution_id_samples` + `endpoint_exposes_top_level_orphaned_and_total` (testcontainers, compile-checked where Docker is unavailable, executed by CI on Linux, per the #543/#544/#601 precedent). **Post-review hardening (consolidated ship-list, PR #1109):** three review lenses + the Gemini bot returned no blockers; the following polish items were applied. (1) **Sample-cap drift guard** — Diesel `sql_query` cannot interpolate the `REACHABILITY_SAMPLE_CAP` const into the SQL string, so the per-shard slice stays a hardcoded `[1:5]` literal; a DB-free guard unit test now fails if the literal and the const drift apart, an inline SQL comment names the invariant, and the const doc was corrected (it aspirationally wrote `[1:REACHABILITY_SAMPLE_CAP]` while the code hardcodes `[1:5]`). (2) **Boot-gate decision coverage** — new `boot_gate_{fail_aborts,warn_allows,fail_allows_clean}` integration tests drive the exact two-step decision path `start_harvest_runtime` composes (`build_workflow_reachability_report` + `startup_orphan_decision`) against a seeded database, each filtering to a unique workflow type for race-free isolation; the private, config/migration/pool-coupled `start_harvest_runtime` shell (thin task-teardown glue over this decision) is not integration-callable. (3) **Default-boot-query cost + drain-first callout** — `safe-deploy.md` now states the reachability check runs **by default** under `warn` on every boot (a bounded cross-shard `GROUP BY … ARRAY_AGG` aggregate; `off` is the only zero-cost setting, the per-group `LATERAL … LIMIT n` fallback bounds memory), and warns that enabling `fail` refuses boot **fleet-wide** until a persistent orphan drains — so confirm `orphaned == false` via the CLI gate before flipping it on. (4) **Readability** — the boot-gate decision compares against the `ReachabilityReportStatus` alias name to match its parameter type, and the cross-shard sample-dedup rationale was corrected (execution ids are globally unique and each lives on exactly one shard). (5) **P1 — run the boot gate BEFORE workers spawn (Codex).** The AC4 gate originally ran *after* `HarvestRunner::start` had already spawned the worker poll loop, so under `orphaned_workflows = fail` + `worker_enabled` a worker could CLAIM and terminally FAIL an orphaned-type execution (no registered handler → `fail_task_and_execution` → `WorkflowFailed` + `FAILED` state) during the boot window, *before* the after-the-fact abort tore the runner down — defeating the gate's protective purpose (default `warn` was unaffected — nothing aborts). Fixed by moving the gate to run BEFORE `HarvestRunner::start` (right after the multi-shard config pre-flight, before any admission globals are published), so no task can be claimed when it fires and an Abort is a bare `return Err` with no runner/gate-refresh/outbox teardown. The gate now calls a new single-shard report core `workflow_reachability::build_reachability_report_single_shard(registered, pool, filter)` that reuses the existing `observe_shard` + `build_report_from_observations` helpers (so it cannot drift from `build_workflow_reachability_report`) but needs NO started runtime: `registered` is derived directly from the owned `BuiltHarvest` (new `BuiltHarvest::workflow_infos()` accessor, workflow names UNION `dags().filter(workflow_handler.is_some())` names — the DAG union replicating `build_workflow_reachability_report`'s registry-key + `registered_dag_names` union exactly, load-bearing because `registry.workflows` omits unified-DAG names), and `gate_pool` is a clone of `harvest_pool` captured before it is moved into the runner resources. The plugin is single-shard-only (multi-shard configs are rejected upstream), so the single-shard report reads the identical rows the started-runtime cross-shard fan-out would. `build_workflow_reachability_report(&HarvestApiState, query)` and the HTTP route are behaviorally unchanged. Crash-loop safety is preserved: a DB read failure encodes as `status == Unavailable` inside the (now infallible) report, and `startup_orphan_decision(Fail, ., Unavailable) == Warn` (never `Abort`). New tests (env-URL local Postgres): `gate_report_core_needs_no_runtime` (structural proof — the abort decision resolves from just a registered set + pool, no `HarvestApiState`) and `gate_is_side_effect_free_orphan_task_untouched` (a seeded orphan's claimable task stays `PENDING`/unclaimed, its execution `RUNNING`, and no `WorkflowFailed` is appended — the deterministic analogue of "no worker touched the orphan run"). **Known follow-up (not fixed here):** the standalone `HarvestRunner::start` embedder path has no orphan gate at all and carries the same latent leak; a separate issue should add an equivalent pre-worker check inside the runner. (6) **P2 — the gate must query the pool the runner will (Codex).** The pre-runner gate cloned its pool from `harvest_pool`, but `PreparedHarvestRuntime::build` gives `WorkerConfig::with_sharded_pool` PRECEDENCE over `harvest_pool` — so a `HarvestBuilder::with_sharded_pool` deployment had the workers poll one database while the gate queried another; under `fail` the gate could validate the wrong DB, miss an orphan, and the worker would then poll+fail it, bypassing the protection. Fixed by extracting the pool-resolution precedence into a **single source of truth**, `runner::resolve_runtime_storage_pool(resources_sharded_pool, worker_config_sharded_pool, harvest_pool)`, called by BOTH `PreparedHarvestRuntime::build` and the plugin gate (the gate feeds it the exact inputs `build` uses — the runner-level override via the new `HarvestRunnerResources::sharded_pool_override()`, which the plugin never sets; WorkerConfig's sharded pool; the `harvest_pool` clone — and then queries `resolved.clone_inner()`, the same default-shard pool the workers poll), so the `sharded_pool`-over-`harvest_pool` precedence can never drift between them. Pinned by `runner::tests::resolve_runtime_storage_pool_precedence` (DB-free — `max_size`-tagged pools assert WorkerConfig's sharded pool wins over `harvest_pool`, a runner-level override wins over WorkerConfig, none falls back to `harvest_pool`) and `gate_resolves_sharded_pool_not_config_pool` (env-URL Postgres — `harvest_pool` unconnectable, the sharded pool the real DB holding the orphan; the decision resolves to `Abort`, only reachable if the shared resolver read the sharded pool's DB, since querying `harvest_pool` would be `Unavailable` → `Warn`). (7) **P2 — an incomplete report must warn, not silently continue (Codex).** A startup DB blip surfaces the single-shard gate as a **successful** report with `status == Unavailable` and no rows, so `orphaned == false`. The prior `startup_orphan_decision` short-circuited `!orphaned → Continue` for every action, so under `fail` a DB blip *silently continued* — no warning that orphan detection never actually ran, contradicting the documented crash-loop-safe intent (degrade an *incomplete* report to a warning rather than ignore it). The "clean boot never warns" deviation over-reached into the "couldn't-determine" case. Fixed the single-source-of-truth `startup_orphan_decision` to the refined table: `Off → Continue`; `Warn`/`Fail` + **incomplete report** (`Partial`/`Unavailable`) → `Warn` regardless of `orphaned` (never `Abort` — crash-loop safety preserved); `Warn`/`Fail` + **complete report** + no orphans → `Continue` (a *confirmed* clean boot never warns); `Warn`/`Fail` + complete + orphaned → `Warn`/`Abort`. Only the cells `(Unavailable|Partial) × !orphaned × (Warn|Fail)` flip `Continue → Warn`; the `Abort` condition is unchanged (`orphaned && Complete && Fail`). This is distinct from the report-builder-`Err` arm (a DB blip is a successful `status == Unavailable` report, not an `Err`), so the fix lives in the decision function. Pinned by a new `unavailable_report_warns_not_silently_continues` truth-table test (both `warn` and `fail` actions, `Unavailable` and `Partial`, `orphaned ∈ {false, true}` → all `Warn`); the existing `fail_aborts_only_on_orphaned_and_complete` / `fail_warns_not_aborts_on_partial_status` / `warn_never_aborts` / `off_skips_entirely` tests stay green unchanged. (8) **P2/P4 — the boot-gate pool selection must be side-effect-free (Codex).** The P2 fix (item 6) had the gate call `resolve_runtime_storage_pool`, whose single-shard case goes `HarvestDbPool::from` → `ShardedDbPool::single`, which **writes the process global `GLOBAL_SHARDED_POOL`**. So the gate's `Abort` (which returns before `HarvestRunner::start` owns anything) left a global installed — a failed second-runtime startup in the same process would point completion-trigger/timeout code at the aborted runtime's DB, breaking the whole point of the early-gate move (an aborting gate must mutate no process global). Fixed by splitting the resolution into two helpers sharing one precedence source of truth (`pick_runtime_pool_source`): `resolve_runtime_storage_pool` (the **install** path, unchanged, used by `PreparedHarvestRuntime::build` on the normal startup path — still installs the global for the single-shard case as intended) and the new `select_runtime_shard0_pool` (the **read** path — returns the shard-0 `DbPool` handle honoring the same precedence but installs nothing: it reads shard 0 from an already-constructed `ShardedDbPool` via `pool_for`, or returns the `harvest_pool` handle directly, and never calls `ShardedDbPool::single`/`from_map`). The gate now calls `select_runtime_shard0_pool`, so it queries the same DB the workers will (P2 preserved) AND installs no global (P4 fixed); the real global install stays exactly where it was in `HarvestRunner::start`, unchanged for the happy path. `HarvestRunnerResources::sharded_pool_override()` now returns a borrow so the gate's selection clones nothing. Pinned by `runner::tests::select_runtime_shard0_pool_precedence` (DB-free — the read selector honors the same precedence as the install helper) and a dedicated own-binary test `gate_no_global_install.rs` (deterministic global state: a fresh process starts with `GLOBAL_SHARDED_POOL` unset; after `select_runtime_shard0_pool` in both the sharded and single cases the global is unchanged, while the contrast call to `resolve_runtime_storage_pool` DOES install it — proving the gate uses the side-effect-free helper).
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Active-workflow population gauge — see issue #770. **Implemented.** New continuously-sampled gauge `harvest.workflow.active` (`METRIC_WORKFLOW_ACTIVE`) reports the count of currently-active workflow executions, labeled by `workflow` (workflow-type name) and `state` (bounded to exactly two values: `running` / `paused`). It is the live in-progress population signal the metric catalogue lacked — a steady rise while `harvest.workflow.terminal` stays flat is the signature of a leak or backlog (starts outpacing completions), distinct from a healthy burst that later drains. **Source & sampling.** A dedicated background sampler `worker::spawn_workflow_active_sampler` (a near-copy of `spawn_history_oversized_sampler`, gated on `metrics.is_enabled()` since it issues SQL) runs on the worker's `poll_interval` and calls `worker::sample_active_workflow_counts`, a shard-local `SELECT workflow_name, state, COUNT(*) … WHERE state IN ('RUNNING','PAUSED') GROUP BY workflow_name, state`. Counts are summed across every shard of the worker's `ShardedDbPool` for a fleet-wide gauge. A read failure on any shard skips the whole tick (never false-clears the gauge during an outage); a `(workflow, state)` pair present last tick but absent this tick is zero-filled so a drained pair falls back to `0` rather than going stale. The emit/skip/ zero-fill decision is the pure, unit-tested `worker::compute_active_gauge_emissions`. **Bounded cardinality.** The `state` label can only ever be `running` or `paused` — enforced by construction via the bounded `worker::ActiveWorkflowState` enum (`from_db_str` maps only `RUNNING`/`PAUSED`, everything else → `None` and is dropped with a debug log as defense-in-depth). Per ADR-0001 §7, `execution.id` is never a label. Total series is bounded by `workflow_types × 2`. `PAUSED` runs (issue #383) count under `state="paused"`; nd-blocked runs (issue #603) stay `RUNNING` and count under `state="running"` — no special handling. **Three-touchpoint metric recipe:** (1) `telemetry.rs` — `pub const METRIC_WORKFLOW_ACTIVE` + `pub const METRIC_LABEL_STATE` + the no-op-default `MetricsRecorder::record_workflow_active(workflow, state: &str, count)` trait method; (2) `metrics_rs_adapter.rs` — the `gauge!` bridge with `workflow`/`state` labels; (3) a real capturing-recorder adapter test asserting the registered gauge key, labels, and `set` value (`5.0`). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no shard-routing/replay change** — read-only over `harvest_workflow_executions.state`, no write path, no event schema surface. **Anti-drift registries:** dashboard panel "Active workflows by type & state" (`docs/dashboards/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json`, `max by (workflow, state)`), `DASHBOARD_PROMETHEUS_SERIES` + `SERIES_LABELS` (`dashboard_pack_docs.rs`), alert rule `harvest_workflow_population_leak` (`docs/alerts/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json`) with a full runbook section (`docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md`), `REQUIRED_ALERTS` + `STABLE_PROMETHEUS_METRICS` (`alert_pack_docs.rs`), README mapping row, ADR-0001 §7 catalogue row, `docs/telemetry.md` call-site + labels tables, `metrics_coverage.rs` `RecordingMetrics` coverage, and a `linux autumn-harvest integration` manifest row for the DB test. **Tests, TDD red→green:** R1 telemetry const/no-op unit tests; R2 bounded-enum `from_db_str`/`as_str` unit tests + R5 `compute_active_gauge_emissions` zero-fill/skip-on-read-failure unit tests (both in `worker.rs`, run under the all-features lib step); R3 capturing-recorder gauge-value bridge test (`metrics_rs_adapter.rs`); R4 DB integration test (`tests/integration/active_workflow_gauge_tests.rs`) asserting the grouped read counts RUNNING/PAUSED per type and excludes terminal executions — executed against a real local Postgres 16.
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): Chain-scoped workflow lifetime cap — see issue #617. A **chain-scoped lifetime cap** (`chain_execution_timeout`) distinct from the per-run `execution_timeout` (#243): it is anchored at the FIRST run's start and CARRIED VERBATIM across every continue-as-new, so a runaway loop cannot escape the cap by continuing-as-new. Enforced by the existing timeout scanner and the existing `WorkflowExecutionTimedOut` event — **no new `WorkflowEvent` variant**. **Storage** (one additive migration `20260714000000_harvest_workflow_chain_timeout`, mirroring #243's dual-column shape): two nullable columns on `harvest_workflow_executions` — `chain_execution_timeout INTERVAL NULL` (the chain-cap DURATION) and `chain_deadline_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL` (the absolute enforcement deadline, `first_run.started_at + chain_execution_timeout`, copied verbatim into every continue-as-new successor). Partial index `idx_harvest_executions_chain_deadline ON (chain_deadline_at) WHERE state = 'RUNNING' AND chain_deadline_at IS NOT NULL`. Both columns added to `schema.rs`, `WorkflowExecution` (read struct — additive serialized fields on the nested `.execution` describe surface, matching the `deadline_at`/`sla_deadline_at` precedent, non-breaking, no contract-registry change) and `NewWorkflowExecution` (insert struct). **Anchor & inheritance rules** (the core semantic): **Fresh chain-origin start** (HTTP start, scheduler tick/backfill, typed stub, etc.): `chain_deadline_at = target_start_time + effective_chain_timeout`. **Continue-as-new successor** (`worker::persist_workflow_continue_as_new`): CARRY BOTH COLUMNS VERBATIM — copy the predecessor's absolute `chain_deadline_at`, never recompute `now + timeout` (the per-run `deadline_at`/`sla_deadline_at` right above it are re-anchored; the chain deadline is not). **Workflow-level retry (#523)** (`worker.rs`): CARRY — `StartWorkflowParams.inherited_chain_deadline_at = exec_ref.chain_deadline_at` used verbatim (a retry is the same logical run continuing). **Reset fork (#148)** (`reset::insert_fork_execution`): RE-ANCHOR — a fresh chain origin (`chain_deadline_at = now + source.chain_execution_timeout`), consistent with `first_exec_id: None`/`schedule_id: None` (the #488 lineage-break precedent). **Child workflow** (`worker.rs`): a fresh chain origin resolving the child's OWN `WorkflowInfo.chain_execution_timeout` at spawn, exactly as it resolves the child's per-run `execution_timeout`/`sla` — awaited children resolve it (`now + effective`); the detached-child path (which resolves no `execution_timeout` at spawn) gets `None`, matching the existing pattern precisely. **Effective resolution + ceiling (AC4 — a deliberate divergence from #243):** the pure `timeout::effective_chain_timeout(workflow, ceiling)` returns the MIN of all present values, and `None` only if both are absent — so the builder ceiling acts as BOTH a cap AND a fleet-wide DEFAULT (`(None, Some(c)) => Some(c)`). This diverges from #243's per-run ceiling (which only caps a *specified* value, `(None, Some) => None`) so an operator can cap every chain even when a workflow under-specifies. Documented in code and `docs/getting-started/07-reliability-knobs.md`. **Config surfaces (AC4):** `#[workflow(chain_execution_timeout = "7d")]` macro attribute (parsed exactly like `execution_timeout`, added to the "unsupported attribute" list); `WorkflowInfo::chain_execution_timeout` field + `with_chain_execution_timeout` fluent builder; `HarvestBuilder::max_workflow_chain_timeout(...)` ceiling + `max_workflow_chain_timeout_ceiling()` accessor (mirrors `max_workflow_execution_timeout`); `WorkflowSchedule::chain_execution_timeout` field + `with_chain_execution_timeout` builder are **currently inert** (not persisted on `harvest_schedules`, not read at tick — at exact parity with #243's own dead `WorkflowSchedule::execution_timeout`; kept for API symmetry). The *functional* schedule-level chain default reaches scheduled runs through the workflow-type `#[workflow(chain_execution_timeout = "…")]` attribute inherited via `WorkflowInfo` at tick, plus the fleet-wide ceiling. **AC4 fleet-wide ceiling threading** (review fix): the ceiling (which doubles as a fleet-wide default) is applied at these ORIGIN start paths — plain HTTP start, signal-with-start, update-with-start, batch start, trigger-now, and workflow backfill (via `HarvestApiState::max_workflow_chain_timeout()`), and the scheduler tick (both the tick-direct and buffered-drain fire sites, tick-throttle and buffered-throttle included) via a new `HandlerRegistry::max_workflow_chain_timeout` field, since the core scheduler has no `api_state`. Debounce/throttle/batch DEFERRED starts carry the declared cap + ceiling through two additive `DebounceStartOptions` fields (`chain_execution_timeout_secs`, `max_workflow_chain_timeout_ceiling_secs`) resolved at admission and threaded at all four fire sites. **Documented limitation (not covered by the fleet-wide default, parity-consistent with their per-run-ceiling treatment):** completion-trigger starts, the Vantage UI manual schedule trigger, the webhook cross-shard outbox, webhook-subscription starts, and the typed Rust client stub's `signal_with_start`/`update_with_start` pass `None`/`None` — a workflow-type `#[workflow(chain_execution_timeout = "…")]` attribute (or the HTTP route) still caps runs from those paths. DAGs carry NO chain cap (the `#[dag]` macro has no chain attr; DAG start paths pass `None`). `StartWorkflowParams` gains three fields (`chain_execution_timeout`, `max_workflow_chain_timeout_ceiling`, `inherited_chain_deadline_at`), defaulted `None` at every construction site except the retry site and the resolving HTTP/scheduler/typed-stub start sites. `WorkflowHandleClient` and the plugin `HarvestApiState` mirror the ceiling (`with_max_workflow_chain_timeout` / `set_max_workflow_chain_timeout` / `max_workflow_chain_timeout()`), wired from `BuiltHarvest::max_workflow_chain_timeout`. **Deliberately NOT threaded into `WorkflowContext`/`ctx.deadline()`/`should_continue_as_new()`** (issue #772 stays bound to the per-run `deadline_at`) — the chain cap is SCANNER-ONLY enforcement, so a runaway loop cannot "escape" it via CAN. **Not shifted on pause/resume** — `chain_deadline_at` is absolute wall-clock (runaway-protection/compliance reading; chain-deadline extension is out of scope). **Scanner (AC2, timeout.rs):** `enforce_workflow_execution_timeouts` selects `state='RUNNING' AND ((deadline_at < NOW()) OR (chain_deadline_at < NOW()))`; the const `workflow_execution_timeout_query()` string reflects the same disjunct. Per expired row, the pure `classify_workflow_timeout(deadline_at, chain_deadline_at, now) -> (fired, TimeoutKind)` decides which fired with **chain precedence** (a chain-only expiry has no per-run `deadline_at` and is handled without panicking). New additive `TimeoutType::WorkflowChain` enum variant (distinct Display "workflow chain lifetime exceeded"; NOT a `WorkflowEvent` variant) used for chain timeouts' error string. **Metric (AC6):** new counter `harvest.workflow.chain_timeout` (`METRIC_WORKFLOW_CHAIN_TIMEOUT`, labels `workflow`/`queue`; additive no-op default `record_workflow_chain_timeout` on `MetricsRecorder`, bridged in `metrics_rs_adapter`). The scanner emits it for `TimeoutKind::Chain` and `harvest.workflow.timeout` for `TimeoutKind::Run`; both still emit `harvest.workflow.terminal{outcome="timed_out"}` (the chain-vs-run distinction lives only in the two timeout counters). Dashboard panel in `docs/dashboards/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json`, catalogue rows in `docs/telemetry.md` and ADR-0001 §7, and the anti-drift `dashboard_pack_docs` coverage gate updated (series + label ground truth). **Backward compatible:** `None` default everywhere; a workflow with no chain cap and no ceiling behaves byte-for-byte as before. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no replay-determinism impact.** **Docs/examples:** `docs/getting-started/07-reliability-knobs.md` (run-cap vs chain-cap decision, runaway-loop story, ceiling-as-default, absolute-wall-clock/pause note); `examples/long_running.rs` (run-cap vs chain-cap usage). **Tests, TDD red→green:** pure unit tests in `timeout.rs` (`effective_chain_timeout` truth table incl. the AC4 divergence, `classify_workflow_timeout` chain-precedence/run-only/chain-only-no-panic, query-const chain disjunct, chain metric name), `error.rs`/`telemetry.rs`/`metrics_rs_adapter.rs` (variant Display, metric const, no-op default + bridge), macro parse + `with_chain_execution_timeout` builder tests (`macros_workflow.rs`); DB integration tests in `tests/integration/chain_timeout_tests.rs` (scanner fires on chain cap where per-run cap alone would not; chain-only expiry no-panic; per-run vs chain counter separation; origin anchor; inherited-verbatim; ceiling-as-default and ceiling-caps-min; and the AC7/AC9 worker-driven money test — a real continue-as-new carries `chain_deadline_at` verbatim, falsifying the re-anchor hypothesis).
- **Phase 3.51** (implemented): `WorkflowIdConflictPolicy` for idempotent plain workflow starts — see issue #685. Splits the single, overloaded `WorkflowIdReusePolicy` into two **orthogonal** axes so an idempotent plain start can express "attach to a currently-running run" without abusing the reuse semantics that were designed for terminal priors: `WorkflowIdReusePolicy` (unchanged, 4 variants) governs **TERMINAL** priors (COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED/TIMED_OUT). New `WorkflowIdConflictPolicy` (`types.rs`, re-exported from `lib.rs`) governs **ACTIVE** (RUNNING/PAUSED) priors: `Unspecified` (default — defer to the reuse policy's native active behavior), `Fail` (→ `Err(AlreadyExists)`), `UseExisting` (attach: return the running handle, `created == false`, no new `WorkflowStarted` event, no task enqueued, no cancel), `TerminateExisting` (cancel + start fresh). Wire values `unspecified`/`fail`/`use_existing`/`terminate_existing`. The two axes **compose** in the start-path admission logic: the conflict axis has no effect on a terminal prior, and the reuse axis has no effect on an active prior (except via the `Unspecified` fallback). Because `Unspecified` maps each reuse policy to its exact documented active behavior (`AllowDuplicate`→Attach, `RejectDuplicate`→Fail, `AllowDuplicateFailedOnly`→Attach, `TerminateIfRunning`→Terminate), **every existing caller is byte-for-byte unchanged (AC-6)**. **Core changes (`execution.rs`):** new pure helpers `ActiveConflictBehavior { Fail, Attach, Terminate }`, `is_active_conflict_state(state)` (RUNNING|PAUSED), `effective_active_conflict_behavior(reuse, conflict)` (all `pub`). `start_will_create_new_execution` gains a `conflict_policy` parameter and branches active-vs-terminal first. `StartWorkflowParams` gains a `conflict_policy: WorkflowIdConflictPolicy` field (swept to `Unspecified` at ~123 literal sites workspace-wide). The start transaction's existing-prior `match` was restructured to branch on active-vs-terminal first: an active prior is resolved by the effective conflict behavior; a terminal prior is resolved by the reuse axis exactly as before. **Admission-gate / pre-check interaction:** the two-transaction `TerminateIfRunning` pre-check cancel and its unlocked POINT-1 gate now fire on `terminate_via_pre_check = (reuse == TerminateIfRunning && effective == Terminate)` — identical to the old `reuse == TerminateIfRunning` for `Unspecified`, and correctly excluding `TerminateIfRunning` + `UseExisting`/`Fail` (so a `UseExisting` override never cancels the prior). A conflict-driven Terminate with a non-`TerminateIfRunning` reuse (e.g. `AllowDuplicate` + `TerminateExisting`) is handled **atomically inside** the start transaction (active branch: `inline_cancel` + `replace_execution`), never via a pre-check cancel that would otherwise route the just-cancelled prior through the reuse policy's attach branch. This deviates from the literal spec's "POINT-1 gates on `effective == Terminate`" (which would wrongly block an attach to a terminal prior); the goal — "the gate is applied exactly when a fresh execution WILL be created, skipped for a genuine attach" — is met precisely. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no persisted field** — `conflict_policy` is a request-time caller concern only, exactly like `reuse_policy`. Plugin/CLI/HTTP wiring of the new axis is a follow-up; the plugin's two `start_will_create_new_execution` call sites and the `#[workflow]` typed-stub currently pass `Unspecified` (behavior-preserving). **Tests:** unit matrix in `execution.rs` (`start_will_create_tests` extended with the active-conflict axis + an explicit legacy-truth-table `unspecified_matches_today` regression guard; new `active_conflict_tests` for the helpers). DB matrix in `integration_e2e.rs`: `conflict_use_existing_running_attaches_no_new_run` (attach, prior stays RUNNING, zero new events), `conflict_use_existing_paused_attaches`, `conflict_terminate_if_running_reuse_plus_use_existing_completed_starts_fresh` and `..._running_attaches` (AC-3 corners, proving the pre-check gate fix), `conflict_fail_running_errors`, `conflict_terminate_existing_running_cancels_and_starts_fresh`, `conflict_unspecified_preserves_allow_duplicate_running_attaches` (AC-6 guard), and `conflict_concurrency_race_use_existing_converges` (the success-metric proof — 20 concurrent `UseExisting` starts against one running prior all converge on the same `exec_id`, zero `AlreadyExists`, zero terminations). `setup_test_db` now honours `HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL` for local-Postgres runs when Docker is unavailable. **Plugin + CLI + HTTP wiring (issue #685, second half)** Exposes and enforces the `conflict_policy` axis on the standalone HTTP start route and the CLI (the core half above landed it behind `Unspecified`-defaulted plugin call sites): **HTTP `POST /workflows/{workflow_name}/start`** (`autumn-harvest-plugin/src/api.rs`): new optional body field `conflict_policy` (`unspecified`|`fail`|`use_existing`|`terminate_existing`), parsed by `parse_conflict_policy` (mirrors `parse_reuse_policy`; unknown value → `400`, echoed). Threaded into **both** the plain and the #808 idempotency-key `StartWorkflowParams`. An attach (`use_existing` over an active prior) returns `200` + `created:false`; a fresh replacement (`terminate_existing`) returns `201`; `fail` over an active prior returns `409`. **`started_fresh` surfacing (AC-4/AC-7):** the no-key success response now includes `started_fresh: Some(start.created)` **only when the request sent a `conflict_policy` field** (even `unspecified`); omitting the field omits `started_fresh` so the response is byte-for-byte identical to a pre-#685/#808 build. **Admin gate (security parity):** the handler's top-of-function admin gate — previously `reuse_policy == terminate_if_running` — now **also** requires admin for `conflict_policy == terminate_existing`, since both can forcibly cancel a live prior. Without admin → `401`. (This closes a privilege gap that would otherwise let `conflict_policy` reach the identical cancel-and-replace behavior without auth.) **Deferred-start mutual exclusion:** a non-default `conflict_policy` combined with a throttle / debounce / batch policy returns `400` (the start is deferred and has no active prior to resolve at request time), mirroring the `idempotency_key`-vs-deferred-start rule. `conflict_policy` + `idempotency_key` compose (allowed). **Contract:** `conflict_policy` added to `management_api_request_fields()` and `docs/api-contract.json` (request field + `401`/`400`/`409` error descriptions + success-note `started_fresh` semantics); `contract_regression` parity guard stays green. **CLI:** `harvest workflow start --conflict-policy <unspecified|fail|use_existing|terminate_existing>` (`autumn-harvest-cli`), mapped 1:1 onto the body field; omitting the flag sends no field. **Docs:** CLAUDE.md "Standalone Start — Conflict Policy" matrix; `docs/getting-started/10-operations.md` "Conflict policies" section. **Tests:** plugin `parse_conflict_policy` unit tests + a DB/HTTP suite `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/conflict_policy_integration.rs` (attach-200, AC-3 terminate_if_running+use_existing corner, fail-409, terminate_existing-201-cancels-prior, omit-preserves-response, unknown-400, throttle-mutual-exclusion-400, no-admin-401, and a 20-way concurrent `use_existing` convergence proof) — wired into `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`. CLI mapping tests (`conflict_policy_tests`) + `contract_coverage` body-field coverage. **Post-review hardening (issue #685 review)** **Capability-precise admin gate (narrowed).** The plugin start handler's admin gate no longer raw-string-matches `reuse_policy == terminate_if_running || conflict_policy == terminate_existing` before parsing. It now parses **both** policies first and requires admin **iff the request can cancel a live run** — i.e. `effective_active_conflict_behavior(reuse, conflict) == ActiveConflictBehavior::Terminate`.
