Emitting in the executor (as an even earlier cut did, via `report_unhandled_signals`) was **upstream** of the ND gate entirely and would re-fire unboundedly during a persistent ND-block. **Known limitation (deliberate, documented):** covers only **Completed and Failed** (a run that reaches a *graceful* terminal via its own logic) — the paths with a driven matcher. **`TIMED_OUT` / `CANCELLED` / `TERMINATED` / parent-close-cascade / history-cap-failure runs with an undrained signal are NOT counted** (a scanner/operator force-kill has no driven matcher to reconstruct the consumed-set, and reconstructing it would need a re-drive; a partial/inaccurate count on a watched SLO metric is worse than none). For the stuck-timed-out case, use the workflow-timeout counter (`harvest.workflow.timeout`) + the stack API instead. `harvest.update.admitted` (`workflow`, `queue` — see the Codex P2 cardinality note below; the update `name` is NOT a label) — a workflow update was durably admitted (`UpdateAdmitted` appended). Emitted **post-commit** at the single admission choke point `store::admit_update_event`, which gained an `Option<&dyn MetricsRecorder>` param and now returns the resolved `(workflow_name, queue_name)`. Threaded through its callers: the HTTP `admit_update` handler and Vantage-UI submit pass the runtime recorder; **the in-process typed client (`handle::execute_update_in_process`) now passes the recorder too** — the client gained a `metrics: Arc<dyn MetricsRecorder>` field wired from the runtime at both `WorkflowHandleClient` construction sites (default no-op), because an in-process admit's *completion* runs through the worker (which emits update.completed/failed), so admitting without recording admitted would leave that path asymmetric; `update_with_start` passes `None` and emits at its own **outer-commit** boundary (gated on `outcome.update_admitted`, labeled by the pre-move `queue_for_metric`) so a rollback never over-counts. `harvest.update.rejected` (`workflow`, `name`) — a workflow update was rejected by its registered validator before admission (a durable pre-admission `422`). Emitted at the two — and, by an independent audit of every `HarvestError::UpdateRejected` construction and every registered-validator invocation, the **only** — durable validator-rejection sites: the `admit_update` and `update_with_start` HTTP handlers. Scope is deliberately limited to **validator** rejections; non-`RUNNING`/paused admission-state conflicts are surfaced as caller errors, not counted here. Not emitted in `WorkflowContext::validate_update` (replay-driven) or `execute_update_in_process` (runs no validator). The scheduler's reuse of the `UpdateRejected` variant for DAG manual-trigger deferral is unrelated and untouched. `harvest.update.completed` (`workflow`, `name`, `queue`) / `harvest.update.failed` (`workflow`, `name`, `queue`) — an admitted update's handler returned success/error (`UpdateCompleted`/`UpdateFailed`). Emitted **post-commit** via the pure, unit-tested `collect_update_result_metrics` helper, which resolves each `RecordUpdateResult` command's `update_id` → update name from the `UpdateAdmitted` events in the loaded history (the command carries only the id). **Fires on every persist path (terminal, suspend, continue-as-new, and the two inline external-signal suspension branches), not just the terminal one.** The primary main-transaction emission (worker `Persisted` arm, post-commit) reads its `RecordUpdateResult`s via the new pure `update_result_command_source(&outcome, &pending_cmds)`: on a **Suspended** outcome the results live in `outcome.commands` (the executor returns `(Suspended{commands}, vec![])`, so `pending_cmds` is empty), on terminal/CAN they ride in `pending_cmds`. An earlier cut collected from `pending_cmds` only and therefore **undercounted the common case** — an update completes and the long-running workflow loops back to a `wait_for_signal`/activity and suspends. The two inline external-signal branches persist their update results outside the main transaction and strip them from the reconstructed suspension, so they emit inline (post-autocommit) via the shared `emit_update_result_metrics` helper. **No emit on the paused-park discard path** (the `ParkedPaused` transaction result returns before the `Persisted`-arm emission). Exactly-once: `RecordUpdateResult` is produced once on live execution (replay short-circuits in `execute_admitted_update`). **Emission discipline:** `record_signal_received` is live-frontier-only by construction (delivery choke point). `record_signal_unhandled` is emitted by the worker **post-commit, only in the `Persisted` arm** when a terminal outcome carries the map — the same durable-commit gating as `harvest.update.completed/failed`, so a `ParkedPaused` discard or a persist failure never over-counts; `WorkflowReplayer` drives the strict/canary executor path (a different function that never populates the map / never reaches the worker), so a replay of an already-terminal history emits zero unhandled samples — AC2, pinned by `replay_of_terminal_history_never_emits_signal_unhandled`. The update counters emit at the same post-commit `Persisted` boundary. Bridged in `metrics_rs_adapter` (`MetricsRsRecorder`) using the existing `METRIC_LABEL_WORKFLOW`/`METRIC_LABEL_NAME`/`METRIC_LABEL_QUEUE` constants (the two signal counters **and `update.admitted`** use `METRIC_LABEL_WORKFLOW`/`METRIC_LABEL_QUEUE` only — no `name`, per the Codex P2 cardinality note below). Two new starter-pack alert rules (`harvest_update_rejected_rate`, `harvest_signal_unhandled_rate` — thresholds documented as starter defaults, not universal SLOs) with full runbook sections; six new dashboard panels (a "Signal & update lifecycle" row) in `docs/dashboards/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json`; ADR-0001 §7 catalogue and `docs/telemetry.md` updated. Tests, TDD red→green (verified RED→GREEN by reverting each fix): `metrics_coverage.rs` (RecordingMetrics impls + reachability + cardinality + exact-bounded-label test); `replay.rs` unit tests for `unconsumed_signals_by_name` (undrained/consumed-by-wait/consumed-by-push-handler/lost-race/multiple-same-name/stashed-but-unconsumed); `executor.rs` tests via `run_workflow_with_state_advancing_clock` proving the terminal outcomes **carry** the map and the executor **emits nothing** (Completed/Failed carry, Suspended does not, recorder sees zero samples); `context.rs` unit tests for the `unhandled_signals` reader; `worker.rs` unit tests for `collect_update_result_metrics` and `update_result_command_source` (the pure test that would have caught the suspend-path undercount), plus `outcome_unhandled_signals_reads_terminal_maps_and_is_empty_otherwise` / `emit_unhandled_signal_metrics_fires_once_per_occurrence` / `emit_unhandled_signal_metrics_is_a_noop_for_the_empty_collected_map` (the pure companions to the Codex-P2 post-commit move: the terminal map is captured before persist, and the `Persisted`-arm emit is a no-op for the empty map a non-terminal / discarded cycle carries); `metrics_rs_adapter.rs` label-content bridge test for all six; `replayer_tests.rs` AC2 test (replay path never emits `signal.unhandled` across ≥5 cycles); doc-enforcement registries in `dashboard_pack_docs.rs`/`alert_pack_docs.rs` extended. DB/worker integration tests: `metrics_integration.rs::update_completed_metric_fires_on_the_suspend_path` (an admitted update that completes while the workflow SUSPENDS emits exactly one `update.completed`) and `nd_block_tests.rs::{genuine_terminal_with_undrained_signal_emits_signal_unhandled, nd_blocked_cycle_does_not_emit_signal_unhandled}` — env-redirectable (`HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL`) so they run against a migrated Postgres without Docker; the suspend-path and genuine-terminal-emits tests were executed green against a real local Postgres 16 (and confirmed RED against a reverted fix), while the ND-block-suppression test (which needs the testcontainer nd-block harness) is compile-checked, its suppression additionally guaranteed by the post-commit `Persisted`-arm placement being strictly downstream of the #603 ND-block gate (the base `divergent_replay_blocks_instead_of_failing` test already asserts `terminal_failed_count == 0` on an ND-block, so the still-later `Persisted` arm is never reached either). **Post-review hardening (Codex P2):** `harvest.signal.unhandled` was initially emitted pre-persistence, co-located with `record_workflow_terminal` (#519), *before* the persist transaction and *before* `check_paused_and_park` could return `ParkedPaused`. On a claimed-then-paused race or a persist failure the counter incremented without a durable terminal event/state, and a retry/resume of that discarded cycle counted the same unhandled signal again. Fixed by mirroring the `harvest.update.completed/failed` discipline exactly: the `unhandled_signals` map is collected into a local (`outcome_unhandled_signals`) *before* the persist transaction moves `outcome`, and `emit_unhandled_signal_metrics` is called *only* in the post-commit `Persisted` arm — reached only after a successful commit, downstream of both the #603 ND-block gate and `check_paused_and_park`. `record_workflow_terminal` (#519) is untouched and keeps its own pre-persist placement. **Post-review hardening (Codex P2 — cardinality):** the initial cut labeled `harvest.signal.received` / `harvest.signal.unhandled` with a `name` (signal name) label. Signals are delivered via the **free-form** route `POST /workflows/{id}/signal/{signal_name}` — the `signal_name` path segment is caller-controlled and, unlike activity names or `#[update]` handler names, has **no declared registry** to bound it, so a caller using per-entity / dynamic signal names would create unbounded metric series (worst for `signal.unhandled`, whose names are by definition the mismatched / unlistened-for ones), violating the ADR-0001 §7 cardinality contract. **Fixed by dropping the `name` label from both signal counters** — they are now labeled `workflow` + `queue` only (both bounded). The signal name remains a span-only attribute on `harvest.signal.deliver`. For `signal.unhandled`, the worker now **sums** the terminal outcome's per-name unconsumed map (`emit_unhandled_signal_metrics`) into one increment per unconsumed occurrence against the single `(workflow, queue)` series, preserving the total unconsumed volume without the unbounded dimension. Per-signal-name diagnostics are explicitly out of scope for this slice (use the per-workflow stack / open-awaitables API). The `MetricsRecorder::record_signal_received`/`record_signal_unhandled` trait signatures dropped the `signal_name` parameter, so a caller-free-form name cannot reach these counters by construction. **AC3 reconciliation (per-name update visibility kept on the resolved counters; every counter bounded by construction).** After the fixes below, **no** `harvest.update.*` counter carries a name that is free-form at emission — so no counter can be driven to unbounded cardinality by a hostile/buggy caller. A boundedness audit found a genuine unbounded risk: the raw route `POST /workflows/{id}/update/{name}` admits **any** name (the validator lookup is best-effort, so an *unregistered* free-form name falls through and is durably admitted), reaching `harvest.update.admitted` with the raw name; the same admitted name then fails the worker's handler lookup (`"update handler '<name>' not found"`), reaching `harvest.update.failed` with the raw name. **Crucial constraint found while fixing it:** update handlers register via *two* paths — declarative `#[update]` (→ `registry.update_handlers`) **and** imperative `ctx.register_update_handler` (→ the per-execution `WorkflowContext`, the common pattern, e.g. `metrics_integration::update_then_suspend_workflow`) — and only the declarative set is visible outside execution. **Bucketing against `registry.update_handlers` would therefore mislabel every legitimately imperatively-registered update as `__unregistered__`** (a worse regression than the theoretical risk; it also fails the existing `update_completed_metric_fires_on_the_suspend_path` label assertion). So each counter is bounded where it can be done *correctly*, and per-name visibility lives on the three post-resolution counters (`completed`/`failed`/`rejected`): **`update.failed`** (the concrete unbounded vector): bounded via the **result**, not the registry. A genuinely-unregistered name is exactly the one whose result is the pure, exact `"update handler '<name>' not found"` error minted by `execute_admitted_update`; the worker's `collect_update_result_metrics` (new pure `is_unregistered_update_failure(name, result)` helper) buckets **only** that case to the new `UNREGISTERED_UPDATE_NAME = "__unregistered__"` sentinel. Every real handler — declarative **or** imperative — keeps its name, because the discriminator is the not-found result, not the declarative registry. This collapses a hostile `POST /update/{RANDOM}` storm's failed samples to one series. **`update.completed`**: inherently bounded — a completed update always ran a real handler, so its name is the app's real handler set. **`update.rejected`**: already bounded — validator rejection fires only for a *registered* handler. **`update.admitted`**: **name dropped — bounded by construction (issue #684, follow-up).** The admission site has no result to key on and cannot see imperative handlers, so it *cannot* bound the name without mislabeling legitimate imperative updates. Rather than carry a raw, caller-controlled name (the earlier "documented residual"), the label is **dropped entirely** — `update.admitted` is now labeled `workflow` + `queue` only (queue is available at both admission sites: `execution.queue_name` in `store::admit_update_event`, `request.queue_name` in `update_with_start`). This is the only way to bound the counter's cardinality by construction. Per-name admission volume is recoverable in practice by correlating with the resolved counters — every real admit resolves to a `completed`/`failed` sample carrying the name, and a hostile-admit storm collapses to `update.failed{name="__unregistered__"}`. The durable `UpdateAdmitted` event always carries the **raw** name (the workflow needs it to resolve its handler); only the metric labels are bounded. **Net cardinality contract:** after this follow-up, **no** signal or update counter carries a name that is free-form at emission — signals are labeled `workflow`+`queue` only, `update.admitted` is `workflow`+`queue`, and `update.completed`/`failed`/`rejected` carry the `name` only after it has been resolved against a real handler (declarative or imperative; `failed` buckets a genuinely-unregistered name to `__unregistered__`). Per-name **signal** observability remains explicitly out of scope (no declared registry exists to bound it).
- **Phase 3.53** (implemented): Auto-heartbeat guard for long-running activities — see issue #682. **Before:** an activity that runs longer than its `heartbeat_timeout` but makes steady progress (a long transcode, a big batch job) had to either sprinkle `ctx.heartbeat(..)` calls through its body or hand-roll a `tokio::select!` + ticker in every such activity, or risk being spuriously reclaimed by the heartbeat-timeout scanner and dead-lettered. **After:** one line — `let _guard = ctx.start_auto_heartbeat_default()?;` — installs a background ticker that keeps the activity's `last_heartbeat_at` fresh for as long as the guard lives. New `ActivityContext` surface: `start_auto_heartbeat(interval)` and `start_auto_heartbeat_default()` (derives `interval = heartbeat_timeout / 3`), both returning a `#[must_use]` RAII `AutoHeartbeatGuard` (re-exported from `lib.rs` and the prelude alongside the sibling RAII handles `TimerHandle` / `Session` / `RaceWinner`); plus a `with_heartbeat_timeout(Duration)` builder and a `heartbeat_timeout` field the worker populates from the task row via the internal `with_heartbeat_timeout_opt` (the single worker.rs edit, on the `new_with_cancellation_check(..)` dispatch builder chain). **#151 read-path preservation.** A liveness-only auto-heartbeat that pings before any manual `ctx.heartbeat(..)` persists a JSON `null` into `harvest_task_queue.heartbeat_details`; a `start_to_close`/crash reclaim that preserves that column (the #151 contract) would then feed `null` back to the retry. `heartbeat_details::<T>()` now treats a stored JSON `null` as *no checkpoint* (`Ok(None)`) rather than a hard `Serialization` error — so a liveness ping never flips the documented `Ok(None)` resume API into a failure (and potential DLQ) or masks a real checkpoint. **Design.** The guard spawns a ticker on `self.cancel.child_token()`, so cancelling the activity's own token auto-stops the ticker while the handler still observes cancellation through `is_cancelled()` / `check_cancellation()` (the guard never swallows it). Dropping the guard — typically when the handler returns — cancels the child token and aborts the ticker. Each tick re-sends the activity's most recent heartbeat payload from a shared last-payload cell that `heartbeat()` now writes on every call (last-write-wins); the cell is seeded from the previous attempt's resume snapshot (`heartbeat_details`) so the first liveness ping preserves — rather than clobbers — the durable checkpoint used by `heartbeat_details()` on a later retry (issue #151 contract). With no manual heartbeat and no resume snapshot the liveness ping is a JSON `null`. A closed heartbeat channel makes the ticker `break` (never `.unwrap()`/panic); a zero-period interval is clamped to 1ms (a zero `tokio::time::interval` panics). **Guardrails.** Both methods reject with `HarvestError::Config` on a local activity or a no-flusher context (heartbeats are unsupported there), and reject when no `heartbeat_timeout` is configured — an auto-heartbeat whose liveness pings are never checked by the scanner would be a silent no-op, so the caller is told to configure `#[activity(heartbeat_timeout = "..")]`. **Liveness tradeoff (documented on both methods):** auto-heartbeat keeps a *progressing-but-not-manually-pinging* activity alive, but necessarily weakens heartbeat-based wedge detection for a live-but-deadlocked future. The independent `start_to_close` / `schedule_to_close` timeouts remain the hard wedge ceiling and are unaffected by heartbeats — pair auto-heartbeat with a `start_to_close` for a guaranteed runtime upper bound. **Invariants:** no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no management-API surface, no scanner/flusher/schema change. The timeout scanner (`timeout.rs`) and the batched heartbeat flusher (`heartbeat.rs`) are untouched — the guard simply feeds the existing flusher channel. **Tests.** Pure unit tests in `context.rs` under paused-clock time (`start_paused = true`): ticking sends payloads, guard-drop stops the ticker, cancellation stops it while `is_cancelled()` stays true, closed-channel exits cleanly (`AutoHeartbeatGuard::into_join_handle().await` returns `Ok(())` — a stronger no-panic proof than `is_finished()`, which is also true for a panicked task), last-write-wins re-send, liveness-only `null` ping, the require-`heartbeat_timeout` rejection (message-pinned) and the local/no-flusher rejection, the AC#2 `heartbeat_timeout / 3` interval derivation (a 9s timeout pings at exactly 3s — distinguishing `/3` from `/2`, `/1`, `*3`), the AC#4 #151 seed-from-resume-snapshot (the first liveness ping re-sends the resumed checkpoint, not `null`), and the stored-`null`→`Ok(None)` read-path. DB integration tests in `tests/integration/auto_heartbeat_tests.rs`: `auto_heartbeat_prevents_spurious_heartbeat_reclaim` drives a real worker + background timeout scanner and proves a long-running activity that only auto-heartbeats is never reclaimed via `TimeoutReason::Heartbeat` and completes (AC#8, success metric; widened freshness margin — 6s window, 2s interval — for CI headroom); `fresh_heartbeat_does_not_defeat_start_to_close` is a pure, deterministic scanner proof that a fresh `last_heartbeat_at` (what auto-heartbeat produces) shields the heartbeat timeout but NOT the independent `start_to_close` ceiling — and that a stale heartbeat IS reclaimed as `Heartbeat`, so the protection is real; `auto_heartbeat_activity_still_reclaimed_by_start_to_close` is the end-to-end complement — a real auto-heartbeating activity that wedges past a tight `start_to_close` is still reclaimed as `StartToClose` (never `Heartbeat`) and the workflow fails, the airtight full-composition proof. Example: `autumn-harvest/examples/auto_heartbeat.rs`.
- **Phase 3.54** (implemented): Update admit→terminal latency histogram — see issue #781. **Observability** (implemented): Closes the residual of issue #781 (PR #1032 shipped the six `harvest.*` signal/update lifecycle **counters**; this adds the remaining success metric — a p99 admit→complete latency panel). New histogram `harvest.update.duration` (`METRIC_UPDATE_DURATION`) records the wall-clock seconds from an update's durable admission (`UpdateAdmitted`) to its terminal result recording (`UpdateCompleted`/`UpdateFailed`). **AC: no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no macro-path change** — a pure additive-metrics slice modelled on the #519/#487 recipe (additive no-op-default trait method + `metrics_rs_adapter` bridge + coverage tests). **Naming / family:** shipped as `harvest.update.duration` (family-consistent with #1032's `harvest.update.*` counters, NOT the issue's literal `harvest.workflow.update.duration`). Prometheus series `harvest_update_duration_{bucket,count,sum}`. **Labels — `workflow`, `name`, `queue`, `outcome`** (all bounded; `execution.id`/`update_id` never a label, ADR-0001 §7). Mirrors the exact label vocabulary of the `harvest.update.completed`/`failed` counters (`workflow`, `name`, `queue` — the update name resolved to the registered/imperative handler set, an unregistered raw-route name bucketed to the `__unregistered__` sentinel by the shared `collect_update_result_metrics`), plus an `outcome` label (`completed`/`failed`) so one histogram covers both terminal kinds. **Rejected updates are excluded** — no handler runs, so they never enter the histogram. **Duration source:** the admit timestamp comes directly from the `UpdateAdmitted.timestamp` field already present in the loaded `history_events` slice (no new event variant, no timestamped-history load). The terminal time is `Utc::now()` at the post-commit emit (`UpdateCompleted`/`UpdateFailed` carry no timestamp). New pure, unit-tested helper `worker::update_admit_duration_secs(admit_ts: Option<DateTime<Utc>>, now) -> Option<f64>` computes `(now - admit).max(ZERO)` in seconds — a clock-skew negative delta **clamps to `0`** (never a garbage/negative sample), and a `None` admit (the admit could not be resolved from history) **skips the histogram sample entirely** (the counter still fires with name `"unknown"`). **Emission point (piggybacks on #1032's exact path — inherits its delivery semantics):** `collect_update_result_metrics` was extended to carry the admit `Option<DateTime<Utc>>` alongside each `(name, completed)` pair, and `emit_update_result_metrics` now captures one `now` per cycle and calls `record_update_duration(workflow, name, queue, outcome, secs)` alongside the existing completed/failed counter emit — at all three call sites (the terminal/suspend `Persisted` arm and the two inline external-signal branches). No separate `is_replaying` gate: `RecordUpdateResult` is produced only on live execution and the emit is only post-commit, so exactly-once is inherited by construction. **Delivery semantics (documented by reference to the #684 counters, not over-claimed):** exactly-once on the happy path; a crash after the persist commit but before the post-commit emit drops the sample (at-most-once for that window, never a double-count). **`metrics_scrape.rs` — deliberately OMITTED (with justification):** the plugin's built-in Prometheus scrape recorder is per-metric hand-maintained (only `workflow_duration`/`activity_duration` histograms have a field + `record_*` override + `push_histogram` call; there is no generic histogram render path). The #1032 update lifecycle **counters are entirely absent** from it — the `HarvestMetricsRecorder` impl implements no `record_update_*`, so all update metrics fall through to the trait no-op and are exposed only via the `metrics-rs` adapter path. Adding `harvest.update.duration` there would be the lone update-family metric in the scrape recorder, inconsistent with its five sibling counters; omission is the consistent choice (the `_bucket` p99 series comes from the metrics-rs Prometheus exporter regardless). Bridged in `metrics_rs_adapter` (`MetricsRsRecorder::record_update_duration` → `histogram!` with the `METRIC_LABEL_WORKFLOW`/`METRIC_LABEL_NAME`/`METRIC_LABEL_QUEUE`/`METRIC_LABEL_OUTCOME` constants). One new dashboard panel (id 908, "Update latency (admit → terminal)") in the "Signal & update lifecycle" row of `docs/dashboards/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json` — p99 `histogram_quantile` over `_bucket` plus a bucket-less `_sum`/`_count` avg fallback, mirroring the `harvest_workflow_pause_duration` panel. **No alert rule added** — panel only (an arbitrary latency threshold is a review-time decision). ADR-0001 §7 catalogue, `docs/telemetry.md` (emission-points + labels tables), and the CLAUDE.md telemetry module row updated; anti-drift coverage extended (`DASHBOARD_PROMETHEUS_SERIES` + `SERIES_LABELS` in `dashboard_pack_docs.rs`). Tests, TDD red→green (verified RED via compile errors + a live anti-drift failure): telemetry constant-name + no-op-default unit tests; `metrics_rs_adapter` label-content bridge test (`bridges_update_duration_histogram_with_bounded_labels`, via `metrics::with_local_recorder`); `worker.rs` pure unit tests (`update_admit_duration_secs` none/positive-delta/negative-clamp, and `collect_update_result_metrics_carries_admit_timestamp` — plus the four existing collect tests updated to the 3-tuple); `metrics_coverage.rs` reachability + bounded-label test (`update_duration_histogram_reachable_with_bounded_labels`); `dashboard_pack_docs.rs` anti-drift gate (panel + series + labels). All executed green in the sandbox (no-DB surfaces); the worker pure helpers run under `--features db --lib` without a live database.
- **Phase 3.55** (implemented): Run WASM-sandboxed polyglot activities inside the Rust worker — see issue #965. **R&D spike (not a committed GA feature)** proving polyglot activities: an activity implemented as a WebAssembly module — compiled from any guest language — runs sandboxed, metered, and hot-swappable inside the existing Rust worker, dispatched through the **standard task-queue path** (JSON in, JSON out, honouring the activity's queue/retry/start-to-close exactly like a native activity). One fleet, any guest language, capability-based sandboxing, per-invocation resource metering, and content-hash hot swap — capabilities no per-language-SDK durable-execution engine offers. Everything is behind the `wasm-activities` Cargo feature; the **default build carries zero new dependencies and is byte-for-byte unchanged** (the feature adds `wasmtime 46` + `wat`, and implies `db`). **Runtime (`src/wasm_activities.rs`).** A wasmtime 46 `Engine` configured once for deterministic resource bounding — `consume_fuel` (per-instruction CPU) + a single global epoch ticker (`harvest-wasm-epoch`, `increment_epoch()` every 1 ms) for wall-clock interruption + `StoreLimits` for a linear-memory ceiling. Each invocation gets a fresh `Store` with its own fuel budget and an **independent** wall-clock deadline: the store arms `set_epoch_deadline(1)` and installs an `epoch_deadline_callback` that, on every tick, compares `Instant::now()` against a per-invocation `hard_deadline` (`Instant` captured at dispatch, `checked_add`ed with the effective ceiling) and either interrupts or extends by one more tick. Bounding by **elapsed time**, not by a countdown of tick callbacks, is load-bearing: the epoch ticker fires every 1 ms but a guest only *observes* it at wasmtime's instrumented check points, so a single long bulk-memory instruction (a 16 MiB `memory.fill`) runs to completion between two checks and a tick-countdown deadline overshoots by that instruction's cost. Measured overrun of the old tick-countdown form was bounded at **1.2–2.3x** (each `memory.fill` is its own check point, so it does not compound) — not unbounded, but the documented ceiling is now exact rather than approximate (`wall_clock_ceiling_bounds_elapsed_time_not_callback_count`). N concurrent guests each get their own deadline off the same monotonic clock — one guest's expiry never trips another's (`concurrent_deadlines_are_independent`). The wall-clock ceiling (`max_wall_clock`, default **300 s**) is **mandatory**: a guest can spin without consuming fuel, and it runs on `spawn_blocking` and cannot be torn down before the ceiling — so fuel alone can never guarantee termination. **Guest ABI is core-WASM + JSON over linear memory:** the guest exports `memory`, `alloc(len)->ptr`, and `run(in_ptr,in_len)->i64` (packed `(ptr<<32)|len`); the host reinterprets the return as `u64` before shifting and bounds-checks every read/write against live guest memory (an OOB `(ptr,len)` is a typed `WasmTrap`, never a host OOB read). **Sandbox is deny-all by default:** a fresh empty `Linker` links a host function only for a capability explicitly granted via `WasmCapabilities` (`allow_clock`/`allow_random`/`allow_env` allowlist); filesystem and network are **not grantable** (no host function backs them), so any guest importing them is denied at instantiation. The granted `env::random_u64` host fn seeds each store's PRNG from a process-global `AtomicU64` counter itself seeded once from `rand::random::<u64>()`, so two processes (and two invocations) never replay the same draw sequence — an ungated fixed constant would make a guest's "randomness" predictable across the fleet (`rng_seed_stream_is_not_a_fixed_process_constant`). Classification is **precedence-ordered**: a `SandboxDenied` instantiation failure is returned *before* the cancellation/deadline reclassification, so a guest that imports a denied capability while its workflow is concurrently cancelled still surfaces the non-retryable denial rather than a retryable cancellation (`sandbox_denial_outranks_a_concurrent_cancellation`). **Storage + dispatch seam (`src/wasm_store.rs`).** Modules are content-hash (SHA-256) versioned and distributed via Postgres — no CDN/S3/broker in core. Table `harvest_wasm_modules` (the single additive migration `20260711000000_harvest_wasm_modules`) has a **composite PK `(hash, activity_name)`** so identical bytes bind to two names independently, plus a **partial unique index `WHERE active`** guaranteeing at most one active version per name. `publish_wasm_module` serialises concurrent publishes for the same name with a per-name transaction-scoped `pg_advisory_xact_lock`, so two workers converge on exactly one active row. `resolve_wasm_dispatch` is **resolve-hash-first**: it resolves the active hash cheaply and serves a compiled module from the in-process content-addressed cache, fetching bytes **only** on a cache miss. Hot swap is atomic and restart-free — a new publish flips the active row; the next attempt sees it while an already-resolved in-flight attempt keeps running its pinned compiled module (`in_flight_dispatch_is_pinned_across_a_mid_flight_republish`). **Startup-seed is wired into `Worker::run`** (`seed_registered_wasm_modules`, the single startup batch helper — SEED not-clobber semantics: activate-only-if-no-active-version, so a restarted older worker cannot flip a hot-swapped shard back to its embedded version), so an embedder gets a working WASM activity by calling `HarvestBuilder::wasm_activity(WasmActivityRegistration::new(...))` alone. The always-activate `publish_wasm_module` remains the operator hot-swap primitive. `MAX_WASM_MODULE_BYTES` (32 MiB) is enforced before any hashing or DB work. `WasmActivityRegistration` carries the per-activity dispatch knobs a WASM activity can honour — `queue`, `max_attempts`/`retry`, `start_to_close`, and (added in review) `schedule_to_close` (`with_schedule_to_close`, `None` by default) — threaded into the generated `ActivityInfo` so a WASM activity gets the same cross-retry wall-clock deadline (#378) a native `#[activity]` does. The knobs deliberately **omitted** (heartbeat timeout, circuit breaker, rate limits, per-activity payload caps, `schedule_to_start`) are enumerated with rationale on the struct's docs — a WASM guest cannot heartbeat, so silently accepting a heartbeat timeout would be worse than not offering one. **Typed failures, no new event surface (AC6).** Every guest-controlled failure maps to a typed `ActivityFailure` recorded as an **ordinary `ActivityFailed`**: sandbox denial → non-retryable `SandboxDenied`; fuel/wall-clock/memory-growth → retryable `ResourceExhausted`; trap/ABI-violation/non-JSON-output/contained host-glue panic → retryable `WasmTrap`; plus `WasmModuleUnavailable` / `WasmModuleInvalid` (non-retryable) / `WasmModuleLookupFailed` (retryable) for the storage layer. A host-glue panic is caught (`catch_unwind`), so a guest can never crash the worker and a runaway module never trips the poison-pill quarantine (#367). A WASM activity is **indistinguishable from a native one in history**: it records the same `ActivityScheduled`/`ActivityCompleted`/`ActivityFailed` events. **Zero new `WorkflowEvent` variants, zero replay impact, exactly one additive migration.** (The memory-growth classification is a string match on the wasmtime error Debug form, guarded by a test — revisit on a wasmtime bump.) **R&D exit criteria (AC8).** Written recommendation in `docs/rnd/wasm-activities-spike.md` covering runtime choice (wasmtime vs wasmer), core-WASM vs component-model ABI, guest interface shape (JSON-over-buffer vs WIT-typed), the **partial** heartbeat/cancellation story (timeouts delivered via epoch/fuel; cooperative heartbeat/cancel host imports are the biggest GA gap — a "cancelled" guest holds a blocking thread until its ceiling), the measured cold-start/instantiation cost, the security posture, and the storage/distribution model — all backed by the working spike. **Success metric — met.** `runs_one_native_and_one_wasm_activity_to_completion` drives a single workflow running **1 native + 1 WASM** activity to COMPLETED through the real worker loop, asserting both outputs are correct **and** that history carries only ordinary `ActivityScheduled`/`ActivityCompleted` (no wasm-specific type). The `#[ignore]`d `dispatch_overhead_wasm_echo_vs_native` microbenchmark measures per-invocation overhead of a **cached** echo (compilation excluded) vs a native closure and now **asserts** the issue's `< 10 ms` p99 budget rather than only printing it: measured WASM p99 ≈ 474 µs, native p99 ≈ 5 µs, **overhead p99 ≈ 469 µs — ~21× under the < 10 ms target** (debug build, so a release worker is faster). The sandbox suite denies 100 % of ungranted FS/network/env attempts. **Example.** `autumn-harvest/examples/wasm_activity.rs` (`required-features = ["wasm-activities"]`) assembles a WAT guest inline via `wat::parse_str`, registers it via `HarvestBuilder::wasm_activity(...)`, and demonstrates a capability grant and a sandbox denial. `autumn-harvest/examples/wasm-guests/` holds the WAT guest source (`echo.wat`, now the single source of truth `include_str!`d by both the example and the integration suite — no more drifting inline copies), an AssemblyScript guest (`echo.ts`) implementing the same `alloc`/`run` ABI **plus its committed `asc`-compiled `echo.wasm` artifact**, and a `README.md` documenting the ABI, the `asc` build command, and why a real-toolchain guest is worth testing alongside hand-written WAT. That AssemblyScript guest is **executed end-to-end in CI** (`worker_runs_an_assemblyscript_compiled_guest_to_completion`), which is what actually substantiates the polyglot claim — and it immediately earned its keep: `asc --runtime stub` emits a module with **zero initial memory pages**, so a naive bump-pointer `alloc` handed back an out-of-bounds address and the first run failed with a `WasmTrap`. A hand-written `.wat` guest declaring `(memory 1)` can never surface that class of bug. The guest's `alloc` now grows linear memory before returning. **Test evidence (recounted precisely — verified by `cargo test` name enumeration, not estimated).** **70 unit tests** across the `wasm` filter: **45** in `src/wasm_activities.rs` (runtime: deadline math, hash/cache, echo round-trip, the three sandbox-deny categories, the three capability grants + in-band env denial, fuel/memory/wall-clock/mandatory-ceiling exhaustion, concurrent-deadline isolation, the elapsed-time wall-clock bound, RNG seed-stream variation, sandbox-denial precedence, and the containment suite), **15** in `src/wasm_store.rs` (registration defaults/setters incl. `schedule_to_close`, binding projection, size cap), plus 2 in `worker.rs`, 2 in `builder.rs`, and 6 in `failure.rs`. **26** tests in `tests/integration/wasm_activities_tests.rs` — **25 run in CI** via the `linux autumn-harvest integration wasm-activities wasm_activities_tests` manifest row (storage round-trips, hot-swap + single-active + composite-PK independence, the concurrent-publish race, oversized-module reject, startup-publish, `resolve_wasm_dispatch` unavailable/invalid/invoke, the worker-e2e echo, the **AssemblyScript-compiled guest e2e**, the sandbox-denial terminal, the in-flight pin, the **live-worker hot swap reaching the next attempt without a restart** (asserted within `< 5 s`), the fuel-retry — which also asserts `crash_strikes == 0` and zero DLQ rows, proving a runaway guest never trips the poison-pill quarantine (#367) — and the 1-native + 1-WASM success-metric e2e) plus 1 `#[ignore]`d overhead microbenchmark. All integration tests **ran green against a local Postgres 16** during development (via `HARVEST_TEST_DATABASE_URL`); CI executes them Docker-backed via the manifest row. CI additionally runs the `wasm_activity` example under the feature on Linux, so the documented embedder entry point is compile- and run-checked rather than prose-only. The `wasm-activities` feature is out of the default build, so the default build and `cargo tree -i wasmtime` (default features) are unchanged / empty. **MSRV note:** the feature has an effective MSRV of **1.94** (wasmtime 46.0.1's own minimum), distinct from the crate's core MSRV of **1.88** — the default build and the CI MSRV job (`cargo check --workspace`, default features) never compile wasmtime and are unaffected, so the crate continues to advertise `rust-version = 1.88.0` for every non-`wasm` consumer.
- **Phase 3.56** (implemented): DAG node input binding: pass data between graph nodes — see issue #702. A `#[dag]` node's activity is fed the DAG's *trigger input* (wrapped in a `{ "conf": …, "dag_task": "<name>" }` envelope), **not** the output of the upstream node it depends on — so a classic `extract → transform → load` pipeline, where each stage consumes the prior stage's output, forced authors to flatten the pipeline into one mega-activity or hand-thread outputs through shared state. **Node input binding** closes that gap: bind a node's activity input directly to one or more upstream node outputs, one builder call per data edge, zero hand-written output-threading. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, core-only** — node inputs are computed deterministically in the workflow body from already-recorded `ActivityCompleted` outputs (frozen in `harvest_events` before the bound node is dispatched), so replay reconstructs byte-identical inputs on every worker and every pass. Bindings take effect on the unified workflow-execution path (`unified-dag-execution`). **API — three fluent `DagTaskRef` methods** (all by-value `self -> Self`): `.input_from(&upstream)` — the bound activity receives that upstream's recorded output **verbatim** (`DagInputBinding::Single`). No `conf`/`dag_task` envelope (AC2). `.input_from_all(&[&a, &b])` — a JSON object merging every upstream's output, keyed by each upstream's **activity name** (`DagInputBinding::Merged`). `.input_from_aliased(&[("k", &up), …])` — the same merge, keyed by the **given alias**. New public types re-exported from `autumn_harvest`: `DagInputBinding { Single(usize), Merged(Vec<DagMergeSource>) }` and `DagMergeSource { key: String, upstream_index: usize }`. **Binding implies the dependency edge (AC4).** Each method auto-adds the upstream to `task.upstreams` (deduped), so no separate `.upstream(&up)` is required — a binding *is* a data edge, and the bound node runs only after its bound upstream(s) have recorded their outputs. An extra explicit `.upstream(&up)` is harmless. This is the faithful reconciliation of AC4's "binding implies a dependency edge": the edge is auto-added at bind time rather than requiring a literal `.upstream(…)` (or a macro-level error for its absence). Binding edges accumulate across calls while the binding itself is last-wins, so a bound upstream also appears in the node's `.condition(|ups| …)` slice in builder call order. **Semver.** Adding a `pub input_from` field to `DagTask` and new variants to the (non-`#[non_exhaustive]`) `DagBuildError` is a minor addition that is breaking only for a downstream exhaustive `match` on those types — consistent with the repo's existing `WorkflowInfo`/`ActivityInfo` public-field-addition norm. **Raw output vs. the trigger-input `dag_task` wrapper (AC2/AC3).** At runtime the unified level walker (`run_unified_dag`) resolves a bound node's activity input via the pure `bind_activity_input(binding, &outputs)`: the raw upstream output for `Single`, or a keyed `serde_json::Map` for `Merged` — with **no** `dag_task` injection and **no** `conf` wrapping. The unbound branch (trigger-input + `dag_task` envelope) is left byte-identical, so an unbound DAG is unchanged (AC3, regression-guarded). **Skipped/failed upstream → deterministic `Value::Null` (AC6).** The `outputs` vector is initialized to `Value::Null` per node, and a skipped-or-failed node never overwrites its slot, so a binding to such an upstream contributes `Value::Null` — never a missing key. A bound node whose upstream was skipped is itself skipped by default; give it `TriggerRule::AllDone` to run anyway and branch on null-vs-payload. **Five build-time error guards** (all in `DagBuilder::build`, caught at compile-of-the-DAG time, never at run time): `DagBuildError::ConflictingInputBinding { task }` — a node declares both an `input_from` binding and a mapped upstream (`.map_activity(…).over(…)`); the two are contradictory input sources. `DagBuildError::DuplicateInputBindingKey { task, key }` — a `Merged` binding has a repeated key: two upstreams sharing an activity name via `input_from_all`, or a repeated alias via `input_from_aliased`. `DagBuildError::EmptyInputBinding { task }` — a `Merged` binding has no upstream sources (an empty `input_from_all(&[])` / `input_from_aliased(&[])` would deliver an empty JSON object). `DagBuildError::InputBindingOnGate { task }` — a signal-gate node declares an `input_from*` binding; a gate dispatches no activity, so the binding is the same category as a binding on a `map_activity` node (`ConflictingInputBinding`) and is rejected. `DagBuildError::InputBindingNotAnUpstream { task }` — a bound source is not a declared upstream; unreachable via the public API (bindings auto-add the edge), validated defensively. An `input_from*` on a signal-gate node is a build error (`InputBindingOnGate`). This closes a review finding: a gate dispatches no activity, so the binding *value* is ignored — but unlike the inert activity-only setters (`.queue()`, `.retry()`, `.start_to_close()`), a binding also auto-adds a dependency edge, which would silently make the gate wait for that upstream before its signal wait. That stray edge is a *structural* effect the earlier "silently ignored" framing hid, so the binding is now rejected rather than swallowed. Use `.upstream()` to add a gate dependency deliberately. **Test evidence — 17 tests (9 unit + 8 integration), TDD-verified.** Unit tests in `dag.rs` cover single/merged binding storage + auto-added edge, activity-name vs. alias keying, all four build-error guards (incl. the empty-binding guard for both `input_from_all(&[])` and `input_from_aliased(&[])`), and that a binding *appends* its edge without reordering prior `.upstream()` edges — so a `.condition(|ups| …)` sees `ups[0]` determined by builder call order (asserted both on the stored `upstreams` vector and via `dispatch_decision`). Integration tests in `tests/integration/dag_input_binding_tests.rs` (`unified-dag-execution` + `testing`, no DB) cover a bound node receiving the raw upstream output live (AC2), a merged binding delivering a keyed object, a bound-to-skipped-upstream yielding null (AC6, condition-skip branch), a bound-to-**failed**-upstream yielding null (AC6, failed branch — live plus a deterministic `WorkflowFailed` replay of a hand-built `ActivityFailed`-without-`ActivityCompleted` history), an unbound DAG staying byte-identical (AC3, regression guard), a bound ETL history replaying deterministically (AC5), a 2-source **1000-replay sweep** with randomized within-level completion order, and a stronger 3-source **1000-replay sweep** rotating the within-level completion order through all 6 permutations — both asserting `ReplaySucceeded` (and thus correct merged keys regardless of completion order) on every iteration. Example `autumn-harvest/examples/dag_data_flow.rs` (a three-stage ETL plus a fan-in merge) carries three additional embedded `WorkflowTestEnv`/`WorkflowReplayer` self-check tests. Docs: "Passing data between nodes (node input binding)" in `docs/getting-started/08-dags-and-schedules.md`.
- **Phase 3.57** (implemented): Live workflow output streaming via `ctx.publish_progress` — see issue #791. **Before:** a workflow author building an AI agent, a long-running import, or any interactive flow had **no way to push incremental, author-defined business output** to a waiting client while the run is in flight. The only surfaces were a query handler (pull, snapshot-only), `set_current_details` (a single overwriting status string, #473/#593), or — for operators only — the admin-gated engine-event SSE tail (#324), which streams `ActivityScheduled`/`ActivityCompleted` *machinery*, not the author's content. Streaming tokens / reasoning steps / per-item progress to an end user meant standing up an external message bus. **After:** one replay-safe method — `WorkflowContext::publish_progress(chunk: impl serde::Serialize) -> HarvestResult<()>` — emits an ordered, author-defined chunk from live workflow code, delivered to a subscriber on the new SSE route `GET /api/harvest/workflows/{id}/stream` over the existing Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY plumbing. **Ephemeral, best-effort, product-UX channel** — not an audit record: chunks are dropped when no subscriber is connected; the durable workflow *result* remains authoritative. **Determinism / append-only invariant — the load-bearing property.** The call is a **pure side effect gated on `is_replaying()`**: on a replay pass it returns `Ok(())` immediately with **no `WorkflowCommand` pushed and no seq consumed** (mirrors `set_current_details`), so a workflow that publishes N chunks produces a **byte-for-byte identical `harvest_events` history** to one that publishes none. Chunk content **MAY be non-deterministic** (LLM tokens, wall-clock timestamps, sampled values) *precisely because* it is never recorded or replayed. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no shard-routing change.** **Core (`context.rs`).** Live path: serialize the chunk to `serde_json::Value` (serialize error → `Err`), cap serialized bytes at `PROGRESS_CHUNK_MAX_BYTES = 7000` (Postgres `NOTIFY` hard limit 8000, with envelope headroom); an oversize chunk is **replaced** — never silently dropped — with the truncation marker `{"_harvest_progress_truncated": true, "bytes": <original_len>}`, preserving the ordered slot and signalling truncation to the client. Pushes a **bookkeeping** `WorkflowCommand::PublishProgress { seq: u64, chunk: Value }` (no `result_tx`, non-suspending; joins the `SetCurrentDetails` family at every exhaustive-match and bookkeeping-classifier site in `worker.rs`, excluded from `executor.rs::is_replay_significant_command`, `Ok(false)` no-op in `testing.rs::apply_command`). **Monotonic seq (AC6):** `seq = (epoch << 24) | (local_index & 0xFF_FFFF)` (`encode_progress_seq`), where `epoch` is the loaded-history length at cycle start (read by locking the matcher directly, the `info()` trick, to avoid the `pump_signal_handlers` side effect) — constant within a cycle and strictly growing across cycles — and `local_index` is a per-cycle `AtomicU64`. seq is therefore lifetime-monotonic (reconnect gap detection) and **idempotent on a crash-retry of the same cycle** (best-effort duplicates are dedupable by seq). Epoch shift uses `saturating_mul`; `local_index` saturates at `2^24 - 1` (no overflow panic). **Notify (`worker.rs` + `notify.rs`).** `notify_progress_from_commands(conn, exec_id, &commands)` fires `notify::notify_workflow_progress(...)` on the worker's **persist connection**, co-located right after every `persist_current_details_from_commands` call site (5 sites: suspension, terminal, local-activity pre-run, 2 panic-strike paths) — so progress flushes on both suspension and terminal cycles, in the same transactional context as the `current_details` write (pg NOTIFY delivers on commit → a rolled-back+retried cycle re-fires live; the deterministic seq makes any autocommit-mode duplicate dedupable). A notify failure is **logged and swallowed**, never fails the workflow — progress is disposable. `notify.rs` adds the per-execution channel `workflow_progress_channel(exec_id)` (`harvest_progress_{32-hex}`, < 63-char `NAMEDATALEN`), `ProgressNotifyPayload { seq, chunk }`, `notify_workflow_progress`, and `WorkflowProgressListener` (`connect` / `wait_for_progress` / `wait_for_progress_timeout` → `ProgressWaitOutcome::{Chunk, TimedOut, ChannelClosed}`), mirroring `WorkflowEventListener` (tokio-postgres driver task + mpsc). All `pub` under `autumn_harvest::notify`. **Plugin SSE route (`api.rs`).** `GET /api/harvest/workflows/{id}/stream` (`text/event-stream`). Frames: `event: progress` (`id:` = seq, `data:` = the raw chunk JSON, **not** re-wrapped in the adjacently-tagged envelope) in publish order; `event: end` (`data: {"reason": <terminal-state>}`) on terminal; `event: error` (`data: {"error": "listen_connection_closed"}`) on channel loss. **Auth (AC5): deliberately NOT `require_admin`** — it is an end-user-facing read path (an app's users stream their own workflows), distinct from the admin engine-event tail (#324). It inherits the general `api_with_auth` middleware the other management routes use; **open if no auth is configured** — the default posture is documented in `docs/streaming-progress.md`, and embedders MUST front untrusted end-users. Clean-close mechanics: `LISTEN` is established **before** the existence check (so a chunk published in the check→listen window is not missed); the pooled DB connection is **dropped** before streaming (SSE streams never hold pool connections — the listener owns its own dedicated `tokio-postgres` connection, shard-resolved via `sse_notification_url(shard)`); an already-terminal execution emits a single `end` frame and closes immediately; on each keepalive `TimedOut` tick the producer polls terminal state (bounding close latency to one keepalive) and detects an idle-disconnected client via `tx.is_closed()`; `ChannelClosed` emits `error` and ends rather than hanging. Read-path decode (#608) does **not** apply — progress chunks are ephemeral author-supplied JSON, never codec-encoded. **Contract / audit registration (AC9).** Route registered in `harvest_api_router`, `management_api_routes()`, `management_api_response_fields()`, `docs/api-contract.json`, and `autumn_harvest::audit`: `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` (**ReadOnly**), `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES` (op **None**), `EXCLUDED_ROUTES`. Pinned classification tests in **both** `audit.rs` and plugin `contract_regression.rs` (the audit exhaustiveness cross-check stays green if a route is dropped from BOTH lists, so both are pinned independently). **Out of scope (per issue):** durable persistence / replay of chunks (that is the durable per-execution logs primitive, #790); at-least-once / exactly-once delivery, cross-reconnect ordering guarantees, or buffering for late subscribers (best-effort only); final-result delivery (#527) and snapshot reads (query handlers / `set_current_details`); client→workflow streaming (that is signals/updates); cross-shard fan-in of one logical stream (a stream is scoped to a single `exec_id` on its owning shard). **Docs / example.** `docs/streaming-progress.md` (API, determinism contract, best-effort delivery model, SSE wire format + `seq` semantics, auth default posture, 7000-byte cap + truncation marker, out-of-scope list, cross-links to #473/#593/#324/#527). `autumn-harvest/examples/streaming_agent.rs` (an AI-agent-shaped workflow publishing per-step chunks interleaved with a mock activity across decision cycles, one intentionally non-deterministic chunk with a SAFE-because-never-replayed comment, a documented `curl -N` consumer, and embedded `WorkflowTestEnv` tests asserting completion + zero-event-footprint + `ReplaySucceeded`). **Tests, TDD red→green.** Core: 5 inline `context.rs` unit tests (replay-suppressed, live-emits-bookkeeping-command, per-cycle local-index increase, oversize→truncation-marker); 2 no-DB integration tests (`publish_progress_leaves_zero_event_footprint` — identical event-type sequence to a no-progress sibling; `publish_progress_replays_with_zero_divergence` — ReplaySucceeded against an activity-only history, AC2); 2 new `notify::` unit tests (progress channel payload round-trip). Plugin: DB integration (`progress_stream_delivers_ordered_chunks_and_ends_on_terminal`, `progress_stream_on_already_terminal_execution_closes_immediately`, `progress_stream_unknown_execution_returns_404`) and no-DB registration/auth-posture tests (`sse_stream_tests.rs`), plus the pinned classification tests. All core no-DB surfaces run green in-sandbox; DB/HTTP suites (`progress_stream_integration`) run under the Docker-backed CI step registered in `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`.
- **Phase 3.x** (implemented): replay: only cross this signal's own deadline timer in `match_signal` — see issue #1071. Follow-up correctness fix on the merged PR #1084 (issue #1071), caught by Codex review. `HistoryMatcher::match_signal`'s interleaved-sibling arm — added by #1084 so a plain `wait_for_signal` tolerates a sibling deadline timer's `TimerFired` recorded before the awaited signal — crossed **any** reserved `__signal_timeout:*` deadline timer *without a rewind*, keyed only on the reserved **prefix** (`signal_timeout_race_name(...).is_some()`). So when a plain `wait_for_signal("a")` runs concurrently with a `receive_signal_timeout("b", …)` in one mixed batch and b's deadline fires before a arrives, the `match_signal("a")` scan advanced the cursor past a **foreign** signal's deadline events (`TimerStarted(__signal_timeout:1:b)` + `TimerFired(...)`) without setting `first_interleaved_command`. The "b" branch's positional `match_signal_or_timer("b")` could then no longer re-anchor on its own `TimerStarted`, so strict replay diverged with `NonDeterminismDetected{EarlyCompletion}` even though both waits genuinely resolved. **Fix (one-line guard narrowing):** the guard changes from name-agnostic `.is_some()` to name-matched `== Some(signal_name)`, so the cross-without-rewind arm fires **only for THIS signal's own** reserved deadline timer. A foreign-name reserved timer instead falls through to the existing generic `TimerStarted` rewind arm (as does a genuine user `ctx.timer` sibling), which sets `first_interleaved_command` so the sibling race re-anchors and resolves `TimerWon` after the win. Behavior is **byte-identical** for the same-name #1071 case (`interleaved_sibling_signal_after_deadline_timer_fired_replays_succeeded`) — `Some("go") == Some("go")` still matches — and the park-forever guard (`matcher_signal_scan_parks_on_lone_open_deadline_timer`) is untouched. The arm's comment, which described (and over-claimed for) the old name-agnostic behavior, is rewritten to state that it only crosses this signal's own deadline timer and that a foreign one is deliberately left to its own race matcher via the rewind path. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration** — a strictly narrowing change to one replay-matcher arm that diverts foreign-name reserved timers to the existing generic rewind path. Regression test `interleaved_two_signal_race_foreign_deadline_timer_replays_succeeded` (in `autumn-harvest/tests/integration/replayer_tests.rs`) encodes Codex's exact composition (`tokio::join!(wait_for_signal("a"), receive_signal_timeout::<Value>("b", 5s))`, "a" polled first, history `[WorkflowStarted, TimerStarted(__signal_timeout:1:b), TimerFired(__signal_timeout:1:b), SignalReceived(a)]`); it **fails pre-fix** with `NonDeterminismDetected(kind=EarlyCompletion, event_index=4)` and **passes post-fix** with `ReplaySucceeded`. Verified green at the pinned CI toolchain 1.97.0: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest --all-features --tests -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p autumn-harvest --no-default-features --features testing --test integration` (961 passed), and `cargo test -p autumn-harvest --all-features --lib` (2138 passed).
- **Phase 3.x** (implemented): Enforce the start-route capability-precise admin gate before the fail-closed runtime check — see issue #685. Heals the no-DB plugin security test `eris_unauthenticated_start_workflow_terminate_if_running_is_blocked`, which began failing on trunk-dev after #1100 (issue #685) narrowed and **reordered** the `POST /workflows/{name}/start` admin gate. **Root cause (not a live-deployment security hole).** Pre-#1100 the admin gate was a raw-string match placed at the top of `start_workflow`, before the fail-closed `api_state.runtime()` check. #1100 replaced it with the capability-precise gate `effective_active_conflict_behavior(reuse, conflict) == Terminate && !admin` and moved it to *after* both policy parses — which sit after the runtime check and the #808 committed-replay probe. In a **running** deployment the gate still correctly returns `401` for every request that can cancel a live run, so there is no live security hole. But in the no-DB `unauthenticated_app()` harness the runtime is unset, so `api_state.runtime()` returns `Config("harvest runtime is not started")` → `400` *before* the gate is reached. The test's `401` assertion now saw `400`. More importantly the reordering made the start-route auth gate **un-observable** in the no-DB harness: a gate-present and a gate-removed build both return `400`, so a test that accepted `400` would catch no regression. **Fix.** Add a surgical, additive, **lenient early auth gate** before the runtime check that reproduces the exact capability-precise condition on the two pure request-body policy strings (no runtime, no DB needed). It is lenient — an unparseable policy string makes the `Ok`/`Ok` guard fail, deferring to the authoritative gate (so #808's "committed replay returns `200` despite an invalid string" and "fresh invalid string → `400`" are preserved). Only a cleanly-parsed `Terminate`-capable combo by a non-admin returns `401`. The authoritative gate after the two parses is kept unchanged as a belt-and-suspenders backstop (reachable only for requests the early gate let through — admin, or non-`Terminate`). This restores the pre-#685 property that a cancel-capable unauthenticated start is rejected with `401` regardless of runtime readiness (defense in depth: authorize before the fail-closed resource check; `401` now precedes the registry `404`, removing an existence oracle — exactly the pre-#1100 ordering), and keeps #1100's narrowing intact: the flagship non-admin idempotent-starter `reuse = terminate_if_running` + `conflict = use_existing` (→ `Attach`) and `+ fail` (→ `Fail`) stay non-admin. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route change.** Running deployments are unaffected (same outcomes, `401` merely enforced earlier). **Tests** (`autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/security.rs`): the previously-failing test now asserts a clean `401` again; four new no-DB cases encode the narrowed contract so a regression in either direction is caught — `conflict_policy = terminate_existing` → `401`; and `terminate_if_running + use_existing`, `terminate_if_running + fail`, `conflict_policy = use_existing` are each `!= 401 && != 403` (allowed past the auth gate). **Also heals inherited trunk-dev Lint red** (out of this change's scope but blocking the `cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest-plugin --all-targets` gate): #1100's `StartWorkflowParams` literal sweep missed `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/progress_stream_integration.rs` (added by #1098), which failed to compile with `missing field conflict_policy`. Added `conflict_policy: WorkflowIdConflictPolicy::Unspecified` matching the sweep's convention. **Post-review hardening (Codex P2): the early gate now defers idempotency-keyed requests.** The early gate above rejected any cleanly-parsed `Terminate`-capable combo by a non-admin with `401` — with no regard for an idempotency key. But the #808 committed-replay claim is keyed on `(workflow_name, idempotency_key)` **alone** — independent of the reuse/conflict policy and the caller's auth — so a keyed `Terminate` start committed by an **admin** can legitimately be replayed by a later **non-admin** retry carrying the same key, which must return the #808 `200` no-op. The early gate's own comment (and the authoritative gate's) claimed "a non-admin can never have committed a `Terminate` start, so no committed replay exists" — flawed reasoning, since the committer and the retrier need not be the same principal. **Fix:** narrow the early gate to fire only when **no** idempotency key is present (a cheap presence-only boolean — header `Idempotency-Key` present, or a non-empty body `idempotency_key`; no validation here, so the downstream resolver still `400`s an empty/over-long key unchanged). Any keyed request defers past the early gate to the downstream path, preserving BOTH #808 outcomes: a committed-replay hit returns its `200` at the committed-replay probe (caller/body-independent), while a genuinely-fresh keyed `Terminate` by a non-admin is still `401`'d by the authoritative gate — which runs **after** that probe, so the narrowing opens no hole. Both misleading comments are rewritten to state the correct invariant (the early gate is an observable, key-absent-only auth check; keyed requests defer downstream). New no-DB regression tests (`eris_keyed_terminate_if_running_defers_past_early_gate`, `eris_keyed_terminate_existing_conflict_defers_past_early_gate`) assert a keyed cancel-capable request is no longer early-`401`'d (in the no-DB harness it fails-closed at the runtime check → non-`401`), contrasted against the unkeyed cases which still assert `401`.
- **Phase 3.x** (implemented): `harvest new <name>` project scaffolding — see issue #692. New local CLI subcommand `harvest new <name> [--path <DIR>] [--force] [--template minimal]` in `autumn-harvest-cli` that scaffolds a complete, compiling, runnable autumn-harvest project so a first-time evaluator reaches one durable workflow execution in **≤ 3 post-scaffold commands** (`docker compose up -d` → `AUTUMN_PROFILE=dev cargo run` → `curl … /workflows/{name}_workflow/start`). The one metric the engine is judged on — time from `cargo add` to first executed workflow — finally has an owning command. **CLI-only, additive.** No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no event-schema or macro-path change, no library API change. `harvest new` is a **local** command (early-return in `run_cli` before the API dispatch path, exactly like `det-check` #778): pure local file generation, no database, no network. **Design decisions:** **Command surface**: `harvest new <name>` only this slice (AC-1's "and/or" is satisfied by `new`; `harvest init` and an ephemeral-Postgres `--demo` mode are noted follow-ups). `ScaffoldTemplate` value_enum ships one `minimal` template. **Embedded templates**: `include_str!` from `autumn-harvest-cli/templates/minimal/` — the first `include_str!` in `src/`; zero runtime fetch. `{{crate_name}}` / `{{ident}}` / `{{workflow_fn}}` / `{{activity_fn}}` / `{{queue}}` placeholders (double-brace so they never collide with Rust `{}`), substituted by a tiny tested `apply_substitutions` helper. **Generated project shape** mirrors `examples/quickstart`: `Cargo.toml` (crates.io **version** deps `autumn-harvest = "0.4"` + `db` feature, `autumn-harvest-plugin = "0.4"`, `autumn-web = "0.5"` — never path deps, since the generated project lives outside the workspace; `edition = "2021"` for the broadest floor), `src/main.rs` (one `#[workflow]` `{ident}_workflow` calling one `#[activity]` `{ident}_activity`, `HarvestPlugin` wiring, a tiny `#[get("/")]` landing route since autumn-web requires ≥1 HTTP route, worker polling the single `["{ident}"]` queue — a workflow start enqueues the workflow task on the worker's first queue and the activity (`queue = "{ident}"`) is enqueued there too, so one queue services both), `README.md` (the ≤3-command runbook + `AUTUMN_PROFILE=dev` auto-migration note, satisfying the DB-bootstrap AC without a manual `diesel migration run`; the result-observing step polls `GET /workflows/{execution_id}` for `.execution.state` and offers the real `harvest … workflow get <id>` subcommand), `compose.yaml` (postgres:16), `autumn.toml`, `.gitignore`. Every emitted identifier is a pure function of `<name>` — no example identifiers survive (AC-5). **Clean identifier derivation**: `derive_crate_ident` lowercases, maps `-` → `_`, collapses runs of `_`, and trims leading/trailing `_`, so any spec-valid name yields a warning-free `snake_case` ident with no double underscore (`my-app` → `my_app`, `MyApp` → `myapp`, `trail-` → `trail`). Only the derived idents are normalized; name **acceptance** is unchanged (keyword/reserved collision is checked against the raw `-` → `_` form), so an uppercase package name like `MyApp` stays accepted per `cargo new` parity (only cargo's own cosmetic uppercase warning), while the generated `main.rs` uses the clean lowercase ident. **Fail-safe** (AC-6): a non-empty target directory without `--force` returns an error and writes **nothing** (validation + full render happen before any file is written); `--force` overwrites but never removes files it did not write (no `rm -rf`). An existing **non-directory** at the target (a plain file) is rejected up front with a clear "is not a directory" message instead of an opaque `create_dir_all` OS error. **Name validation**: rejects empty / over-64-char / non-`^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$` / Rust-keyword-resolving / reserved names before any write, so an invalid name can never produce an invalid `Cargo.toml`. **Scaffold-rot guards (AC-8):** A **content-parity** unit test ties the template's `main.rs` wiring tokens to the CI-compiled `examples/quickstart/src/main.rs` (read at test time), so template drift from the shape CI actually builds fails the test. A Linux-only `scaffold-smoke` CI job **generates, builds, and runs** the scaffold to a terminal state — the literal AC-8 assertion. It builds the generated project against the **published** crates.io deps (no `[patch.crates-io]`) — exactly what a real user gets — behind a `postgres:16` service whose user/password/db match the scaffold's generated `autumn.toml`, boots the app (`AUTUMN_PROFILE=dev` auto-migrates), POSTs a workflow start, and polls `GET /workflows/{id}` until `state == COMPLETED`, failing the job on a bad terminal state or timeout. This closes the earlier "runtime execution deferred to a fast-follow" gap: the headline metric (scaffold → first executed workflow) is now asserted end to end in CI against the published API. **Mechanism note.** The end-to-end run lives in a dedicated CI job with a `postgres:16` service (rather than an in-crate integration test registered in `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`) because it must scaffold, build, and run a *generated standalone cargo project* as a subprocess — which does not fit the in-crate cargo-test harness and would be far heavier on disk. **Tests (TDD red→green→refactor):** 22 integration tests in `autumn-harvest-cli/tests/integration/new_cli.rs` (derive names, substitution, no-placeholder-survives across every file, crates.io-deps-no-path, identifier substitution in `main.rs`, hyphenated/uppercase/repeat-separator names → clean `snake_case` idents in `main.rs` with no double underscore, README 3-command path, README result-observing commands, quickstart wiring parity, writes-all-files, fail-safe-non-empty, `--force` overwrite preserving unrelated files, existing-file target rejection, `--path` creates missing dir, over-length + reserved-name rejection, invalid-name-no-write) + 7 lib unit tests (`clap` parse of `Commands::New` with flags and defaults, clean `derive_crate_ident`, keyword rejection, valid-name acceptance, uppercase cargo-new parity). **Local end-to-end verification.** The scaffold was built against the published `autumn-harvest 0.4.0` / `autumn-harvest-plugin 0.4.0` / `autumn-web 0.5.0` (registry sources, no patch) and driven to `COMPLETED` (output `hello, World!`) against a local Postgres, confirming both the published-deps build and the single-queue wiring.
- **Phase 4** (implemented): Replay tolerates interleaved sibling terminals in forward-scan matchers — see issue #1071. Fixed a pre-existing **core** replay limitation (shared by the Postgres engine, surfaced by the SQLite backend work #1068/#1069): an *ideal, correct* workflow history that interleaves a sibling terminal event next to the event a matcher is scanning for would falsely fail replay with `NonDeterminismDetected(EarlyCompletion)`. The canonical case is a timer-first mixed suspension batch — `tokio::join!(ctx.timer(...), ctx.execute_activity(...))` with the timer command emitted first — recording `WorkflowStarted, TimerStarted, ActivityScheduled, ActivityCompleted, TimerFired`: `HistoryMatcher::match_timer_strict`'s forward `TimerFired` scan **broke at the still-unconsumed `ActivityScheduled`**, never recognized the timer as fired, skipped the re-arm, and diverged. The mirror `join!(activity, timer)` (activity first) happened to replay fine. **Fix (matcher-scan logic only, in `impl HistoryMatcher`, `autumn-harvest/src/replay.rs`):** each intolerant forward-scan matcher now tolerates an interleaved sibling terminal at its recorded position — the same non-consuming-skip / rewind template `match_signal_or_timer` (#476) already uses — across all four documented manifestations: **`match_timer_strict`** — a rewind arm for interleaved unconsumed sibling *commands* (`ActivityScheduled | LocalActivityScheduled | MarkerRecorded | SideEffectRecorded`) plus transparent non-consuming skip arms for interleaved sibling *terminals* and *foreign `TimerFired`* (a `TimerFired` whose id ≠ this timer's belongs to a sibling). Fixes manifestation #1 (timer-first mixed batch) and #4 (reversed multi-timer same-batch fire order). **`scan_activity_terminal`** — added `LocalActivityScheduled` to the interleaved-command arm and a transparent skip for `TimerFired (any id) | ChildWorkflow{Completed,Failed} | LocalActivity{Completed,Failed}`. Fixes manifestation #2 (sibling timer fires before an activity's terminal). **`match_signal`** — transparently crosses a sibling deadline timer's `TimerStarted`/`TimerFired` recorded ahead of the awaited signal; a reserved `__signal_timeout:{seq}:{name}` timer (a concurrent `receive_signal_timeout` race, #476) is crossed without a rewind so the signal-win advances the cursor past it (no false `EarlyCompletion`), while a genuine user `ctx.timer` sibling keeps its rewind. Fixes manifestation #3 (deadline timer fired before an awaited plain-wait signal). **Contract-preserving by construction: no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no change to event emit / suspension-batch command ordering** — the persisted contract is untouched; this only changes how the matcher *reads* an existing history. Foreign events are never marked consumed, so each crossed sibling stays claimable by its own matcher in program order. **Tolerance does not over-swallow — genuine non-determinism still diverges:** guarded by `interleaved_sibling_multi_timer_wrong_one_fires_still_diverges`, `interleaved_sibling_signal_stray_timer_fired_still_diverges`, `interleaved_sibling_signal_stray_timer_started_still_diverges`, the matcher-unit `matcher_signal_scan_parks_on_lone_open_deadline_timer` (a lone open deadline timer parks rather than being falsely nd-blocked), and the retained `replay_activity_history_for_timer_workflow_detects_timer_mismatch` (a genuine timer-id mismatch still diverges via the untouched positional anchor). **Known limitation (pinned + documented):** composing a plain `wait_for_signal` with a cancellable timer (#768) in one `join!` where the cancellable `TimerFired` is recorded before the `SignalReceived` still diverges on strict replay (self-heals live; use `ctx.receive_signal_timeout` #476 for the supported signal-or-deadline shape) — pinned by `known_limitation_signal_wait_composed_with_cancellable_await_fire_diverges_on_reversed_order`. **Cross-crate pin flip:** one now-obsolete `autumn-harvest-sqlite` known-limitation control (`reversed_timer_fire_order_breaks_core_replay`) is renamed to `reversed_timer_fire_order_replays_on_core_after_1071` with its assertion flipped from `NonDeterminismDetected` to `ReplaySucceeded` — the core fix makes that reversed multi-timer history replay-succeed, so the stale pin would otherwise fail the `cargo test -p autumn-harvest-sqlite` CI step. No sqlite workaround *logic* changed (the `arm_seq` fire-order tie-break is retained but is no longer a replay-*correctness* prerequisite). The sqlite `join!(activity, timer)` "activity branch first" and plain-`wait_for_signal`-with-deadline guidance become unnecessary and are flagged for a follow-up docs cleanup (not changed here); the WASM branch #1072 inherits the same core matcher. Tests: `autumn-harvest/tests/integration/replayer_tests.rs` gains the four manifestation replay-succeeds tests (`interleaved_sibling_timer_first_mixed_batch_replays_succeeded`, `interleaved_sibling_timer_fires_before_activity_terminal_replays_succeeded`, `interleaved_sibling_signal_after_deadline_timer_fired_replays_succeeded` + `interleaved_sibling_signal_after_plain_user_timer_fired_replays_succeeded`, `interleaved_sibling_multi_timer_reversed_fire_order_replays_succeeded`), the child-workflow coverage variant `interleaved_sibling_child_workflow_terminal_before_timer_replays_succeeded`, the divergence guards above, and the known-limitation pin; `replay.rs` gains the `matcher_signal_scan_parks_on_lone_open_deadline_timer` unit test. CI reproduced at cargo 1.97.0: integration `960 passed`, all-features lib `2071 passed`, clippy `-D warnings` + fmt clean, sqlite `125/125`.
- **Phase 4** (implemented): Vantage UI: DAG run-graph page (issue #957) + execution timeline/Gantt page (issue #960) — see PR #1085. Adds the two remaining Phase 4 Vantage dashboard pages, both server-rendered inline SVG in `autumn-harvest-plugin/src/ui.rs` (the Workers #142 / DLQ #226 precedent — no JS, no client-side charting library), both read-only except one already-audited mutation. **No new backend endpoint, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no core change.** The only `api.rs` touch is a shared-impl extraction (below). Diff confined to `ui.rs`, `api.rs`, and `tests/ui_integration.rs`. **DAG run-graph page (issue #957)** New DAG run-graph rendered on the per-DAG detail page (`GET /api/harvest/dags/{dag_name}`). `dag_detail_ui` now derives topology, per-node status, and timings **solely** from `dag_graph::build_run_graph` — the same in-process derivation the #690 API handler calls — so the picture and the #366 retry action can never disagree about what "failed" means. The previous UI-side status fork (`map_node_states`/`DagNodeState`/`dag_node_state_label`/`merge_dag_task_state`/`infer_skipped_node_state`/`parse_dag_skip_marker_index`) is **deleted** (its unit tests deleted with it; grep for every symbol is empty), satisfying #957's "must not fork its own node-status derivation" AC. Topology renders as level-by-level inline SVG (`build_graph_layout`, one `<line>` per `depends_on` edge), each node filled **and** icon-marked per status (`succeeded`/`failed`/`timed_out`/`cancelled`/`running`/`pending`/`skipped`) so status is distinguishable without color (accessibility), with `role="img"`+`aria-label` and per-node `<a>`/`<title>`. Node index alignment (`nodes[i]` ↔ `tasks()[i]` ↔ `execution_levels()`, all from one `DagDefinition`) is pinned by a regression test. Geometry is fully clamped/guarded — no panics on zero-node, cyclic-impossible, or huge-fan-out runs; ≥ 200 nodes fall back to a scrollable container. Click-through node detail panel shows `status`/`started_at`/`finished_at`/`attempts`/`error_type` + truncated error first line. A failed node offers **"Retry from this node"** whose confirmation names the exact widened node set (#366's level + downstream-closure semantics) before commit. **`api.rs` change (the only one): `retry_dag_run`'s handler body extracted into `pub(crate) retry_dag_run_inner` + `DagRetryFailure` (with `human_message` + `into_http_response`).** The HTTP `retry_dag_run` handler delegates to it, preserving the #366 wire contract byte-for-byte (every original status/body arm reproduced). The UI dry-run confirm and the commit both call the same audited `retry_dag_run_inner` (`OP_DAG_RETRY`, `source = SOURCE_UI`); the whole `/dags/{dag_name}/runs/{run_exec_id}/retry` route (GET confirm + POST commit) is `require_admin`-gated to match the API, so the UI adds no unaudited mutation path. **Behavior changes:** classic (non-unified) DAG runs — which #690 rejects with `400` — now render the explicit "no topology available for classic DAG runs" degraded message (required to source statuses solely from `build_run_graph`); and an explicitly-provided-but-unknown `?run=` now returns the 404 message (AC7) instead of silently falling back to the first valid run (an omitted `?run=` still defaults to the latest run). **Execution timeline / Gantt page (issue #960)** New **Timeline** tab on the execution detail page (route `GET /workflows/{id}/timeline`, read-only, non-admin — parity with the #739 API). `workflow_timeline_ui` calls `derive_timeline` in-process (the same shipped #739 function — not a forked history-derivation). Renders one horizontal span per step on a shared wall-clock axis, lane-grouped by `step_kind`, colored by `outcome`, with the `wait_ms`/`exec_ms` split drawn as two segments **only when #739 provides it** (a single undivided span otherwise — never fabricating a split). Gantt geometry is clamped/guarded (`x_scale` clamps to axis width; `GanttAxis::new` forces `end > start`; zero/open spans use a min-width; casts are bounded) — no panics on never-started, still-running, clock-skew, or null-split histories; in-flight steps render as open-ended spans to "now". Uniquely versus every competitor, engine interventions render as first-class bands because those states are durable columns: operator **pauses** (#383) render as a full-height shaded band with reason/actor (active pause only); **ND-blocks** (#603) render as a distinct marker with the block reason.
