The failure stays **retryable** (a caught panic follows the activity's retry policy exactly as `Err(String)` does — honoring a `HandlerPanic`-non-retryable classification). **No core export needed** — `ERROR_TYPE_HANDLER_PANIC`, `ActivityFailure::retryable`, and `IntoActivityErrorString::into_error_payload` are all already `pub` in `autumn_harvest::failure` and reachable under `default-features = false`. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no schema change, no core change.** Regression tests (verified RED against the pre-fix plain-string code): `worker.rs` unit `handler_panic_activity_envelope_encodes_retryable_handler_panic` (the encoder emits a TYPED envelope — not a bare string — that `parse_typed_payload` decodes with `error_type = "HandlerPanic"`, `non_retryable = false`, and `parse_error_payload_full` decodes with the raw message preserved); and two `tests/cross_backend.rs` integration tests — `caught_activity_panic_records_handler_panic_error_type_and_replays` (a catching workflow whose `panicky` activity has `max_attempts = 1` → the terminal `ActivityFailed` records `error_type = "HandlerPanic"` (RED pre-fix: `"Error"`), the raw panic message is preserved with no wire envelope leak, and the history replays `ReplaySucceeded` on the core `WorkflowReplayer`) and `caught_activity_panic_honors_handler_panic_non_retryable_policy` (a typed `execute_activity(&info, …)` call whose per-call `RetryPolicy` marks `HandlerPanic` non-retryable → the panicking body runs exactly ONCE and fails terminally with `error_type = "HandlerPanic"`, `attempt = 1`; RED pre-fix: retried to `max_attempts = 3` and recorded `"Error"`). **Codex #1069 review (commit `c2dcdc1`) — P2: signal-timeout correlation DECLINED as a pre-existing core-matcher limitation (#1071), documented.** The finding proposed correlating each `WaitForSignal` ingest with its exact timeout timer id so `ingest_awaited_signal` never reorders an *unrelated* deadline ahead of a plain wait's signal, motivated by a workflow that composes a plain `wait_for_signal("go")` AND a sibling `wait_for_signal_timeout("go", …)` on the SAME name concurrently (a signal after the sibling deadline records that `TimerFired` before the plain wait's `SignalReceived`, and `match_signal` cannot skip it). Verified empirically on the core `WorkflowReplayer` that this is the same core-matcher limitation as #1071, NOT a backend correlation gap: a hand-built history `[WorkflowStarted, TimerStarted(__signal_timeout:0:go), TimerFired(__signal_timeout:0:go), SignalReceived(go)]` fed to a plain-`wait_for_signal("go")` handler yields `NonDeterminismDetected(kind=EarlyCompletion, event_index=1)` — the plain wait's `match_signal` stops at the interleaved unconsumed `TimerFired` regardless of how the signal was ingested. Critically, the finding's own suggested fix (exact per-wait timer correlation, so ingest only reorders the timeout wait's OWN deadline) does NOT resolve the wedge: the sibling `wait_for_signal_timeout`'s deadline is a legitimate durable timer, so its `TimerFired` is recorded in history regardless of ingest order, and the plain wait's `match_signal` still hits it. A correct fix requires a CORE-matcher change (make `match_signal` tolerate an interleaved `TimerFired` at its recorded position) — the same class tracked in #1071 (and behind the earlier-declined activity-vs-timer reorder). DECLINED the backend correlation change (it would not fix the wedge) and instead documented (crate docs `lib.rs`, this changelog) that composing a plain `wait_for_signal(name)` with a `wait_for_signal_timeout(name, …)` on the SAME signal name concurrently is subject to the #1071 core-matcher limitation, with `wait_for_signal_timeout` used ALONE as the supported signal-with-deadline path (it arms exactly the `__signal_timeout` deadline this backend reorders, and is covered by the late-signal-vs-deadline tests). A threaded reply with this rationale (incl. the `WorkflowReplayer` evidence) was posted on the finding, and #1071 was annotated with this further instance of the `match_signal` interleaved-`TimerFired` intolerance. **Codex #1069 review (commit `eaf334e`) — P2 ×2: reject unsupported `WorkflowInfo`-level features at registration, closing the "silently-dropped `WorkflowInfo` feature" class.** `SqliteRuntime::register_workflow(&WorkflowInfo)` retained ONLY `name` + `handler` (`self.workflows.insert(info.name.to_string(), info.handler)`), silently dropping every other field the `#[workflow(...)]` macro / fluent builder populates. Two findings on this commit named the concrete casualties: a `#[workflow(execution_timeout = …)]` workflow (`runtime.rs:602`) threaded `None` into the executor — no `deadline_at`, no `ctx.deadline()`, never hard-timed-out — and a `#[workflow(retry(…))]` (workflow-level `retry_policy`) workflow (`runtime.rs:686`) sealed `FAILED` on the first author error with no retry successor. Rather than patch those two arms, the whole class is closed at the single registration choke point — the same pattern the crate already uses at the command layer (`cancellable_timer_unsupported`) and the `ScheduleActivity`-field layer (`apply_schedule_activity`): a new pure `runtime::unsupported_workflow_feature(&WorkflowInfo) -> Option<(feature, hint)>` audits the incoming info, and `register_workflow` **PANICS at registration** (setup-time — mirroring the Postgres `HarvestPlugin::build()` panic on registration misconfiguration; a `Result` return would force ~60 mechanical `.unwrap()` edits across the existing test suite, the explicit "too disruptive" fallback condition) if a declared execution- or admission-affecting feature is set, naming the specific feature and pointing at the supported alternative. Honoring these features (an execution-timeout scanner, workflow-level retry orchestration, the admission gates) is real, out-of-v0.1-scope work tracked as issue #1068 follow-ups — hence a loud reject over a partial, silently-wrong implementation. The full `WorkflowInfo`-field audit: | Field | Disposition | Rationale | | `name` | honor | the registration key | | `handler` | honor | the dispatch fn | | `execution_timeout` (#243) | **reject** | no execution-timeout scanner exists here → a declared hard deadline would never fire; enforce it in-body with `ctx.timer`/`ctx.sleep_until` | | `retry_policy` — `#[workflow(retry(…))]` (#523) | **reject** | no workflow-level auto-retry orchestration → a `retry(…)` workflow would seal FAILED on the first strike; use per-activity retry (honored in full) | | `concurrency` (#247) | **reject** | per-key limits need the shared-queue claim-time advisory lock; no single-writer analog | | `debounce` (#499) | **reject** | pre-start admission-gate feature; no equivalent | | `batch` (#518) | **reject** | pre-start admission-gate feature; no equivalent | | `throttle` (#607) | **reject** | pre-start admission-gate feature; no equivalent | | `max_input_bytes` (#252) | **reject** | a raised per-workflow cap is not threaded into the replay caps → the global default would apply and silently REJECT an input the workflow declared acceptable; rejected so the divergence surfaces at setup, not as a surprising runtime `PayloadTooLarge` | | `sla` (#487) | accept, inert | observability-only (no scanner → no `harvest.workflow.sla_breached` metric); the run's lifecycle is unaffected either way — NOT silently-wrong | | `owner` / `runbook_url` / `severity` (#372) | accept, inert | ops metadata; execution never consults it | | `description` + `input_schema`/`output_schema`/`error_schema` (#373) | accept, inert | HTTP-edge discovery/validation; this backend has no HTTP edge | | `mcp` (#597) | accept, inert | HTTP-edge MCP tool exposure; the core never consults it | | `module` | accept, inert | diagnostics | **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no schema change, no core change** — a registration-time audit of an already-`pub` struct's fields. Docs: a new "Unsupported `WorkflowInfo`-level features — rejected at registration" section in the crate docs (`lib.rs`) with the full partition. Tests: four in-crate unit tests (`runtime.rs`, `feature_gate_tests`) pinning the pure `unsupported_workflow_feature` audit — a plain workflow registers, EVERY execution-affecting field is rejected with an actionable hint, all metadata/observability fields are accepted-inert, and the first-match ordering (`execution_timeout` before `retry_policy`) is deterministic — plus four integration tests on the PUBLIC API (`tests/workflow_info_features.rs`): a `#[workflow(execution_timeout = "30s")]` and a `#[workflow(retry = …)]` workflow each `#[should_panic]` with the feature named (RED pre-fix — `register_workflow` silently succeeded), while a metadata-only (`description`) workflow and a plain no-attribute workflow both register and RUN to completion unchanged. **Codex #1069 review (commit `7aaa629`) — P2 ×3: enforce payload-size caps at every ingress boundary, closing the "unbounded payload / silently-accepted oversized payload" class (issue #252).** The Postgres path rejects an oversized payload at every boundary; this backend enforced none of them directly, so it could store an unbounded history row and accept a payload other backends reject. Three findings on this commit named the concrete boundaries — a **workflow START input** (`runtime.rs:264`) inserted the execution + appended `WorkflowStarted` without measuring the serialized input; a **signal payload** (`runtime.rs:346`) staged unvalidated so the next `wait_for_signal` recorded an oversized `SignalReceived`; and an **activity RESULT** (`worker.rs:340`) wrote `ActivityCompleted` with the full oversized payload instead of the Postgres worker's non-retryable `PayloadTooLarge` normalization. Rather than patch only those three, the WHOLE payload-cap class was audited and closed: | Boundary | Cap constant | Enforced pre-fix? | Disposition | | Workflow input (START, `start_workflow`) | `DEFAULT_MAX_WORKFLOW_INPUT_BYTES` (2 MiB) | ❌ no | **FIX A** — reject at ingress before insert/append | | Workflow input (continue-as-new) | — | n/a | `ContinueAsNew` is `Unsupported` (rejected before any input persists) | | Activity input (schedule time) | `DEFAULT_MAX_ACTIVITY_INPUT_BYTES` (2 MiB) | ✅ yes (reused core `WorkflowContext`) | unchanged — the executor threads `payload_max_activity_input` and enforces it | | Activity result (completion, worker) | `DEFAULT_MAX_ACTIVITY_RESULT_BYTES` (2 MiB) | ❌ no | **FIX B** — normalize oversized `Ok` → non-retryable `PayloadTooLarge` `ActivityFailed` | | Signal payload (ingress, `send_signal`) | `DEFAULT_MAX_SIGNAL_PAYLOAD_BYTES` (256 KiB) | ❌ no | **FIX C** — reject at ingress, after not-found/terminal, before stage | | Signal payload (`signal_external_workflow`) | — | n/a | external signals are `Unsupported` | | Side-effect value | `DEFAULT_MAX_WORKFLOW_INPUT_BYTES` (2 MiB) | ✅ yes (reused core `WorkflowContext` — `with_payload_caps` sets `payload_max_side_effect = max_workflow_input`) | unchanged | | Child-workflow input | — | n/a | child workflows (`StartChildWorkflow`/`SpawnDetachedChildWorkflow`) are `Unsupported` | | Update / query payloads | — | n/a | declarative update/query handlers are not threaded on this backend (none supported) | **FIX A (`runtime.rs`, `start_workflow`)** measures `serde_json::to_string(&input).len()` and returns the new typed `SqliteError::PayloadTooLarge { kind: "workflow_input", observed_bytes, cap_bytes }` BEFORE `self.conn.transaction()` is even opened, so no `harvest_executions` row and no `WorkflowStarted` event are written — mirroring the Postgres start path's pre-insert `PayloadTooLarge` rejection. **FIX C (`runtime.rs`, `send_signal_as_of`)** measures the payload the same way and rejects with `kind: "signal_payload"` — placed AFTER the existing not-found (`ExecutionNotFound`) / terminal (`WorkflowNotRunning`) checks (the prompt's chosen order: the target's existence/state is the precondition for accepting ANY signal, so a typoed/sealed target reports THAT rather than a size complaint). The Postgres HTTP boundary happens to check the cap *before* `send_signal`'s state check; both reject and neither stages the row, so the only observable difference is the error KIND for the pathological "oversized payload to an unknown/terminal target" case (a caller bug either way) — documented in the code comment and covered by `signal_cap_yields_to_not_found_and_terminal_checks`. **FIX B (`worker.rs`, `finalize_within_tx`)** normalizes the result at the TOP of the finalize body — before `record_attempt` — so the audit row, the terminal decision, and the appended event all reflect the same outcome: an `Ok(output)` over `DEFAULT_MAX_ACTIVITY_RESULT_BYTES` becomes a NON-RETRYABLE `PayloadTooLarge` `ActivityFailure` envelope (a new crate-local `worker::payload_too_large_activity_envelope` built from the same `pub` `autumn_harvest::failure` primitives — `ActivityFailure::non_retryable("PayloadTooLarge", …).into_error_payload()` — the Postgres worker's `handle_activity_result` uses VERBATIM) routed through the SAME terminal-failure path as an ordinary `Err`, so it fails terminally on the FIRST attempt (non-retryable, regardless of `max_attempts`) and records `ActivityFailed { error_type: "PayloadTooLarge", non_retryable: true, message: "activity '…' result exceeds cap: … bytes (cap … bytes)" }` — decoded by the SAME `parse_error_payload_full` the Postgres `finalize_activity_failure` uses, so the histories stay byte-equivalent and no unbounded `ActivityCompleted` row is ever stored. All caps use the GLOBAL default constants (already `pub` in `autumn_harvest::builder` and reachable under `default-features = false`; the sqlite backend has no per-workflow/per-activity cap override, exactly like the activity-INPUT cap the reused executor already enforces with the global); a `0` cap = uncapped, matching the core convention. **No core export needed** (`DEFAULT_MAX_*`, `ActivityFailure::non_retryable`, `IntoActivityErrorString::into_error_payload`, `parse_error_payload_full` are all already `pub`), **no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no schema change, no core change**. New error variant `SqliteError::PayloadTooLarge { kind: &'static str, observed_bytes, cap_bytes }` (ingress rejections only; the activity-result path surfaces as an `ActivityFailed` event, not this error). Docs: a new payload-cap bullet in the crate-docs fidelity list (`lib.rs`) with the full boundary partition. Tests (verified RED against the pre-fix code — 3 in-crate + 3 integration tests fail without the checks): `worker.rs` units `payload_too_large_activity_envelope_encodes_non_retryable`, `finalize_oversized_result_records_non_retryable_payload_too_large_terminal` (an oversized `Ok` with `max_attempts = 3` records a NON-retryable `PayloadTooLarge` terminal `ActivityFailed` — not `ActivityCompleted`, not retried — with no wire-envelope leak; RED: appended `ActivityCompleted` with the full payload), and `finalize_under_cap_result_completes_normally`; `runtime.rs` `feature_gate_tests` units `oversized_start_input_persists_nothing` (0 `harvest_executions` + 0 `harvest_events` rows) and `oversized_signal_payload_stages_no_row` (0 `harvest_signals` rows); and `tests/payload_caps.rs` (7 public-API integration tests: START-input reject + runtime-not-wedged, signal-ingress reject + still-parked + valid-signal-delivered, the not-found/terminal ordering, the end-to-end oversized-activity-result → `PayloadTooLarge` failure, and three under-cap happy-path controls). **Codex #1069 review (commit `d4c8e07`) — P2: reject/honor unsupported `ActivityInfo`-level features at registration, closing the THIRD (and final) author-declared-feature ingress surface.** The prior audits closed the first two ingress surfaces — the `ScheduleActivity` **command** fields (`apply_schedule_activity`) and the **`WorkflowInfo`** fields (`unsupported_workflow_feature`) — but a THIRD remained, and the "same pattern the crate already uses at the command layer and the ScheduleActivity-field layer" framing above did not yet account for it: a `#[activity(...)]` can declare *dispatch-time defaults the Postgres worker enforces from `ActivityInfo` at dispatch but which are NOT copied into the `ScheduleActivity` command* (verified against core `context.rs`: `execute_activity`/`execute_activity_with_opts` copy only `default_queue`/`default_retry_policy`/`default_start_to_close` into the command; `default_schedule_to_close`, `default_heartbeat_timeout`, `default_schedule_to_start`, `circuit_breaker`, `rate_limit_*`, `max_concurrent`, `requires`, `is_local`, and the per-activity cap raisers are enforced by the PG worker via its `HandlerRegistry` lookup, not the command). The crate's registration surface retained only a body + max-attempt fallback (`register_activity(name, ActivitySpec)`), so those defaults were **neither honored nor rejected** — the concrete casualty (Codex `runtime.rs:39`): an activity with a total `schedule_to_close` deadline (issue #378) and a retry policy could keep backing off/retrying PAST the declared deadline and eventually complete instead of recording `ActivityTimedOut`. **The core async `ActivityInfo::handler` cannot be used to derive an executable body** (it requires an `ActivityContext` + async invocation, which the crate's synchronous inline `drain_ready` deliberately does not have — "activity execution is a simple registered closure, no `ActivityContext`, no I/O framework"), so — using the reviewer-sanctioned "you MAY keep an `ActivitySpec`-based path" allowance — the audited path takes BOTH the `&ActivityInfo` (for the audit + declared defaults) AND the caller-supplied synchronous body: `register_activity(name, ActivitySpec)` is renamed to `register_activity_raw` (the unaudited hand-made escape hatch, analog of `execute_activity_raw`), and the new `register_activity(&ActivityInfo, body)` becomes the primary, audited path (analog of `register_workflow`). It runs the new pure `runtime::unsupported_activity_feature(&ActivityInfo) -> Option<(feature, hint)>` and **PANICS at registration** (setup-time, mirroring `register_workflow`) for a field it cannot honor. The partition: **HONORED** — `default_schedule_to_close` (issue #378 — resolved BY NAME from the registry at dispatch, exactly as the PG worker resolves `ActivityInfo` from its `HandlerRegistry`; persisted as an ABSOLUTE deadline on a new nullable `harvest_tasks.schedule_to_close_at` column via `apply_schedule_activity`/`persist_scheduled_activity`/`queue::enqueue_activity`, carried back on `ClaimedTask`, and enforced by `worker::drain_ready` — a task drained at/after it — AND `worker::finalize_within_tx`'s retry branch — a retry whose next attempt would land at/after it — records a terminal `ActivityTimedOut { ScheduleToClose }` instead of running/retrying, byte-equivalent to the Postgres `schedule_to_close_deadline_exceeded` path; via the pure `worker::schedule_to_close_exceeded(at, deadline)`), `default_retry_policy` (fallback attempt cap; the whole policy also reaches the worker per-dispatch via the command's `retry_policy_override`), `default_start_to_close` (via the command), `default_queue` (recorded). **REJECTED** (a dispatch-admission / cross-worker semantic with no single-writer analog, or a cap raiser that would otherwise silently apply the STRICTER global cap): `default_heartbeat_timeout` (no heartbeating in the inline drain), `default_schedule_to_start` (no queue-wait scanner), `circuit_breaker` (#369), `rate_limit_*` (#332), `max_concurrent` (#247), `requires` (capability routing), `is_local` (local-activity `RunLocalActivity` dispatch is a command-layer non-goal), and a raised `max_input_bytes`/`max_result_bytes` (#252). **ACCEPTED, inert**: `name`, `module`, and a lone `concurrency_key`. With this third surface closed, the author-declared-feature ingress is now exhaustive across **all three** surfaces — the `ScheduleActivity` command, `WorkflowInfo`, and `ActivityInfo` — so no author-declared feature can silently take wrong effect. **No core export needed** (`ActivityInfo` is already `pub` and reachable under `default-features = false`), **no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, the additive `schedule_to_close_at` column needs no migration (brand-new crate), no core change**. Docs: a new "Unsupported `ActivityInfo`-level features — honored or rejected at registration" section in the crate docs (`lib.rs`), and the `register_activity` doc example updated to the info-based path. Tests, TDD (RED verified against the pre-fix code by neutering the enforcement → the honor test wedges at `WaitingTimer`): `runtime.rs` `activity_audit` units (a plain activity registers; every honored/inert field passes the audit; EVERY rejected field is rejected BY NAME — exhaustive, via struct-update over a macro-built base `ActivityInfo`); `worker.rs` unit `schedule_to_close_exceeded_truth_table` (`None`/non-positive = no cap; `>=` semantics for both the pre-run and retry checks); and `tests/activity_info_features.rs` (5 public-API integration tests: the money `schedule_to_close_deadline_records_activity_timed_out_not_retry_or_complete` — a `schedule_to_close = "1s"` + `retry = fixed(5, 30s)` always-failing activity records a terminal `ActivityTimedOut { ScheduleToClose }` (never `ActivityCompleted`, never a retry-exhaustion `ActivityFailed`) and replays `ReplaySucceeded` on the core `WorkflowReplayer`; RED pre-fix — the run wedges/retries past the deadline; a generous-deadline control; two reject `#[should_panic]` tests naming `heartbeat_timeout` / `local = true`; and a plain-activity no-regression). The ~30 existing test call sites were mechanically migrated from `register_activity` to `register_activity_raw` (their hand-made bodies carry no declared defaults).
- **Phase 5.1** (implemented): autumn-harvest-sqlite v0.1 hardening: freeze activity defaults, reuse-policy matrix, race fairness — see issue #1068. Implements three follow-up hardening checkboxes tracked on #1068 (v0.1 PR #1069 deferred each with an explicit Codex P2 reply). Footprint: the `autumn-harvest-sqlite/` crate only — **zero core changes** (both required core types, `WorkflowIdReusePolicy` and `WorkflowEvent::WorkflowCancelled`, are already re-exported without the `db` feature). **Item 1 — Freeze resolved activity defaults on the durable task row.** The retry policy (`max_attempts`/backoff/non-retryable list), the cross-retry `schedule_to_close` deadline, and per-attempt `start_to_close` are now resolved ONCE and frozen on the `harvest_tasks` row — at schedule time when the activity is already registered, else at first claim (the sanctioned fallback for a late-registered activity, guaranteed present since an unregistered activity is released back to PENDING and never claimed). Later claims read the frozen values verbatim and never re-consult the mutable in-memory registry, so a crash/reopen or a re-registration of the activity between attempts can no longer shift an in-flight task's policy/deadlines (matching the Postgres path, which stores these on the task). Two additive columns on `harvest_tasks`: `schedule_to_close_at` (frozen absolute deadline = `scheduled_at + schedule_to_close`) and `defaults_frozen` (a flag disambiguating "not yet resolved" from "resolved to None", so a genuinely-None field is never re-resolved from a changed registry). Existing DB files are upgraded by an additive `schema::migrate()` — a `PRAGMA table_info` probe + `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` (never drop/rename, idempotent on every open). Frozen scalars live only on `harvest_tasks`, never `harvest_events`, so replay determinism and the append-only invariant are untouched; the `max_attempts` read-site is self-enforcing (a frozen task never falls back to `spec.max_attempts`). **Item 2 — `(workflow_name, workflow_id)` reuse-policy matrix for `start_workflow_with_id`.** Previously every call minted a fresh `ExecutionId`, so duplicate webhook/business-id delivery created multiple executions and repeated side effects. The core PLAIN-start `WorkflowIdReusePolicy` matrix is now implemented faithfully (verified cell-by-cell against `autumn-harvest/src/execution.rs`), enforced atomically in the single-writer start transaction (no Postgres-style partial unique index — that would fail to build on reopen of a pre-#1068 file already holding duplicate active ids; a non-unique lookup index is added instead). `start_workflow_with_id` becomes idempotent-by-default (`AllowDuplicate`); a new `start_workflow_with_reuse_policy(name, id, input, policy) -> StartOutcome{exec_id, created}` takes an explicit policy and surfaces the new `SqliteError::AlreadyExists`. Matrix over the states the backend holds (none/RUNNING/COMPLETED/FAILED): AllowDuplicate → return existing; RejectDuplicate → AlreadyExists; AllowDuplicateFailedOnly → replace a FAILED prior (seal + fresh) else return existing; TerminateIfRunning → cancel-if-RUNNING (append `WorkflowCancelled` + release pending tasks/timers) + seal + fresh. "Seal" mirrors core's `replace_execution` (prior → `CONTINUED_AS_NEW`); the active-prior lookup excludes the sealed set `{CONTINUED_AS_NEW, TERMINATED}`, faithfully reproducing core's uniqueness-excludes-terminal nuance (RejectDuplicate rejects COMPLETED/FAILED priors but creates fresh over a sealed prior). No new `WorkflowEvent` variant. sqlite's single-writer `TerminateIfRunning` forcefully seals the prior (equivalent observable outcome to core: prior inactive + cancellation recorded, new run active) since the prior is immediately replaced and never driven again. **Item 3 — `ctx.race()` fairness under zero-delay retry policies.** Previously a race branch using `RetryPolicy::fixed(_, 0ms)` requeued at the same `now` keeping its original lower `seq`, so `claim_next_ready_task(... ORDER BY seq ...)` re-selected it before any ready sibling — letting the lowest-index branch monopolize the drain and settle the race by failing, cancelling a ready sibling that would have won. On an IMMEDIATE (zero-delay) requeue (`run_at <= now`), the task is now moved to the BACK of the ready queue via a fresh `MAX(seq)+1` (`requeue_task_to_back`), so `ORDER BY seq` yields to every ready sibling before the just-failed branch re-runs (round-robin). A genuine backoff (`run_at > now`) already yields via its future `run_at` and is left byte-for-byte unchanged. The winner remains a pure function of recorded history (the core `race_winner:` marker + terminal-event order), so replay is deterministic. **Review & gate.** A four-lens adversarial review (determinism/replay, schema-migration/durability, core-fidelity, test-quality) found no P1/P2 issues and confirmed all three claims + cell-by-cell matrix fidelity + zero core changes; five P3 nits were closed (self-enforcing `max_attempts` read-site, a late-registration first-claim-freeze coverage test, a `seq` index, two doc comments). Local CI gate at the exact CI toolchains is green: `cargo +1.97.0 fmt --check`, `cargo +1.97.0 clippy -p autumn-harvest-sqlite --all-targets -- -D warnings` (two 1.97-only lints fixed that a 1.94.1 run missed), `cargo +1.97.0 test -p autumn-harvest-sqlite` (156 tests), and `cargo +1.88.0 check --workspace` (MSRV). New/changed tests: `freeze_activity_defaults.rs` (+ claim-time-freeze + migration), `reuse_policy.rs` (full matrix, 15), `race_fairness.rs` (fairness + replay-determinism), all TDD RED→GREEN.
- **Tooling** — Test INIT_SQL bundle migration-drift guard (PR #1031). **Tooling/testing** (implemented): Test suites build their Postgres schema from hand-maintained `const INIT_SQL = concat!(include_str!(".../migrations/.../up.sql"), ...)` lists. When a migration adds a column to a hub table, a bundle that misses it fails **at runtime** (`column "..." does not exist`) — but `include_str!` compiles fine, and dozens of these suites are **compiled but never executed** in CI, so the drift is invisible until someone runs them locally. This bit CI ≥4 times in one week (latest: `nd_block_tests` missing the #604 build-ramp migration, with no CI run step at all). This slice makes both failure modes hard CI errors going forward, ships a drift-proof shared schema bundle, and fixes the concrete known gaps so they actually run in CI. **No product-code behavior change.** **Paved path** — `autumn_harvest::full_migrations_sql()` (new, `build.rs`-generated): the complete migration set concatenated in timestamp order, proven to apply cleanly on Postgres 16. New/migrated tests use this instead of a hand-rolled subset, so their schema can never drift. **Migration-hygiene guard** (`tests/integration/migration_hygiene.rs`, no-DB, every OS): asserts no two migration dirs share a version timestamp (Diesel silently drops one — this bit trunk this week) and that the generated bundle is complete. Replaces a copy that was triple-feature-gated and never ran in CI. **CI-run-step coverage guard** (`tests/integration/ci_run_coverage.rs`, no-DB, fail-closed): enumerates every db-gated test and asserts each has a Docker-backed run step in `ci.yml` or is on a reason-annotated allowlist. Feature-aware (a `testing+db` suite's step must carry `--features testing`), self-testing (fails loudly if a `ci.yml` reformat breaks the parser), and ratcheted (`ALLOWLIST_MAX_LEN` forbids silent growth). Once a db suite actually runs, Postgres itself catches future column drift — no brittle static analyzer needed. **Fixed drift + harness bugs** by running suites against a live DB: 4 concrete drift bugs (`nd_block`, `completion_callback`, `worker_session` all missing `build_policy_ramp`; plugin `build_ramp` missing `harvest_audit_log`) each swapped to `full_migrations_sql()`; plus a second, pre-existing nd_block harness bug where 6 tests fired a durable timer but never made the parked task claimable (`make_task_claimable_now` existed but was unused), so the divergent worker never re-claimed it — these tests had never actually executed, now 8/8 green. Docker-backed run steps were wired for `nd_block`, `worker_session`, and plugin `build_ramp` (all verified green on local PG16) and removed from the allowlist. **Residuals (tracked, not fixed here):** running the never-run suites showed drift is systemic — **73 db-gated suites** (42 core + 31 plugin) are still compiled-but-never-run in CI, now explicitly tracked by the coverage-guard allowlist, each with a reason; most still use hand-rolled bundles. Two genuine non-schema bugs surfaced and were handed off: `completion_callback_tests::scanner_scopes_claims_...shared_pool` (duplicate-key on the active-uniqueness index, test-logic, #605 — kept allowlisted so its run step stays blocked) and `event_batch_tests::size_triggered_flush_threads_completion_callbacks_into_the_started_execution` (a separate pre-existing failure, unmodified here). **Recommended follow-up:** sweep all remaining hand-rolled INIT_SQL bundles onto `full_migrations_sql()`, then progressively wire run steps and shrink the allowlist toward zero — the guards + paved path make that mechanical and block any *new* drift or never-run suite in the meantime. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no new migration, no route/contract change, no replay/determinism impact, no production-logic change** — test infra only (the nd_block fix is test-harness code). Verification (local CI mirror; DB suites executed on Postgres 16): guards 8/8 in the no-DB CI leg (all OSes); `nd_block` 8/8, `worker_session` 17/17, `build_ramp` 6/6 against live PG16; fmt / clippy (harvest `--all-features --tests`, plugin `--all-targets`, macros) / no-DB tests (95 lib + 823 integration) / `--all-features --tests --no-run` all green.
- **Tooling** — Wire 3 previously-never-run DB test suites into CI (PR #1037, follow-up to #1031). **Tooling/testing** (implemented): PR #1031's CI-run-step coverage guard surfaced that three db-gated core integration suites — `workflow_retry_tests`, `completion_callback_tests`, `event_batch_tests` — compiled in CI but never executed against a live Postgres, hiding **5 test-harness bugs** (not production regressions: each failing test was contradicted by a *passing sibling* encoding the real production contract). This slice fixes all 5, wires the three suites into Docker-backed CI run steps, and removes them from the coverage-guard allowlist. **No product-code behavior change** — every fix corrects a test to assert a TRUE production contract already proven by a passing sibling. **The 5 fixes** (all in `autumn-harvest/tests/integration/`): `workflow_retry_tests::cancelled_workflow_is_not_retried` — waited for `wait_for_state(exec, &["SUSPENDED"])`, but `"SUSPENDED"` is not a persisted state (a timer-parked run's row is `"RUNNING"` with `worker_id IS NULL`; the state CHECK constraint forbids `"SUSPENDED"`). Fixed: the `timer_wait_handler` timer is lengthened to 3600s so it cannot fire during the poll window, and a new `wait_for_parked` helper polls the `harvest_timers` table for the durable timer row (the unambiguous "parked" signal) instead of an unreachable state string. The cancel + not-retried assertions now actually run. `workflow_retry_tests::workflow_non_retryable_error_no_retry` — the fixture returned `Err("NullPointerException: bad input")` with `non_retryable_errors: ["NullPointerException"]`, but `RetryPolicy::is_non_retryable` matches on **exact equality**, not substring (documented, and proven by passing siblings `workflow_sentinel_string_non_retryable_message_no_retry` and `workflow_typed_non_retryable_error_type_no_retry`). Fixed by converting `non_retryable_fail_handler` to return a **typed** `WorkflowFailure::new("NullPointerException", "NullPointerException: bad input")` (mirroring the passing typed sibling), so the #523 retry gate's typed `error_type` class match fires on exact class equality. The typed form was chosen over a bare exact-string `Err("NullPointerException")` because it faithfully preserves the fixture's intent — exception CLASS as `error_type` + detail as the human message — and matches the passing sibling's shape exactly. `workflow_retry_tests::workflow_retry_exhaustion_counts_as_one_failure` — its final block loaded executions filtered by the ORIGINAL `workflow_id`, but a #523 retry run gets a **distinct UUID `workflow_id`** (the tested contract, per passing `retry_run_has_fresh_history_and_correct_linkage`), so the attempt-2 row was never found and `.expect("attempt 2 must exist")` panicked. Fixed by selecting the retry run via the `retry_of_exec_id` FK — using the file's own `wait_for_retry_state` helper — matching this file's `failed_count` loop. `completion_callback_tests::scanner_scopes_claims_to_the_assigned_shard_when_shards_share_a_pool` — the `insert_terminal_execution` helper hardcoded `(process_refund, wf-1)`; this test inserts two COMPLETED rows, colliding on the partial active-uniqueness index `harvest_we_workflow_name_workflow_id_active_key` (COMPLETED is not excluded). Fixed by parameterizing the helper with a `workflow_id` arg and giving the two execs distinct ids (`wf-0`/`wf-1`); all other callers pass their existing `wf-1` id, so they are unchanged. `event_batch_tests::size_triggered_flush_threads_completion_callbacks_into_the_started_execution` — admitted the SAME callback array on all 3 batch admissions and asserted the stored column equals the single-element array. Production intentionally **concatenates** per admission (issue #921) and dedups only at delivery, so the stored value is `[hook, hook, hook]` (len 3), not `[hook]` — the concatenate-and-merge contract proven by the passing sibling `a_later_admissions_completion_callbacks_are_merged_not_dropped` (two distinct targets → len 2). Fixed the assertion to expect the concatenated union. **CI wiring + allowlist:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s Docker-backed step for `workflow_retry_tests::workflow_typed` (a `::` sub-filter that masked the other tests) was expanded to run the full `workflow_retry_tests` module, and new Docker-backed run steps were added for `completion_callback_tests` and `event_batch_tests` (matching the file's `-p autumn-harvest --test integration -- <module> --test-threads=1`, `if: runner.os == 'Linux'` convention). The three entries were removed from `ci_run_coverage.rs`'s `ALLOWLIST`, `ALLOWLIST_MAX_LEN` dropped 77 → 74, and the two now-unused reason constants (`ALLOWLIST_WORKFLOW_RETRY_REASON`, `ALLOWLIST_COMPLETION_CALLBACK_REASON`) removed. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/contract change, no replay/determinism impact, no production-logic change** — test-harness fixes + CI wiring only. Verified against a local Postgres 16: all three suites fully green; plus fmt / clippy (`-p autumn-harvest --all-features --tests -- -D warnings`) / no-DB unit + integration tests / the `ci_run_coverage` guard.
- **CI** — manifest-driven integration-suite runner (test-infra). Replaced the ~35 copy-pasted per-suite `cargo test` steps in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `test` job — 29 Docker-backed run steps, the shared 17-token plugin `--no-run` compile line, the `mcp_tools_integration` compile step, and 5 all-OS target-run steps — with **one parameterized runner** (`.github/ci/run-suites.sh`) reading a **line-oriented, `merge=union`-safe manifest** (`.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`). Adding an integration suite is now **one sorted manifest line** — no `ci.yml` edit, no shared-tail conflict. **Root cause fixed.** Three shared append-tail regions made any two concurrent suite-adding PRs collide: the per-suite Docker run steps, the one physical plugin `--no-run` line (every new plugin suite appended a `--test` token to it), and the Rust `ALLOWLIST` array. The manifest is `merge=union` (see `.gitattributes`), so two PRs each appending a line both land with **no textual conflict**; a union-merge duplicate/reorder residue is caught deterministically (never a conflict) by `ci_run_coverage.rs::manifest_is_sorted_and_unique`, which prints a one-command `sort -u` fix. **Manifest schema** (`osclass crate target features filter`, whitespace-columnar, `#`-comment tolerant, `-` = none): `osclass` ∈ `linux` (run serial on Linux against Docker Postgres + compile-checked on every OS) | `allos` (run on all 3 OSes, parallel, no live DB) | `compileonly` (`--no-run` on every OS, never executed). `--test-threads=1` and `--no-run` are **derived from `osclass`** by the runner and never written in the manifest — so the `--test-threads=1`-after-`--`-after-filter ordering is correct by construction (kills the mis-emit class). For `autumn-harvest` `integration` `allos` rows the runner adds `--no-default-features` (strips the crate's `default = ["db", "unified-dag-execution"]`, since `allos` has no Postgres); this reproduces the old `:142`/`:145` commands byte-for-byte while leaving the `property` `allos` row (which keeps `db`+`unified-dag-execution`) unchanged. **Every generated command is byte-faithful to the pre-refactor `ci.yml`.** **Runner** (`.github/ci/run-suites.sh`, `run <linux|allos>` and `compile` modes) is bash-3.2 / Git-Bash portable (no associative arrays, no `mapfile`; compile-mode batching groups by `(crate, features)` via `sort` + adjacent-run walk). It wraps each suite in `::group::`/`::endgroup::`, **collects failures instead of aborting on the first** (a strict improvement over the old fail-fast leg, which hid every suite after the first failure), and exits non-zero at the end printing every failed suite. `compile` mode regenerates both the shared plugin `--no-run` batch and the `mcp,unified-dag-execution` batch from the manifest, so every `linux`/`compileonly` plugin target is still compile-checked on macOS/Windows. **Gating preserved exactly.** The 3 replacing steps keep **per-step** `if:` (`allos`/`compile` → `needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'`; `linux` → `runner.os == 'Linux' && needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'`) and `shell: bash` — never hoisted to a job-level `if:` on the matrix job (which would strip the leg contexts and hang branch protection). The heterogeneous steps (fmt/clippy, `--lib`, the core blanket `--all-features --tests --no-run` compile, `cargo build --example`, whole-crate and example runs, `cargo clean`) stay hand-written. **Coverage guard rewrite** (`autumn-harvest/tests/integration/ci_run_coverage.rs`) now derives "which suites have a real CI run" from the **manifest** (structured columns) instead of scraping `ci.yml` `run:` lines: the `--test-threads=1` special-casing, `--no-run` string-grepping, and `module::filter` re-tokenization are deleted. Preserved: the ratcheted `ALLOWLIST` + `ALLOWLIST_MAX_LEN` cap (73 entries / cap 77, unchanged — the covered set is identical), feature-awareness (a `testing`+`db` suite's manifest row must carry `testing`), the plugin dir-scan, the all-`#[ignore]`d handling, and the stale-allowlist check. Added: (i) `ci_yaml_invokes_the_runner_against_the_manifest` (a manifest can't be silently ignored — `ci.yml` must invoke `run-suites.sh {compile, run allos, run linux}` and the script must reference the manifest path), and (ii) `manifest_is_sorted_and_unique` (union-artifact self-heal with a `sort -u` fix message). The guard was proven fail-closed: deleting one `linux` line makes it fail naming that suite and printing the exact manifest line to re-add. **Adding a suite going forward:** append one sorted line to `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt` (keep the header comment on top; `sort -u` the data lines). No `ci.yml` edit; no `ALLOWLIST` edit for a wired suite. No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no runtime-code change — CI infrastructure only.
- **Docs** — Child-timeout hard-cap deadline-cleanup known limitation (PR #1041, follow-up to #1029). **Docs-only** (implemented): documents a pre-existing edge of the `execute_child_workflow_timeout` / `spawn_child_workflow_timeout` primitive (issue #779): if the parent hits its event-history hard cap on the same decision cycle the deadline branch resolves, the seal routes through `fail_workflow_for_history_cap` → `move_workflow_to_dlq_for_history_cap`, which bypasses `persist_terminal_outcome_commands` and therefore drops the deadline branch's `CancelRaceLosers` cleanup — the over-deadline child is not request-cancelled and its `__child_timeout:` timer row is left `fired = false`. This is the same terminal-seal-drops-pending-commands class as the #782 panic path and the #601 fan-out limitation, only reachable on a run already being force-killed at the hard cap; the awaited child runs to its own natural terminal (or its `execution_timeout`, #243) as orphaned work, and remediation is an operator cancel/terminate of that child. Added as a new "Known limitation" bullet in CLAUDE.md's Child-or-Deadline "Composition caveats" list (consistent with the sibling panic-limitation bullet), and appended as a matching sentence to the primitive's `# Known limitation` doc comment in `autumn-harvest/src/context.rs` so the source doc and CLAUDE.md agree. **No code/behavior change, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no replay/determinism impact** — prose only.

- **#476-parity — signal-or-deadline race follow-ups (from PR #1029 review).** Two fixes to the issue #476 `receive_signal_timeout` / `wait_for_signal_timeout` machinery, porting fixes already made to the issue #779 child-timeout twin (PR #1029). `context.rs`-only plus one pure read-only `replay.rs` helper; **no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration.** (1) **Timer-retention leak on signal-win:** the still-armed `__signal_timeout:{seq}:{name}` durable timer was left `fired=false` in `harvest_timers` forever (a completed workflow's task is never re-claimed to ingest `TimerFired`, and `retention::should_skip_candidate` treats any pending timer as an inflight dependency), permanently pinning the run against retention. The `SignalOrTimerMatch::SignalWon` arm now pushes `WorkflowCommand::CancelRaceLosers { timers: [timer_id] }` (applied by `worker::apply_race_loser_cancellations` → `queue::delete_pending_timer`), **gated on the new pure `HistoryMatcher::history_contains_timer_started(&timer_id)`** so the stashed-signal-before-race short-circuit (which records no `TimerStarted`) emits no spurious teardown — a discriminator the child twin doesn't need (a winning child always records `ChildWorkflowStarted`+`TimerStarted`). The redundant `CancelRaceLosers` push in `race_timer_signal_impl` was removed (exactly one teardown per race-win). Re-pushing on every strict-replay cycle is divergence-free (`CancelRaceLosers` appends no event; `delete_pending_timer` is idempotent). Inherited residuals — a workflow-handler panic before persist (#782) or a history-hard-cap seal on the same cycle drops the pending teardown — documented not fixed, identical to the twin. (2) **Canary-frontier false non-determinism:** `match_signal_or_timer`'s `InProgress` arm errored unconditionally under `strict_replay`, so a deploy replay canary (`run_workflow_canary`) over a parked signal-timeout race false-reported non-determinism. Now suppressed under `self.canary_mode && at_frontier` (`at_frontier = !m.has_non_lifecycle_unconsumed()`), byte-identical to the child twin's `InProgress` guard; non-canary strict `WorkflowReplayer` runs still error (fixture-problem detection intact) and a genuine `Diverged` result always errors. (3) **Over-deadline reorder — deliberate refute:** unlike child terminals (appended out-of-band by worker child-wake / operator cancel-terminate / child execution-timeout), signals have no out-of-band `SignalReceived` append — `send_signal` only queues a `harvest_signals` row and wakes; `SignalReceived` is materialized solely by `ingest_due_timers_and_signals`, which atomically interleaves signal-vs-deadline by DB clock via `merge_wake_events` (`received_at < fires_at` ⇒ signal-first) — so the twin's `materialize_due_child_timeout_deadlines` hazard is structurally unreachable. Documented as a rustdoc asymmetry note on `wait_for_signal_timeout`; the existing `signal_timeout_timeout_branch_with_ignored_late_signal_replays_succeeded` replayer test already pins the "late signal after `TimerFired` loses" contract. **This supersedes the stale Phase 3.24 note** that "`wait_for_signal_timeout` itself still leaves its timer armed on signal-win — the same latent retention leak, tracked as a separate follow-up." Tests (red→green, no-DB): two `context.rs` unit tests (exactly-one / zero teardown), a `history_contains_timer_started` matcher test, four `replayer_tests.rs` canary-parity tests.

Neither the existing `migration_hygiene` completeness guard nor the `ci_run_coverage` run-coverage guard catches a reintroduced hand-rolled bundle. **After:** a no-DB guard in `tests/integration/migration_hygiene.rs` fails if any file under `autumn-harvest/tests/**` or `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/**` contains a hand-rolled migration `include_str!` outside a small, commented allowlist — making the paved path self-enforcing. **No product-code behavior change.** **Allowlist** (deliberately-partial fixtures, each entry commented with why): `integration_e2e.rs` (legacy upgrade-path / workflow-start-uniqueness excluded); `schedule_update_integration.rs` (omits `harvest_start_throttle` for the `to_regclass` graceful-degradation path); `timeline_integration.rs` (inserts into `harvest_dag_runs`, which the full bundle drops — `20260514000000_drop_harvest_dag_runs`); and `outbox_integration.rs` (a separate plugin app-DB `harvest_workflow_outbox` migration, not part of the core `migrations/` bundle). Adding a new partial fixture requires a conscious allowlist edit + documented reason. **Design:** the guard is *bidirectional* — it fails both on a new offender outside the allowlist **and** on a stale allowlist entry (a fixture later converted to `full_migrations_sql()` that no longer contains a hand-rolled include), so the allowlist can't rot. Detection is text-based (per-line: `include_str!` + `migrations` + `up.sql`), so it catches a reintroduction regardless of `#[cfg]` gating; the guard file itself is excluded (it carries those tokens as literals), and `ci_run_coverage.rs`'s own non-migration `include_str!(".github/...")` lines are correctly not flagged. A pure unit test (`line_detector_flags_a_handrolled_include_and_ignores_others`) locks the detector semantics. **No new suite** — a test fn added to the already-run no-DB `migration_hygiene` target, so no `integration-suites.txt` change; `ci_run_coverage` is unchanged (stays 13/13). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no new migration, no route/contract change, no replay/determinism impact, no production-logic change** — test infra only. The structural check is also strictly more precise — the tokens must belong to a real `include_str!` argument — so prose/doc comments merely mentioning `migrations/…/up.sql` are no longer flagged. The 4-entry allowlist and the single-line `line_is_handrolled_migration_include` unit predicate are unchanged.

The two remaining #1045 failures — the start-throttle admission-gate and `query_integration::ac6` (`drive_query_replay` misclassifying a `yield_now` spin as `410` instead of `408`) — turned out to be real production bugs and are tracked in separate PRs.
- **Fix** — query-replay suspension classification: spinning terminal query is 408, cold-park query serves fast (issue #612). `executor::drive_query_replay` (the read-only replay driver behind post-mortem queries on terminal workflows, issue #612) misclassified `Poll::Pending` cycles because it inferred workflow suspension from a custom `QueryReplayWaker` flag — assuming `tokio::task::yield_now()` calls the waker synchronously — but inside a tokio runtime (the real HTTP query path) `yield_now` **defers** its wake to the scheduler queue rather than invoking the custom waker synchronously. The sync driver's tight manual poll loop never yields back to the scheduler, so the deferred wake was never delivered and a genuinely-spinning terminal query was misread as a command-suspension → `classify_terminal_query(Suspended, sealed=false)` → **410** instead of the #612-documented **408**. **Fix (executor-scoped redesign):** discriminate a `Poll::Pending` by a **per-poll delta** on the emitted replay-significant command count, then a **three-way** suspension discriminator: **Case 1 — command this poll** (positive delta): a genuine workflow suspension on a durable command (`WaitForActivity`/`StartTimer`/`WaitForSignal`/`StartChildWorkflow`/`ContinueAsNew`/…) → `Suspended`. **Case 2 — self-wake spin** (zero delta, `QueryReplayWaker` flag set): a `tokio::task::yield_now()` spin → keep driving to the deadline → `TimedOut` → 408. **Case 3 — command-less cold park** (zero delta, flag cold): the workflow parked waiting on an external re-poll that never comes during a query drive (the sole engine primitive that does this is non-timeout `ctx.await_condition`, which pushes no command and leaves its waker cold) → `Suspended` **immediately**, so a RUNNING query over such a park serves its partial state fast rather than burning the whole `query_timeout` budget, and a terminal run sealed while parked on it serves 200 (not 408/410). The command signal is now a **delta** (`WorkflowContext::count_commands`), not a bare "any pending" peek: the command buffer is never drained during a query drive, so an "any pending" check stays true forever after the first command and would misclassify a *later* cold `await_condition` park as still making progress and busy-drive it to 408 — the delta reflects only what THIS poll emitted. Command classification reuses the executor's shared `is_replay_significant_command` deny-list (`UpsertSearchAttributes`/`SetCurrentDetails`/`CancelRaceLosers`), also used by the `run_strict_with_ctx`/`run_workflow_canary` non-determinism checks, so command kinds are never re-enumerated by hand. **Sync + async twin driver.** The 16 pure `#[test]` callers run out of a tokio runtime (where `yield_now` fires synchronously) and keep the synchronous `drive_query_replay`; the single production caller (`hydrate_ctx_for_query`, already async) now uses `drive_query_replay_async`, which opens a **single `tokio::task::yield_now().await` quiet window** on a zero-delta poll to observe tokio's *deferred* `yield_now` wake before deciding case 2 vs case 3 — replacing the old busy-wait `std::thread::yield_now()`, so a spinning query cooperatively yields the runtime each cycle instead of hard-pinning a core. Both loop over one shared, `!Send`-safe `poll_query_step` helper that **builds and drops the `waker_ref`/`std::task::Context` internally**, so nothing `!Send` crosses the async driver's `.await` (the returned future stays `Send`, as the axum handler requires). **Behavior change:** a spinning query on a terminal workflow returns **408** (retryable request timeout) instead of a misleading **410**; a RUNNING or sealed-while-parked query over `await_condition` now serves fast/200 instead of burning the full budget. The #612 contracts are preserved: sealed-while-parked runs still `Suspended` → **200**, truncated history (no terminal seal) still → **410**, code-drift still → **410**, unregistered name still → **404**. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route change** — production files only (`executor.rs`, `context.rs`, plugin `api.rs` call site). Pure `query_terminal` suite green (19/19, incl. the new RED→GREEN `await_condition` fast-suspend and sealed-while-parked tests, both proven to busy-drive to timeout under the old `any_pending_command` guard); `query_integration::ac6_spinning_replay_returns_408` still 408. Both suites run in CI.
- **`harvest det-check` CLI — the runnable front door for `det_check`, plus one first-party hop of transitive reachability (issue #778).** Turns the already-shipped `det_check` engine (DET001–DET011, `harvest-suppress`, `DetCheckReport`, `has_hard_blockers`) — which had **no runnable front door** — into a governance gate authors actually invoke, and closes the exact coverage gap #386 punted: a non-deterministic call (`chrono::Utc::now()`, `rand::random()`, …) factored out of a `#[workflow]` body into a **first-party helper function the body calls directly** used to sail past `cargo build`, the macro lint, and the body scanner, only to DLQ post-deploy. **Read-only source analysis: no `WorkflowEvent` variant, no event-schema change, no migration, no change to the `::autumn_harvest::` macro-path contract, no runtime code touched.** *(PR #1055.)* **Engine (`autumn-harvest/src/det_check.rs`):** (a) **serde (AC2)** — `DetSeverity` (with `#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]` → `"error"`/`"warning"`), `DetLocation`, `DetFinding`, `DetSuppression`, and `DetCheckReport` now derive `serde::Serialize` for `--format json`. (b) **`DetLocation.col` (AC1)** — a new `pub col: u32` (always `> 0`), computed as the 1-based character column of the matched substring in the raw source line for the substring-table rules (DET001–DET009, DET011); the bespoke DET010 pass and any offset-less site report `1`. (c) **`DetFinding.via_helper: Option<String>` (AC4)** — `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if)]`; `None` for a direct-in-body finding (`workflow_name = Some(wf)`, unchanged), `Some(helper)` for a transitive finding (`workflow_name = Some(entry_point)`, `location` = the offending line inside the helper). (d) **Transitive reachability** — the old `#[workflow]`-only `extract_workflow_bodies` is generalized to `extract_all_functions`, which walks each file tracking brace depth and captures every **top-level** (file-depth-0) `fn` definition with `is_workflow`/`is_activity` flags and an owned body (so a cross-file index can outlive per-file line buffers); methods inside `impl`/`trait` blocks (depth > 0) are never captured. `check_source` resolves one-hop calls within one file; `check_dir` first builds a first-party function index across every `*.rs` in the tree, then follows one hop of **direct free-function calls** (`helper(` — never `x.helper(` method calls, never `m::helper(` path-qualified calls, never identifier-continuation) from each `#[workflow]` body into plain (non-workflow, non-activity) helpers, scans those helper bodies with the *same* per-body analysis (all rules, suppressions included), and attributes findings to the entry point via `via_helper`. **One hop only** (workflow → A → B is not followed into B); **`#[activity]` callees are skipped** (an activity legitimately reading the clock reached from a workflow is not flagged); a helper **name defined by more than one plain helper is ambiguous and never resolved**, so an ambiguous resolution can never introduce a false positive. Findings are deduped by `(rule_id, entry-workflow, file, line)`. `check_dir` now also **skips `target` and hidden directories** so a scan of a repo root stays fast and never lints generated code. **CLI (`autumn-harvest-cli`):** new `harvest det-check [PATHS...]` subcommand (default `.`). Local `--format text|json` flag (distinct from the global `--output`), `--deny-warnings`, and `--list-suppressions`. Handled entirely in-process before the HTTP execute path (mirrors the Tui early-return; `api_request()` for it is `unreachable!`). Text mode prints `file:line:col DETxxx (safe alternative: …)` per finding — with `[in helper `H` reached from workflow `W`]` for a transitive finding — plus an always-echoed `suppressed:` audit footer (AC5). `--list-suppressions` prints `file:line RULEID "reason"` per active suppression and exits `0` (AC6). Exit codes: `0` clean, `1` on any hard-blocker (or, with `--deny-warnings`, any warning); findings/JSON are always on stdout before the non-zero exit. New `CliError::DetCheckFindings { errors, warnings }` (exit code `1`, the default arm). Formatting/gating live in pure, unit-testable helpers (`det_check_report_for_paths`, `format_det_findings_text`, `format_det_suppressions`, `format_det_suppressions_list`, `det_check_json`, `det_check_gate`, `run_det_check`). **AC4 boundary (mirrors #386):** `#[activity]` bodies, method/path-qualified calls, two-plus hops, third-party crates, trait-object dispatch, function pointers, and closures-captured-by-reference are all out of scope. **AC8 (tree is clean):** `harvest det-check autumn-harvest/src autumn-harvest/examples autumn-harvest-plugin/src autumn-harvest-cli/src` reports **zero** hard-blocker findings in ~0.9 s. One pre-existing offender surfaced and was resolved with the sanctioned escape hatch: `autumn-harvest/examples/deterministic_primitives.rs` reads `std::env::var("DEPLOY_REGION")` **inside a `ctx.side_effect(...)` closure** (a deterministic, recorded-once read the text scanner can't see through) — suppressed with `// harvest-suppress: DET004 "env read is wrapped in ctx.side_effect(); recorded once and replayed deterministically"`. A whole-workspace `harvest det-check .` scan (~1.4 s) surfaces only the deliberately-non-deterministic trybuild fixtures under `autumn-harvest/tests/compile_fail/` — **true positives** that exist precisely to be rejected by the compile-time guardrail, left unmodified (a comment line would shift their committed `.stderr` snapshots and break the macro tests). **Docs (AC7):** new "Running the check in CI" section in `docs/workflow-determinism-guide.md` — flags, exit-code contract, the AC4 boundary, a GitHub Actions job snippet, and a git pre-commit hook, plus the note that the shipped examples/fixtures pass. **Success metric (proven by test):** a 14-workflow fixture (7 hard-blocker classes × {direct-in-body, one-hop-in-helper}) flags **100% of the 7 helper-reachable (transitive) violations** — the class today's macro lint + scanner catch 0% of — and produces exactly 14 findings (zero false positives on the fixture), with the self-scan of `autumn-harvest/src` staying clean (well under the < 5 s / no-DB / no-dependent-build budget; ~0.9 s measured). **Tests:** engine — transitive same-file / cross-file (`check_dir` over a tempdir) / two-hop-not-flagged / activity-callee-not-flagged / method-call-not-resolved / clean-helper boundary tests, the 14-fixture success-metric test, and `via_helper`/`col`/serde-round-trip metadata tests in `autumn-harvest/tests/integration/det_check_tests.rs`, plus `fn_decl_name`/`is_activity_attr` module unit tests. CLI — inline `#[cfg(test)]` tests in `src/lib.rs` (parse → `Commands::DetCheck { format: Json, .. }`, defaults, `DetCheckFormat::default() == Text`, the text-line/suppression formatters, `det_check_gate`, exit-code, JSON serialization) and black-box integration tests in `tests/integration/det_check_cli.rs` (text + JSON attribution over a tempdir, clean tree → Ok, `--deny-warnings` gating, `--list-suppressions` listing, hard-blocker → exit 1, missing-path read error). Deliberately **not** added to `request_mapping.rs`/`contract_coverage.rs` (no HTTP route — mirrors Tui/Events). **Post-review hardening (four-agent review):** (1) **AC8 — bare `harvest det-check` at the repo root now exits `0`.** `collect_rs_sources` / `check_paths` skip any directory named `compile_fail` (alongside `target` and hidden dirs), so the deliberately-broken trybuild fixtures under `autumn-harvest/tests/compile_fail/` — true positives that exist to be rejected by the compile-time guardrail and carry committed `.stderr` snapshots — are no longer lint-flagged by the text pre-check; a bare `det-check` (default `.`) reports zero findings. (2) **Zero-FP — closures and fn-pointer params never resolve to a same-named free helper** (#386 explicitly excludes function pointers and closures). `collect_direct_free_fn_calls` now shadow-suppresses any call whose name is bound by the caller: parameter names (`FnDef.params`, over-collected from the param list via `extract_fn_params`) plus body `let`/closure bindings (`collect_body_let_idents`, reusing `det010_parse_let`). Safe-direction: a name that is both shadowed and legitimately a free-fn call is conservatively skipped (an accepted false-negative, never a false-positive). (3) **Multi-file / symlink / non-UTF-8 — one shared cross-path index.** New engine entry point `check_paths(&[&Path])` collects the full `.rs` source set across **all** path arguments into a **single** first-party index and scans once, so a cross-file transitive violation is caught even when the two files are passed as **separate** arguments (the `det-check $(git diff --name-only '*.rs')` changed-files CI pattern that per-file scanning silently missed — a false-negative on a determinism gate). It de-duplicates overlapping arguments (a dir plus a file inside it, or a repeated path) by canonicalized path so nothing double-counts; skips symlinked files and directories via `entry.file_type()?.is_symlink()` (a self-referential dir symlink can no longer explode the scan, and a `../..` symlink can no longer pull out-of-tree files in); and skips a single unreadable / non-UTF-8 `.rs` file mid-walk with a warning naming the file rather than `?`-aborting the whole scan. A missing top-level path argument still surfaces as an error. `check_dir`/`check_file` are unchanged. The CLI's `det_check_report_for_paths` now calls `check_paths` once instead of merging per-path `check_file`/`check_dir` reports. (4) **`--list-suppressions --format json` now emits JSON** (via the new `det_suppressions_json` helper) instead of silently falling back to the text listing; default stays text. (5) **Docs:** the AC7 GitHub Actions job and pre-commit hook use the now-clean argless `harvest det-check` (the old `det-check src examples` recipe failed on this repo, which has no root `src/`), with a note that a larger downstream workspace can enumerate specific crate `src` directories; a new "Known limitations (conservative, safe-direction)" note documents the ambiguity guard, local shadowing, path-qualified/associated-call non-resolution, and turbofish/space-before-paren call-form gaps as deliberate false-negatives (never false-positives) that the body-only compile-time #386 guardrail **also** misses (it does not hard-block a violation inside a skipped helper), backstopped by runtime replay (`WorkflowReplayer` / the live `HistoryMatcher`) plus manual review rather than #386; a "Flag scope" note records that `det-check` has its own local `--format` and ignores the global network/`--output` flags; and a DET010/DET011 reconciliation sentence clarifies that `det-check` surfaces the entire shared engine (including the pre-existing DET010 HashMap-iteration and DET011 select rules) — #778 adds no new HashMap/data-structure linting, but does not hide the engine's existing DET010 output. **Post-review tests:** engine — `check_dir_excludes_compile_fail_fixtures`, `check_dir_skips_target_and_hidden_dirs`, `fn_pointer_param_call_is_not_resolved_to_free_helper`, `local_closure_call_is_not_resolved_to_free_helper`, `shadowing_does_not_suppress_a_genuinely_reached_helper`, `check_paths_resolves_cross_file_between_two_file_args`, `check_paths_dedups_overlapping_args`, `check_paths_does_not_follow_directory_symlinks` (`#[cfg(unix)]`), `check_paths_skips_non_utf8_file_and_continues`, `check_paths_errors_on_a_missing_top_level_path`, `transitive_helper_det010_is_flagged_via_helper`, `finding_column_is_exact`, `one_bad_helper_reached_by_two_workflows_yields_two_findings`, `suppression_inside_transitive_helper_is_honored` (all in `det_check_tests.rs`). CLI — `det_suppressions_json_is_valid_json_containing_the_suppression`, `run_det_check_list_suppressions_json_exits_ok` (inline), and `two_separate_file_args_resolve_cross_file_transitive`, `overlapping_dir_and_file_args_do_not_double_count` (`det_check_cli.rs`). **Post-review hardening (Codex P1 — module-scoped workflows).** The initial `extract_all_functions` rewrite tracked a **flat** brace-depth counter and skipped every line at depth `> 0`, which conflated a `mod NAME { … }` opener with an `impl`/`fn`/`struct` block — so a `#[workflow]` (or its first-party helper) declared inside a Rust module was **never scanned**, a broad false-negative: `harvest det-check .` could pass despite hard-blocker code in module-scoped workflows. **This was a regression introduced by #778's rewrite** — the superseded `extract_workflow_bodies` on trunk scanned for `#[workflow]` at any brace depth and therefore did scan module-nested workflow bodies (it simply lacked transitive helper resolution). The fix makes extraction **module-aware**: a `Vec<ScopeKind>` scope stack classifies each opening brace as transparent `Module` (`mod NAME { … }`, keep item-scanning inside, at any nesting depth) or `Opaque` (`impl`/`trait`/`struct`/bare block, skip contents), so module-scoped `#[workflow]` entry points and their module-scope helpers are scanned for direct and one-hop transitive violations while **methods inside `impl`/`trait` blocks remain excluded** (the #386 boundary — never indexed as free helpers, a `self.method()`/`Type::method()` callee is never resolved). `#[activity]` bodies remain unscanned at any nesting; a `fn` body's internals are still consumed wholesale by `extract_fn_body` (local fns inside a body are not indexed as top-level helpers). New pure helpers `is_mod_block_decl` (inline `mod NAME { … }` vs. external `mod NAME;`), `strip_leading_visibility`, and `apply_line_braces`/`apply_line_braces_stripped` (the scope-stack walker); the now-unused `code_brace_delta` was removed. Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed against the pre-fix scanner): `module_scoped_workflow_direct_violation_is_flagged`, `module_scoped_workflow_transitive_helper_violation_is_flagged` (asserts `via_helper`), `nested_module_workflow_direct_violation_is_flagged`, `module_scoped_det010_hashmap_iteration_is_flagged`, and the two negative guards `module_scoped_activity_violation_is_not_flagged` / `impl_method_callee_is_not_resolved_as_helper` (in `det_check_tests.rs`); `is_mod_block_decl_matches_inline_modules_only`, `strip_leading_visibility_handles_pub_forms`, `apply_line_braces_classifies_module_vs_opaque` (unit tests in `det_check.rs`); and `module_scoped_workflow_direct_violation_trips_the_gate` (CLI behavioral test in `det_check_cli.rs`). **Post-review hardening (Codex P1/P2 — scope-aware same-name resolution + turbofish calls).** Two false-negatives the module-aware rewrite left, both fixed TDD red→green. **(P1) Scope-aware same-name helper resolution.** The prior code marked any identifier defined by more than one plain free helper as globally ambiguous (`None`) and never resolved *any* workflow call to it — even when the calling workflow's own in-scope sibling was the obvious, Rust-correct target (e.g. `mod a { #[workflow] async fn wf() { stamp(); } fn stamp() { chrono::Utc::now() } }` alongside an unrelated `mod b { fn stamp() -> String }` reported no findings, skipping the reachable hard-blocker in `a::stamp`). Resolution is now Rust-accurate nearest-scope: a candidate in the caller's **own module** (same file + `module_path`) wins, else the sole candidate in the caller's **file**, else a **globally unique** candidate, else (multiple candidates, none in the caller's module/file scope) the call is conservatively skipped — the only remaining safe false-negative. This is a strict accuracy improvement with no added false-positive risk (preferring the same-module/same-file definition is exactly what the compiler resolves a bare call to). Shadow-suppression still runs first, so a locally-bound name is never resolved. Implementation: `FnDef` gains a `module_path` (the `mod`-nesting path, tracked in `extract_all_functions` via a `mod_stack` maintained in lockstep with the `Module` scope entries — new `extract_mod_name` + `apply_line_braces_scoped`); the helper index changed from `HashMap<&str, Option<usize>>` to `HashMap<&str, Vec<usize>>`; new pure `resolve_helper(candidates, fns, caller)`. **(P2) Turbofish call form.** A generic first-party helper called with a turbofish (`bad::<u64>()`, `bad::<Vec<u8>>()`) had the byte `:` (not `(`) after the ident, so the call-paren matcher never scanned the helper body and a reachable violation was missed. `collect_direct_free_fn_calls` now skips an optional balanced `::<…>` segment (new `skip_balanced_angles`) before requiring `(`. The `.`/`:` before-guard is unchanged, so method (`x.method::<T>()`) and associated (`Type::assoc::<T>()`) turbofish calls are still never resolved. **Both fixes preserve every existing guarantee** — `#[activity]` bodies unscanned, impl/trait methods never indexed or resolved (#386), closure/fn-pointer shadow-suppression, and zero false positives on the real tree. Tests: `same_module_helper_resolves_over_unrelated_same_name`, `same_file_different_module_helper_disambiguates`, `genuinely_ambiguous_same_name_helper_is_skipped`, `same_name_impl_method_is_not_resolved_via_method_call`, `turbofish_helper_call_is_resolved`, `nested_generic_turbofish_helper_call_is_resolved`, `method_and_assoc_turbofish_are_not_resolved` (in `det_check_tests.rs`); `extract_mod_name_reads_the_module_identifier`, `skip_balanced_angles_matches_nested_generics` (unit tests in `det_check.rs`). **Post-review hardening (Codex P2 — source-order shadow tracking).** The zero-FP shadow-suppression above used a **whole-body** shadow set: any locally-bound name (params + every `let` binding anywhere in the body) suppressed a call to that name, regardless of where the binding sat relative to the call. That over-suppressed a genuinely in-scope call: a free helper called **before** a later same-name `let` binding is resolved by Rust to the free helper (the binding is not yet in scope), but the whole-body set wrongly skipped it — a false-negative in AC4 transitive coverage (e.g. a free `fn bad()` reading `chrono::Utc::now()`, reached by a `bad()` call preceding a later `let bad = |x| …`, went unreported). Suppression is now **source-order aware** (`collect_body_let_idents` → `collect_body_let_binding_lines`, name → earliest binding line; `collect_direct_free_fn_calls` takes `params` + `let_binding_lines` and compares each call's source line): a `let` shadow suppresses a call only on a strictly-later source line (so a pre-shadow call — and a call on the binding's own line, `let bad = bad();` — resolves to the free helper, matching Rust); params still bind for the whole body. **No new false positive** — this only ever suppresses *less* than the whole-body set, so every previously-suppressed post-shadow call stays suppressed and the original closure / fn-pointer-param FP-avoidance (`local_closure_call_is_not_resolved_to_free_helper`, `fn_pointer_param_call_is_not_resolved_to_free_helper`) is preserved. A `let` shadow bound in an inner block already closed before an outer call still suppresses it (source-order, not full brace-scope tracking) — a documented safe-direction residual false-negative, never a false-positive. Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed against the pre-fix whole-body set): `pre_shadow_call_resolves_to_free_helper_not_the_later_binding` and the residual pin `block_confined_shadow_before_call_is_a_documented_false_negative` (in `det_check_tests.rs`). **Post-review hardening (Codex r4 — false-positive fix + raw identifiers).** Two more findings, both fixed TDD red→green. **(C) Removed the Rust-inaccurate same-file-different-module resolution (false positive).** `resolve_helper`'s prior order preferred the sole same-**file** helper (any module) before falling back to global uniqueness, but a bare call in a child module does **not** resolve to a same-file helper in a *different* module (a parent/sibling module of the file) unless brought in by a `use` — which this text-level analysis cannot see. So a module-scoped workflow doing `use crate::pure::helper; helper();` (real target: a clean `helper` imported from another file) had its call wrongly resolved to an unrelated file-root `fn helper()` and got that helper's `chrono::Utc::now()` reported as a hard blocker — a false positive that could **fail CI on innocent code**. Resolution is now: a **globally unique** helper resolves directly, else a helper in the caller's **own module** (same file + `module_path`), else — multiple candidates, none in the caller's own module — conservatively skipped (ambiguous). Removing the same-file preference is strictly *more* Rust-accurate and only ever resolves **fewer** calls (removes an FP; cannot add one); shadow-suppression and source-order tracking still run first, and the same-module nearest-scope resolution (the #386 module-nested P1 fix) is untouched. **(D) Raw-identifier function names are now parsed.** `fn_decl_name` accepts an optional `r#` prefix (`async fn r#gen(…)` — `gen` is a reserved keyword in edition 2024, so `r#gen` is a valid, increasingly-real workflow name), retaining the `r#` on the extracted name; previously the parser stopped at `r`, failed the tail sanity check, and the `r#`-named workflow's body was **never scanned** (a direct `chrono::Utc::now()` in it passed with zero findings — a false negative). Transitive `r#name()` *call* resolution is not added (a safe false-negative — the required coverage is that an `r#`-named workflow's own body is scanned). Tests, TDD red→green: `same_file_different_module_helper_is_not_resolved` (converts the now-incorrect `same_file_different_module_helper_disambiguates`, which asserted the buggy FP behavior — the real target is a `use`-imported helper, so the file-root helper's violation is not reachable and must not be flagged), `raw_ident_workflow_body_is_scanned` (in `det_check_tests.rs`), and raw-ident assertions added to the `fn_decl_name_handles_visibility_and_async` unit test (in `det_check.rs`). The FP fix improves accuracy and adds no new false positive; `same_module_helper_resolves_over_unrelated_same_name` (the #386 module-nested resolution) and the source-order shadow tests are unchanged and still pass. **Post-review hardening (Codex r5 — restrict one-hop resolution to same-module, ending the cross-module false-positive family structurally).** Codex found a second aliased-import false positive after r4: a `mod inner` workflow doing `use crate::pure_helper as helper; helper();` (real target: a clean, aliased-in helper from another file) still had its bare `helper()` call resolved cross-module — via the surviving **globally-unique (`[only]`) branch** — to an unrelated file-root `fn helper()` reading `chrono::Utc::now()`, reported as a hard blocker that would **fail CI on innocent code**. Root cause is fundamental: the line-based front-door **cannot see `use` imports/aliases**, so *any* cross-module resolution keeps producing this false-positive class (r4 was the same-file-different-module case with two candidates; r5 is the single globally-unique candidate; both are the same bug). Rather than chase each variant, resolution is now restricted **structurally to same-module candidates only**: `resolve_helper` resolves a bare call **only** to a helper declared in the caller's own module (same file + `module_path`), and treats **everything else** — cross-module, cross-file, `use`-imported, aliased, and even a *globally-unique* helper that is not same-module — as ambiguous and skips it (a safe false-negative, never a false-positive). The earlier globally-unique (`[only]`) and same-file-different-module fallbacks are **deleted**; this makes an import/alias false positive impossible by construction. For a CI gate a false positive (failing CI on innocent code) is the worst outcome and outranks marginal recall; because #386 is likewise body-only, it does not hard-block a violation inside a skipped cross-module helper either, so the backstop for these transitive false-negatives is runtime replay (`WorkflowReplayer` / the live `HistoryMatcher`) plus manual review, not #386. Shadow-suppression + source-order tracking (r3) still run before resolution; turbofish call matching (r2), raw-identifier parsing (r4), module-nested `#[workflow]` scanning (r1), and the `#[activity]` / impl-method exclusions (#386) are all orthogonal and unchanged. Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed against the pre-fix `[only]` branch): `aliased_import_bare_call_is_not_resolved_to_root_helper_same_module_only` (the r5 aliased-import FP — a globally-unique cross-module root helper is no longer resolved); the two prior cross-file resolution tests are **converted to boundary tests** pinning the same-module-only limit rather than deleted — `transitive_cross_file_via_check_dir_is_flagged` → `transitive_cross_file_via_check_dir_is_not_resolved_same_module_only` (asserts a cross-file `check_dir` helper is NOT resolved) and `check_paths_resolves_cross_file_between_two_file_args` → `check_paths_cross_file_helper_is_not_resolved_same_module_only` (asserts a cross-file helper across two separate file args is NOT resolved; the `check_paths` shared-index dedup / symlink-skip / non-UTF-8 robustness tests are untouched — only the resolution they enabled changed). `same_module_helper_resolves_over_unrelated_same_name` (the core same-module resolution) still flags `a::stamp`; `same_file_different_module_helper_is_not_resolved` (r4) still yields no finding, now via same-module-only; the 14-workflow success-metric fixture still flags all 7 direct + 7 transitive (each transitive helper is same-module as its workflow — no fixture move needed) for exactly 14 findings, zero fixture FP; and the `autumn-harvest/src` self-scan stays clean. Same-module-only resolves strictly *fewer* calls than before, so it can only remove false positives — it cannot add a finding. **Post-review hardening (Codex r6 — block-local `use` imports shadow same-module helpers + raw-identifier calls).** Two more Codex P2 findings, both fixed TDD red→green. **(E) Block-local `use` imports now shadow same-module helpers (false-positive fix).** Even under r5's same-module-only resolution, a `use` **inside a workflow body** rebinds a name to an import, so Rust resolves a bare call to that import — not a same-module sibling `fn` of the same name.
