A module-scoped workflow doing `use crate::pure::helper; helper();` in its body (real target: a clean imported `helper`) still had `helper()` resolved to a same-module `fn helper()` reading `chrono::Utc::now()` and reported as a hard blocker — a false positive that would **fail CI on innocent code**. The workflow-body shadow set (the r3 source-order set of params + `let`/closure bindings) is now extended to also include names bound by a **block-local `use`** in the body: `use path::name;` binds `name`, `use path::orig as alias;` binds `alias`, grouped `use path::{a, b as c};` binds `a` and `c`, and an unnameable glob `use path::*;`. New pure helpers `collect_body_use_bindings`, `parse_use_bindings`, `parse_use_single`, and `extract_use_ident` (all retain an `r#` raw-identifier prefix; `use<'a>` RPIT precise-capture clauses are ignored via a whitespace-after-`use` guard); `collect_direct_free_fn_calls` gains the `use` shadow params. **Only body-local `use` statements are in the shadow set** — a module/file-level `use` is not a body line (`extract_fn_body` captures body lines only), so the common top-of-file prelude-glob case is unaffected by construction, and a module-level `use` + a same-name `fn` is itself a compile error, making a block-local `use` the last same-module rebind vector. Adding `use` imports to the shadow set only ever suppresses *more*, so it introduces **no new false positive**. **(F) Raw-identifier calls (`r#gen()`) are now tokenized correctly (false-negative fix).** r4 indexed a `fn r#gen` def under the key `r#gen`, but the call tokenizer in `collect_direct_free_fn_calls` split `#`, tokenizing `r#gen()` as `r`/`gen`, so the call never matched the def and a reachable hard blocker in a raw-identifier same-module helper was silently missed. The call tokenizer now consumes an optional leading `r#` as part of the call identifier (so `r#gen(` yields the token `r#gen`), completing raw-identifier support on **both** the def and call sides; the `.`/`:` before-guard (still excluding `x.r#method()` / `Type::r#assoc()`) and the turbofish skip (`r#gen::<T>()`) both compose with it unchanged. Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed against the pre-fix scanner): `block_local_use_import_shadows_same_module_helper` (Codex's exact repro), `block_local_use_alias_shadows_same_module_helper`, `block_local_use_group_shadows_same_module_helper`, `block_local_glob_use_conservatively_suppresses_later_same_module_calls`, `same_module_call_without_block_local_use_is_still_resolved` (regression guard: a genuine same-module call with no shadow is still flagged — r5 preserved), `module_level_use_is_not_treated_as_a_body_shadow` (a file-level `use ...::*;`/`use path;` does not suppress a same-module call), `raw_ident_helper_call_is_resolved_and_flagged` (a `r#gen()` helper call is resolved and flagged transitively), and `raw_ident_method_call_is_not_resolved` (a `x.r#gen()` method call is still not resolved) — in `det_check_tests.rs`. All prior-round fixes are preserved: same-module-only resolution (r5), source-order shadow tracking (r3), turbofish calls (r2), raw-ident def parsing (r4), module-nested scanning (r1), and the `#[activity]`/impl-method exclusions (#386); the 14-workflow success-metric fixture still flags all 14 direct + transitive violations, and the `autumn-harvest/src` self-scan stays clean. **Post-review hardening (Codex r7 — block `use` imports shadow the whole body, not source-order).** r6 added body-local `use` bindings to the shadow set but applied them **source-order** (a `use` only shadowed calls on strictly-later lines, like a `let`). That is wrong for `use`: unlike a sequential `let`, a Rust block `use` item is in scope for the **entire enclosing block** regardless of textual position, so a bare call may **precede** the `use` and still resolve to the import. A body doing `helper(); use crate::pure::helper;` therefore still false-positived — the call preceded the `use`, so r6's source-order check did not suppress it, and same-module resolution scanned the sibling `fn helper`'s `chrono::Utc::now()` and reported a hard blocker on code that never reaches that helper. Fix: body-local `use` bindings (and a body-local glob) now shadow the called name across the **whole body**, matching Rust's block-wide `use`-item scope — `collect_body_use_bindings` returns `(HashSet<String>, bool)` (a presence set + "any glob in the body") instead of source-line maps, and `collect_direct_free_fn_calls` suppresses a call whenever its name is in that set or any glob is present, on every line. **`let`/closure/param shadows stay source-order (r3) — only the `use`/glob half becomes whole-body.** This only ever suppresses *more*, so it introduces **no new false positive** (a genuine same-module call with no body `use` for that name — and no glob — is still resolved and flagged; a module/file-level `use` is still never a body shadow). Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed against the r6 source-order check): `block_use_shadows_a_call_before_the_use_statement` (Codex's exact call-before-`use` repro → no DET001) and `block_glob_use_shadows_a_call_before_the_glob` (a glob preceding-call variant) in `det_check_tests.rs`; the r6 use/alias/grouped tests, the `same_module_call_without_block_local_use_is_still_resolved` regression guard, and `module_level_use_is_not_treated_as_a_body_shadow` all stay green, and the 14-workflow success-metric fixture and the `autumn-harvest/src` self-scan are unchanged. **Post-review hardening (Codex r9 — two false-positive fixes: top-level symlink PATH args + column-aware same-line `let` shadow).** Two more Codex P2 findings, both false positives that could fail CI on innocent code (the worst outcome for a gate), fixed TDD red→green. **(G) Top-level symlink PATH arguments are no longer followed.** The nested directory walker already skips symlinks, but a symlink passed **directly** as a top-level `det-check` PATH argument was classified with `std::fs::metadata` (which **follows**) before the walker ran, so `det-check link.rs` (a symlink to a file) linted the target and `det-check link-to-dir` walked the target — pulling **out-of-tree contents** into the report, contradicting the documented no-follow contract. `check_paths` now classifies each top-level argument with `std::fs::symlink_metadata` (which does **not** follow) first: a symlinked argument is **skipped with a warning** (`det-check: skipping symlink <path>`), mirroring the nested walker's no-follow and the existing non-UTF-8 skip-with-warning; only after confirming the argument is not a symlink is it classified as a file (scan) or directory (walk) as before. A missing top-level path still surfaces as an error (`symlink_metadata` errors on a nonexistent path). **(H) `let`/closure shadow suppression is now column-aware within a line.** The r3 source-order shadow suppression was **line-granular** — a `let` binding only suppressed a shadowed call on a strictly-later **line** — so a same-line `let helper = || 0; helper();` was **not** suppressed, and a same-module `fn helper()` reading `chrono::Utc::now()` had the same-line `helper()` call wrongly resolved to that unreachable helper (a hard-blocker false positive). Rust resolves the second call to the local `let`. The suppression is now **column-aware for the same-line case**: `collect_body_let_binding_lines` records each binding's scope-entry point as a `LetBinding { line, in_scope_col }`, where `in_scope_col` is the byte column of the statement-terminating `;` (via the new depth-tracking `let_stmt_terminator_col`, so a `;` inside a closure block or nested expression is skipped; `usize::MAX` for a multi-line `let`); `collect_direct_free_fn_calls` suppresses a same-line call only when its column is **past** that `;`. This is deliberately **not** a conservative "suppress all same-line calls" approach — that would wrongly suppress a genuine pre-shadow `bad(); let bad = ...;` call — nor a "suppress when past the bound ident" approach, which would wrongly suppress the RHS of a self-referencing `let bad = bad();`. Column-awareness against the statement-terminating `;` keeps `let helper = ...; helper();` suppressed while the RHS of `let bad = bad();` (before the `;`) and a pre-shadow `bad(); let bad = ...;` call (before the binding) both **stay flagged** — avoiding a new false negative. Cross-line behavior (strictly-later line suppressed, earlier line flagged) is unchanged. Both fixes only ever **skip more** (a narrower followed set / more shadow suppression), so neither introduces a new false positive. Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed against the pre-fix scanner): `check_paths_does_not_follow_a_top_level_symlink_file` and `check_paths_does_not_follow_a_top_level_symlink_dir` (`#[cfg(unix)]`, both RED before the fix), `check_paths_still_scans_real_file_and_dir_args` (regression: real file/dir args still scan), `same_line_let_binding_before_call_is_suppressed` (the FP, RED before), `same_line_call_before_let_binding_is_still_flagged` and `same_line_self_referencing_let_rhs_call_is_still_flagged` (regressions: pre-shadow / self-ref RHS calls stay flagged) in `det_check_tests.rs`. All prior-round fixes are preserved: same-module-only resolution (r5), whole-body `use` shadow (r6/r7), source-order `let`/closure shadow (r3), turbofish (r2), raw-ident def+call parsing (r4/r6), module-nested scanning (r1), and the `#[activity]`/impl-method exclusions (#386); the `check_paths` dedup / non-UTF-8 / nested-symlink-skip robustness is untouched; the 14-workflow success-metric fixture still flags all 14 direct + transitive violations; and the `autumn-harvest/src` self-scan stays clean. **Post-review hardening (Codex r10 — nested `fn` declaration false positive + documented block-scoping boundary).** Closes the Codex review loop with one false-positive fix and one documented safe-direction false-negative. **Fixed the nested-`fn`-declaration false positive.** A workflow body containing a nested item `fn helper() {}` had its **declaration** token `helper(` treated as a **call** by `collect_direct_free_fn_calls` (which only checked for a following `(`), resolved to a same-module `fn helper()` reading `chrono::Utc::now()`, and reported as a hard blocker on an *uncalled* helper — an FP that could fail innocent CI. Two FP-preventing parts, both TDD red→green: (a) the call collector now **skips a `NAME(` token that is a declaration** — the ident is preceded (ignoring whitespace) by the `fn` keyword (new word-bounded `is_ident_preceded_by_fn` helper); the existing `.`/`:` before-guard is retained; and (b) block-local `fn NAME(...)` item names declared in the workflow body are collected into the **whole-body shadow set** (new `collect_body_fn_bindings`, reusing the raw-`r#`-aware `extract_use_ident`), exactly like block-local `use` items (r7), so a *genuine* call to a body-local nested `fn NAME` resolves to that nested fn (which shadows the module item) instead of the same-module `fn NAME`. Adding `fn` names to the shadow set only ever suppresses *more*, so it introduces no new false positive; a `fn(..)` pointer TYPE has no following ident and binds nothing. **Documented the nested-block `use`/`fn` whole-body over-suppression as a safe-direction false-negative (a line-based-granularity boundary), declined in favor of the zero-FP whole-body treatment.** A block-local `use`/`fn` inside a **nested block** is scoped by Rust only to that inner block, but the whole-body shadow (r7/r10) suppresses a same-named call in a sibling or outer block *after* it too — a false **negative** (under-reports, never over-reports). Precise block-scoping would add brace-range-per-item machinery and risk reopening the ordering false-*positive* the whole-body treatment was chosen to eliminate, for a contrived shape; the code fix is **declined** and the boundary is instead documented in `docs/workflow-determinism-guide.md` "Known limitations" as an explicit line-based-granularity boundary, with the runtime replay net (`WorkflowReplayer` / the live `HistoryMatcher`) + manual review as the backstop. Tests, TDD red→green (red confirmed against the pre-r10 collector): `fn_declaration_in_body_is_not_collected_as_a_call` (a nested `fn helper() {}` decl + a same-module violating `fn helper` → no finding), `body_local_fn_shadows_the_module_helper_on_a_real_call` (a body-local `fn helper() {}` + a genuine `helper()` call → resolves to the nested fn, not the module helper → no finding), and `same_module_call_without_body_local_fn_is_still_flagged` (regression: a genuine same-module `helper()` call with no body-local `fn`/`use` is still flagged) in `det_check_tests.rs`. All prior-round fixes are preserved; the 14-workflow success-metric fixture still flags all 14 direct + transitive violations; and the `autumn-harvest/src` self-scan stays clean.
- Published interaction schema + `/interface` discovery + boundary validation (issue #610). Extend the #373 workflow input/output schema story to a workflow's **interaction surface** — its signals, queries, and updates. Each handler can publish an argument/response JSON Schema and a description: `QueryHandlerInfo`/`UpdateHandlerInfo` gain `description`/`arg_schema`/`response_schema` fields; a new `SignalHandlerInfo` type (arg-only, no response). Fluent builders `with_description`/`with_arg_schema_fn`/`with_response_schema_fn` and, under the `schema` feature, `with_schemas::<Arg, Resp>()` (`<Arg>` for signals). The `#[query]`/`#[update]`/`#[signal]` macros parse `description = "…"` and emit a public `{fn}_info()` alias; `signals![…]` collector added. New read-only management route **`GET /workflows/registered/{name}/interface`** returns a `WorkflowInterfaceRecord { signals, queries, updates }`, each entry `{ name, description?, arg_schema?, response_schema? }`, sorted by name and deterministic across calls. `404` for an unregistered workflow name. Signals never carry a `response_schema`. **Boundary validation:** when a signal or update handler has a published `arg_schema`, the payload is validated *before* durable enqueue at the three HTTP entry points — the signal-send route, `POST /workflows/{name}/signal-with-start`, and the update route. On failure returns `400` `{ "error": "…validation failed", "violations": [{ "message", "field_path" }] }` (RFC 6901 pointer), reusing #373's `validate_against_schema`. A handler with no published schema is not validated (unchanged behavior). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no adjacently-tagged JSON change, no replay impact** — validation runs at the HTTP boundary before enqueue, and discovery is a read-only projection of the registry. Example `autumn-harvest/examples/interface_schema_workflow.rs` (`--features schema`). **Source-visible change:** each `#[query]`/`#[update]`/`#[signal]`-annotated function now also emits a public `{fn}_info()` symbol (consistent with the existing `#[workflow]`/`#[activity]` convention). A downstream crate that already defines a hand-written `foo_info()` beside `#[query] fn foo` would need to rename one of them.
- **Trunk hardening** — heal the batch-route gate-bypass test (Refs #1085, #1053, #1073). **Test-code-only. No production change, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration.** The Docker-only plugin test in `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/start_throttle_integration.rs` that #1073 added for issue #1053 had a wrong runtime expectation. The plugin suite spins a testcontainers Postgres, so CI runs it Docker-backed but #1073 could only compile-check it — the assertion never actually executed. It is the deterministic ubuntu **Test**-leg red blocking every open PR (surfaced in #1085). Same class as the recent trunk heals #1076/#1077/#1078. **Root cause — a wrong test EXPECTATION, not a code bug.** The test seeded a `COMPLETED` prior for an explicit `workflow_id`, armed a fleet admission gate, submitted a non-atomic batch item under the batch route's hardcoded `AllowDuplicate` policy, and asserted `status != "rejected"`. But the batch route reports an *attach-to-existing* (`start_or_load_workflow_execution_collect` returning `created == false`) with `status: "rejected"` + the duplicate message `"workflow_id '…' already has an existing execution"` + the prior's `execution_id`. That mapping is a long-standing convention meaning "no NEW row was inserted" — authored 2026-07-09 (PR #991), six days *before* #1073 (2026-07-15); #1073's only `api.rs` change is the single Phase-1 gate-bypass hunk `@@ -12677,25 +12677,45 @@`. It is **not** an admission-gate block: a gate rejection produces `error = "admission blocked by gate …"` with `execution_id: null` in Phase 1 and never reaches the attach path. The active uniqueness partial index `(workflow_name, workflow_id) WHERE state NOT IN ('CONTINUED_AS_NEW','TERMINATED')` does not release `COMPLETED`, so `_collect`'s `on_conflict_do_nothing` insert is a no-op and it returns the existing run (matrix-consistent — no rejection thrown by `_collect`), and `start_will_create_new_execution(Some("COMPLETED"), AllowDuplicate) == false`, so the item correctly **bypasses** the gate and attaches. The old assertion conflated the benign duplicate-attach `"rejected"` with a gate block, and the `#1073` code is correct. (This refutes an early hypothesis of a code bug in the batch existence check.) **The test's name over-promised.** It was named `..._uses_start_will_create_predicate_not_bare_existence`, but verified against the #1073 diff, the OLD `has_execution` boolean it replaced used the *same* non-sealed-prior filter (`state NOT IN ('CONTINUED_AS_NEW','TERMINATED')`) the new predicate query uses, and the batch route hardcodes `AllowDuplicate` (`BatchStartItem` has no reuse-policy field). So the predicate and the old bare-existence heuristic are **behaviorally identical for every prior state** through this route (both attach for any present non-sealed prior, both create for `None`/sealed, including `TERMINATED`). The predicate-vs-bare-existence *implementation* distinction is therefore **not black-box observable** through the batch route today — #1073 calls it exactly this: a structural/defensive change that becomes observable only if a per-item reuse policy is ever added. The genuine predicate distinction is unit-tested directly in `autumn_harvest::execution::start_will_create_tests`. **Fix — heal the red AND make the test genuinely meaningful.** Renamed to `batch_gate_bypasses_an_attaching_item_but_blocks_a_would_be_fresh_create` and rewritten to guard the property it actually *can* prove: the end-to-end bypass DECISION OUTCOME, via a case that splits by will-create. Under one armed fleet gate, in one non-atomic batch: a `COMPLETED` prior → the item **bypasses** the gate and **attaches** (error is the duplicate message, not a gate block; an `execution_id` is present); a `TERMINATED` prior (sealed → excluded from the uniqueness index → `_collect` would CREATE fresh) → the item does **not** bypass; it **faces the gate and is blocked** (`error = "admission blocked by gate …"`, `execution_id: null`). The `TERMINATED`-prior gate block is the load-bearing assertion: it proves the gate is enforced exactly for an item that would create a NEW admission — the substance of #1053/#1073. (It does not, and cannot, distinguish the predicate from bare-existence; both block a sealed prior. The doc comment states this precisely.) The rewritten test (and the full `start_throttle_integration` suite) was **run green** against a local Postgres 16 via a temporary, uncommitted `setup_database` adaptation (Docker is unavailable in this sandbox), which was then reverted so only the test rewrite + this fragment remain.
- **Tooling** — Heal two RED `trunk-dev` failures after a merge burst (PR #1094). A merge burst left `trunk-dev` red on two independent gates; this PR heals both (precedent: PR #1078 folded two lint heals into one PR). **1. Missing route classification (`contract_regression`).** PR #1092 added the read-only route `GET /workflows/registered/{name}/interface` to the plugin's `management_api_routes()` but never classified it in `autumn_harvest::audit`, so the plugin's `contract_regression::every_management_route_is_classified` test — which enforces that every `management_api_routes()` entry has a `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` entry (issue #776 AC4 read-only enforcement source of truth) — failed on every trunk-based branch. Classified the route `ReadOnly`, exactly mirroring its existing sibling `GET /workflows/registered/{name}/schema`, across all four audit lists in `autumn-harvest/src/audit.rs`: `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES` (`RouteClass::ReadOnly`), `EXCLUDED_ROUTES` (read, no audit trail), `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES` (op `None`), and the `newly_classified_reads_are_read_only` pin test. `CLASSIFIED_ROUTES.len()` and `ALL_MUTATION_ROUTES.len()` stay balanced (one entry added to each), so `classified_routes_count_matches_route_manifest` still holds. **2. `clippy::redundant_closure_for_method_calls` (`-D warnings`).** PR #1093 merged while draft (CI skipped), introducing a redundant-closure lint failure in `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/start_throttle_integration.rs` — `body["results"].as_array().map_or(0, |a| a.len())`. Replaced the closure with the method itself (`Vec::len`), which is behavior-identical and accepted by both clippy 1.94.1 (stable) and 1.97.0. The sibling `.map_or(0, |e| e[...].as_i64().unwrap_or(0))` on line 1896 is a non-trivial closure and is correctly not flagged. No production code or runtime behavior change beyond making the already-shipped `/interface` route reachable by a read-only principal and excluded from audit (consistent with the `/schema` sibling). No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration.
- **Trunk heal** — add `StartSource` fields to `ui_integration` test literals (semantic merge conflict #1095 × #1085). **Test-code-only — no production code changed.** Trunk-dev went RED on the Lint leg (`cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest-plugin --all-targets -- -D warnings`), which blocks every branch off trunk repo-wide, with a hard compile error: ``` error[E0063]: missing fields `start_source`, `start_source_ref` and `started_by` in initializer of `StartWorkflowParams<'_>` --> autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/ui_integration.rs:3670:9 ``` Root cause: a **semantic merge conflict** between two independently-green PRs. PR #1095 (issue #740, StartSource provenance, merged as `3fa812d2`) added three **required** fields to `StartWorkflowParams` in `autumn-harvest/src/execution.rs` — `start_source: StartSource`, `start_source_ref: Option<&'a str>`, `started_by: Option<&'a str>` — and updated every construction site that existed at the time (its CI was green). PR #1085 (Vantage DAG run-graph + timeline pages, merged *after* #1095 became ready) added a **new** `StartWorkflowParams { .. }` literal in the `dag957_seed_run` helper of `ui_integration.rs` that predates the field additions. Git merged the two cleanly (no textual conflict), but the combination does not compile: the new literal is missing the three now-required fields. Fix: add the three fields to the one un-updated literal, mirroring #1095's own neutral test convention verbatim (`StartSource::Api` / `None` / `None`, inserted right after `completion_callbacks: None,` — identical to the four sibling literals #1095 updated in this same file at the `insert_workflow_on_url` / `insert_child_workflow_on_url` / `workflow_detail_ui_*` helpers). A brace-tracking scan of every `StartWorkflowParams { .. }` literal across the whole workspace confirmed this was the **only** straggler — all core-crate and other plugin literals were already updated by #1095. Because `start_source` is metadata only (never read during replay), this is not a behavioral change: **no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/contract change, no replay/determinism impact.** Validation (Docker-backed Postgres 16): the 8 DAG run-graph/retry `ui_integration` tests that seed via the fixed `dag957_seed_run` helper (`ui_dag_run_graph_*`, `ui_dag_retry_*`) all pass end-to-end — exercised, not merely compile-checked (10/10 in the `ui_dag_` filter). Gates green: `cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest-plugin --all-targets -- -D warnings` at both stable and 1.97.0 (plus the `mcp,unified-dag-execution` / `webhooks` / `metrics` feature combos), `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and MSRV `cargo +1.88.0 check --workspace`.
- **CI** — gate `webhook_receiver_integration` and fix its `TestApp::plugin` deadlock (test-infra). **Tooling/testing** (implemented): the Docker-gated plugin suite `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/webhook_receiver_integration.rs` (issue #344) was absent from `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt`, so CI only *compile-checked* it — it had **zero runtime regression coverage** and was listed in the `ci_run_coverage.rs` `ALLOWLIST` as a `webhooks`-feature-gated, all-`#[ignore]`d suite that "no CI run can execute". This slice reproduces and fixes a genuine test-harness **deadlock** in 5 of its 6 tests, un-`#[ignore]`s the suite, and wires it into the manifest so it runs for real against Docker Postgres. **Test-harness change only — no production webhook code touched, no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no route/contract change.** **Root cause — current-thread runtime + `TestApp::plugin`.** `TestApp::plugin(HarvestPlugin)` runs the plugin startup hook on a spawned thread via `Handle::block_on` while the test thread blocks on its join; under a plain `#[tokio::test]` (single current-thread runtime) that mutual block **deadlocks**. PR #1095 (issue #740) discovered this when it added `webhook_start_records_webhook_source` and fixed *that one* test with `#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]` — but the 5 pre-existing tests, never actually run in CI (`#[ignore]` + no manifest row), kept the plain-`#[tokio::test]` shape and the latent deadlock. **Red→green.** Reproduced against a live Postgres 16 (testcontainers, `--include-ignored`, 90 s per-test timeout): the 5 pre-existing tests (`duplicate_webhook_delivery_creates_exactly_one_execution_with_same_exec_id`, `duplicate_webhook_delivery_to_signals_target_delivers_signal_exactly_once`, `blank_delivery_id_is_rejected_as_missing_for_signals_target`, `upstream_idempotency_key_header_does_not_trip_throttle_mutual_exclusion_on_starts`, `distinct_deliveries_sharing_an_upstream_idempotency_key_are_not_collapsed`) all **hung/deadlocked** (killed at the timeout); `webhook_start_records_webhook_source` (already multi-thread) passed in 1.88 s. After applying the same multi-thread flavor to the 5, two consecutive serial full-suite runs were fully green: `test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored` (4.55 s, then 2.56 s). **Fix pattern (mirrors #1095 exactly).** Each of the 5 pre-existing tests changed from `#[tokio::test]` to `#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]`, with a one-line rationale comment pointing at the fuller note on `webhook_start_records_webhook_source`. **Gating (the actual runtime-coverage enabler).** The manifest `linux` runner never passes `--include-ignored`, and `ci_run_coverage.rs::all_tests_ignored` disqualifies an all-`#[ignore]`d suite from being credited — so the `#[ignore = "requires Docker (testcontainers)"]` attribute was removed from **all 6** tests (matching every other `linux` plugin suite, e.g. `fail_now`/`timeline`, which are un-ignored and run against Docker Postgres). The file's `#![cfg(feature = "webhooks")]` gate means a plain `cargo test -p autumn-harvest-plugin` (no `webhooks` feature) still compiles it away entirely, so no default-feature developer flow is affected. Added one sorted manifest line — `linux autumn-harvest-plugin webhook_receiver_integration webhooks -` — and updated the coverage guard: dropped `webhook_receiver_integration` from the `paved_path_db_tests_are_classified_and_flagged_all_ignored` all-ignored self-test, and removed its `ALLOWLIST` entry (it is now covered by a real `linux` run). `webhook_durable_integration` and `mcp_tools_integration` stay all-ignored/allowlisted (out of scope). **Verification.** Full local CI mirror green: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (1.97.0), `cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest --all-features --tests -- -D warnings` (covers `ci_run_coverage.rs`), `cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest-plugin --all-targets --features webhooks -- -D warnings` (covers the webhook suite), MSRV `cargo +1.88.0 check --workspace`, and the 13-test `ci_run_coverage` guard (all green, including `manifest_is_sorted_and_unique` and `every_db_gated_test_has_a_ci_run_step_or_is_allowlisted`).
- **Explicit shard pinning for data-residency workflow placement** (implemented) — see issue #697. Before, the only way a new workflow landed on a shard was rendezvous hashing over `(workflow_name, workflow_id)`; `docs/sharding.md` documented an ID-prefix workaround and admitted it was unreliable, so an embedder with a data-residency obligation had no supported mechanism. Now the start path accepts an **optional explicit placement**, and residency is transitive across the whole workflow tree. **Core (`shard.rs`)**: new `ShardPlacement` enum (`Auto` (default) / `Shard(ShardId)` / `ResidencyKey(String)`), typed `ShardPlacementError` (`UnknownShard` / `ShardNotWritable` / `UnknownResidencyKey` / `EmptyResidencyKey`, each naming the valid set), a `residency_map: BTreeMap<String, ShardId>` field on `ShardRouter` with the fluent `ShardRouter::with_residency_map(...)`, and `ShardRouter::resolve_placement(&placement, workflow_name, workflow_id) -> Result<ShardId, ShardPlacementError>`. `ShardPlacement`/`ShardPlacementError` are re-exported from `lib.rs`; `ShardPlacementError` converts into `HarvestError::Config` (→ HTTP 400). `WorkflowHandleClient::resolve_shard_placement` is the client-side sibling of `pick_shard_for_new_workflow`. **AC1 — `Auto` is byte-for-byte today's routing**: `resolve_placement(Auto, ..)` delegates verbatim to `pick_for_new_workflow`, pinned by a unit test that compares both across 200 ids. **AC3 — residency keys resolve through an operator-DECLARED map, never a hash** (the load-bearing design decision): rendezvous hashing deliberately re-balances (~1/N keys move when a shard is added) and cannot know which physical database is in which jurisdiction, so a hash can satisfy neither half of AC3. The declared map gives the guarantee residency needs — *the same key resolves to the same shard across process restarts AND across a widening of `writable_shards`*, changing only when an operator edits the map. Pinned by `residency_key_resolution_is_stable_across_a_widening_of_the_shard_set`, which also asserts the *hash* DOES move those keys, so the test proves the map buys something. An **unmapped** key is a typed error, never a silent hash fallback (a silent hash is exactly the failure mode that produces a compliance breach). Map misconfiguration (blank key, or a target outside `readable_shards`) **panics at `ShardRouter` construction**, consistent with `ShardRouter::new`'s documented panic contract, so it fails at boot rather than at the first request. **AC2 — a pin outside `readable_shards` is rejected**, never defaulted; the `UNENCODED` (`0xFFFF`) sentinel and a negative `shard_id` are likewise rejected. **Deliberately stricter than AC2's literal wording**: a pin to a shard that is readable but NOT in `writable_shards` (a draining shard) is also rejected (`ShardNotWritable`), because (i) placing new work on a shard the operator is draining contradicts the drain, and (ii) the #808 mint loop can never converge to a non-writable shard and would spin to `MINT_CAP` and warn. **AC6 — HTTP surface**: `POST /workflows/{name}/start` gains two optional, mutually-exclusive `#[serde(default)]` body fields, `shard_id: Option<i32>` and `residency_key: Option<String>`, parsed by the pure `parse_shard_placement` (both-supplied / negative / sentinel / blank-key all rejected). Every rejection is a `400` JSON error with a **failed audit row** (new `audit_start_failure` helper) — never a `500`, never a silent re-hash, never a quiet fall back to the default shard. An explicit placement **overrides** both hash routes (the plain rendezvous pick and the #808 idempotency-key pick). **AC5 — observability with no new column**: `StartWorkflowResponse` gains `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] shard_id: Option<i32>`, populated **only when a placement was requested**, so an unpinned start's response stays byte-for-byte the pre-#697 shape; the chosen shard is also readable from the encoded `ExecutionId` (`exec_id.shard()`) and the execution row's existing `shard_id` column. **AC4 — residency is transitive** across the workflow tree. Two genuine bugs were found and fixed here (RED→GREEN): the **awaited** child path (`context.rs`) and the **`ctx.race()` child branch** both minted `ExecutionId::new()` — the `UNENCODED` sentinel — so a child's row landed on the parent's shard (the worker sets the row's `shard_id` from the parent) while its **encoded id** routed every later id-based lookup to the deployment's *default* shard. Both now mint `ExecutionId::new_for_shard(self.exec_id.shard())`, matching the detached path and the child-timeout race, which were already correct. `continue_as_new` (`worker.rs`), workflow-level retry (#523), and reset forks (#148) were audited and already inherit. **#808 interaction**: the bounded rejection-sampling mint loop that re-mints an auto-generated `workflow_id` so it hashes to the target shard now also runs for a **pinned** start, closing the `(workflow_name, workflow_id)` per-shard uniqueness hole for auto-generated ids (a pin moves a run off its hash-derived shard, so a later *unpinned* start of the same id would route elsewhere and could duplicate). For a caller-supplied **explicit** `workflow_id` this cannot be closed mechanically — be consistent (always pin it or never pin it), the same documented consistency requirement idempotency-key routing already carries. Placement is resolved **before** the #808 committed-replay probe (the probe needs the shard), so a retry of a keyed start must carry the same placement as the original delivery. **Registries + CLI**: `shard_id`/`residency_key` added to `management_api_request_fields()`, `shard_id` to `management_api_response_fields()`, and both plus the extended 400/success notes to `docs/api-contract.json` (the `contract_regression` cross-check stays green). CLI: `harvest workflow start --shard-id <N>` / `--residency-key <KEY>` (clap `conflicts_with`, so the mutual exclusion is caught at parse time), emitting the fields only when supplied. **AC7 — `docs/sharding.md`** replaces the unreliable ID-prefix workaround with a full "Explicit shard placement and data residency" section (the two placement forms, the resolution rule + stability guarantee and *why* it is a declared map, the rejection table, the three observation surfaces, the transitivity table, a worked two-region EU/US example, and the uniqueness / retry-consistency caveats); the three "see the concurrency routing guidance above" back-references now point at it. **AC8 — no new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no change to the adjacently-tagged JSON contract, no replay-determinism impact**: placement is a pre-start routing decision, and the shard was already encoded in the `ExecutionId`. **Two unanswered design questions were resolved by documented assumption** (the user was asked and did not answer): (a) residency-key resolution is a declared map rather than a hash, for the AC3 reasons above; (b) a pin to a drained (readable-but-not-writable) shard is rejected rather than accepted. **Success metric**: `residency_conformance_n_workflows_across_k_keys` exists at both levels — a pure router test (2 keys × 100 runs) and a DB/HTTP test (2 keys × 12 runs against two genuinely separate shard databases) — each asserting **100%** of starts land on the intended shard, with no sampling and no tolerance. **Tests**: 15 pure unit tests in `shard.rs` (Auto-equals-rendezvous, unknown/drained/sentinel rejection, unmapped-key rejection, the AC3 stability money test, conformance, two `#[should_panic]` construction tests); 3 no-DB context tests (awaited / raced / detached child shard inheritance); 7 `parse_shard_placement` tests + `handle.rs` error-conversion test; 9 DB/HTTP tests in the new `autumn-harvest-plugin/tests/shard_placement_integration.rs` (three genuinely separate shard databases: explicit-pin observability, residency-key pin, the conformance metric, unpinned-is-unchanged, and the four rejection paths — each asserting the row exists on the intended shard **only** and that a rejection starts nothing); and the real-worker e2e `worker_child_of_a_shard_pinned_parent_inherits_the_parents_shard` proving AC4 end to end through worker persistence. Registered in `.github/ci/integration-suites.txt` for the Docker-backed Linux run; all DB tests were additionally **executed green against a real local Postgres 16** (Docker unavailable in this sandbox), with the two AC4 fixes confirmed RED against the pre-fix code. **Post-review hardening (four review agents: replay/determinism, sharding-invariants, security/API-contract, and tests/AC-evidence — all findings addressed):** (1) **P1 — placement discarded on a deferred start.** A `shard_id`/`residency_key` on a **debounced** (#499) or **batched** (#518) workflow was silently ignored: those admit a start without creating an execution, so the placement had nothing to apply to and the eventual scanner-fired run hashed by the debounce/batch key. Combining them is now a `400` with a failed audit row, mirroring the three sibling deferred-start mutual-exclusion guards. A **throttled** (#607) start is deliberately excluded — it defers the same concrete placement to its scanner, so a pin there is honoured. (2) **P1 — silent residency breach on a routable-but-unpooled shard.** The start path resolved its connection through `HarvestDbPool::pool_for`, which **falls back to the default shard's pool**. The router's shard set and the pool map are configured independently, so a shard the router accepts with no pool of its own (a real state mid a shard-add rollout) would have written residency-bound data to the **default** database while the response, the encoded `ExecutionId`, and the row's `shard_id` column all claimed the pinned shard. New `HarvestDbPool::exact_pool_for` (no fallback) + `db_conn_for_pinned_shard` make the **pinned** branch fail closed with a `503`; the unpinned branch is untouched. Proven RED: reverting the branch yields `201` with `shard_id: 3` and an `ExecutionId` encoding `0003` while the row lands on EU's database. (3) **P2 — a committed keyed replay must survive its shard being drained.** Placement resolution is split into `resolve_placement` (readable **and** writable — the placing path) and `resolve_placement_for_lookup` (readable only), so the #808 committed-replay probe can still resolve its shard and return the original `200` after the pinned shard is drained; the writable check is re-applied, by delegating back to the router, only on the genuinely-fresh path. (4) **P2 — rejection messages enumerated the deployment.** `Display` stays rich for operator logs, but the HTTP body now uses a new `ShardPlacementError::client_message()` that names only what the caller asked for and never the shard set, drain state, or declared key list — a start endpoint is often reachable by a lower-trust caller than the operator surfaces. The full error is logged via `tracing::warn!`. (5) **P2 — unbounded `residency_key`.** Capped at `MAX_RESIDENCY_KEY_LEN` (128) at the request boundary so a caller-supplied string is not reflected back unbounded. (6) `ShardPlacement` and `ShardPlacementError` (enum **and** per-variant) are `#[non_exhaustive]`, `with_residency_map` trims keys on insert and warns when a declared target is readable-but-drained, and `ShardRouter::is_writable` was added. **Test-evidence hardening (from the tests/AC-evidence review):** the success metric's *"and remain on across children/CAN"* clause and CAN inheritance had **no** falsifying test — the CAN mint site was audited by reading only. Added the real-worker e2e `worker_pinned_child_and_continue_as_new_successor_stay_on_the_pinned_shard` (one run spawns a child **and** continues-as-new; asserts the encoded `ExecutionId` **and** the row's `shard_id` for both descendants, on a **non-default** shard 5 so a `default_shard` regression is caught too — confirmed RED at `ShardId(65535)` vs `ShardId(5)`); `workflow_retry_stays_on_the_predecessor_shard` for the #523 retry path (non-default shard 6, confirmed RED); `child_timeout_race_inherits_the_parents_shard` for the #779 child-or-deadline race; four `WorkflowHandleClient::resolve_shard_placement` unit tests (it previously had **zero** callers and zero tests); `routable_but_unpooled_shard_fails_closed_503_and_writes_nothing`; and `negative_and_sentinel_shard_ids_are_rejected_400_over_http` (previously parse-layer only). The reset fixture's source shard moved from `0` — which was that suite's *default* shard, so it could not catch a "always use `default_shard`" regression — to a non-default shard. Two non-falsifiable assertions were removed/repaired: `post_start` now parses the body **strictly**, so a `text/plain` `400` fails (AC6 says *400 JSON*, and every rejection test's `body.get("execution_id").is_none()` was trivially true against `Value::Null`), and a `row_count(.., ExecutionId::new())` assertion that counted rows for a random never-inserted UUID (unconditionally `0`) was replaced. The placement suite is now **13** DB/HTTP tests. `docs/sharding.md`'s rejection table was corrected to the messages callers actually receive, and gained the fail-closed `503`, the deferred-start and rollout-ordering caveats, the residency-key cardinality note, and an explicit statement that `signal-with-start`/`update-with-start` and the in-process SDK start APIs carry **no** placement field (a documented residency gap, not a silent one); `docs/security-posture.md` gained a "Data residency and shard placement" section stating that `shard_id` is **not** a capability — placement selects a database, it does not authorise access to one. **Post-review hardening round 2 (Codex bot review of PR #1138 — two P1, two P2, all fixed):** (1) **P1 — a pinned committed-replay probe could resolve out of the DEFAULT shard's database.** The #808 committed-replay probe resolved its connection with `pool_for`, whose default-shard fallback is exactly what fix (2) above closed on the *fresh-start* path — but the probe was missed. For a **pinned** request at a routable-but-unpooled shard the probe would therefore query the default database, and a same-key claim living there (from an earlier unpinned start) would be returned as a successful replay **echoed as belonging to the requested residency shard** — a silent cross-shard breach on the read path. The probe now uses `exact_pool_for` when a placement was requested (returning `None` = probe MISS, so the caller falls through to the fresh pinned path and fails closed with `503`); the unpinned branch keeps `pool_for` byte-for-byte. Proven RED: reverting it returns `200` with `"shard_id": 3` and an `execution_id` encoding shard `0000`. (2) **P1 — a shard above `0xFFFE` silently truncated through the `ExecutionId` encoding.** `ShardId::new` is unbounded (`i32`) but `ExecutionId::new_for_shard` masks with `& 0xFFFF`, so a router (mis)configured with e.g. shard `0x1_0000` would accept a pin to it and mint ids that read back as shard `0` — placing residency-bound data in the wrong jurisdiction while every observation surface agreed with the caller. New `shard::MAX_ENCODABLE_SHARD` (`0xFFFE`) + `shard::is_encodable_shard`, checked at the **top** of `validate_pinned_shard` (so it rejects even when the router is configured to accept the value) and mirrored at the HTTP boundary in `parse_shard_placement`. The reserved `0xFFFF` sentinel is rejected for a *different* reason — it round-trips byte-for-byte but means "no shard encoded, fall back to the default shard" — and the two cases are pinned separately. (3) **P2 — conflicting residency keys that collide after trimming.** `with_residency_map` trims keys on insert, so two raw keys differing only in whitespace normalise to one entry; from an unordered source which mapping survived could vary across restarts, breaking the AC3 stable-mapping guarantee (and potentially moving work between jurisdictions). The builder now takes `impl IntoIterator` and **panics** on a post-trim duplicate that disagrees on the shard, consistent with `ShardRouter::new`'s documented boot-time panic contract; a duplicate that *agrees* is accepted. (4) **P2 — a throttled deferred start did not echo its pin.** A throttled (#607) start honours a placement — the resolved shard is threaded into `reserve_or_defer` — but its `202` body omitted `shard_id`, so a caller had no way at all to audit where a deferred pinned start would run (there is no `execution_id` to decode yet). The `202` now carries `shard_id` when placement was requested and omits it entirely otherwise, keeping an unpinned deferral byte-identical to a pre-#697 build. All four are covered by falsifiable tests confirmed RED against the pre-fix code: `pinned_committed_replay_probe_never_falls_back_to_the_default_shard` and `throttled_deferred_start_echoes_the_pinned_shard` (+ the `unpinned_throttled_deferred_start_omits_shard_id` control) in the placement suite — now **16** DB/HTTP tests — and `shard_outside_the_encodable_range_is_rejected_even_when_configured`, `encodable_shard_predicate_matches_the_uuid_round_trip`, `conflicting_residency_keys_that_collide_after_trimming_panic`, plus a duplicate-agreeing control in `shard.rs`. **Post-review hardening round 3 (Codex bot review of `697d0fa`, one P2):** the operator-facing effective-config snapshot (issue #695) reported only `readable_shards`/`writable_shards`/`default_shard`, so two replicas deployed with **conflicting residency maps** serialized identically while placing the same `residency_key` in **different jurisdictions** depending on which replica served the request — the highest-blast-radius misconfiguration this feature can have, and invisible. `ShardTopologyView` gains a `residency_map: BTreeMap<String, i32>` projection (`BTreeMap`-ordered, so a byte diff across replicas is meaningful; the keys are operator-declared jurisdiction labels, never caller input or credentials, and the endpoint is admin-gated — a deliberate asymmetry with the *rejection* path, which still never enumerates the declared key set to a lower-trust start caller). **Root cause was a missing coverage guard, not a missed line:** #695's exhaustive-destructure guard covers `WorkerConfig` but `ShardTopologyView::from_router` had none for `ShardRouter`, so the `residency_map` field this PR introduced slipped through silently. Closed with a **two-hop** guard — new `ShardRouter::parts() -> ShardRouterParts<'_>` (re-exported from `lib.rs`) destructures `Self` exhaustively, and `from_router` destructures `ShardRouterParts` exhaustively, both with **no `..`** — so a new placement-affecting router field is a compile error at *both* hops until surfaced. Both hops were verified by temporarily adding a probe field and confirming `E0027 pattern does not mention field` fires at each. `docs/sharding.md` gains a "Verifying fleet consistency *before* accepting pinned starts" section with the `jq -S`/`diff` recipe; `docs/api-contract.json`'s `/admin/config` description updated. Test: `shard_topology_surfaces_the_residency_map_so_replica_drift_is_visible` builds two routers with identical topology but **mirrored** maps and asserts the topology fields compare equal while `residency_map` differs — the projection is what makes the drift detectable — plus byte-stability across calls.
- **Per-key activity rate limits** (implemented) — see issue #699. Extends the static per-activity rate limiter (#332) so an activity's rate-limit bucket key is resolved **per-execution from the workflow input** (dot-path), giving each tenant its own RPS bucket instead of sharing one cluster-wide bucket. Mirrors the per-key concurrency design (#247) and the workflow-start throttle's composite-key reuse of `harvest_rate_limit_buckets` (#607). **Declaration**: new nested `#[activity(rate_limit(key = "input.tenant_id", rps = 50, burst = 10))]` attribute (modelled on `#[workflow(concurrency(key = …, limit = …))]`; `key` and `rps` required, `burst` optional) or `ActivityInfo::rate_limit_key_expr` directly. The pre-existing **flat** `rate_limit_rps`/`rate_limit_burst`/`rate_limit_key` attributes are unchanged (AC3). The nested form is **rejected at compile time on `local = true` activities** (mirroring `circuit_breaker`) — local activities bypass the dispatch path where rate limiting is enforced. **New `ActivityInfo` field** `rate_limit_key_expr: Option<&'static str>` (the dot-path; presence selects dynamic mode). All workspace `ActivityInfo` construction sites initialise it to `None`. **Composite-key scheme**: `queue::dynamic_rate_bucket_key(expr, resolved: Option<&str>) -> "dyn-rate:{expr_component}:{resolved_component}"` — namespaced by both the key *expression* and the resolved *value* so activities declaring the same expression share one bucket per resolved value (matching the static limiter's "same key → shared bucket → must agree on rps" rule), while distinct tenants get independent buckets. The distinct `dyn-rate:` prefix can never collide with a static key (bare activity name / user string) or a throttle key (`start-throttle:`). An execution whose key expression cannot be resolved (missing / null / non-object input) is passed as `None` and falls back to a shared `dyn-rate:{expr}:U` bucket (the distinct `U` marker) so it is still bounded, not unbounded — kept **distinct** from `Some("")`, a legitimately-resolved empty-string tenant (which buckets under `dyn-rate:{expr}:L0:`), so a malformed/missing input never cross-throttles a real empty-string tenant (Codex round-5 P2; see the post-review bullet below). The `expr` is **normalized** by stripping a leading `input.` (so `key = "input.tenant_id"` and `key = "tenant_id"` — which `resolve_concurrency_key` treats as the same field — share one bucket and are validated together), and **both** the normalized `expr` and the resolved value are **length-bounded** (`MAX_KEY_COMPONENT_LEN = 256`, via the shared `bound_key_component` helper): a component longer than the bound is replaced with a stable, **collision-resistant SHA-256** digest so a pathological resolved value (a giant tenant id) *or* a pathological expression (a very long dot-path / hand-built `ActivityInfo.rate_limit_key_expr`) can never blow the `harvest_rate_limit_buckets` btree PRIMARY KEY size limit and wedge the enqueue transaction in a retry loop. With both components bounded the whole composite key is **provably ≤ ~530 bytes** regardless of the macro or a hand-built `ActivityInfo`. The key is **injective by construction** (post-review, Codex P2): `bound_key_component` emits each component as either a **length-tagged literal** `L{byte_len}:{value}` (self-delimiting: after the `L`, the decimal length up to the next `:` says exactly how many bytes follow) or a **fixed-width collision-resistant hash** `H{64hex}` (full 256-bit SHA-256, hex-encoded). The `L`/`H` first-byte tags are **structurally disjoint**, so (a) a literal value that happens to equal a hash's string encoding never collides with that hash — the earlier `h:{digest}` hash form was itself a valid short literal, so a long value hashing to digest `D` and a short literal value equal to the string `h:{D}` produced the same component (cross-tenant sharing without a hash collision), now closed because a literal `H0123…` encodes to `L{len}:H0123…` while the hash stays `H0123…`; and (b) a `:` inside `expr` (a dot-path can address a JSON key containing `:`) or inside `resolved` can never split ambiguously — the `(expr, resolved)` pair maps to exactly one key and vice-versa, whether either component passed through unchanged or was hashed. Without this self-delimiting encoding, `key = "a"` + resolved `"b:c"` and `key = "a:b"` + resolved `"c"` would both flatten to `dyn-rate:a:b:c` — two genuinely-distinct exprs colliding onto one bucket, and because builder validation keys on the (normalized) expr, their independently-validated (possibly different) rps configs would collide first-writer-wins. **Resolution at the worker enqueue site** (`worker::persist_scheduled_activities`): when `activity.rate_limit_key_expr` is `Some`, the key is resolved against the **workflow input** (`WorkflowExecution.input`, the plain start input, threaded into the function) via `concurrency::resolve_concurrency_key` and set as `params.rate_limit_key`. The static path is unchanged when `rate_limit_key_expr` is `None`. **Lazy bucket registration** (`queue::ensure_rate_limit_bucket`, shared with the static startup registration): the composite bucket is `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING`-registered in the **same enqueue transaction** so the fail-closed `EXISTS` gate in `queue::claim_task` (and the circuit-breaker dispatch-time `try_consume_rate_limit_token`) always has a bucket row to read (else the task would stall forever). `refill_rate = rate_limit_rps`, `burst = rate_limit_burst.unwrap_or(rps)`. Static-limiter startup registration skips dynamic-key activities. **Claim / gate / debit unchanged**: `claim_task` keys entirely off the row's `rate_limit_key` value and is static-vs-dynamic agnostic. The circuit-breaker split (#369) is preserved — a breaker activity skips the claim-time gate and consumes at dispatch via `try_consume_rate_limit_token`, which now holds the composite key and works unchanged (its bucket exists because it was ensured at enqueue). **Cardinality landmine fixed** (team convention / ADR-0001 §7): `record_rate_limit_throttled` uses its argument as a metric **label**, and a composite dynamic key embeds unbounded tenant input. The metric is now labelled by the **bounded activity name** (`METRIC_LABEL_ACTIVITY`), never the raw bucket key — at the dispatch-defer site (`worker::process_activity_task`, passing `activity_name`) and the sampler site (`queue::check_throttled_keys` now returns distinct bounded `activity_name`s, not raw keys). The `harvest.rate_limit.throttled` metric's label changed from `key` to `activity` (BREAKING for operators — see post-review hardening below). The per-key token/refill **gauges** are separately fixed to exclude the unbounded key families (post-review #1). **Builder validation** (`validate_rate_limit_keys`): a dynamic-key activity without `rate_limit_rps` → `RateLimitKeyWithoutCap`; two activities declaring the same `rate_limit_key_expr` with different rps/burst → `RateLimitKeyMismatch`. Dynamic keys are validated in an **independent map keyed on the expression**, so a static key and a dynamic key_expr sharing the same string are never conflated. **SQLite guard** (`autumn-harvest-sqlite`): a dynamic-key activity is rejected at registration with the same unsupported-feature error as the static form. **Management API (AC7)**: `GET /admin/rate-limits` already enumerates all bucket rows, so composite `dyn-rate:…` keys appear automatically — no new surface; covered by a plugin HTTP test. A single-key fetch (`GET /admin/rate-limits/{key}`) works for a composite key too, but the key contains `:` and (for a nested path) `.`, so it **must be URL-encoded** in the path. **Post-review hardening** (issue #699 review): **BLOCKER — per-key gauge cardinality (#1)**: the per-key token/refill **gauge** sampler (`worker::spawn_rate_limit_sampler`) emitted the bucket `key` as a metric label with no filter, so an unbounded `dyn-rate:{expr}:{tenant}` key (buckets are never GC'd) would create one time-series per tenant forever. The sampler now runs through `queue::sample_rate_limit_buckets`, whose SQL excludes the unbounded key families (`RATE_LIMIT_GAUGE_SAMPLER_FILTER` = `WHERE key NOT LIKE 'dyn-rate:%' AND key NOT LIKE 'start-throttle:%'` — the pre-existing throttle family, #607, is the same class of unbounded caller-resolved key and was silently exposed too, so it is excluded here as well). Bounded static keys keep their per-key gauges; per-tenant bucket state is observable via `GET /admin/rate-limits`, not metrics. **BREAKING metric-label change (#2)**: `harvest.rate_limit.throttled` is now labelled `activity` (bounded) instead of `key` — any dashboard/alert keyed on the old `key` label must move to `activity`. The starter-pack dashboard panel, the anti-drift ground truth (`dashboard_pack_docs.rs`), and ADR-0001 §7 are updated. **Worker-level resolution test (#3)**: a worker-driven DB test proves the composite key is resolved from the **workflow input**, not the activity's own input — two executions of one workflow/activity that differ only in workflow input (`{"tenant_id":"acme"}` vs `{}`) resolve to `dyn-rate:L9:tenant_id:L4:acme` and the unresolved fallback `dyn-rate:L9:tenant_id:U` respectively, while the activity input is identical for both. **Coupled key-set with bucket-ensure (#4)**: `params.rate_limit_key` is stamped only inside the `if let Some(refill_rate)` block, so a dynamic key is never set without its bucket being ensured in the same transaction (a stamped key with no bucket row would stall the fail-closed claim/dispatch gate forever). **`input.` prefix normalization (#6)** and **resolved-key length bound (#5)** — see the composite-key scheme above; both spellings share one bucket and are validated together, and an oversized resolved value is hashed. **Flat + nested rejected at macro parse time (#7)**: combining the flat `rate_limit_rps`/`rate_limit_burst`/`rate_limit_key` attributes with the nested `rate_limit(...)` form is a compile error (they configure the same bucket incompatibly); trybuild fixture `rate_limit_flat_and_nested.rs`. **Concurrency-contention safe-side test + documented known limitation (#9)**: `claim_task`'s `rate_limit_debit` CTE debits a token even when the `claimed` UPDATE matches 0 rows because a per-key concurrency (`concurrency_key`) advisory-lock race was lost. This is a **pre-existing** (byte-identical to trunk `claim_task`), **safe-side** (it over-throttles — the invariant "a real call always holds a token" is never violated; the leak only ever reduces dispatch below budget, never allows a claim without a token), **bounded** (≤1 token per lost claim), and **self-healing** (refills within one interval) leak, shared with the static-rate + concurrency path. The `claim_task` SQL is deliberately **not** modified (all reviewers praised its byte-for-byte invariant, and the fix would touch the hot path for a harmless-direction edge); documented in a code comment near the CTE and covered by a two-connection advisory-lock-contention DB test asserting RUNNING count never exceeds the cap nor the rate budget. **Burst-fairness success-metric test (#10)**: a 10:1 burst DB test drains tenant A's bucket to 0 while B's is full and asserts B is claimed at exactly its burst while A is never claimed (zero cross-key bleed), making the headline "one noisy tenant cannot starve another" falsifiable. **Dynamic-form builder error wording (#11)**: a dynamic-key activity missing `rps` now returns `RateLimitKeyExprWithoutCap` (names `rate_limit(key = "…", rps = N)`), not the static `rate_limit_key … remove the rate_limit_key` wording. **Key delimiter injectivity (#13, and the follow-up Codex P2)**: the composite key is now **injective by construction** via self-delimiting, structurally-disjoint per-component encodings (`L{len}:{value}` literal / `H{64hex}` SHA-256 hash, `dyn-rate:{expr_component}:{resolved_component}`) rather than relying on `expr`/`resolved` being `:`-free or on the earlier ambiguous `h:{digest}` hash form — see the composite-key scheme above for the full rationale, the `key = "a"` + `"b:c"` vs `key = "a:b"` + `"c"` collision, and the literal-equal-to-a-hash collision it closes. The **payload-offload landmine (#14)** is noted below. **Both key components length-bounded (Codex P2)**: the earlier fix bounded only the *resolved* value, leaving the *expression* unbounded — a very long dot-path or a hand-built `ActivityInfo.rate_limit_key_expr` could push the composite btree PRIMARY KEY past Postgres's ~2704-byte limit, so `ensure_rate_limit_bucket`'s `INSERT` would fail and roll back the enqueue transaction (the workflow can't schedule its activity). The bound-or-hash logic is now factored into a shared `bound_key_component` helper applied to **both** the normalized `expr` and the `resolved` value, and the injective length prefix is taken over the *bounded* expr component — so the whole PK is provably ≤ ~530 bytes regardless of the macro or a hand-built `ActivityInfo`. Distinct oversized exprs still hash to distinct keys (no cross-tenant bleed). **`dyn-rate:` prefix reserved from static author keys (Codex P2)**: a static `rate_limit_key` is an unrestricted author string; a value like `rate_limit_key = "dyn-rate:L9:tenant_id:L4:acme"` would collide with the generated dynamic bucket for `rate_limit(key = "tenant_id")` tenant `acme`, and since static and dynamic keys are validated independently and both register `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, they'd race first-writer-wins on the shared bucket's rate/burst. A static `rate_limit_key` beginning with the reserved `dyn-rate:` prefix is now **rejected at the macro parse site** (compile error; trybuild fixture `rate_limit_key_reserved_prefix.rs`), **in `HarvestBuilder::try_build`** (`RateLimitKeyReservedPrefix`), **and — for a worker built via a direct `HandlerRegistry` that bypasses both — in the worker path itself** (Codex P2, second review round): `persist_scheduled_activities` returns `HarvestError::Config` (failing the schedule/suspension transaction, so no `ActivityScheduled` event and no task row — the activity is never enqueued under the colliding key) and `register_rate_limit_buckets` logs a `tracing::error!` and skips the colliding bucket at startup, consistent with the round-3 dynamic-no-rps guard which likewise lives in both places. This keeps the static and dynamic bucket namespaces provably disjoint on every start path. Covered by a worker-driven DB test asserting the workflow never completes and neither the activity task row nor the colliding bucket row is ever registered. (The `start-throttle:` prefix from #607 is a separate pre-existing namespace; this PR reserves only `dyn-rate:` — the one it generates — and leaves `start-throttle:` as a follow-up.) **Invalid dynamic key without `rps` fails loudly at schedule time (Codex P2)**: `HarvestBuilder::try_build` rejects a dynamic `rate_limit(key = "…")` with no `rps` (`RateLimitKeyExprWithoutCap`), but an application that builds the public `HandlerRegistry` **directly** bypasses that validation, so an `ActivityInfo { rate_limit_key_expr: Some(..), rate_limit_rps: None, .. }` could reach `persist_scheduled_activities`. Because the composite-key stamping and bucket-ensure both sit inside the `if let Some(refill_rate) = activity.rate_limit_rps` block (item #4 above), such an activity previously left **both** `params.rate_limit_key` and `dynamic_rate_buckets` unset and was silently enqueued with **no** rate limit — the exact failure a rate-limiting feature exists to prevent. `persist_scheduled_activities` now guards this: an activity with `rate_limit_key_expr.is_some() && rate_limit_rps.is_none()` returns `HarvestError::Config` **before** the stamping block, failing the schedule/suspension transaction (which rolls back — no `ActivityScheduled` event, no task row, so the activity is never enqueued unrated) rather than proceeding unrated. The failure surfaces loudly (logged `tracing::error! "task execution failed"`; the suspension-persist error propagates via `persist_workflow_outcome`'s non-terminal `Err` branch, so the task is re-dispatched and re-errors on the same invalid config — a loud retry-loop, strictly better than a silent no-limit, and only reachable on an unvalidated direct-registry build). A defensive `tracing::error!` in `register_rate_limit_buckets` also surfaces the invalid declaration at worker startup, before the first enqueue. Covered by a worker-driven DB test asserting the workflow never completes and the activity task row is never enqueued. **Comprehensive rate-limit validation at worker startup (Codex round-5 P2)**: the public `HandlerRegistry` path bypasses ALL `HarvestBuilder::try_build` rate-limit validation, so an invalid config slipped through and was only caught piecemeal (or not at all) by the schedule-time guards. Rather than keep bolting on per-case schedule-time guards, the whole class is now validated **once at the fallible `Worker::new` startup boundary**: the builder's validation is factored into a shared `builder::validate_activity_rate_limits` (accepting an iterator of `&ActivityInfo` so both the builder's `Vec` and the registry's `HashMap::values()` validate without an owned copy — `ActivityInfo` is not `Clone`), and `Worker::new` calls it (mapped to `HarvestError::Config`) before its poll loop and first enqueue. This also closes two gaps the schedule-time guards never covered: (a) a dynamic `rate_limit(key = …)` on a **local** activity — which the `#[activity]` macro rejects at parse time but a hand-built `ActivityInfo` bypasses, silently running unrated inline via `run_local_activity_inline` — now rejected with the new `HarvestBuilderError::RateLimitKeyExprOnLocalActivity` (Codex worker.rs:4693); and (b) two activities sharing a normalized key-expression with **conflicting rps/burst**, whose shared `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` bucket would otherwise be insertion-order dependent (Codex worker.rs:4826). The schedule-time guards in `persist_scheduled_activities`/`register_rate_limit_buckets` remain as **defense-in-depth** behind this primary startup gate. Scope: the local reject covers the **dynamic** form only; the pre-existing static-rate-on-local #332 asymmetry stays a documented follow-up. Covered by direct-registry startup tests (`worker_startup_rejects_dynamic_rate_limit_on_local_activity`, `worker_startup_rejects_conflicting_rps_for_same_key_expr`, `worker_startup_accepts_valid_direct_registry`, plus the reframed dynamic-no-rps / reserved-prefix startup tests). **Unresolved key distinct from an empty-string tenant (Codex round-5 P2, worker.rs:4720)**: `resolve_concurrency_key` returns `Some("")` for a real empty-string tenant (`{"tenant_id": ""}`) and `None` for missing/null/non-object input, but the enqueue site's `.unwrap_or_default()` collapsed **both** onto the same `L0:` fallback bucket — cross-throttling malformed/missing executions against a legitimate empty tenant. `dynamic_rate_bucket_key` now takes `resolved: Option<&str>` and encodes `None` as the structurally-disjoint single-byte `U` marker (`dyn-rate:{expr}:U`) while `Some("")` still encodes as `L0:` (`dyn-rate:{expr}:L0:`), so the two are provably distinct buckets (the `U`/`L`/`H` first-byte tags keep the whole composite key injective). The worker call site passes `resolve_concurrency_key(...).as_deref()` through instead of `.unwrap_or_default()`. Covered by `dynamic_rate_bucket_key_none_unresolved_is_distinct_from_empty_string_tenant` and the updated absent-field worker-resolution assertion. **Collision-resistant SHA-256 digest for oversized key components (Codex P2, queue.rs:150)**: `bound_key_component`'s oversized (`H…`) form originally used a 64-bit `seahash::hash`, which is NOT collision-resistant against tenant-influenced input — two distinct >256-byte resolved values (or expressions) sharing a 64-bit digest would silently share one `dyn-rate` bucket (the `L`/`H` tags fix *format* collisions, not *digest* collisions). The `H` form is now the **full 256-bit SHA-256** of the component's UTF-8 bytes, hex-encoded (`H{64hex}`, 65 bytes; the `sha2` crate is already an unconditional `autumn-harvest` dependency, used by `payload_store.rs`/`completion_callback.rs`), so a digest collision is computationally infeasible and distinct oversized components get distinct buckets in practice. The `H` first-byte tag (disjoint from `L`/`U`) is preserved, so injectivity and the literal-vs-hash disjointness are unchanged; the composite key stays well under the ~2704-byte btree PK limit (both-oversized ≈ 140 bytes). `seahash` usage elsewhere (shard routing, jitter, build-id hashing, history-export digests) is untouched — only this tenant-facing bucket-key component needed collision resistance. The oversized-component tests recompute the expected digest via SHA-256; the disjointness test asserts the fixed 65-byte `H{64hex}` width. **Reject non-finite / non-positive rate & burst in the shared validator (Codex P2, builder.rs:2330)**: the shared `validate_activity_rate_limits` (now run by both `try_build` and `Worker::new`) only checked that a dynamic key *had* an rps — not that `rate_limit_rps` (and `rate_limit_burst`, when set) is finite and strictly positive, which the `#[activity]` macro enforces universally (`n <= 0.0` → compile error). A direct-registry `rate_limit_rps: Some(0.0)` therefore started the worker, created a `burst = tokens = 0` bucket, and left every scheduled dynamic activity permanently unclaimable (the token gate can never reach 1). The validator now rejects any activity (static OR dynamic — the macro's positivity check is universal) whose `rate_limit_rps`/`rate_limit_burst` is `!is_finite() || <= 0.0` with the new `HarvestBuilderError::RateLimitRateNotPositive { activity, field }` (stricter than the macro: also catches `NaN`/`±inf`, which `n <= 0.0` alone lets through). Because it runs at both boundaries, the `HarvestBuilder` and the direct-`HandlerRegistry`/`Worker::new` paths are both covered. Covered by `worker_new_rejects_non_positive_dynamic_rate_limit_rps`, `worker_new_rejects_non_positive_or_non_finite_rate_limit_burst`, and `worker_new_accepts_valid_positive_dynamic_rate_limit`. **Forward-looking payload-offload note (#14)**: if the start-path `WorkflowStarted` input is ever routed through the large-payload claim-check offloader (#524), `WorkflowExecution.input` would be a small reference envelope rather than the real input object, so a dynamic key would resolve to `None` and land in the shared `dyn-rate:{expr}:U` fallback bucket for every such execution. That is deterministic (no replay bug) but degrades per-key isolation to a single shared bucket; the resolution site should inflate the offloaded input first, or resolve the key before offloading, when that path lands. **Pre-existing asymmetry (follow-up, not fixed here)**: the **static** rate-limit attributes are NOT rejected on `local = true` activities (only the new dynamic `rate_limit(...)` form is). A static rate-limited local activity silently bypasses rate limiting (local activities run inline, off the dispatch path). Flagged as a follow-up. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no replay/determinism impact, no shard-routing change.** Buckets and enqueue are **shard-local** (consistent with per-key concurrency #247 and the activity limiter): a documented, out-of-scope limitation is that cross-shard global rate coordination is not attempted, so a key's effective rate across a multi-shard cluster is `per-shard-rate × shards` (see `docs/sharding.md`). **Tests**: pure unit tests for `dynamic_rate_bucket_key` (`queue.rs`); macro-expansion tests for the flat (AC3) and nested forms + two trybuild compile-fail fixtures (`rate_limit(...)` on `local = true`, `rate_limit(key = …)` missing `rps`); builder-validation tests (dynamic-without-rps, same-expr mismatch, matching/distinct exprs, static/dynamic independence); DB integration tests in `autumn-harvest/tests/integration/rate_limit_key_tests.rs` (cross-tenant isolation / success metric, shared bucket, defer-not-fail AC6, lazy registration, static-unchanged AC3, compose-with-#247-concurrency AC8); plugin HTTP integration test (`GET /admin/rate-limits` lists the composite key).
- Partial availability for cross-shard fan-out READ endpoints (issue #756). Before, a single unreachable shard's pool turned every cross-shard **read** endpoint into a whole-request `500`: each fanned-out loop did `acquire_conn(shard_pool).await?` inside `iter_shards()`, so one down shard `?`-propagated into a top-level error even though the other shards' data was readable. Now these endpoints **collect-and-continue**: a reachable shard's rows still flow, an unreachable shard is named in a machine-readable `unavailable_shards`, and the endpoint returns `200 OK` with the union plus a `status` verdict rather than failing wholesale. **Writes keep strict failure semantics**, and the single-execution business-id resolver (#805) keeps its `503`-to-avoid-false-`404` behavior. **Reuses the existing `shard_fanout` scaffold** rather than reinventing partial-availability. New shared, pure, unit-tested helper `shard_fanout::collect_fanout_rows(observations) -> FanoutRows<R>` (`{ rows, status: FanoutStatus, unavailable_shards: Vec<UnavailableShard> }`) flattens per-shard `ShardObservation<R>`s into the union of reachable rows plus a `complete`/`partial`/`unavailable` verdict, alongside the existing `expected_shards`/`pools_by_shard`/`summarize_shard_errors`/`FanoutStatus`/`UnavailableShard` used by `workflow_count`/`usage`/`workflow_reachability`. A new async `api.rs::observe_shards(api_state, query_shard)` helper drives the collect-and-continue fan-out across `expected_shards` (so a router-known but pool-less shard mid a shard-add rollout is reported `unavailable`, never silently omitted), and `api.rs::fanout_list_json(items_key, rows, status, unavailable)` serializes the conditional envelope. The duplicate `api::UnavailableShard` struct (structurally identical to `shard_fanout::UnavailableShard`, used by the external-handoff coverage) was removed so the partial-availability shape is single-sourced. **Response-shape design — conditional envelope for bare-array endpoints, additive fields for object endpoints (deviation from the initial "envelope-always" sketch, driven by AC3 + a large consumer audit).** The five legacy **bare-array** list endpoints — `GET /workflows` (standard default + the `?no_progress_minutes` stalled loader), `GET /workers`, `GET /admin/schedules`, `GET /dead-letters`, and `GET /dags` — keep their **byte-for-byte bare-array shape on the happy path** (every shard reachable, `status == complete`) and only switch to the `{ <items>, status, unavailable_shards }` envelope **when degraded** (`status != complete`). This is the literal reading of AC2 ("*every degraded* response carries the indicator") + AC3 ("no breaking change for existing clients on the happy path"): wrapping the default bare array unconditionally would (a) be a genuine breaking change for external clients that parse the default `GET /workflows` array — which AC3 forbids — and (b) break ~57 internal test assertions across 6+ files (`workflow_filter_integration.rs`, `stalled_workflow_tests.rs`, `api_scheduler_integration.rs`, `batch_operations_integration.rs`, `build_routing_ui_integration.rs`, `legal_hold_integration.rs`) that parse those responses via `.as_array()`. The conditional switch keys on `status != FanoutStatus::Complete` (not `unavailable_shards.is_empty()`) so a degenerate `Unavailable`-with-empty-`unavailable_shards` verdict still surfaces as an envelope, never a silently-empty bare `[]`. The three **object** shapes get the two fields **additively (always present, `complete`/empty on the happy path)**: `GET /workflows?paginated` (`WorkflowListPage` gains `status` + `unavailable_shards`), `GET /workers/health` (`FleetHealth` fields stay top-level, `status` + `unavailable_shards` inserted alongside via a manual `serde_json::Value::Object` map insertion — no field collision, core `FleetHealth` untouched), and `GET /dead-letters/aggregate` (the pre-#385 hard-`?` fan-out is now collect-and-continue; `DlqAggregateResponse`'s fields stay top-level with the two additive fields inserted the same way — core `merge_dlq_aggregates` unchanged). The `GET /dead-letters` runbook-enrichment secondary read was also made best-effort (skip a shard that goes unreachable mid-request rather than `500`). **Total storage-layer unavailability is an honest `503`, not a `200 []`.** `observe_shards` guards on `storage_pool()` up front: when no pool is installed at all (misconfiguration or the boot window) it returns `503 Service Unavailable` — we cannot even enumerate shards, so a bare `200 []` would mask a whole-storage outage. Per-**shard** unreachability still degrades to `200 partial`. A router-known but pool-less shard mid a shard-add rollout is resolved exactly (`pools.get(&shard_id)`, mirroring the #805 business-id resolver), **never** through `ShardedDbPool::pool_for`'s default-shard fallback (which would silently query the DEFAULT shard's DB in its place, duplicate default-shard rows, and let `status` falsely read `complete`); it is folded into `unavailable_shards` instead. **Consumer audit finding:** the Vantage UI (`ui.rs`) queries the shard DBs *directly* (it does not consume these HTTP JSON endpoints), so wrapping the JSON never affects UI rendering — the only internal Rust caller of `load_workflows_from_shards` (the UI workflow list) reads `.executions` and shows reachable-shard rows on a partial read, and now also renders a "⚠ Partial results" banner naming the unreachable shard(s) so a partial list is not mistaken for the authoritative fleet state. The `harvest` CLI is a generic passthrough that renders whatever JSON returns; on a degraded cross-shard read (`workflow list`/`worker list`/`schedule list`/`dlq list`/`dag list`) it emits a `WARNING: cross-shard read is partial; N shard(s) unavailable: <id>: <reason>, …` notice on **STDERR** (new `fanout_partial_notice` helper, `eprintln!`'d by the caller) — keeping **STDOUT** a clean, parseable body (`-o json | jq`) on both the happy and degraded paths, so programmatic consumers of the partial-availability data are not corrupted by a prepended warning line. **Scope:** Tier 1 (the seven AC1-named loaders + `GET /dags`) is fully converted: `load_workflows_from_shards` (→ `WorkflowFanoutPage` + pure `build_workflow_fanout_page`), `load_stalled_workflows_from_shards` (→ `FanoutRows` + pure `build_stalled_fanout`), `load_schedules_from_shards` (→ `FanoutRows` + pure `build_schedule_fanout`; now the single source of truth shared by both `list_schedules` and `list_dags`, so `GET /dags` degrades and neither duplicates the query + effective-name sort), `load_dead_letters_from_shards` (+ pure `build_dead_letter_fanout`), `aggregate_dead_letters`, `list_workers_handler`, and `workers_health`. Tier 2 (`GET /audit`, `GET /workflows/summaries`, `GET /admin/schedules/decisions`) is **deferred** to keep the PR reviewable and the contract churn bounded — each is a clean candidate for the same pattern but adds contract/CLI/test surface; noted as follow-up. The internal `query_running_count` scheduler read is deliberately left fail-loud (it's a correctness counter, not an operator read). **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, no shard-routing change** — this is entirely a plugin-layer read-path shape change.
